author: jddandrewlauren
body:
Closes #59.

The review pass over the whole 300-square F1 pool: every generated line read, the defects
fixed at their source, and deck feasibility proved rather than asserted.

## The taste gate: this pool is 300 squares, not ~180

**This is the decision the PR review needs to make, and I did not make it for you.**

#53 decision 6 targeted ~70 handcrafted / ~110 generated at roughly 60 certain / 90 medium /
30 rare. What #57 and #58 actually built is **300 squares at 40 / 191 / 69**. The ~110 estimate
was arithmetically incompatible with the template roster it was written beside: seven of the
fourteen templates apply to all three entity tiers, so 22 drivers x 7 templates is 154 generated
squares before the ambition templates add anything.

Two reasons I did not prune ~120 lines to force the number:

1. **Pool size is not a pacing lever.** PLAN.md D6 is explicit: "Pacing is governed by the
   rarity mix of a *card*, not pool size. Pool size only controls variety across a season."
   A deck takes at most 3 squares per template (`MAX_PER_TEMPLATE`), so generated supply is
   capped at 42 selectable whether the pool holds 110 generated squares or 230. Pruning 120
   lines would cost season variety — which drivers show up week to week — and buy nothing
   measurable.
2. **The 40/191/69 spread is not a mix problem, it is a tier-honesty problem** (below), and
   pruning does not fix it. Neither does the override mechanism, which can reword and prune
   but cannot retier.

#59's own acceptance criteria are all met at 300 squares. If you want ~180, say so on the issue
and it is a follow-up that edits `templates.json` tier rules — not a rework of this PR.

### The tier-honesty finding

Reading all 230 lines against CONTEXT.md's tier definitions (certain ~ most races, medium ~
roughly every other race, rare ~ a few times a season), the medium tier is systematically
over-assigned:

- `driver_penalty`, `driver_swears`, `driver_battery_moan`, `driver_moans_at_team` are `medium`
  for all 22 drivers. A *named* driver being penalised in a given race is nearer 15% than 50%.
  Honest tiering would put points/field drivers at `rare` for all four.
- `driver_dnf` is `medium` for points and field. Modern reliability puts a given driver's DNF
  at 2-3 races in 24.
- `driver_wins` is `medium` for all seven podium-tier drivers. Seven drivers cannot each win
  roughly every other race; realistically three can.
- `driver_leads_lap` is `certain` for all seven podium-tier drivers, which reads as a
  pit-cycle lead rather than a real one.

Retiering honestly would move ~100 squares from medium to rare — **away** from 60/90/30, not
toward it. Reaching that spread needs the *entity* tiers or the template roster to change, and
#53 decision 4 marks entity tiers operator-set. That is why this is a question and not a commit.

## Overrides and prunes

`overrides.json` is still `{"prune": [], "reword": {}}`, and that is the review's finding rather
than an omission. Every prose defect the read turned up was template-wide, so the honest fix was
the template — patching three symptoms through overrides while the source keeps emitting them is
worse engineering. No generated line earned a prune.

| Fix | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| `driver_battery_moan` exclusivity `battery_moan:{driver}` -> `radio_moan:{driver}` | A battery moan *is* a moan over team radio about the car. "Verstappen moans: no battery" + "Verstappen moans at Red Bull" was one radio clip marking two cells — D6's prohibition. #58 had already filed handcrafted "Max Complains About the Car" under `radio_moan:VER`; this finishes it for all 22 drivers. |
| `team_slow_stop` description -> "A pit stop for {team} goes wrong — ..." | Read "A Alpine pit stop", "A Audi pit stop", "A Aston Martin pit stop" for three of eleven teams. Reworded to avoid the article rather than override three squares. |
| `hand:rain_arrives` label -> "Rain Starts Falling" | The only one of 70 handcrafted labels not in title case. |
| `hand:orange_smoke` description -> "Verstappen fans light flares/smoke." | Carried an authoring note into player-facing copy: "Track-dependent — strongest in Europe". The note is dropped and the operator's surviving sentence is byte-for-byte untouched — nothing else in the field changed. |

ids are unchanged by all four, so `poolVersion` stays `v2` per themes/README's rule.

## Tier and source counts

`pool:build` -> 300 squares. Selectable = what one deck could actually draw, under the 3-per-template cap.

| Tier | Pool | Handcrafted | Generated | Selectable | Deck quota |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| certain | 40 | 25 | 15 | 34 | 13 |
| medium | 191 | 32 | 159 | 64 | 20 |
| rare | 69 | 13 | 56 | 34 | 7 |

| Source | Pool | Selectable | Deck quota |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| handcrafted | 70 | 70 | 24 |
| generated | 230 | 42 | 16 |

235 distinct exclusivity groups, against the 24 a card needs.

The joint constraint has slack too, which the per-axis table hides: the deck's 16 generated
squares can all come from medium (32 selectable), leaving handcrafted to supply 13/4/7 against
25/32/13 available.

## Feasibility, executable

`composeDeck`'s `assertPoolCanSupply` passes against the committed artefact, and the seeded deal
smoke test deals a compliant card — both already pinned by #58's tests, which still pass.

Added to `apps/api/test/deck.test.ts`: **composes and deals for every seed, not just a lucky one**.
One seed proves the pool can be drawn from; it does not prove the pool is comfortable. A pool that
only just reaches the quotas succeeds on some seeds and exhausts all 200 draw attempts on others.
25 seeds, each composing a full 40-square deck to exact tier and source quota and dealing six
players' cards, is what "without straining" means as a test. It passes, including after the
exclusivity-group merge above tightened the pool.

## Longest labels, for the legibility pass (#47)

The pool sits at **both** ceilings with zero margin — 30 characters (build-enforced) and a
10-character unbreakable run (documented in themes/README, *not* enforced).

Longest by characters:

| Chars | Longest run | Label |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 30 | 8 | Lindblad moans at Racing Bulls |
| 30 | 8 | Steward Decision Baffles Booth |
| 29 | 8 | Engineer Says "We're Looking" |
| 28 | 10 | Hulkenberg moans: no battery |
| 28 | 10 | Verstappen moans: no battery |
| 28 | 10 | Verstappen moans at Red Bull |
| 28 | 9 | Both Cadillacs in the Points |
| 28 | 6 | Alonso moans at Aston Martin |

**27 squares sit at the 10-character run ceiling**, all of them driven by three names:
`Verstappen`, `Hulkenberg`, `Antonelli` (9), plus the handcrafted `Hammertime`, `Grandstand`,
`Retirement`, `Strategist`, `Blistering`, `Dangerous!"`.

`driver_moans_at_team` at 30 characters for Lindblad/Racing Bulls is the tightest template: any
longer driver-team pairing added later fails the build. That is a loud failure rather than a
production one, so it is a note, not a blocker.

## Findings not fixed here

Posted to #59 as well:

1. **Remaining single-event-marks-two-cells overlaps.** Unlike the battery/radio moan case these
   are partial overlaps, not subsets, so grouping them would wrongly exclude the non-overlapping
   half. Judgement call, left for the taste gate: `out:{driver}` vs `gravel:{driver}` (a
   race-ending beaching marks both, but gravel is explicitly "race over or not");
   `stewards:time_penalty` vs `penalty:{driver}`; `retirement:early`/`retirement:power_unit` vs
   `out:{driver}`; `team:cadillac_overperforms` vs `in_points:PER`/`in_points:BOT`.
2. **"Nobody Retires" contradicts 22 DNF squares.** `hand:nobody_retires` (rare) is not grouped
   with any `out:{driver}`, so a card can carry both it and "Albon DNFs". Not a double-mark — a
   dead cell, which is arguably the point of a rare square, but worth a decision.
3. **Diacritic inconsistency in entities.json**: `Pérez` carries its accent, `Hulkenberg` does
   not. Both are 10-char runs either way,

author: ferousco-dev
body:
## The deployment problem

Vercel's Git integration deployed straight from the push. It never looked at the CI result, so **a red build shipped anyway** — the checks were reporting on a release that had already gone out.

Two changes make that impossible:

1. `apps/web/vercel.json` sets `git.deploymentEnabled.main: false`, so the integration stops deploying.
2. Two jobs become the only path to a deployment, both `needs: verify`:

| Job | Trigger |
| --- | --- |
| `deploy-preview` | pull request |
| `deploy-production` | push to `main` |

A failed check now means **no deployment happened**, rather than a deployment marked as failed.

## Three details worth calling out

**Production deploys are serialised** (`concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: false`). Two racing deploys is how an older commit ends up live.

**The deployment is smoke-checked.** The job fails unless the new URL answers 200 on both `/` and `/api/health`. A deploy that builds, boots, and then falls over on the first request should not report success.

**The credential check is a step, not a job-level `if`** — secrets are not available in job conditions. This keeps the workflow green before the Vercel token exists instead of failing every run until it is added, and emits a warning annotation so a skipped production deploy is visible rather than silent.

## Header

It offered "Sign in" and "Start free" to people who were already signed in.

Resolved on the client rather than during render: reading the session server-side would make the most visited page in the product dynamic in order to change two links. `getSession` reads the existing cookie with no network round trip.

The unresolved frame holds its width rather than guessing, so a signed-in visitor never sees "Sign in" flash and then correct itself. Both the desktop header and the mobile sheet use the same component, so they cannot drift.

Not a security boundary — the middleware still guards `/dashboard`.

Verified against a real session:
```
signed out   Sign in -> /login,  Start free -> /signup
signed in    Open dashboard -> /dashboard    (no Sign in, no Start free)
```

typecheck 8/8, lint 6/6, build pass.

## What you need to add

I set `VERCEL_ORG_ID` and `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` as repo secrets already — they are identifiers, not credentials. **One thing is left, and only you can create it:**

```
VERCEL_TOKEN
```

Generate at **vercel.com → Settings → Tokens**, scope it to the `ferouss-projects` team, then add it under **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**.

Until it exists, CI stays green and production simply is not deployed, with a warning on the run saying so.

author: billbinaz
body:
This pull request introduces two main features: the container now prints its image tag on startup, and you can optionally run the Plex trash cleanup once immediately when the container starts by setting an environment variable. The changes include updates to the Docker build process, the entrypoint script, documentation, and tests to support and validate these features.

**New Features and Behavior:**

* The container prints the image tag (baked at build time) during startup, helping with traceability and debugging. (`Dockerfile`, `src/entrypoint.sh`, `.github/workflows/build-docker-on-pr.yml`, `.github/workflows/build-docker-on-tag.yml`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-dd2c0eb6ea5cfc6c4bd4eac30934e2d5746747af48fef6da689e85b752f39557R5-R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b088b6b580ca5a4a792e94aada1f7b8f581b83b987ff10fd15321f24b4ea68b6R121-R122) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f7e4972b0b45a5b809ad4f866d6f9185d7021754b8ba51acd172e5a22b4a758aR116-R117) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b085bf173708890f767512dee6bcf4737c31e3f038639176fe6679abee5b5593R23-R60) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-b085bf173708890f767512dee6bcf4737c31e3f038639176fe6679abee5b5593R146)
* Added support for a `PLEX_DELETE_RUN_ON_STARTUP` environment variable. When set to a truthy value, the container will run the trash cleanup job once on startup before starting the cron schedule. (`src/entrypoint.sh`, `README.md`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b085bf173708890f767512dee6bcf4737c31e3f038639176fe6679abee5b5593R11-R12) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b085bf173708890f767512dee6bcf4737c31e3f038639176fe6679abee5b5593R23-R60) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b085bf173708890f767512dee6bcf4737c31e3f038639176fe6679abee5b5593R160-R166) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R99-R104)

**Build and Docker Image Improvements:**

* The Docker build process now injects the image tag as a build argument and persists it to `/app/image-version`, which is read and logged by the entrypoint. (`Dockerfile`, `.github/workflows/build-docker-on-pr.yml`, `.github/workflows/build-docker-on-tag.yml`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-dd2c0eb6ea5cfc6c4bd4eac30934e2d5746747af48fef6da689e85b752f39557R5-R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b088b6b580ca5a4a792e94aada1f7b8f581b83b987ff10fd15321f24b4ea68b6R121-R122) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f7e4972b0b45a5b809ad4f866d6f9185d7021754b8ba51acd172e5a22b4a758aR116-R117)

**Documentation Updates:**

* Updated the README to document the new startup run feature and that the container prints its image tag during startup. (`README.md`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R99-R104)

**Testing Enhancements:**

* Added and updated tests to check for the new constants, environment variable handling, image tag logging, and the presence of new logic in the entrypoint script. (`tests/test_entrypoint.py`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2d6b0a1cb7d28ceccc01b5cab65c43817d2ff0f84ce30d84227099d40629ef5bR52-R56) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2d6b0a1cb7d28ceccc01b5cab65c43817d2ff0f84ce30d84227099d40629ef5bR191-R192) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2d6b0a1cb7d28ceccc01b5cab65c43817d2ff0f84ce30d84227099d40629ef5bR207-R229)

author: danicek555
body:
Dvě veřejné stránky, `/privacy` a `/terms`, na doméně aplikace. Google do souhlasné obrazovky vyžaduje čitelnou stránku, ne dokument ke stažení.

## Zásady ochrany osobních údajů

Obsah odpovídá tomu, co aplikace skutečně dělá, ne obecné šabloně:

- tabulka zpracovávaných údajů včetně IP adresy u schválení fáze a hashovaných PIN kódů,
- cookies: přihlašovací na 12 hodin, portálová na 7 dní, žádné analytické,
- dodavatelé: Vercel, Neon, Resend, OpenAI a Google, u každého co se k němu dostane,
- u OpenAI je uvedeno, že jde o podklady o zakázce a posledních pět zpráv, a že se volá jen na vyžádání,
- sekce o napojení Google účtu: `gmail.send` neumí čtení pošty, `drive.file` vidí jen na soubory, které aplikace vytvořila, tokeny jsou šifrované,
- odstavec o Limited Use podle Google API Services User Data Policy — bez něj neprojde verifikace.

## Podmínky užívání

Provozovatel, účel nástroje, účty a přístupy, pravidla užívání, odpovědnost za data, dostupnost bez SLA, omezení odpovědnosti, rozhodné právo ČR.

## Nedokončené údaje

Identifikace provozovatele je v `src/lib/legal.ts` a je zatím prázdná. Dokud je, obě stránky nahoře hlásí, že dokument není dokončený a že se adresa nemá zadávat Googlu — vyjmenují i to, co chybí. Doplnění je jedna změna v jednom souboru.

## Ostatní

- `robots.txt` povoluje `/privacy` a `/terms`, zbytek aplikace zůstává zakázaný.
- Odkazy na obě stránky jsou v patičce přihlášení a klientského portálu.
- `docs` doplněno do `INTERNAL_PATH` v `proxy.ts` — nepřihlášený se odklání už v middleware.

## Ověření

`tsc` a `eslint` čisté, testy 122/122, produkční build prošel a obě stránky se prerendrovaly staticky; text jsem si ověřil z vygenerovaného HTML včetně upozornění o nedokončenosti.

author: vreyesm
body:
## Alcance

Auditoría legal del cálculo de asistentes técnicos en establecimientos SLEP: bonificación de zona, salud/IUSC y situaciones previsionales AFP. No se extiende a VTF, JUNJI, Integra ni a regímenes previsionales cuyas tasas no están modeladas.

## Hallazgos, base legal y corrección

| Hallazgo confirmado | Base legal revisada | Cómo se corrigió |
| --- | --- | --- |
| La bonificación de zona podía resultar en cero cuando faltaba el bruto efectivo del mes anterior, sin distinguir “no corresponde” de “falta antecedente”. | Ley N.º 21.819, artículo 4. | Se agregó `zoneCalculationStatus`. Cuando existe porcentaje de zona pero falta el bruto previo, el motor devuelve estado incompleto, la UI bloquea el avance y no presenta un líquido numérico como válido. |
| El plan Isapre completo se descontaba del líquido, pero la base del IUSC no rebajaba toda la cotización adicional permitida. | Ley sobre Impuesto a la Renta, artículo 42 N.º 1; SII, ORD. N.º 2.406 de 2016. | La base tributable rebaja la cotización efectiva de salud hasta el límite conjunto de `7% × tope imponible previsional`. |
| No existía una combinación correcta para pensionados por vejez o invalidez total que deciden continuar cotizando AFP. | Decreto ley N.º 3.500, artículo 69; Ley N.º 19.728, artículo 2. | Se creó un estado explícito que conserva AFP y salud, pero excluye AFC. La exención declarada mantiene salud y elimina AFP/AFC. |
| Un estado genérico de pensionado que continuaba cotizando también podía excluir erróneamente AFC a una persona con invalidez parcial. | Ley N.º 19.728, artículo 2, que exceptúa la invalidez parcial de la exclusión del Seguro de Cesantía. | El estado sin AFC se acotó por tipo y UI exclusivamente a vejez/invalidez total. La invalidez parcial usa el flujo AFP ordinario con AFP, salud y AFC; se agregó una regresión específica. |
| Un régimen previsional no modelado podía seguir mostrando un “sueldo líquido estimado” numérico. | Deber de no sustituir tasas y topes de un régimen distinto por parámetros AFP. | El motor marca el cálculo como no soportado, la UI bloquea “Ver resultado” y el resumen muestra “Líquido no disponible” en lugar de una cifra incompleta. |

## Fuentes oficiales

- Ley N.º 21.819, artículo 4: https://www.bcn.cl/leychile/navegar?idNorma=1224471
- Decreto ley N.º 3.500, artículo 69: https://www.bcn.cl/leychile/navegar?idNorma=7147
- Ley N.º 19.728, artículos 2 y 5: https://www.bcn.cl/leychile/navegar?idNorma=184979
- Ley N.º 21.109, artículo 31: https://www.bcn.cl/leychile/navegar?idNorma=1123513
- SII, ORD. N.º 2.406 de 2016: https://www.sii.cl/pagina/jurisprudencia/adminis/2016/renta/ja2406.htm

## Límites explícitos

- La zona exige el bruto efectivo anterior y no se autocompleta.
- Un régimen distinto de AFP permanece sin cálculo automático.
- No incluye jardines VTF ni otros empleadores o modalidades.

## Validación

- `pnpm test`: 104/104.
- `pnpm test:automation`: 13/13.
- `pnpm check`: 0 diagnósticos.
- `pnpm build`: 30 páginas.
- `git diff --check`: correcto.
- Firma OpenPGP del head `2347930`: válida.
- Cloudflare Pages: exitoso.
- Revisión independiente final: sin findings accionables.

```
total 674 checks: 670 passed, 0 failed, 4 known, 0 fixed
```

## なぜ広げたか

C++ 対応で難しいのは翻訳ではなくリンクの側にある。`.cpp` を `c++` へ渡す
だけなら拡張子を見れば済むが、F-008 の失敗様式は**「ソースが `.c` だけの
実行ファイルが C++ に依存する」**場合に出る。前回はその**直接の形**しか
見ていなかった。

## 依存の閉包

### `chain/` — 間に純 C の層を挟む

```
topc[C] → mid[C] → deep[C++]
```

`topc` は C++ のライブラリを**直接には知らない**。「直接の依存が C++ なら」
で判定している実装は、ここで取りこぼす。リンクが `c++` で行われ、
二層越しに `std::string` を使う関数が動くところまで見る。

### `reverse/` — 向きを変える

C++ の実行ファイルが C のライブラリに依存する。「C++ のソースがあるか」
だけを見ていると、依存の側が C であることに引きずられる実装がありうる。
C++ のテストターゲット自体も置いた。

## 記号が解決するだけでは足りない

引数の形を見るだけでは、実行時が本当に繋がっているか分からない。
`cpplib` に3つの異なる機構を持たせた。

| | 何が要るか |
|---|---|
| `cpplib_len` | 標準ライブラリ（`std::string`） |
| `cpplib_throws` | **例外の巻き戻し**。記号が揃っていても機構が無ければ abort する |
| `cpplib_ctor_ran` | **書庫の中の大域オブジェクトの構築子**（`.init_array`） |

判定は C の側で行い、**終了状態でどれが欠けたかまで分かる**ようにしてある。

## 増分

depfile は driver が出す。C++ の側でも同じように出て、同じように読まれ
なければ、C++ のヘッダを編集しても波及しない。`05-incremental` は C だけを
見ているため、この経路は通っていなかった。

C だけが読むヘッダと C++ だけが読むヘッダを分けて置き、それぞれの編集が
それぞれの側に届くことを見る。`mixed` の終了状態には両方の値を載せた
（C 側 × 10 + C++ 側）ので、**片方だけが古いまま残っても値が変わる**。

## ほかのツールチェーンとクロス

g++ と clang++ の双方。**C は gcc・C++ は clang++** という組み合わせも通る
こと。

クロスでは `aarch64-linux-gnu-g++` で組み、純 C のテストが別アーキテクチャ
向けの C++ ライブラリを使い、qemu 経由で走るところまで通す。driver の選択と
トリプルの選択が同時に効く経路である。

## 観測したが所見にしなかったこと

書庫の作成には `ar` が無修飾で使われる（クロスでも `aarch64-linux-gnu-ar`
ではない）。手元と CI の binutils では問題なく通り、成果物も正しい。
`[toolchain]` に `ar` の項が無い以上これが現状の設計なので、README に
記録するだけにした。

コンパイラ自身の誤りに対して `--message-format=json` に診断が出ない点も、
C と C++ で挙動が同じであることを確かめたうえで所見にしていない。利用者の
コードの誤りに対して dowel が別の診断を作る筋合いは無く、F-008 が問題に
したのは**構成の誤りがコンパイラの誤りとして出ること**であって、これとは別である。

## そのほか

`run.sh` と CI が `g++` / `clang++` / `aarch64-linux-gnu-g++` を要求する
ようにした。

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/TomasVotruba/type-coverage/compare/2.2.2...2.3.0)

#### Type Perfect rules are now part of this package

[rector/type-perfect](https://redirect.github.com/rectorphp/type-perfect) has been merged into `tomasvotruba/type-coverage` ([#​68](https://redirect.github.com/TomasVotruba/type-coverage/issues/68)). Its rules live in `packages/type-perfect` and keep the `Rector\TypePerfect\` namespace, so existing `ignoreErrors` patterns still match.

The extension is registered automatically via `phpstan/extension-installer` — no extra `includes` needed.

**If you use both packages, drop `rector/type-perfect` from `composer.json`** to avoid duplicate rules:

```diff
 "require-dev": {
     "tomasvotruba/type-coverage": "^2.3",
-    "rector/type-perfect": "^2.1"
 }
```

#### All Type Perfect rules are opt-in

Four rules used to report right after install, with no way off short of `ignoreErrors`. They now match the rest of the set — off by default, one parameter each ([#​69](https://redirect.github.com/TomasVotruba/type-coverage/issues/69)):

```diff
 parameters:
     type_perfect:
         narrow_param: false
         narrow_return: false
         no_mixed: false
         null_over_false: false
+        no_param_type_removal: false
+        no_array_access_on_object: false
+        no_isset_on_object: false
+        no_empty_on_object: false
```

Enable what you want:

```yaml
parameters:
    type_perfect:
        narrow_param: true
        narrow_return: true
        no_mixed_property: true
        no_mixed_caller: true
        null_over_false: true
        no_param_type_removal: true
        no_array_access_on_object: true
        no_isset_on_object: true
        no_empty_on_object: true
```

What each of those 4 catches:

```php
// no_isset_on_object / no_empty_on_object
if (isset($object->property)) { }   // bad - hides typos and nulls
if ($object->property !== null) { } // good

// no_array_access_on_object
$object['key'];       // bad
$object->getKey();    // good

// no_param_type_removal
public function run(string $name)  // parent
public function run($name)         // bad - child drops the type
```

#### Type coverage checks are unchanged

`return_type`, `param_type`, `property_type` and `constant_type` behave exactly as in 2.2.2 — upgrading adds rules, it does not change existing measurements.

#### Housekeeping

- `symfony/dom-crawler` bumped to `^8.1` (dev only) ([#​70](https://redirect.github.com/TomasVotruba/type-coverage/issues/70))

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/TomasVotruba/type-coverage/compare/2.2.2...2.3.0>

### Description
This PR resolves four related administrative security and API issues:

1. **Admin Session Revocation (Closes #49)**: Added `POST /api/admin/sessions/revoke` endpoint allowing admins to revoke session JTIs, invalidating compromised or stale credentials.
2. **Admin Auth Health Guard (Closes #45)**: Enhanced `adminMiddleware` to verify token freshness and check session revocation via `AuthService.isTokenRevoked` prior to granting admin privileges.
3. **Admin Reason Code Helper (Closes #47)**: Implemented `validateAdminReason` helper and integrated audit reason handling into stream clawback and administration endpoints.
4. **OpenAPI Admin Security Specification (Closes #48)**: Updated `openapi.yaml` and `openapi.json` to define `securitySchemes.adminAuth` and reference it under all admin routes, verified by automated drift tests.

### Changes Included
- Added `POST /api/admin/sessions/revoke` endpoint in `src/routes/admin.auth.routes.ts`.
- Updated `adminMiddleware` in `src/middleware/admin.middleware.ts` with token freshness and revocation guards.
- Created `src/lib/adminReason.ts` and updated `src/controllers/stream.controller.ts`.
- Updated `src/docs/openapi.yaml` and synced `src/docs/openapi.json`.
- Updated drift tests in `src/__tests__/openapi.drift.test.ts` and added unit test suites:
  - `src/__tests__/adminReason.test.ts`
  - `src/__tests__/admin.session.revoke.test.ts`

### Verification
- Ran all Jest test suites (74/74 tests passing, 0 failing).
- OpenAPI specification drift checks verified clean.

Closes #45
Closes #47
Closes #48
Closes #49

author: t0k0sh1
body:
## Summary

A follow-up full-codebase audit (3 parallel agents covering persistence/storage, auth/API/network, and search/evaluate/core logic) surfaced 6 remaining issues, all fixed here:

- **oauth/limits — lock poisoning**: `oauth.rs` (client/code/access/refresh stores) and `limits.rs` (rate-limiter buckets) still used `std::sync::Mutex` with `.lock().unwrap()`, despite the project's documented parking_lot policy (Cargo.toml) and the registry already following it. A panic while one of those locks was held would poison it and permanently 500 every OAuth authentication or rate-limit check until restart. Both migrated to `parking_lot::Mutex`.
- **ship/hydrate — corrupt replication record**: `read_replication_record` treated an unparseable record as absent, which would boot a possibly half-hydrated cache directory as pre-#128 independent local truth — hiding every not-yet-localized context from the registry and risking a lineage fork on the next claim. The read is now tri-state (`Ok(None)` absent / `Ok(Some)` parsed / `Err` corrupt) and boot paths refuse the corrupt case with an operator-actionable message; the claim's `hydrated_from` carry-forward stays best-effort. New test covers the refusal on both `prepare` and `prepare_replica`.
- **ship — pre-manifest restore path validation**: the listing-driven restore fallback joined bucket-supplied file and lane names under the output directory without the `safe_manifest_name` check the manifest path gets. Defense-in-depth: the typed `object_store` path API makes real traversal unconstructible, but the documented "checked once, inherited everywhere" guarantee now actually holds.
- **hydrate — non-UTF-8 cleanup gap**: the cache cleanup sweep skipped files whose names fail UTF-8 conversion, leaving them on disk forever; they are now removed (a non-UTF-8 name cannot be a manifest name).
- **main — blocking I/O on async workers**: the config-watch loop read the config file with `std::fs::read` directly on a Tokio worker; a stalled network-mounted config could stall HTTP handlers sharing the thread. Reads now go through `spawn_blocking`.
- **compact/extract/benchmark — duplicate flags silently last-wins**: these three parsers accepted `--config a.env --config b.env` (and every other value flag twice) silently, while every other subcommand rejects duplicates as usage errors. All value flags now return the same `"given twice"` usage error, with tests in `tests/cli.rs` and `benchmark::args_tests`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets` (zero warnings)
- [x] `cargo test` (1,698 tests, 0 failures — includes new corrupt-record boot-refusal and duplicate-flag tests)

author: nuniesmith
body:
## What was red

Six of the twelve unexpected failures on pristine main, all in `tests/e2e/charts.spec.ts`. **Neither cluster is an app defect.** Both are the spec depending on something it does not control.

## Cluster 1 — `.chart-overlay` never clears (5 specs)

`timeframe buttons change active state`, `EMA indicator toggle`, `BB indicator toggle`, `RSI sub-pane toggle`, `quick pick selects symbol and updates badge`:

```
expect(locator).not.toBeVisible() failed
Locator:  locator('.chart-overlay')
Expected: not visible
Received: visible
Timeout:  10000ms
```

The overlay was not stuck — it was **right**. `.chart-overlay` renders for `loading` **or** `!loading && candles.length === 0`, and the second branch was live:

```
GET /bars/MGC/candles?interval=5m&days_back=30&limit=5000  →  200 {"candles":[]}
```

`hooks.server.ts queryCandles()` catches an unreachable QuestDB and returns `[]`, so the page painted its honest empty state — read off the running page:

```
∅  No data
No stored candles for MGC · 5m. Live ticks will populate as they arrive.
```

These five specs could therefore only ever pass on a host that happens to run QuestDB **with stored MGC 5m bars**. That is a gate measuring the box, not the build → category **(c) environmental**.

**Fix:** route-mock the backend seams, the pattern `cockpit.spec.ts` already uses (`installCockpitMocks`) — `/bars/:sym/candles`, `/api/chart/:sym/indicators`, `/api/assets/:sym`, and janus's indicator catalog (empty, i.e. its documented unreachable degradation). The `.chart-overlay` wait is **kept** and is now a real assertion — *given history, the chart paints* — instead of a probe for QuestDB. Mocking `/api/assets` also keeps the run off `wss://ws.kraken.com/v2`, which the crypto branch dials for real.

## Cluster 2 — `layout switch changes grid`

```
expect(locator).toBeChecked() failed
Locator:  getByRole('radio', { name: /1×2/ })
Expected: checked
Received: unchecked
9 × locator resolved to <button role="radio" aria-checked="false" aria-label="1×2 layout" …>
```

A pre-hydration click, dropped. `waitForLoadState("load")` is not a hydration signal: the grid toolbar is server-rendered, so every `.layout-btn` is visible, enabled and stable — Playwright-actionable — before Svelte attaches a single `onclick`. Measured directly: **first click leaves `aria-checked="false"` permanently; a second click 1.5 s later flips it to `"true"` and drops the grid to 2 charts.** Ablation proves the mocks alone do *not* fix it (2 of 3 runs still red) → category **(c) flaky**.

**Fix:** gate on a signal only the client can produce. `MiniChart` ships `loading=true` in the SSR HTML and clears `.mc-loading` in `initChart()`'s `finally`, which needs `onMount` plus the `lightweight-charts` dynamic import — so zero spinners proves all four children mounted and the parent's handlers are live. No assertion weakened, no click retried.

## Nothing was weakened — mutation-verified

With `aria-pressed` pinned `false`, menu `aria-checked` pinned `false`, `setSymbol` no longer assigning, and the grid's layout `onclick` made a no-op, **exactly these six specs fail**, and each fails on its own assertion — `aria-pressed`, `aria-checked`, `.sym-badge` `"MES"` vs `"MGC"`, `toBeChecked` — never on the ready gate. App files restored; **this PR touches tests only** (`tests/e2e/charts.spec.ts`, +250/-44).

## No real regressions in this stream

Chart UI, overlay logic and grid layout all behave correctly. The one thing worth a second look is **adapter-side, not chart-side and not touched here**: `/bars/:sym/candles` answers `200 {"candles":[]}` for *both* "QuestDB has no rows" and "QuestDB is unreachable", so the UI cannot tell a real empty history from an outage and shows "No data" for both. The chart already has the vocabulary for the difference (`barsError` → "Failed to load data … Couldn't reach the bars service"), but the seam never lets it fire. Same shape as Q-1 (#87). Needs a `hooks.server.ts` owner.

## Gates

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `charts.spec.ts` before (JSON, `--workers=2`) | 5 expected / **6 unexpected** |
| `charts.spec.ts` after (JSON, `--workers=2`) | **11 expected / 0 unexpected / 0 flaky**, 3 consecutive runs |
| full suite on this branch | 177 expected / 5 unexpected / 6 skipped — the 5 are `settings-risk`, `smoke`, `workspaces`; **none in charts** |
| `npm run check` | 0 errors 0 warnings |
| `npm run test:unit` | 602 passed (47 files) |

Also spotted for whoever owns `smoke.spec.ts`: `keyboard shortcut 2 navigates to charts` fails with `Expected pattern /\/charts/ · Received "http://localhost:5291/"` — the same dropped-pre-hydration-input class that `viewport.spec.ts:574` already documents and works around with a retried keypress.

author: aurtechmx
body:
Preset descriptions advertised effects the code does not perform. Each removed claim was traced to code before deleting it.

Not implemented, so removed from the wording: `aoStrength` (`ssaoApproximation()` returns a Float32Array no pass consumes, and there is no AO setter in `src/`), `elevationPalette` (nothing outside the preset literals reads it; `colorForMode` defaults to turbo and no preset value reaches it), `hillshade` (a DEM raster product in the Analyse panel, not a point-cloud render control).

Implemented, so kept: EDL enable and strength, point size and mode, sky, colour mode, and the classification palette, which is real — `colorByClassification` reads the ASPRS categorical table.

The old terrain description also said "warm sky" for `terrain-sand`, which is `#20251f`, a dark olive. Descriptions now name the sky preset id, which cannot drift from the hex.

Tests hold the descriptions to the fields in both directions: reserved vocabulary is banned, the colour-mode word is required, and the stated EDL and pixel figures are parsed back out and compared against `edlStrength`, `pointSize`, `pointSizeMode` and `sky`.

`lastPresetAoStrength` was a public field nothing read. Grepped the whole tree: two references, both its own declaration and assignment. Removed. The tuned values stay in `ReservedPresetCapabilities`, whose type name says they are not applied, and a source-text guard keeps the field and any `.reserved.` read out of `Viewer.ts`.

Partial application is now reportable. `applyPresetColorMode` returns which layers changed, which kept their mode and why, and how the streaming source responded, with only a genuinely unavailable source counting as a shortfall. Layers are classified in one pass before any mutation, so the report describes the starting state rather than the state its own writes produced. `Viewer.applyPreset` returns that instead of `void`, so a caller reads the outcome before announcing the preset as active.

Verification, each run and observed: `tsc --noEmit` 0, 47 tests across three files 0, `lint:claims-language` 0, `lint:monolith-size` 0 with Viewer.ts at 7070, three lines below baseline. Tamper check: restoring "high EDL plus AO" and forcing `partial: false` fails 4 assertions.

author: pmaxhogan
body:
## The flake

`crates/driven-s3/tests/s3_e2e.rs` panicked with
`creating the MinIO bucket failed: 503 Service Unavailable` in 0.52s on PRs
that touch nothing S3-related (#224). Too fast to be a real round trip: the
suite was creating its bucket before the MinIO it had just spawned was able to
serve.

MinIO is not started by the workflow - `ci.yml` / `coverage.yml` only `curl`
and `install` the binary; the harness itself spawns `minio server <tempdir>`.
So no workflow file changes here.

## Why the existing wait did not work

The harness already polled a health endpoint - `/minio/health/live` - and
treated any 2xx as ready. That endpoint cannot carry that weight. From
upstream `cmd/healthcheck-handler.go`:

```go
func LivenessCheckHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if objLayer := newObjectLayerFn(); objLayer == nil {
		w.Header().Set(xhttp.MinIOServerStatus, unavailable) // Service not initialized yet
	}
	...
	writeResponse(w, http.StatusOK, nil, mimeNone)
}
```

It returns **200** while the object layer is still nil and records that only in
an `x-minio-server-status: offline` header. `ReadinessCheckHandler`
(`/minio/health/ready`) is written the same way - so switching to `/ready`, the
obvious fix, would have been a no-op.

`/minio/health/cluster` is the real gate: it runs `checkHealth()`, which
answers **503** until the object layer, `globalBucketMetadataSys` **and**
`globalIAMSys` are all initialised. The IAM condition matters here because
every request this suite makes is signed.

Confirmed empirically against the installed `RELEASE.2025-09-06T17-38-46Z`,
race-probing all three endpoints from the instant of spawn:

```
t=  0.205 /minio/health/cluster  503 server-status='offline'
t=  0.206 /minio/health/live     200 server-status='offline'
t=  0.206 /minio/health/ready    200 server-status='offline'
t=  0.210 /minio/health/cluster  503 server-status='bucket-metadata-offline'
t=  0.215 /minio/health/cluster  200 server-status=''
```

Both `live` and `ready` say 200 in the exact window where the server cannot
serve. That window is sub-10ms on this Mac and evidently much wider on a
loaded GitHub runner.

## What changed

All of it in `crates/driven-s3/tests/s3_e2e.rs`:

- `wait_for_minio_ready(endpoint, timeout)` polls `/minio/health/cluster` on a
  real `Instant` deadline (100ms backoff, 60s budget), treating both
  connection-refused and 503 as "keep waiting". Returns `Err(reason)` rather
  than panicking, so the caller can attach diagnostics and so the timeout path
  is testable.
- A startup failure is still a **hard failure**. `spawn_minio()` returns `None`
  only for "no `minio` on PATH"; a MinIO that is installed but never comes up
  panics with the budget, the last status code, the last
  `x-minio-server-status` value (`offline` / `bucket-metadata-offline` /
  `iam-offline` names the subsystem that stalled) and the last 40 lines of
  MinIO's own output, which is now captured instead of sent to `/dev/null`.
  The log file lives beside the data dir, not inside it - MinIO serves every
  entry at the root of its data dir as a bucket, and a phantom `minio.log`
  bucket would corrupt the suite's own listings.
- `create_bucket` gets a bounded retry (5 attempts, linear backoff) on 5xx and
  transport errors, re-signing per attempt, treating
  `BucketAlreadyOwnedByYou` / `BucketAlreadyExists` as success (a retry after a
  lost response otherwise manufactures a new failure) and breaking out
  immediately on any other 4xx.

### Was the mid-run retry needed?

The readiness gate should be sufficient for `ServerNotInitialized`, which is
what the observed 503 was. The retry is there for the one thing readiness
cannot promise - a busy server answering `503 SlowDown` mid-run. `S3Store`
itself already classifies and retries that
(`driven_s3::error::classify_s3_response` maps `503 SlowDown` to
`RateLimited`; `execute_retrying` covers idempotent requests), so the whole
suite is covered except this one raw `reqwest` call in the harness. Cheap
belt-and-braces on the only uncovered surface.

## Verification

**Observed:**

- The race probe above, against the real installed MinIO.
- `cargo test -p driven-s3 --test s3_e2e`: 5/5 pass, MinIO suite runs for real
  (`[minio] suite passed`).
- Three new tests, none of which need a `minio` binary, driven by a path-aware
  HTTP stub that reproduces upstream's handlers (`live`/`ready` always
  200-while-offline; `cluster` 503-then-200):
  - the wait rides out three 503s and then succeeds;
  - a server that never initialises times out with a message naming the budget
    and `bucket-metadata-offline`;
  - a port with nothing listening exercises the transport-error branch.
- **The new tests were confirmed to fail against the old gate.** Temporarily
  pointing `wait_for_minio_ready` back at `/minio/health/live` makes two of
  them fail (`cluster probes served: 0`, and the permanently-unready server
  wrongly satisfying the gate), so they are load-bearing rather than
  self-confirming.
- `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D
  warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`: all clean.

**Reasoned, not proved:** that this is *the* mechanism behind the CI failure. A
GitHub runner's timing cannot be reproduced locally, so the causal chain
(loaded runner -> wider init window -> `live` 200s early -> CreateBucket 503)
is inference from the handler source plus the local probe, not a reproduction.
What is proved is that the previous gate could pass while the server was
unable to serve, and that the new one cannot.

## Note on the brief

This deliberately does **not** poll `/minio/health/ready` as originally
suggested - see the handler source and probe output above; `ready` has the same
200-while-offline behaviour as `live`, so it would not have fixed anything.

### Motivation
- Provide real external images for the five project rarities and avoid storing any image assets in-repo. 
- Make project cards compact and modular so build progress is visually clear and distinct from the real inventory. 
- Add developer tooling to quickly populate test data including unlocking the real Album using the canonical Album API.

author: davidlee18
body:
**Stacked on #104** — base is `catchall-arms-dispack-grzip`, so review that first.
I'll retarget to `main` once #104 merges.

The first codec of `RUST_PORT_PROGRESS.md` §10b item 4. #104 established that
three DisPack catch-alls were dead by proving, by hand from a 40-year-old C
header, that `flags & F_TYPE` is a two-bit field. That proof should be the
compiler's job.

## What changed

Three enums in `tables.rs` — `Mode` (the low two bits), `ImmSize` and `AddrType`
(the high two, one meaning per mode) — plus `mode_of` / `imm_of` / `addr_of`.

Two deliberate boundaries:

* **The opcode tables stay `u8`.** They must reproduce the C's bytes exactly, and
  converting them would be a large diff over the part of this codec that *is*
  literally the archive format. The nibble is decoded once, at the point of use.
* **The conversions are 4-element array lookups** indexed by a value masked to
  `0..=3`, not a `match` on the `u8`. A match would reintroduce the very
  catch-all this removes, just relocated.

Net: all four dispatch sites become exhaustive matches, and the three
`unreachable!()`s #104 added are **deleted**. No arm anywhere in DisPack now
exists for a value that cannot occur.

## It does what the item promised

Adding a hypothetical fifth `ImmSize` variant fails the build at the decision
sites, in both directions:

```
encode.rs:296 error[E0004]: non-exhaustive patterns: `ImmSize::Qword` not covered
filter.rs:344 error[E0004]: non-exhaustive patterns: `ImmSize::Qword` not covered
```

That is the "one compiler error instead of several diagnostic runs" this line of
work exists for. Note it points at the *decision* sites, not the lookup array —
a 5-variant enum for a 2-bit field is nonsense, and the error lands where the
judgement has to be made.

## An asymmetry the types made legible

The C tests the ModR/M mode **differently in each direction**: `(flags & fMODE)
== fMR` when encoding (`DisPack.cpp:496`) but `flags & fMR` when decoding
(`:782`) — the latter true for `fMEXTRA` as well. Two similar-looking bit tests
that are not the same test, which is easy to misread as a port bug in either
direction (I did, briefly, and checked the C rather than "fixing" it). They are
now `mode_of(flags) == Mode::ModRm` and `matches!(mode_of(flags), Mode::ModRm |
Mode::ModRmExtra)`, which says what it means.

## Verified

Byte-identical against the pinned C (`5c2c6ce`), both directions:

| harness | result |
|---|---|
| `dispack-check.sh` | **0 differing**, 3 block sizes × 13 inputs |
| `dispack-filter-check.sh` | **0 differing over 108** comparisons |

`cargo clippy --all-targets` clean; `cargo nextest -p darc-codecs` 182 passed.

**The conversion arrays are the whole risk** — a swapped entry silently remaps a
mode, and only byte-identity would ever notice. So each was sabotaged, and each
was caught by `dispack-filter-check`:

* `MODES` swap Address/ModRm → caught
* `IMM_SIZES` swap Byte/Word → caught
* `ADDR_TYPES` swap Absolute/DwordAbsJump → caught

## Next codecs

Same shape, one PR each, each gated by its own difftest: GRZip's mode bits, MM's
filter selector, TTA's `byte_size`, Tornado's `encoding_method` /
`caching_finder`. GRZip needs care — its rec mode arrives **from the compressed
stream**, so its fall-through must survive as a no-op (see #104); the enum there
wants an explicit `Unknown` variant rather than an exhaustive four.

author: ksa170
body:
## Summary

The stoch alert's actionable prices were buried in analysis jargon — "🎯 OB target" and "🛑 OS boundary — stays oversold below this" — and the actual **stop-loss price was never stated**: the alert showed the boundary, while the "place your stop a bit past it" rule lived only in conversation. This PR makes the alert lead with an explicit trade plan.

## Before → after

**Before:**
```
🎯 OB target: $693.40 — drift-to-overbought level
🛑 OS boundary: $688.10 — stays oversold below this
```

**After:**
```
💰 Entry: $690.78 · 5m bars
🌀 Slow %K: 17.9 → 28.4 · fast 45.2 · curled up from oversold

🎯 Target: $693.40 (+0.38%) — take profit here
🛑 Stop loss: $687.07 (−0.54%) — exit if reached
target = drift-to-overbought level · stop sits just below the stays-oversold boundary ($688.10)

🎫 Contract / 💵 Quote / 🧾 Cost / 📐 Est P&L rows unchanged
```

Two prices, plainly labeled, each with its % move from entry. The stochastic reasoning still rides along as an italic footnote for anyone who wants it.

## The stop is now a real stop, not the boundary

New per-rule **Stop buffer (%)** setting (default 0.15, clamp 0–2): the stop price sits this far *beyond* the boundary — below it for calls, above the stays-overbought ceiling for puts. Rationale from the validated trades: a normal in-band flush routinely *tags* the boundary on the low tick of a winning trade (the 7/20 trade flushed to $698.54 against a $698.26 boundary and then hit its target — its stop survived only because it sat past the band). Setting the buffer to 0 puts the stop exactly at the boundary for anyone who prefers that.

Consistency fix that falls out: the 📐 loss estimate now uses the buffered stop price, so the risk number in the alert matches the stop the alert recommends.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `alerts.py` | `stop_buffer_pct` param; signals carry `stop_price` / `target_pct` / `stop_pct`; `opt_loss` computed off the buffered stop; formatter restructured (Entry / Target / Stop loss rows + footnote; jargon labels removed) |
| `templates/index.html` / `static/app.js` | "Stop buffer (%)" field in the stoch criteria dialog + param plumbing |

Existing rules pick up the 0.15 default automatically — no rule edits needed.

## Test plan

- [x] 18 new assertions: param default/clamping; call side (stop below boundary by exactly the buffer, stop < entry < target, signed pcts); put-side mirror (target < entry < stop, stop above ceiling); `opt_loss` matches the buffered-stop arithmetic; formatter regexes for the Target/Stop rows, both footnote variants, and absence of the old jargon labels; buffer=0 → stop at the boundary.
- [x] Re-arm suite (16) still green; Python/JS syntax checks.
- [ ] Post-merge: next fired alert should read Entry/Target/Stop loss at a glance — no manual steps.

author: aurtechmx
body:
Three defects in the queue itself. Nothing is enabled: `maxItemBytes` and `onCommitError` are opt-in and no caller sets them.

**A throwing commit no longer corrupts accounting.** Bytes are subtracted and the identity freed before caller code runs, so a throw is that item's failure rather than the pass's. It books a failure, fires `onDiscard('commit-failed')` exactly once, reports through a fenced diagnostics hook, and continues, because stopping would punish every node queued behind one bad payload and continuing cannot replay an item already removed. `process` never throws; its caller is the render loop. The one-item budget waiver now counts commit attempts rather than successes, so a run of throwing items cannot walk the whole queue past its budget in a single frame.

**Duplicate items are refused rather than coalesced.** Identity is `(datasetId, generationId, id)` joined on NUL, since dataset ids are paths and node ids are octree keys and a colon can collide. First in line wins: under one generation both payloads are the same node's decode and interchangeable, so the queue has no basis to prefer the newer one, and refusing is the only policy where accepted byte accounting is never rewritten. The loser is released by `enqueue` before it returns, so a caller that ignores the result still cannot leak.

**A hard per-item ceiling now sits under the soft per-frame budget.** `budgetMs`, `maxBytes` and `maxNodes` stay soft, and one item per pass may overshoot them so the queue cannot deadlock. `maxItemBytes` is checked before that waiver, for every item. Over it, the item is released once with a typed `oversized-item` reason and a counter, and the pass continues. It cannot spin, because refusal removes the item, and it cannot be a silent drop.

**A latent defect this uncovered.** `_commitDecoded` enqueued `id: String(node.record.key)`, and `record.key` is a `VoxelKey` interface, so every node in every scan enqueued as the literal string `[object Object]`. Harmless only because the queue is dormant; the instant it goes live, every node collides with every other. Fixed to `node.record.id`, the deterministic `depth-x-y-z`. Restoring the old expression fails 4 of 8 integration assertions, which is how it was found.

One behaviour frozen rather than fixed: a `commit` that re-enters `clear()` used to crash the pass with a TypeError as the list shrank under the index. It now ends the pass cleanly with one outcome per payload. Who may detach mid-commit is the scheduler's lifecycle question, and the test says so.

Verification, each run and observed: `tsc --noEmit` 0, 53 tests across four queue files 0, `lint:upload-queue-wired` 0, `lint:monolith-size` 0 unchanged at main.ts 7355 and Viewer.ts 7073.

author: jakebromberg
body:
## What

Adds `/dashboard/album/legacy/[legacyId]` — a server-rendered front door that resolves a tubafrenzy **legacy release id** to the Backend-Service **serial** `library.id` and redirects to the canonical `/dashboard/album/[serial]`.

External callers (LML lookups, the Slack request line, wxyc.info) hold the legacy id, but the canonical album route and `GET /library/info?album_id=` are keyed on the serial — a distinct id space (BS stores the legacy id in a separate `library.legacy_release_id` column). A naive `/dashboard/album/{legacy_id}` would link to the *wrong* release; this front door bridges the two id spaces server-side via `GET /library/info?legacy_release_id=`, authenticated with a server-minted bearer JWT.

## Behavior

- **Resolved** → `permanentRedirect()` (308) to `/dashboard/album/<serial>`. The serial is stable once assigned, so the hop is safe to cache permanently.
- **Miss** (no catalog row / bad id / transient failure) → a **non-cacheable** "not in the catalog yet" 200 state, never a cacheable redirect. A `library.db` release not yet synced into BS Postgres can start resolving after a later daily sync, so the miss must not be cached. The page reads `cookies()` (forces dynamic render) and fetches with `cache: "no-store"`.

## Structure

The dashboard layout renders the `@information`/`@modern`/`@classic` parallel slots but not the `children` slot, so the resolve + redirect + not-found UI lives in the `@information` slot; the `children` page is a routability stub (the URL would 404 without it). Mirrors the merged route skeleton from #1036. Static `legacy` wins over the dynamic `[id]` sibling, so there is no collision.

Extracts a shared `getServerJwtToken` helper into `server-client` (behavior-preserving; replaces the private copy in `organization-utils.server`). Anchors the personal-scratch `.gitignore` rule to `/legacy/` so it no longer swallows the `legacy` route segment.

## Testing

`tsc --noEmit` clean; full unit suite green (3850 tests). New coverage: resolver status mapping (200/404/400/5xx/network/invalid-id/no-token/missing-backend-url), `getServerJwtToken`, and the page's redirect-vs-render behavior. Build/lint/E2E deferred to CI (local build blocked only by the worktree's `node_modules` symlink).

## Deploy note

Merging to `main` deploys dj-site to production via Cloudflare Pages. The Backend-Service endpoint this consumes (WXYC/Backend-Service#1880 / #1881) is already merged and deployed to prod, so end-to-end resolution works on merge.

Closes #1049. Builds on #1036 / #979. Unblocks the downstream LML `library_url` swap and the wxyc-shared `api.yaml` description update.

Kiểm tra và chuẩn hóa cách trình bày Hero trên toàn bộ Brian sau khi áp dụng hệ thống typography chung, nhưng vẫn giữ bản sắc đồ họa riêng của từng site.

- Thêm component runtime và stylesheet Hero dùng chung.
- Mount tại global shell.
- Không thay đổi dữ liệu, API, Supabase hoặc logic nghiệp vụ.

author: kimchankwon
body:
## Try it

- **Playable app** — https://pet-village-pr-120.netlify.app
- **Feature explanation** — https://pet-village-pr-120-explain.netlify.app

## TL;DR

A tired pet can no longer be sent into a mini-game. Every booth charges its run up front, refuses a pet that can't cover it, and pays out at a rate consistent with every other booth.

## The problem

Three of the six games charged nothing. Skip Rope handed out 20 coins a clear, Sled Run up to 22, and Fishing cost only bait — while Bump and Get paid 5–12 energy up front for 6–26. The door-gate was one flat `MIN_GAME_ENERGY = 5` regardless of what the booth actually cost, so a pet with 6 energy could walk into a game that charged 12 and be drained to zero. Paper Toss took 3 a throw, up to 30 a run, and could hit zero mid-run.

## What changed

| Game | Energy | Charged | Win pays | Coins/energy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bump | 5 / 8 / 12 | bout start (unchanged) | 6 / 14 / 26 | 1.20 / 1.75 / 2.17 |
| Get | 5 / 8 / 12 | run start (unchanged) | 6 / 14 / 26 | 1.20 / 1.75 / 2.17 |
| Sled Run | 5 / 8 / 12 | **new** — at the countdown | 8 / 14 / 22 (1st) | 1.60 / 1.75 / 1.83 |
| Skip Rope | 10 | **new** — run start | 20 on a clear | 2.00 |
| Paper Toss | 10 / 14 / 18 | **new** — up front, was 3/throw | 1/2/3 a basket + 2/3/5 a level | ~1.60 / 1.71 / 1.89 |
| Fishing | 4 | **new** — per cast | a fish + 4/7/11 happy | food, not coins |

Beyond adding costs:

- **Paper Toss** moved from per-throw drain to one up-front charge, so a run is never cut short half-paid. Its payouts had to scale with difficulty — a flat 2 a basket made Easy the best farm in the game. A retry that resumes on the failed second level pays for that level alone.
- **Fishing** checks energy *before* spending bait, so being tired never costs a bait. A landed fish now cheers the pet; previously a cast gave nothing immediate.
- **Sled Run** is multiplayer, so the leader is blocked from starting a run their pet can't pay for, and a racer the leader pulled in without enough energy drops out and walks back to the park rather than sitting at the top of everyone else's hill.
- Every refusal path is covered: the booth outside, unaffordable difficulty rows greyed with their cost, the picker subtitle when even Easy is out of reach, and each result panel's retry button.

Costs live in `src/systems/gameEnergy.ts`. `src/systems/gameEnergy.test.ts` asserts the coins-per-energy band across all six booths, so a future payout edit can't quietly unbalance one. A park booth's `sceneKey` is typed `MiniGameKey`, so a booth cannot point at a scene that has no gate.

## How to try it

Tuck the pet in for a full 100, then play: the cost is on every difficulty row and in the toast when a run starts. Play until under 10 and the Skip Rope and Paper Toss booths turn you away by name; under 4 and even a fishing cast is refused.

## Review pass applied before merge

- The park's walk-in gate no longer falls open on an unknown scene key: a booth's `sceneKey` is typed `MiniGameKey`, so a typo is a compile error rather than a silently ungated booth. The string-lookup helpers it replaced are gone.
- Sled Run: pressing RUN AGAIN while spent now says why instead of only dimming; a pet that can't pay leaves the room immediately rather than holding a slot for the 2.6s message beat; and the tired state is one guard at the top of `refreshUi` instead of an empty branch and three repeated conditions.
- Fishing's catch card greys its button and labels it `[ Too tired ]`, matching the existing `[ Out of bait ]` treatment, instead of offering a `[ Cast again ]` that refuses.
- `cheerFromPlay` lost its meaningless default argument.

## Verification

- `npm test` — 269 tests pass (203 + 13 + 53 across the three suites).
- `npm run build` — clean.
- Browser (`npm run dev:frontend`, guest save): Skip Rope refused at 6 energy; Sled Run entered at 6, charged 5 at the countdown, then refused at 1; Bump and Get pickers with Easy playable and Medium/Hard greyed; Paper Toss charging 10 for an Easy run; Fishing charging 4 a cast, then refusing while keeping the bait, with the catch card's button reading `[ Too tired ]`.

Shipped as **1.26.0** (`src/appVersion.ts`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`).

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Mini-games now charge energy upfront, with difficulty-based costs and clear “too tired” guidance.
  * Fishing catches provide happiness rewards, while Paper Toss rewards and retry costs reflect difficulty and progress.
  * Mini-game entry and replay options now prevent starts when the pet lacks sufficient energy.

* **Documentation**
  * Updated gameplay guides, controls, and Paper Toss instructions with energy costs and revised scoring.

* **Chores**
  * Updated the displayed app version to 1.26.0.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

author: gforgalen
body:
## What changed

- Add layout and timer API modules plus a reusable polling hook with 3-second foreground polling, 15-second hidden-tab polling, immediate visibility recovery, single-flight requests, abort handling, and silent retries.
- Add server clock calibration using the request midpoint and one shared one-second dashboard tick.
- Add a proportional 16:9 floor canvas with ResizeObserver fitting, pan/zoom/pinch controls, fit-to-screen and true virtual-pixel 100% modes, grid rendering, and throttled zoom percentage updates.
- Add memoized accessible table nodes for idle, running, paused, warning, and overtime states, including reduced-motion handling.
- Add warning/overtime banners, status chips, name search, table detail dialog, responsive layout behavior, and the admin-only layout editor entry point.
- Add timer display/clock-calibration tests and update module progress documentation.

## Why

Module 5 turns the authenticated shell into the live floor view used by store staff. The UI now derives countdowns locally between server polls while preserving the server as the durable source of truth across refreshes, restarts, and other devices.

## User impact

Store users can see all enabled tables at their configured positions, identify urgent states immediately, search or filter the floor, inspect a table, and navigate large layouts smoothly on desktop or mobile.

## Validation

- `server`: `npm test` — 14/14 passed
- `client`: `npm test` — 9/9 passed
- `client`: `npm run build` — passed
- Browser acceptance covered the seeded eight-table layout, per-second countdown, running → warning → overtime transitions, three-second polling visibility, warning/overtime banners, table dialog, search, zoom controls including true 100%, refresh recovery, network-outage data retention, and 375 px layout without horizontal overflow.
- Demo data was restored after acceptance: warning threshold 10 minutes and zero active timers.

## Known specification conflict

The acceptance script suggests starting a five-minute timer, applying `-240` seconds, then another `-60` seconds. The backend correctly enforces the shared minimum planned duration of 60 seconds, so the second adjustment is rejected once the first adjustment reaches that floor. Overtime was therefore validated by allowing the remaining sub-minute duration to cross zero naturally, without bypassing the service rules or editing persisted data directly.

author: pranavrnambiar
body:
## What
Split the Finny agent's LLM calls into two tiers by task shape:

- **Haiku 4.5** — mechanical work: transaction-email parsing (`parser.py`), merchant categorisation (`categoriser.py`), and merchant enrichment (`merchant_intel.py`).
- **Sonnet 4.6** — reasoning/narrative work: talking to Finny + Manny (chat), and the daily/weekly digests.

All routing is via constants in `agent/llm.py`; no hardcoded model strings elsewhere.

## Why
A head-to-head eval (30 ground-truth cases across 5 bank formats, run twice per model against the exact production prompts) found:

| | Sonnet 4.6 | Haiku 4.5 |
|---|---|---|
| Parser (full-row exact) | 100% | 100% |
| Categoriser | 100% | 96.9% (1 defensible edge case) |
| Parser latency (mean) | 2006 ms | 1315 ms (~34% faster) |
| Categoriser latency | 1565 ms | 940 ms (~40% faster) |
| Cost / 1k transactions | $4.46 | $1.62 (~2.8× cheaper) |

Haiku matches Sonnet on the structured-extraction path while being faster and cheaper. Conversation and digests stay on Sonnet where reasoning matters.

## Also
Corrected the `cached_system()` docstring: prompt caching is a no-op at current prompt sizes (all below their model's cache floor — 1024 Sonnet / 4096 Haiku), and padding to force it would be a net cost increase given sparse email arrival vs the 5-min TTL. Wrapper kept for future prompts that legitimately grow past the floor.

## Scope
Only `agent/llm.py` changed (+28 −7 across 2 commits). No prompt, parsing, or post-processing changes.

author: palash-c
body:
Found while setting up five Custom MCP servers end to end against the newly published guide (#3975): Notion, AWS Knowledge, arXiv, PostHog, and Composio Connect. Every auth mode (`NO_AUTH`, `API_KEY`, `DCR_OAUTH`) was exercised against a real server.

Additive only — 48 insertions, no existing content changed.

## 1. New "Connect an account" section

The main gap. The lifecycle says step 3 is "Connect an account if the server uses an API key or DCR OAuth," and the auth table says "Create an active connection" / "Authorize a connection" — but nothing shows *how*. Sync requires an active `connected_account_id`, so the page as published doesn't get a reader to working tools.

Uses the same `session.authorize()` pattern as [Manual auth management](https://docs.composio.dev/docs/manually-authenticating) and links out rather than restating it. Verified that `authorize()` works on a `CUSTOM_*` slug for **both** auth modes — it returns a normal Connect Link (`connect.composio.dev/link/lk_…`), so no auth-config plumbing needs documenting here:

| Toolkit under test | `session.authorize("CUSTOM_…")` |
| --- | --- |
| DCR OAuth (Notion) | `INITIATED` + Connect Link ✅ |
| API key | `INITIATED` + Connect Link ✅ |

## 2. Slug and name rules

Not previously documented, and the first is an easy trap:

- The `CUSTOM_` prefix is **always** prepended, so passing `CUSTOM_ACME` yields `CUSTOM_CUSTOM_ACME`
- Slugs are uppercased; `A-Z`, `0-9`, `_` only — dashes and spaces fail with a bare `Error in payload.slug: Invalid`
- `toolkit_config` accepts only `name`, `app_url`, `auth_schemes`; any other key fails validation

## 3. Two additions to Known gaps

**No sync-status field.** For a no-auth server the initial sync runs in the background during registration and nothing reports completion. Adds the `meta.tools_count` polling workaround.

**DCR registration can fail against multi-scope servers.** Registering PostHog fails with `500 Failed to register dynamic client`. Root cause is a scope delimiter mismatch in hermes:

- `fieldGenerator.ts:313` builds the auth-config `scopes` default as `scopes_supported.join(',')` — comma-delimited
- `dcrOauth.ts:320` uses `getScopeSeparator() → ' '` — space, which is what the OAuth `scope` parameter requires

PostHog advertises 203 scopes, so they reach the registration endpoint as one comma-blob, are read as a single unknown scope name, and get rejected. Verified against PostHog's live `registration_endpoint`:

| `scope` sent | Result |
| --- | --- |
| omitted | `201` |
| 203 scopes, space-delimited | `201` |
| 203 scopes, comma-delimited (as persisted) | `400 None of the requested scopes are available to self-registered clients` |

Notion and Apify are unaffected because they advertise a single scope (`["default"]`), where comma and space are indistinguishable.

> [!NOTE]
> This is a **code** fix, not a docs fix, and it is **not scoped to Custom MCP** — `apify_mcp` is `type: native` on `DCR_OAUTH` with `composio_managed_auth_schemes: []`, so it runs the same path. The doc entry describes only the observable symptom and the workaround. Happy to drop it if a fix is imminent and you'd rather not carry the doc debt.
>
> The outgoing scope string is encrypted in logs, so the delimiter conclusion is inference from the persisted auth config plus an exact error-message match — high confidence, not log-confirmed.

## On curl usage

Reworked after review feedback. `creating-triggers.mdx` has 0 bash blocks, 3 Python, 3 TypeScript and 6 internal links; this page was 434 lines with 10 bash blocks and 2 links. Anything reachable through the SDK now uses Python/TypeScript tabs and links out.

The 6 remaining bash blocks are the lifecycle endpoints only (register ×3 tabs, sync ×2, delete). Those are genuinely API-only — absent from the SDKs, and absent from the [API reference](https://docs.composio.dev/reference), because `/api/v3.1/custom/toolkits/*` is not in the published OpenAPI document (`docs/public/openapi.json` has 73 paths; none match). Until those routes appear in the spec there is nothing to link to. Worth fixing separately — it would let a follow-up delete most of the curl from this page.

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lines | 434 | 390 |
| bash blocks | 10 | 6 |
| Python / TypeScript | 2 / 2 | 3 / 3 |
| internal doc links | 2 | 4 + 1 reference |

## Testing

`bun test tests/static/` → 97 pass, 3 fail. The 3 failures are pre-existing on `next` (a `fumadocs-openapi` loader error), confirmed by stashing this change and re-running. `validate-links.ts` fails to boot on a pre-existing module-resolution error, so link targets were verified by hand: both target files exist, the `hosted-authentication-connect-link` anchor resolves to `### Hosted Authentication (Connect Link)`, and `/reference/api-reference/auth-configs` is already used elsewhere in the docs. MDX tag pairs and fences balanced.

## Excluded

- **Logo and rename limitations** — project-scoped upsert is landing imminently, so documenting them would go stale immediately.
- **v3 tools listing** — already covered correctly; `toolkit_versions=latest`, `version=latest`, and `"version": "latest"` all verified working.

author: dezodemius
body:
## Что сделано

- `GET /shop/{share_code}` — публичная витрина без авторизации: имя/описание/статус лавки + позиции с эффективной ценой (override торговца или, если он `null` по конкретной валюте, цена карточки предмета) и остатком (`null` = бесконечно).
- `POST /shop/{share_code}/buy` `{character_id, merchant_item_id, quantity}` — покупка одной транзакцией: `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` на позицию торговца и на персонажа, проверки по порядку `is_open` → сток → владение персонажем → средства (AR §4.5), затем списание денег строго по валютам цены без конвертации, декремент стока и создание/увеличение `InventoryEntry`.
- `CharacterService.apply_purchase(...)` (`app/characters/service.py`) — блокирует персонажа, проверяет и списывает кошелёк, зачисляет предмет в инвентарь (мёржит в существующую позицию по `item_id`, если она уже есть). Коммит не делает сам — им управляет `merchants.service.buy`, чтобы всё легло в одну транзакцию вместе с блокировкой позиции торговца.
- `ContentQueryService.get_item_by_id(...)` (`app/content/service.py`) — точечный метод, нужен `merchants`-модулю для эффективной цены без импорта чужих моделей.
- Новые доменные ошибки: `shop_closed`, `out_of_stock`, `not_your_character` (`app/merchants/errors.py`, все 400/404 по конвенции проекта), `insufficient_funds` (`app/characters/errors.py`, т.к. кошелёк — сущность модуля `characters`).

## Как проверял

- `pytest` — 242/242 зелёных (`tests/test_shop_api.py` — новые 13 тестов, весь остальной набор — регрессия).
- `ruff check .` — чисто.
- `alembic downgrade base && alembic upgrade head` на тестовой БД — миграции накатываются с нуля без ошибок (в этой задаче новых миграций нет, схема не менялась).
- Тесты `tests/test_shop_api.py` покрывают все критерии приёмки issue:
  - витрина видна без токена, эффективная цена (override и fallback на карточку);
  - витрина по несуществующему `share_code` → 404 `merchant_not_found`;
  - успешная покупка: точное списание по валютам, декремент стока, создание `InventoryEntry`; повторная покупка того же предмета увеличивает существующую запись;
  - `insufficient_funds` — состояние не меняется;
  - `out_of_stock` (нехватка стока) и покупка при бесконечном стоке (`quantity: null`);
  - `not_your_character` — покупка на чужого персонажа;
  - `shop_closed` — покупка в закрытой лавке;
  - покупка без авторизации → 401;
  - покупка несуществующей позиции торговца → 404 `merchant_item_not_found`;
  - конкурентный тест (`asyncio.gather`) — два одновременных `buy` последней единицы стока: ровно один 201/200-успех, второй `out_of_stock`, финальный сток — 0.

## Решения и допущения

- `POST /shop/{code}/buy` требует авторизации (`get_verified_user`) — без неё нет «своего персонажа» и не проверить `not_your_character`; в AR §4.5 явно указана проверка владения персонажем, значит буер обязан быть залогинен. `GET /shop/{code}` остаётся полностью анонимным, как того требует BR.
- `not_your_character` и «персонаж не существует» дают одинаковый ответ (404, один и тот же текст) — намеренно, чтобы не раскрывать существование чужого `character_id` (IDOR, security-review skill), при этом код ошибки соответствует явно заданному в API-контракте и issue.
- `GET /shop/{code}` отдаёт витрину и для закрытой лавки (`is_open: false`) — блокируется только сама покупка (`shop_closed`). DND-070 требовал «закрытая лавка недоступна для операций», не для просмотра.
- Ответ `buy` — плоский DTO (`inventory_entry_id`, `quantity_bought`, `character_gold/silver/copper`, `merchant_item_remaining_quantity`), без вложенных объектов — по аналогии с плоскими схемами `CharacterRead`/`MerchantRead` в проекте.
- Статус ответа `buy` — `200` (не `201`): это операция над существующими сущностями (кошелёк, сток), а не создание нового ресурса — так же оформлены `level-up`/`level-rollback`/`campaigns/join` в проекте.

## Что НЕ вошло и почему

- `POST /shop/{code}/sell` — отдельная задача DND-072 (зависит от DND-071).
- Rate-limit на `/shop/*/buy` — отдельная задача security-аудита (BACKLOG), не часть скоупа DND-071.
- Лог транзакций, коэффициент скупки, попадание проданного в сток — фаза 2 (BR §6), не трогалось.


Closes #32

## Summary

- restore 852 platform-specific optional dependency records removed from `package-lock.json`
- disable the implicit install in `setup-vp`

Lock-file maintenance commit `f347d5d` removed most Vite+, Oxfmt, Oxlint, and tsgolint platform binding records while their parent packages continued to declare those optional dependencies. author: kennethkoontz
body:
## Why

The plugin only ever showed issues assigned to the viewer, so there was no way
to find unclaimed work. Adds an **Unassigned** tab, and shows cycles in list
rows.

## What

**Unassigned tab** — issues with nobody assigned. Covers triage, backlog,
unstarted, and started. Completed and canceled are left out: an unassigned done
ticket is not work.

Backed by the top-level `issues` connection with `assignee: {null: true}`. That
connection is workspace-wide, so it scopes itself — an explicit `teams`
allowlist wins, otherwise it falls back to the teams the viewer belongs to
(fetched with the viewer at boot).

**Cycles in every list row** — `cycle` moved into the shared issue fields, so
rows show a cyan `C25` marker next to the project. Plain ASCII on purpose:
`visibleWidth()` counts code units, so an ambiguous-width glyph would break the
column math. The detail view spells out the number and name, and now also shows
the assignee, or `unassigned` when there is none.

**Two fixes found along the way**

- `triage` was missing from every tab, including **All**. It is where unassigned
  work usually lands, so it was the state type most worth adding. `duplicate` is
  now in **All** too, so "All" means all.
- A tab that hit `page_size` showed a bare count, indistinguishable from "that
  is all of them". Both fetchers now return `hasMore` from the connection's
  `pageInfo`, and the header renders `50+`.

## Verification

Schema shapes were probed against the live API before building on them:
`assignee: {null: true}` resolves (`assignee: {id: {null: true}}` does **not**),
and `triage` / `duplicate` are accepted in a state-type filter.

Both paths were then exercised end to end:

- Live API — Active, All, and Unassigned tabs plus a detail view.
- `HERDR_LINEAR_FIXTURE` — rendered at 120, 80, and 40 columns to check the
  column math with and without the cycle chip.

The fixture gained three unassigned issues (one in triage, one in a cycle) and
an explicit `assignee` on the existing four, so the tab has something to show
with no key and no network.

author: xphox2
body:
Server half of making the connection map show IPSec paths from both ends. Pairs with **Firewall-Collector v1.3.30** (merged first — the poller backs off from collectors that don't know the new command type).

### The map couldn't see OPNsense at all

Zero `vpn_status` rows, ever. VPN collection walks the SNMP interface table for names beginning `ipsec` — right for route-based IPSec, but a policy-based box installs kernel SPD entries through `enc0` and creates no per-tunnel interface. Its actual interface list is `dtsec0-4, enc0, lo0, pflog0, pfsync0`. Even a match wouldn't have helped: an interface carries no traffic selectors, and the selectors were the missing thing.

### Most of the fix already existed

`internal/vpnsession` landed in v0.11.171 under the changelog heading *"not yet wired to a poller"* — 548 lines, 452 lines of tests, fixtures captured from the live box — and **nothing had ever called it**. It correlates three session documents on `reqid` and emits one row per child SA with selectors, byte counters and uptime, already handling the rekey double-count and the `reqid` that's a string in one document and a number in the other.

So this is wiring: a recurring `ipsec_telemetry` command carrying the three GETs (all parameterless — which is why POST-only `searchPhase2` is unusable and SPD/SAD is the route taken), enqueued every five minutes, well inside the 30-minute freshness window. Parsing stays server-side, where the parser and its fixtures live and where IPSec device documents are already parsed from command results.

### The expected-children trap

A **down** child leaves no trace in either document, so without an expected list an outage is invisible. That list comes from `ProvisionedTunnelPair.PathsFor(deviceID)` — which already filters to enabled paths and orients them for the reporting device.

Deliberately **not** `TunnelIntent.PathsFor`. That returns the *full cross product* with each pair flagged, and the index never compacts by design. Fed in unfiltered, every path an operator switched off would become a permanent `down` row — manufacturing exactly the outage the mechanism exists to detect.

### Fixed: the stored-result cap could silently discard a whole cycle

Truncation happened **before** the command row — and therefore its type — was read, so one 64 KiB limit, sized for compacted preflight reports, applied to everything. Three raw session documents can exceed it, and a truncated envelope is invalid JSON: the parse fails, no rows are written, and the command still reports `succeeded`. Identical on every poll, so a tunnel would simply age out with nothing anywhere saying why.

Truncation now happens after the row loads, uses a raised per-type limit (per-type, not global — the base cap is the anti-bloat guard for the whole table, and this is the first *recurring* command at 288 results per device per day), and is **recorded explicitly** so a consumer reports it rather than inferring it from a syntax error.

### Two more silent-failure guards

Results are parsed inline **gated on `applied`** — the collector re-POSTs cached results on redelivery, and ungated every redelivery would insert the batch again.

The poller backs off from an old collector on the literal `"unknown command type"` answer **only**, never on failure in general: a transient failure (device unreachable for sixty seconds) would otherwise latch telemetry off permanently and silently. The back-off is time-bounded, so it recovers on its own once the collector is upgraded rather than needing a nudge.

### Verification

`gofmt` clean · `go vet` clean · `go build ./...` · `go test ./... -count=1` green · `internal/shell` at `-count=1`.

New tests cover truncation being reported rather than inferred, documents matched by path (matching by index would feed SPD in as SAD and produce quietly wrong counters), a missing document failing loudly, the collector's own error surfacing, all three steps being GET, and unknown vendors staying quiet. Mutation-verified: removing the truncation check and switching to index matching each fail exactly the test that covers them.

Live verification against `fwm-t12` — which currently has four installed children — follows deployment.

author: isaacviera
body:
The Lyve health check had been **commented out since it was written**, and the address in the comment pointed at `s3.us-east-1.lyvecloud.seagate.com` — a legacy alias whose TLS certificate expired 2026-07-19. Enabling it verbatim would have monitored a host we deliberately don't use.

Lyve is now probed at `s3.{LYVE_REGION}.global.lyve.seagate.com:443`, defaulting to `us-west-1` to match the driver (closest to SLC). A test asserts the retired `lyvecloud.seagate.com` hostname can't come back.

## Second fix in the same code

Backends are now probed **only when their credentials are configured**. Previously `quotaless` was registered and dialled unconditionally at boot, so startup reached out to a third party even in deployments and CI runs that never use it — a known flake source. An unparseable endpoint now skips that one backend instead of disabling health checks for everything.

## Shape

Extracted `configuredBackends(getenv)` so the env-to-backend mapping is unit-testable without touching process environment, and moved registration there from `NewServer` — so the set of *registered* backends and the set of *probed* backends can't drift apart, which is how the Lyve entry ended up half-wired in the first place.

Six tests: nothing configured → nothing probed; Lyve regional host; Lyve default region; quotaless requires a key not just an endpoint; a bad endpoint skips only itself; multiple backends together.
