author: dejuknow
body:
One commit that was pushed to this branch after #29 merged, so it never reached `main`. Its whole purpose is to be read at the moment someone is about to make a specific mistake, and stranded on a merged branch it does the opposite.

## Why

The review pass on the protected-container work reached a design verdict it deliberately did not act on: the container ranges are computed with regexes, each container's scan excludes the others, and four rounds of fixes have now taught one of those regexes about a case another one already knew. The fourth cost a silently lost comment. The verdict is that #30 should replace the computation with ranges derived from the real parse, where the two consumers cannot disagree.

That rewrite was correctly left alone: it replaces the module the UI, the MCP routes and the CLI all sit on, and doing it inside a review pass would ship a large unreviewed change under the heading of a review.

But recording the decision in a PR description is useless. The decision arrives when someone is editing the relocation block, not when they are reading merge history, and every individual fix looks smaller than the rewrite every time. Four of them already did.

## What it does

Two notes, in the two places someone will actually be standing:

- a comment at the relocation block in `src/lib/comment-parser.ts`, for whoever is editing it
- a paragraph under Protected containers in `AGENTS.md`, which is what an agent reads before touching this code

Both point at #30 for the substance rather than restating it, and both give the same mechanical trigger: the next container bug that lands here is the trigger to do the rewrite. The trigger is deliberately mechanical precisely because the judgement call has already been made wrong four times.

Comments and docs only. No behaviour change.

author: jejin
body:
Three items from user feedback in one sitting.

## Run rate in the planner output

The cost arithmetic already existed but only ran on a *cluster*, so sizing a single deployment said nothing about what it costs. The sizing view now reports `$/hr`, the monthly figure, and **cost per million tokens** from the same formulas already documented in §9 — the per-Mtok figure being the one that compares plans across SKUs rather than across GPU counts. At GLM-5.2 / 128×H200 that's `$576.00/hr`, `$420,480/mo`, `$18.44/Mtok`.

## FP16 TFLOPS in the GPU list

Added, with a footnote on which column drives which half of the plan — because the question behind this was "are the throughput numbers from PFLOPS?", and they are not:

- **Bandwidth** sets throughput. Decode is memory-bound: `tp × bw_tbs × MBU`. TFLOPS never enters it.
- **`tflops_fp16`** sets TTFT. Prefill is a dense GEMM: `FLOPS × MFU`, up to 2× for sub-16-bit.

### A bug behind the column

`tflops_fp16` was missing from `gpuSkuSchema`, and Zod strips unknown keys — so **every GPU write dropped it**. Re-saving a seeded SKU, or importing a catalogue, silently downgraded that SKU's TTFT to the optimistic weight-streaming floor. Now in the schema, editable in the admin form for the first time, and covered by a server test that round-trips H200 through the API.

## Where the reserve floor gives out

The activation term only exceeds the 2.5 GiB floor above `1 GiB / (hidden_size × 12)` — ~21.8K tokens at hidden 4096, ~10.9K at 8192, ~31K at 2880. That is why raising the prefill chunk looks like it does nothing, and it was previously only discoverable by bisecting the input. It is now shown next to the derived reserve.

The planner also starts at an **8192**-token chunk instead of 2048. The two defaults are kept deliberately distinct: 2048 stays documented as *vLLM's* default (so the emitted `vllm serve` command still names the flag only when a plan differs from vLLM), while 8192 is what [vLLM's tuning guide](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/configuration/optimization/) recommends for throughput, which is what this tool sizes for. **No plan changes** — no catalogue model is wide enough to leave the floor at 8192 — but the launch command now states the chunk rather than implying the latency-tuned one.

### Deliberately not done

The 12-bytes-per-token-per-hidden-unit coefficient still ignores that MLP intermediate activations are column-parallel and **shard by TP**, so it over-reserves at TP16 and under-reserves at TP1 (true peak nearer ~30 B there). Fixing that properly needs `intermediate_size` in the model catalogue, which does not exist yet — flagged rather than guessed at.

## Verification

139 domain + 17 server tests. New: the floor chunk asserted exactly at its boundary (floored at `c-1`, above the floor at `c+1`) for four models of different widths; 8192 still floors for every catalogue model, which is what makes the new default safe; TFLOPS surviving an API round-trip. Methodology parity holds across both copies. `npm run build` clean. All three changes photographed in the running app.

body:
Spindle PR: https://github.com/prolix-oc/lumiverse-spindle-types/pull/37
> Update Spindle Types
> Rebuild the frontend needed for Termux
## Summary
This adds a some additional regex functionality that some alternate platforms offer (guess). They come in the form of 3 flags that you can toggle for your regexes in the UI. Here's basically what each does:
Replace Positioning:
- Bottom: the replaced string will be moved to the bottom of the message that it matches, no matter the match location.
- Top: the replaced string will be moved to the top of the message that it matches, no matter the match location.
> These are useful in case you want the AI to generate something and have that show always at the top or bottom  of a message.
- Carry Forward Replacement: If the current message matches, the rule performs its normal replacement, if the current message does not match, it copies the first regex match from the most recent earlier match into the current message. You can pick where to insert it in the current message out of: append, prepend, append on a new line, prepend on a new line. 
> e.g. If the previous assistant message contains <status>HP: 8</status>, but the new assistant message forgets the status block, this option can carry that old status block into the new message. This is useful as it provides a fallback for state blocks that the model sometimes omits, or provides a persistent UI for the user if you don't  want the model to re-emit a state block that didn't change.
- Macro Eval on Find Regex Only: Exactly what it sounds like. Only do macro evaluation in the find regex field, and don't evaluate any macros in the replace field.
> Might be good if you want to chain regex rules together to separate out functionality, or if you just need your find rule to have macro support and don't want to do full macro eval for optimization purposes.
---
Also adds the relevant Spindle API exposure for completeness.

author: andrewgazelka
body:
Comment only. No behaviour change; `cargo test -p smash` and
`cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` both clean.

Follow-up to #1096, which fixed the respawn half of this and landed before the
review note asking for the other half to be written down.

`arm_double_jump` and `spend_double_jump` both carry `.without(Eliminated)` and
`.without(RespawnAt)`, which leaves `MayFly` and `Flying` stale for anyone
inside that window. For a player who **respawns** that was a real defect — a
`JumpsLeft` the client would not spend, and a press from before death replayed
at the spawn point — and #1096 resets all three in `lives.rs`'s `respawn`.

For an **eliminated** player nothing resets them, and that is deliberate. The
problem is that a deliberate inconsistency with no reason attached looks exactly
like the bug sitting next to it, so the next person to read it either files it
again or "fixes" it by moving the reset to the death transition — which is the
race `respawn` is deliberately avoiding. `Op::Spectating` only sets the
`Gamemode` component and defers publication to hyperion's roster, so a
`Flight::Disarmed` pushed beside `set_spectating(true)` can land *after* the
gamemode packet and tell a spectator it may not fly, on every death rather than
only the airborne ones.

So the comment records the two facts that make leaving it stale correct:

* a spectator's flight comes from their gamemode, not from this packet, so the
  stale `allow` bit is inert;
* if `Eliminated` is ever cleared, the grounded check in `spend_double_jump`
  refuses a press from somebody standing on the floor while `arm_double_jump`
  recomputes and pushes what is actually true — so it heals on the next tick
  without granting a jump.

A known-benign inconsistency with its reason written down costs nothing. The
same inconsistency undocumented costs somebody an hour, or an outage if they
resolve it the wrong way.

author: cmloegcmluin
body:
The tracked-tree test catches a banned term after it is already a commit, and on
a public repo a commit is effectively permanent: a history rewrite is partial
protection at best, since unreferenced objects stay reachable for a while and
clones, forks and caches outlive the rewrite. The only free fix happens before
the commit exists.

So `tools/sanitize_guard.py` grows the CLI its own docstring has always promised
-- `--staged` and `--message FILE` -- and `tools/githooks/` gets a `pre-commit`
and a `commit-msg` that call it. Two hooks, not one: a pre-commit hook never sees
the message, and the message is where terms have actually landed, because a commit
that sanitizes a file tends to describe what it took out.

`--staged` reads the index rather than the working tree. The index is what becomes
the commit, so a partially-staged file has to be judged on its staged half.

The hooks install by pointing `core.hooksPath` at `tools/githooks` --
`python tools/githooks/install.py`, once per clone. That beats copying into
`.git/hooks` on two counts: a copy goes stale the moment the tracked hook
changes, and `.git/hooks` would need the copy repeated per worktree, while
`core.hooksPath` lives in the shared config and covers the primary checkout and
every worktree at once. It is also reviewable, being in the tree.

Both hooks stay silent when they cannot work -- no blocklist, no usable
interpreter -- because a guard that blocks commits when it cannot run gets
switched off. `--no-verify` still bypasses them, and says so in the failure text.

The tests drive real `git commit` calls through the real hooks in a throwaway
repo, rather than asserting on `main()`'s return code: what matters is that git
refuses. One of them pins the index-not-disk rule, since a file staged clean and
then dirtied must still commit.

### Description

author: avatarsd
body:
`hazard_slot_t::store` allocates a node when its free list is empty. As shipped in #647, a failure left the previous value published and returned `void` — so `vertex_t::store` went on to report success. **A dropped write reported as taken**, which is precisely what [#477](https://github.com/avatarsd-llc/libtracer/issues/477)'s nothrow soft-fail doctrine exists to prevent. It was documented in the header, which is not the same as being handled.

## The contract

The policy surface grows a return value and loses an overload:

```cpp
[[nodiscard]] bool store(value_ptr_t, std::memory_order = seq_cst);
void              clear(std::memory_order = seq_cst);
value_ptr_t       load() const;
```

That is the same three operations `lkv_slot.hpp` already said a vertex performs — publish, clear, read — now actually spelled that way instead of expressing "clear" as a store of an empty handle. A clear *releases* resources rather than acquiring any, so it cannot fail and says so in its type; the `[[nodiscard]]` on `store` turns ignoring a declined publish into a compile error rather than a code-review question. `sp_atomic_slot_t` allocates nothing and returns `true` unconditionally.

`vertex_t::store` maps `false` onto the `nullptr` → `BACKPRESSURE` path an LKV allocation failure already takes, so the failure reaches the graph through machinery that already exists and is already tested. `revert_to_placeholder` calls `clear(release)`.

## The failure path is now driven, not argued

`lkv_slot_test` replaces **this binary's** nothrow `operator new`, forwarding to the throwing form on success so every pointer stays a real `::operator new` pointer and ASan keeps its heap intact. (Replacing the whole new/delete family with `malloc`/`free` would have been simpler and would have blinded the sanitizer leg this test most needs.)

The probe runs on a **fresh thread** on purpose: a participant that has already published owns a recycled node and never allocates again, so a cold participant's first publish is the entire exposure — and now the entire test. It asserts the publish is declined, that the previously published value is still what reads back, that the same participant recovers once memory returns, and that a clear succeeds with allocation rigged to fail.

## Two things found while testing it

- **`retire_and_flush` skipped the domain's orphan list** when the flushing thread's own list was empty. Values parked by a thread that has since exited therefore waited for process exit instead of being released when their slot died. One relaxed load on a normally-null pointer closes it — and it strengthens the ADR-0039 lifetime rule the flush exists for in the first place.
- **`bench_lkv_slot`'s model arms were named `sp_atomic_slot_t` and `hazard_slot_t`**, which since #647 are real library types with a different interface. Given that ADR-0069's erratum history is *entirely* about conflating a bench arm with the real thing, that shadowing is a trap. Renamed to `model_*`; the `RESULT` mode strings are untouched, so no perf history moves.

## Verification

Six configurations green, 65/65 each: Release, ASan+UBSan+LSan, and TSan, each against both slot bindings. `clang-format` and the Doxygen gate clean. (One unrelated `ws_transport` flake appeared once under TSan and passed 3/3 in isolation plus on a full rerun.)

ADR-0069 §6's third correction bullet and `core/CHANGELOG.md` both record the contract.

author: osho-20
body:
## Summary

TRA dashboard **Re-run → failed tests only** was re-running the *whole* Cypress suite for EasyJet (browserstack-cypress-cli 1.36.13, GitHub Actions). Root cause is a spec-list **format bug in the CLI**: obs-api passes the failed specs comma+**space** separated (`BROWSERSTACK_RERUN_TESTS="a.ts, b.ts"`), but the re-run code path fed that raw string into the spec glob without stripping the spaces — so the glob never matched the intended specs and the run fell back to the full suite.

## What lands here

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `bin/helpers/utils.js` | `setUserSpecs` — route `BROWSERSTACK_RERUN_TESTS` through `fixCommaSeparatedString` (the same normalisation every other spec source already gets) before assigning `run_settings.specs`. |
| `bin/testObservability/helper/helper.js` | `getReRunSpecs` (local `cypress run` path) — trim each entry of the rerun list before passing to `cypress --spec`, where a leading space silently drops every spec but the first. |
| `test/unit/bin/helpers/utils.js` | Regression test on the rerun branch of `setUserSpecs` using the ticket's exact 5-spec value. |

## Why the whole suite ran

`sanitizeSpecsPattern` wraps a multi-comma spec string in braces for glob. With the raw value it produced:

```
"{FO-E2E-05.ts, FO-E2E-02.ts, FO-E2E-06.ts, FO-E2E-07.ts, FO-E2E-03.ts}"
```

Brace alternatives keep the leading space (`" FO-E2E-02.ts"`), so only the first (space-free) alternative can match. Locally the glob resolves **1/5**; on BrowserStack the malformed pattern resolves to nothing and the runner falls back to the full suite — the "every spec re-ran" symptom in the ticket (child build 141199119 ran all 9 specs, incl. 4 never in the payload).

After normalisation the pattern is `{FO-E2E-05.ts,FO-E2E-02.ts,...}` and resolves to exactly the 5 failed specs.

## Test plan

- [x] New regression unit test (`setUserSpecs` … `SDK-7124`) — **fails** on the pre-fix line (asserts the space-mangled string), **passes** after the fix.
- [x] Full `test/unit/bin/helpers/utils.js` suite: **391 passing** (was 390) — the +1 is this test; the 5 failing (`setLocalArgs`/`setNodeVersion`/`getVideoConfig`) are pre-existing and unrelated (present on a clean `master` checkout too).
- [x] Standalone reproduction against a 9-spec fixture with the ticket's exact env value, using real `glob@7` + the verbatim `sanitizeSpecsPattern`/`fixCommaSeparatedString`: pre-fix matches 1/9, post-fix matches exactly the 5 failed specs.

## Notes / scope

- Backward compatible: `fixCommaSeparatedString` is a no-op on already-clean lists; non-rerun runs are unaffected.
- This fixes the **CLI-side** handling. If the failed-spec env never reaches the runner in a given CI setup (e.g. a GitHub *native* workflow re-run that replays without env injection), that is a separate Integrations/obs-api delivery concern outside this repo — this change ensures the CLI does the right thing whenever the list *is* present.

## Release

- [x] patch — bug fix only.

Fixes SDK-7124.

author: hoseokna-ims
body:
## 🐛 문제

기존 가드는 **`patch==0` 만** 검사합니다. 그래서 "버전이 채널에 맞는가"는 보지만 **"버전이 실제로 올라갔는가"는 보지 않습니다.**

| 가드 | 검사 | 0.48.0 재배포 |
|---|---|---|
| `.husky/pre-push` | master 푸시 시 `patch != 0` 차단 | 0.48.0 → patch=0 → **통과** |
| `prod.yaml` Version guard | `patch != 0` 이면 실패 | 0.48.0 → patch=0 → **통과** |

이 때문에 세 가지 우회 경로가 전부 열려 있습니다:

1. **래퍼 우회** — `git flow hotfix finish` 를 직접 호출하면 bump·changelog 가 실행되지 않고, 태그는 로컬에만 생깁니다. 그 상태로 master 를 푸시하면 **이전 버전으로 운영 배포**됩니다.
2. **동일 버전 재배포** — 이미 태그가 존재하는 버전을 다시 배포. 태그가 가리키는 커밋과 실제 운영 코드가 어긋나 **태그 기준 롤백이 깨집니다.**
3. **수동 머지 푸시** — 정상 플로우를 아예 경유하지 않는 경로.

0.49.0 사고에서 실제로 1번이 일어났고, **이 가드가 있었다면 잡을 수 있었던 유일한 지점**입니다.

부수 문제로 기존 검사가 **워킹트리의 `package.json` 을 읽습니다.** master 를 푸시할 때 다른 브랜치가 체크아웃돼 있으면 오판합니다(staging 브랜치에서 master 푸시 → 잘못 차단, 반대 방향으로는 우회 가능).

## 🛠 수정

**태그 정합성 규칙**: master 로 나가는 커밋은 *자기 `package.json` 의 version 과 같은 이름의 태그가 자신을 가리켜야 한다.*

정상 플로우(`yarn release/hotfix finish`)는 master·develop·태그를 `--atomic` 으로 함께 푸시하므로 통과합니다. 우회 경로만 정확히 걸립니다.

**`.husky/pre-push`**
- 태그 부재 / 태그 불일치 각각 별도 진단 + 다음 행동 안내
- **버전을 워킹트리가 아니라 푸시되는 커밋(`git show ${local_sha}:package.json`)에서 읽도록 수정** — 기존 patch 검사도 이 값을 쓰므로 오판이 함께 해소됩니다
- 브랜치 삭제 푸시(`local_sha=0000…`)는 대상에서 제외해 훅이 죽지 않게 처리

```
❌ 태그 0.48.0 이 다른 커밋을 가리킵니다 — 버전 bump 없는 재배포입니다.
   태그 0.48.0 → 1e8e217cb…
   푸시 대상    → 05dda7fe4…
   → 새 버전으로 릴리스하세요: yarn hotfix start && yarn hotfix finish
```

```
❌ 태그 0.27.0 이 없습니다 — 정상 릴리스 플로우를 경유하지 않은 푸시입니다.
   → yarn release finish 또는 yarn hotfix finish 로 진행하세요.
     (git flow 를 직접 호출하면 bump·changelog·태그가 생성되지 않습니다)
```

**`.github/workflows/prod.yaml`** — 동일 검사를 `Tag guard` 스텝으로 추가(CI 이중화). 태그 조회를 위해 checkout 에 `fetch-depth: 0` + `fetch-tags: true` 추가.

## ✅ 검증 (격리 저장소, 훅을 `.git/hooks/pre-push` 로 설치해 실제 push 경로에서 실행)

**18/18 통과.**

| ID | 케이스 | 결과 |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | `yarn hotfix finish` 전체 경로 → 통과, 오탐 없음 | ✅ |
| **T2** | **사고 재연: `git flow hotfix finish` 직접 호출 후 master 푸시 → 차단** | ✅ |
| T2b/c | 재배포 진단 + 다음 행동 안내 출력 | ✅ |
| **T2d** | **원격 master 무변경 = 배포 트리거 안 됨** | ✅ |
| T3 | 태그 없이 수동 bump 후 푸시 → 차단 + 우회 원인 안내 | ✅ |
| T4 | 스테이징 버전(0.26.1) master 푸시 → 차단 (기존 가드 회귀) | ✅ |
| **T5** | **다른 브랜치 체크아웃 상태에서 master 푸시 → 통과** (워킹트리 오판 해소) | ✅ |
| T6/T7 | develop · staging/* 푸시 → 검사 미적용, 통과 | ✅ |
| T8 | 삭제 푸시(`0000…`) → 훅 정상 종료 | ✅ |
| C1~C3 | prod.yaml Tag guard 로직 시뮬 — 일치/불일치/부재 3분기 | ✅ |

T2 는 이 PR 의 존재 이유입니다. 실제 사고와 동일한 순서(hotfix 브랜치 → `git flow` 직접 호출 → master 푸시)를 재현했고, 푸시가 차단되어 원격이 무변경으로 남았습니다.

## 🔍 리뷰 요청 사항

- **버전 읽기 방식 변경**(워킹트리 → 푸시 커밋)이 기존 `patch != 0` 가드의 동작에도 영향을 줍니다. 더 정확해지는 방향이지만 기존 동작 변경이라 확인 부탁드립니다.
- `--atomic` push 에서 master 와 태그가 같은 트랜잭션으로 올라가므로 CI 가 태그를 볼 수 있다고 판단했습니다(`fetch-tags: true` 전제). 실배포 리포에서 이식 시 이 부분 실측이 필요합니다.

## 📌 참고

- 설계 문서 §4.5 (`docs/release-flow-hardening.md`, #26)
- #26·#27·#28 과 파일 겹침이 없어 독립적으로 머지 가능합니다
- 이식 시: `imsform-mobile-web` 의 `.husky/pre-push` 는 tsc·test 검사가 앞에 있으므로 **기존 버전 가드 블록에 append**. `prod.yaml` 은 stub 이 아닌 실배포 워크플로라 checkout 옵션 확인 필요

Issue #56（ターミナルの分割表示）の導入計画のうち **PR 1**。10本中4本目。
**これで前提工事（0-a / 0-b / 0-c / 1）が完了し、次の PR 2 から分割表示の本体に入ります。**

## 何を

`matchShortcut` は `ctrlKey` / `altKey` が押されていたら無条件で `null` を返していました。

分割表示ではペイン間移動に `Cmd+Option+矢印` を併設する計画ですが、**このガードがあるためそのキーは絶対に発火しません**。しかも**その挙動が単体テストで不変条件として固定されていた**ので、分割の実装時にここを踏むと「なぜ効かないのか」の調査から始まることになります。

design-review が「5人全員が独立に指摘した前提の誤り」の1件目として挙げた項目です。

## なぜ矢印キーだけ例外なのか

macOS では **Option+英数字が特殊文字の合成**に使われます（Option+e はアクセント記号の dead key、Option+u はウムラウト）。これを横取りすると文字入力そのものを壊します。**矢印キーは Option と組み合わせても文字を生成しません。**

`Cmd` が付いていない `Option+矢印` は Terminal.app / iTerm2 / シェルの readline で単語単位のカーソル移動として日常的に使われています。`metaKey` を必須にしているため構造的に到達しませんが、**単体テストでも固定しました**。

## `AppAction` は1つも増やしていません

ペイン間移動の割り当ては PR 4 以降の担当です。**`Cmd+Option+矢印` は今も何も起きません**（ガードを通った後、どの分岐にもマッチせず `null` に落ちる）。

## テストが変更を固定していなかった問題（レビューで差し戻し）

最初の実装は `matchShortcut(Cmd+Option+矢印)` が `null` を返すことを assert していました。**これはガードを緩める前も後もまったく同じ結果**なので、`shortcuts.ts` の変更を丸ごと revert してもテストは green のまま通ります。テスト名は「ガードに弾かれない」と主張しているのに、それを1ミリも検証していませんでした。

**「テストがある」と「テストが変更を固定している」は別物です。**

判定を `passesModifierGate` としてエクスポートした純粋関数に切り出し、それを直接見る形に変えました。**ガードの変更だけを revert すると、このテスト1件だけが赤くなることを実測で確認済みです**（予想ではなく実測）。

同じ形の切り出しはこのリポジトリで **4例目**です（`shouldSendResize` / `computeYourTurnSince` / `rovingTabindex` / `passesModifierGate`）。**繰り返し必要になるということは、これが既定の作法**ということだと思います。

## 補足: 計画書の行番号がまたずれていました

`design-review.md` は `shortcuts.ts:15` / `renderer-lib.test.ts:36-39` と書いていますが、実際は `:72` / `:106` でした。**この Issue で3件目**です（0-b の行番号、0-c の「ランドマークは0件」に続く）。

- `make check` — unit **201 passed**
- `make e2e` — 全 green

author: nc1107
body:
Finding 9. `Uri.replace`'s `path` parameter resolves `.` and `..` segments per RFC 3986, and every path in this client is interpolated from values it did not choose - `'/messages/$messageId/reactions/$emoji'`, with the server accepting any 64-byte emoji string.

## what this is and is not

**Nothing is usefully reachable today**, and the audit's analysis of why is worth not re-deriving: DELETE is unreachable through the reaction chip, because the method comes from a flag that is only true for a reaction the viewer created, and a reaction whose PUT landed somewhere else never gets created. Every body-free PUT that fits in the remaining ~58 characters needs a JSON body the reaction call does not send, and `PUT /roles/{role_id}/members/{user_id}` needs two UUIDs and does not fit.

So this is hardening, not a fix for something exploitable, and the commit message says so too.

What is actually wrong is narrower and worth stating plainly: the method and path a request lands on stop being decided by the calling code and start being decided by content. The two things keeping that safe are a length constant in a different crate and the absence of a body-free PUT, and neither of them is something this file controls or would be told about if it changed.

## one choke point

Both `_send` and `_fetchBytes` already share a place where a path becomes a `Uri`, so that is where this goes. A per-call-site fix is the same defect waiting for the next call site, and this client has dozens.

The path is split on the separators this code wrote, and the pieces go to `pathSegments`. Each piece is then one opaque value, so an embedded `/`, `%`, or non-ASCII byte in it cannot introduce a new separator.

## `pathSegments` alone is not enough

This is the part that would have been missed by reasoning about it rather than testing it, and it is in a doc comment so the next reader gets it for free.

A segment whose value is **exactly** `.` or `..` is still resolved away by `Uri`'s internal normalization, even when it arrives through `pathSegments` rather than a raw path string. Only embedded slashes, percent signs and non-ASCII bytes are made opaque that way. So those two literals get their dots escaped, and every other segment renders exactly as `pathSegments` already renders it - verified in both directions against Dart, not assumed.

## what is deliberately untouched

`client_messages.dart` has a comment about colons, and it turned out to document a design decision (colons are left unescaped on purpose) rather than a guard that this fix would subsume. It is still accurate under the new implementation, colons still pass through unescaped, and there is a test pinning that - so there was nothing redundant to remove and two layers that could disagree were never created.

## the related bound one layer out

`router.dart` interpolated a URL-supplied `channelId` with no length cap on web, which the finding notes as a wider version of the same shape. An over-long one renders the empty state now rather than seeding itself into every request that pane goes on to make. No harmful target exists there either; it is the same reasoning as above.

## on the tests

Six cases: `../` traversal, `%2e%2e` traversal, an embedded `/`, a unicode emoji producing the same URL it produces today, a UUID unchanged, and a colon unchanged. The last three matter as much as the first two - the wire is additive-only, and this must change no path any existing call produces for well-formed input.

Mutation-tested: reverting to the old `replace(path: ...)` kills exactly the two traversal tests and leaves all four equivalence tests green.

The schema-coverage gate still parses every `_send` call site, since no call site's shape changed.

body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

Treat blank Glue AWS access and secret keys as absent so that Iceberg uses the AWS default credential chain.

Validate that static access and secret keys are configured together, and add unit coverage for blank and partial credential values.

### Why are the changes needed?

Optional Glue credential properties may be stored as empty strings. `GlueIcebergTableHelper` previously checked only for null values and installed `GravitinoGlueCredentialsProvider`, which then failed with `Access key ID is not set`.

This prevented Iceberg metadata enrichment and caused Gravitino to fall back to Glue-derived metadata.

Fix: #12270

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Glue Iceberg catalogs with blank static credential properties now use the AWS default credential chain. A partially configured static credential pair fails fast.

No API or property keys are changed.

### How was this patch tested?

```bash
./gradlew :catalogs:catalog-glue:test \
  --tests org.apache.gravitino.catalog.glue.TestGlueIcebergTableHelper \
  -PskipITs
```

author: merlimat
body:
### Motivation

Union-like messages declare many singular message fields but only ever set one or two. Pulsar's `BaseCommand` has 52 singular fields, and three hot methods walked a guard per declared field on every cycle:

- `clear()` (runs at the start of every `parseFrom()` and every fill): 60 sequential `if (hasX()) x.clear()` guards
- `_writeTo()`: a `has()` guard per field
- `getSerializedSize()`: a `has()` guard per field

Fresh flame graphs (post-#11/#12) surfaced the `clear()` guard chain at ~5–7% of self time; removing all three walks measured far larger than the profile share — dozens of correlated branches per call cost more in branch-prediction pressure than their sample counts suggest.

### Changes

**`clear()`** (all message shapes with ≥ 4 singular message fields): iterate the set bits of `_bitFieldN & _MSG_FIELDS_MASKN` with an `Integer.numberOfTrailingZeros` loop and a dense `switch`, clearing only the children actually present — O(set fields) instead of O(declared fields). The presence bit implies the child was allocated, the same invariant the guarded form relied on.

**`_writeTo()` and `getSerializedSize()`** (messages where *every* field is singular and non-oneof, ≥ 8 fields): the same set-bit traversal. Set bits ascend, so fields are emitted in declaration order and the output bytes are identical to the guard walk — verified by the round-trip tests against protobuf-java. proto3 implicit-presence fields keep their non-default check inside the case; required fields always have their bit set once `checkRequiredFields()` has passed. The two methods share the traversal emitter, so they agree exactly on which fields contribute (writeTo fills an array sized by getSerializedSize).

Messages with repeated, map or oneof fields keep the guard walk for serialization (those fields carry no presence bits, so ordering across them could not be preserved), and small messages generate byte-identical code to before — `MessageMetadata`, `Frame` etc. are unaffected and were verified flat as benchmark controls.

### Results

JMH, Apple M-series, ops/µs, same-session baselines, 2–3 forks:

| Benchmark | before | after | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| BaseCommand serialize | 25.4 | **43.4** | **+71%** |
| BaseCommand deserialize | 36.1 | **52.3** | **+45%** |
| MessageMetadata serialize | 14.5 | 14.2 | unchanged (control) |
| MessageMetadata deserialize | 16.7 | 17.1 | unchanged (control) |

(Per-commit split: the clear() change contributes +17% ser / +33% deser; the writeTo/size change adds a further +50% ser.)

BaseCommand vs protobuf-java: serialize 1.5× → **2.6×**, deserialize 2.8× → **4.1×**.

### Verification

Full test suite green — including byte-identical round-trips against protobuf-java (which pins the serialization order) and the instance-reuse suite from #11 exercising clear/reparse cycles on pooled instances.

author: waieiches
body:
## 작업 내용

`ctr_model_training`이 `feast_offline_feature_build`의 완료를 기다리지 않고 **병렬로 시작**하던 경합을 제거합니다.

두 DAG가 같은 raw Dataset을 구독하고 있었습니다.

```python
# ctr_training/dag.py (수정 전)
schedule=[RAW_YOUTUBE_TRENDING, RAW_ACTION_LOG]

# feature_store_build/dag.py
schedule=[RAW_YOUTUBE_TRENDING, RAW_ACTION_LOG]
```

`lake_to_bigquery_incremental` 한 run이 두 raw Dataset을 모두 갱신하면 두 DAG가 동시에 뜹니다. 실측으로 확인됩니다.

```
feast_offline_feature_build | dataset_triggered__2026-07-29T08:44:41.990394+00:00
ctr_model_training          | dataset_triggered__2026-07-29T08:44:41.990403+00:00
```

의도한 순서는 `raw 적재 → feature build → 학습`인데 실제 배선은 2·3단계가 **형제**였습니다. 그래서:

- 학습이 feature 빌드보다 먼저 끝나면 **전날까지의 spine·feature로 학습**합니다
- feature 빌드가 실패해도 학습은 그대로 돌아 성공합니다 — 데이터가 갱신되지 않았다는 사실이 학습 쪽에 드러나지 않습니다
- 실행 순서가 두 DAG의 상대 속도에 달려 있어 **날마다 달라질 수 있습니다**(재현 불가능한 학습 입력)

2026-07-29에는 이 경합이 다른 결함에 가려 보이지 않았습니다 — 그날은 KSA 누락(`Autoresearch-infra#427`)으로 두 DAG가 모두 403으로 죽었기 때문입니다. #194에서 spine 빌드를 고치고 backfill로 데이터를 채운 지금은 경합만 남습니다.

## 변경 사항

- `dags/ctr_training/dag.py`: schedule을 feature Dataset 3종으로 교체
  ```python
  schedule=[*FEAST_OFFLINE_FEATURES, FEAST_TRAINING_ENTITY]
  ```
  Dataset schedule은 AND 조건이므로 `user_dynamic_feature` / `video_feature` / `training_entity`가 **모두** 갱신돼야 학습이 시작합니다. `feast_offline_feature_build`의 두 태스크가 이미 이 셋을 outlet으로 선언하고 있어(#194) 배선만 이어주면 됩니다
- `dags/common/datasets.py`: "현재 이 Dataset을 schedule로 소비하는 DAG는 없다"는 주석이 더 이상 사실이 아니므로 갱신했습니다. 이제 여기서 테이블을 빼면 학습의 선행 조건이 조용히 느슨해집니다
- 모듈 docstring에 배선 변경 이유와 fail-closed 성격을 명시했습니다

## ⚠️ 이 PR이 만드는 동작 변화 — fail-closed

**feature 빌드가 실패하면 학습이 아예 돌지 않습니다.**

- 수정 전: "낡은 데이터로 조용히 학습" (성공으로 보임)
- 수정 후: "학습 안 함" (트리거 자체가 안 됨)

후자가 안전하다고 판단했습니다. 다만 **세 테이블 중 하나만 실패해도 학습이 막힌다**는 뜻이기도 하므로, 이 트레이드오프에 동의하지 않으시면 되돌리기 쉽게 변경을 schedule 한 줄로 좁혀 두었습니다.

학습 시작 시각도 feature 빌드 소요만큼 뒤로 밀립니다(최근 실측 기준 빌드는 15초 내외).

## 검증

`python -m pytest` (CI와 동일) — **204 passed** (기존 203 + 신규 1).
`python -m compileall dags` 통과, `git diff --check` 통과.

추가한 교차 DAG 테스트가 핵심입니다.

`test_training_schedule_matches_feature_build_outlets` — 학습의 `schedule`과 feature build 두 태스크의 `outlets` 합집합이 **정확히 일치**하는지 검사합니다. 이 배선은 어긋나도 조용히 깨지는 종류입니다.

- schedule에만 있고 아무도 갱신하지 않는 Dataset이 있으면 → 학습이 **영영 트리거되지 않습니다**
- outlet에만 있고 schedule에 없는 테이블이 있으면 → 그 테이블이 갱신되기 전에 학습이 시작합니다 (**#194의 `training_entity`가 정확히 이 상태였습니다**)

테스트가 공허하게 통과하지 않는지도 확인했습니다 — 양쪽 집합이 각각 3개 URI이고 서로 같습니다.

기존 parse 테스트에도 두 가지를 못박았습니다.

- schedule에 `training_entity`가 포함될 것 (빠지면 학습이 다시 spine 없이 시작)
- schedule에 `data_lake_raw`가 없을 것 (raw를 직접 구독하면 병렬 트리거 재발)

## 검증하지 못한 것

- 실제 클러스터에서의 트리거 순서는 머지 후에 확인해야 합니다
- **머지 직후 학습이 한 번 자동으로 뜰 수 있습니다.** 오늘 backfill로 세 Dataset이 모두 갱신된 기록이 남아 있어, schedule 전환 시 Airflow가 조건 충족으로 판단할 가능성이 있습니다. 현재 spine 데이터는 정상이므로(07-27·07-28, 클릭 5,685건) 돌아도 무해합니다
- 이 PR은 학습 윈도우를 건드리지 않습니다. `ctr_training/config.py`의 기본 윈도우는 `D-6 ~ D`인데 spine은 #194로 `D-1`까지만 만들어지므로 마지막 하루는 항상 비어 있습니다. 데이터가 줄 뿐 정확성 문제는 아니라 별도로 판단할 사안입니다

## 관련 이슈

Closes #197

관련: #194 / PR #195 (spine 일일 빌드 배선), `SKYAHO/Autoresearch`#421 / PR #422 (라벨 단일 클래스 가드 — 이 경합이 만들 수 있는 결과를 학습 쪽에서 막는 안전망)

author: sunholo-voight-kampff
body:
Fixes #538

## The bug

The nightly detector filed **"Nightly regression: `<bench>`"** — and pinged Discord — for benchmarks that had **never been green**. The K=3 escalation backstop promoted `SUSPECTED-FLAKE` straight to `REGRESSION`, the only label reaching `--type bug`.

Live instance, #537 (closed as refuted this morning): `config_file_parser` has passed **1 of 14 trials over 7 nights**, and its own filing printed `prior window 1/10 over 5 nights` while asserting *"Investigate this solid-window break"*. The failures aren't even one bug — `TC_ARITY_001` twice, an `Option[α50]`/`int` unification, a `logic_error`, `undefined variable: null`, a `case`-vs-`match` parse cascade, and `thrash_aborted` on the trial-2s.

## The fix

Escalation now emits a distinct terminal **`SUSTAINED-FAILURE`** label. It still files `--type bug` — chronic failures must not hide, which is why iteration 113 added the backstop — but with an honest title/body and **no Discord ping**: the ping means *"something broke tonight"*, and a sustained failure is the absence of a change. Side effect: the ping's own wording becomes true again.

**What deliberately did NOT change: the GAP exemption.** #538's original framing (*"a strictly worse benchmark gets the quieter label"*) was **wrong**, and the issue carries the correction. The ladder is ordered by *evidence of achievability*, not badness — flake-guard D4 guarantees *"no benchmark that has ever passed goes unpaged past its 3rd consecutive failing night"*, and a never-passed benchmark is gap-finder territory. A test now **locks** the exemption.

M1/M2/M3 are one commit on purpose: the routing block **silently drops unrecognised labels**, so the classifier change alone would take chronic failures from mislabelled-but-visible to *invisible*. Splitting them would not be bisect-safe.

## Verification

All gates re-run **outside** the codex sandbox — a sandbox verdict is not evidence:

| gate | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `make test-nightly-classifier` | rc=0, 60 PASS | **rc=0, 71 PASS** |
| replay | `guarded_regressions=2 suppressed=4` | `guarded_regressions=1 sustained=1 suppressed=4` |
| CI anti-skip floor | 55 | **67** |
| `shellcheck` / `bash -n` / `git diff --check` | — | rc=0 / rc=0 / rc=0 |
| `nightly_classify.py` size | 689 | 690 / 800 |

The replay moves **non-vacuously**: `csv_to_json_converter`'s K=3 escalation stops inflating the regression count. The number reaching bug routing is unchanged at 2 — this suppresses a *mislabel*, not a signal.

**Nine mutations run, all RED, all reverted byte-identical** (six by the controller, three invented independently by the evaluator): escalation label reverted · both `PAGING_CLASSES` halves · GAP allowed to escalate · shell extractor deleted (the vanishing trap) · injected Discord ping · `--type bug` downgraded to `note`.

**Live-stream check** on the real banked history for `config_file_parser`:

| tonight | label | pages? |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-07-30 | `SUSTAINED-FAILURE` | yes, once |
| 2026-07-31 | `SUSPECTED-FLAKE` | **no** |
| 2026-08-01 | `SUSPECTED-FLAKE` | no |

It pages **once**, not nightly — and 07-31 is suppressed by matching 07-30's banked **legacy** `class="regression"`, which is why `PAGING_CLASSES` retains that string. Dropping it would re-page tomorrow; mutation 3 proves the guard is live. An `INVALID` night still files nothing, so #524's validity gate is not bypassed.

## Bonus: a reachability finding

D4's claim that the backstop is *"label-agnostic across SUSPECTED-FLAKE and INSUFFICIENT-HISTORY"* — widened in the flake-guard's **quorum round 1** to close "unbounded low-history chains" — guards a state that **cannot occur**. Reaching `consecutive >= 3` requires three nights at `trials >= 2`, which already satisfies `min_nights`/`min_trials`. Brute-forced **19,607** streams: the only escalation pair observed is `(SUSTAINED-FAILURE, SUSPECTED-FLAKE)`, positive control confirming reachability. A quorum objection was satisfied by a fix for a phantom — the same shape as the dead `ast.ListType` generator arm (iter 121) and the unreachable `RunAgentBenchmark` verify call (iter 105). The condition stays (still correct if thresholds are retuned); only the docs change, so nobody designs against it.

## Review

Independent evaluator (sonnet — distinct provider from the OpenAI codex executor): **PASS 90/100, round 1, zero blocking findings.** Its two administrative gaps are resolved: F-4 is filed as **#541**, and `Fixes #538` appears above.

Related: #539 (wrong-dialect keyword diagnostics, found here and **explicitly not oversold** — the hypothesis that it caused the sustained failure was refuted by per-night data) · #540 (the honest capability-gap filing, so closing #537 doesn't discard the real signal) · #541.

author: abid112
body:
First-time players were handed a random name from a list of 15 (`Mochi`, `Biscuit`, `Noodle`, …). The field now starts **blank** and the player names their own cat. Start stays disabled until they type something.

A returning player still gets the name they used last time, restored from localStorage — that's their own name, not a default, so it's kept.

`CUTE_NAMES` and `randomName()` are removed as dead code.

## Comment cleanup that came with it

Two places justified the `player_id` column by pointing at the random-name list. That rationale referenced a feature that no longer exists, so I reworded it. The conclusion is unchanged and still correct, just for a plainer reason: nothing stops two unrelated players both naming their cat "Mochi", so grouping the leaderboard by name would still merge strangers.

`db/migrations/002_add_player_id.sql` keeps its original wording — it was accurate when written, and applied migrations are best left immutable.

## Verification

In the browser, with storage cleared to simulate a brand-new machine:

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| First-ever visit | field empty, placeholder "Name your cat", **Start disabled** |
| Whitespace-only (`"   "`) | **Start stays disabled** |
| Real name typed | Start enabled |
| Clicking Start | name written to localStorage |
| Reload (returning player) | field restored to the saved name, Start enabled |

`build`, `lint` and `typecheck` all pass.

## Summary

- Fix macOS calendar tray failure where EventKit helper spawn crashed with
  `(0, n.spawn)(...).As is not a function`.
- Root cause: production Rslib/Rspack tree-shook the bare side-effect import that
  installs `Object.prototype.As` (`package.json` had `"sideEffects": false`), while
  `spawn(...).As()` remained in the minified main bundle.
- Switch the Swift one-shot runner to free-function `As(...)` (named import), mark
  `as` + CSS modules as side-effectful, add a regression test, document production
  guidance, and bump to **1.17.1**.

- Applies no-store and restrictive browser security headers.
- Documents the required `LEADHUTCH_UNSUBSCRIBE_ORIGIN` Vercel environment variable.

## Why

LeadHutch runs locally for the MVP. Its signed unsubscribe confirmation must remain recipient-accessible over HTTPS without exposing the locally authenticated API or showing ngrok's browser interstitial.

## Verification

- `npm run build`
- Production route appears as `ƒ /api/emails/unsubscribe`.
- Browser-like request through the built proxy returned LeadHutch's expected `400` for an invalid signed token, rather than ngrok's warning page.

## What changed

- Release Sunox 0.2.1 and document the Browser Bridge installation and compatibility contract.
- Harden invisible challenge startup, redirect/response handling, MV3 cold-start cleanup, and cross-runtime activation.
- Make terminal challenge delivery exact, idempotent, flush-before-acknowledge, and retry-safe across ambiguous HTTP responses.
- Retry one fresh silent Turnstile widget when the provider returns no callback, without opening a tab, window, or isolated browser.

After several successful generations, Turnstile could stop producing a callback. At the same time, Browser Bridge lifecycle and result-delivery races could remove response rules too early, mix old/new extension runtimes, or lose the terminal result when the HTTP acknowledgement was ambiguous.

The extension remains invisible and fail-closed while handling repeated challenges more reliably. It does not create a Suno tab, minimized window, popup, or separate browser process.

author: tybot02
body:
## Summary

  - Add `--no-editable` to `uv sync` so `kb_ai` is copied into site-packages instead of referenced via a `.pth` file pointing to the CI build machine's source tree
  - Add cross-machine portability checks to `verify-install.sh` that catch absolute symlinks, absolute `.pth` paths, and broken imports — issues previously invisible because the verify script runs on the same machine that
  built the tarball
  - Add local dev setup instructions (create `etc/kaas-dev.toml` with LLM credentials) before `make dev` in both READMEs

  ## Root Cause

  `uv sync` defaults to editable installs for local packages, writing a `.pth` file:
  /Users/runner/work/kaas/kaas/py/src
  This path doesn't exist on the user's machine → `python3 -m kb_ai` fails with `No module named kb_ai`.

  This was latent before PR #3 — the broken Python symlink caused KAAS_HOME detection to fail, so the daemon fell back to `uv run --directory py kb-ai daemon` (which resolves packages from source, bypassing site-packages).
  PR #3 fixed KAAS_HOME detection, which activated the `python3 -m kb_ai` code path and exposed the editable-install issue.

  ## Why verify-install.sh didn't catch this

  The script builds and installs on the **same machine**. Absolute paths pointing to the local filesystem resolve correctly — the failure only manifests when the tarball crosses machine boundaries (CI → user). New
  portability checks detect:
  - Absolute symlinks under `py/` escaping the install directory
  - `.pth` files containing absolute paths
  - `pyvenv.cfg` home pointing to a foreign location
  - `python3 -c "import kb_ai"` failure

  ## Test plan

  - [x] `bash scripts/build-tarball.sh` — tarball contains `site-packages/kb_ai/` (real package dir, no `.pth`)
  - [x] Fresh extract → `python3 -c "import kb_ai"` succeeds
  - [x] Fresh extract → `python3 -m kb_ai daemon` prints `__READY__`
  - [x] `bash scripts/verify-install.sh` passes with new portability checks
  - [x] Docker path unaffected (uses own Dockerfile, `KAAS_WEB_DIR` env var, `uv run`)
  - [x] agent-quickstart path unaffected (uses `uv tool install`, no tarball)

author: joop973
body:
Umsetzung der Änderungswunschliste. Kein Phasenthema.

## Gegner

| Typ | Änderung |
|---|---|
| Grüner | 2 Abpraller (vorher 0) + Vorhaltezielen (`leadAim`), `accuracy` 0.8 → 0.9 |
| Gelber | `aggression` 0.17 → 0.08 |
| Pinker | `accuracy` 0.5 → 0.72 |

„Intelligenter" habe ich beim Grünen als Vorhaltezielen umgesetzt — die stärkste vorhandene Zielmechanik (bisher nur beim Schwarzen). Es gäbe noch eine zweite Lesart: der ungenutzte Abpraller-Rechner (`requiresBounceShot`), der ihn zu einem echten Bankshot-Gegner machen würde. Sag Bescheid, falls das gemeint war.

## Karten

- **Streuschuss**: kein Magazin-Bonus mehr, bleibt reiner Fächer
- **Scharfschütze**: 3× Tempo (statt 2,2×), 2 statt 1 Kugel
- **Krallenfalle**: alle 300 statt 600 px
- **Annäherungsmine**: nach 0,1 s scharf
- **Nachbrenner**: nur noch 1 Stufe
- **Turbo** und **Schild**: jetzt `legendary`
- **Entfernt**: `durchschlag`, `zielsucher` (samt ihrer `cfg.js`-Blöcke)

Die Engine-Felder `phaseWalls`/`homing` bleiben in `bullet.js` erhalten — generische Geschoss-Eigenschaften, aktuell von keiner Karte gesetzt. `terrain` hat durch den Wegfall von `durchschlag` noch 5 Stacks; Pionier bleibt freischaltbar, der Regressionstest wacht darüber.

## Minen global

Explosionsradius 64 → 51 px (−20 %), Wurfweite 72 → 58 px und der Touch-Wurfstick 142 → 114.

## Mechanik-Änderungen

- **Wolframkern** reißt die Wand ein und **fliegt weiter**, statt dabei zu verschwinden. Ohne Abpraller-Verbrauch und mit der Möglichkeit, im selben Schritt eine zweite Wand zu treffen; zerstörbare Wände (Phase 11) zählen jetzt mit.
- **Aasgeier** gibt das volle Magazin zurück: neues Bullet-Feld `magFreed`. `killTank()` markiert alle eigenen fliegenden Kugeln, `liveBulletsOf()` überspringt markierte. Sie fliegen und töten normal weiter, blockieren aber keinen Magazinplatz mehr — genau wie beschrieben.
- **Konterschild wirkt nur noch in Elite-/Verflucht-/Bossräumen.** Dafür neu: `cfg.js: applyRoomContext(cfg, { elite, boss })`, aufgerufen an denselben drei Stellen wie `applyRoomModifier()`. In normalen Räumen fällt der ganze Schild weg, nicht nur der Kugelkranz.
- **Klebemine** hatte praktisch nie gehaftet: der Haft-Test lief über den Minenradius von 7 px, der Gegner musste die Mine fast berühren. Jetzt eigener `stickRadiusPx: 42`.

## Raumvorschau

Die eigenen Upgrades erscheinen als **antippbare Chips mit Wirkungstext** — dasselbe Muster wie die Gegnerliste darüber. Vorher stand dort nur eine Namenszeile ohne Erklärung.

## Tests

Drei neue Wirkungsnachweise (Aasgeier, Konterschild-Gating, Wolframkern), jeder mit bestandener Gegenprobe. Suite grün, USP-Quote weiterhin bei 61,8 %. Browser-Smoke ohne Fehler, neue Vorschau-Chips im Browser geprüft.

body:
💡 **What:** Wrapped the `ToolCallCard` and `CodeBlock` components with `React.memo()`.

🎯 **Why:** During WebSocket token streaming, parent message components re-render very rapidly as tokens arrive. Previously, this forced all sub-components (such as `ToolCallCard` and particularly the expensive `CodeBlock` syntax highlighters) that belong to that message to also re-render, resulting in significant O(N) performance overhead over time. 

📊 **Impact:** Sub-components within an actively streaming message will no longer blindly re-render on every new token. This reduces layout and computation work, resulting in a noticeably smoother scrolling experience and reduced CPU usage during generation, particularly in long threads with extensive tool calls or large blocks of code.

🔬 **Measurement:** Open Chrome DevTools Performance Profiler. Start recording, then trigger a prompt that generates multiple tool calls and large code blocks. Compare the total time spent in scripting/rendering in the profiler. You should see a marked decrease in total React component tree re-renders per incoming token frame.

author: siixquant
body:
## What

Two things: ship a service that was missing from customer installs, and add a check so the next one can't go missing quietly.

### 1. `marketdata` service added

The stack definition upstream turns this service on by default. This compose file never picked it up, so on a customer install the live-quote path had no process behind it: the control plane relays quote requests to a service that simply wasn't there.

Ported here, adapted to this file's conventions rather than copied verbatim:

- image resolves the same way `scheduler` does (`AURACLE_IMAGE_SCHEDULER` / `AURACLE_IMAGE_TAG`, defaulting to `:latest`) — no new image to pull, no `build:` block, and it stays on whatever tag the rest of the stack is pinned to
- `IBKR_HOST` / `IBKR_PORT` default to this file's values (`host.docker.internal` / `4002`), not upstream's docker-gateway values
- volumes trimmed to what a pre-built image needs: `./data/keys` and `./logs`, both already pre-created by `install.sh`
- kept as-is from upstream: the entrypoint, the dedicated client id, the internal HTTP surface (never published to the host), `mem_limit`, restart policy, network, `depends_on: db healthy`, and the database-reachability healthcheck

Safe on a keyless install: with no broker configured the service starts, detects that, and idles healthy. It does not crash-loop and does not place orders.

One deliberate addition over upstream: the concurrent-line cap is passed through to the container. Upstream relies on the in-code default, so setting that variable in `.env` there has no effect. Since it is documented in the env template here, it needed the passthrough to actually work — worth mirroring upstream.

### 2. Control-plane wiring

`AURACLE_MARKETDATA_URL` (default `http://marketdata:8137`) and `AURACLE_MARKETDATA_TOKEN` added to the control plane's environment, matching how upstream wires the relay. The token is optional; when set it must match on both sides, and it is read from one variable so there is no way to set half of it.

### 3. `.env.example`

New optional block after the broker section, every line commented so the compose defaults apply untouched: `AURACLE_MARKETDATA_URL`, `AURACLE_MARKETDATA_TOKEN`, `AURACLE_MARKETDATA_CLIENT_ID` (137), `AURACLE_MARKETDATA_HTTP_PORT` (8137), `AURACLE_MARKETDATA_MEM_LIMIT` (1g), `AURACLE_MARKETDATA_LINE_BUDGET` (100).

### 4. Drift guard

`scripts/check-compose-drift.py` plus a `compose-drift` workflow. One rule, one direction: every service that starts on a plain `docker compose up -d` upstream (no `profiles:` key) must exist here. Profiled/opt-in services, volumes, networks, and per-service details are ignored on purpose — the two files legitimately differ there. Extra services here are reported, never failed on.

A service can be held out of customer installs deliberately, but it has to be recorded in the script with the reason, and every run prints those entries. That keeps an intentional gap visible instead of letting it decay into the exact silent drift this check exists to catch.

**Honest limitation:** the source of truth is a private repo, and a workflow's built-in token is scoped to this repo only, so out of the box this check **skips** — it cannot read the file it needs to compare against. This repo already hit the same wall once (see the note in `gitleaks.yml`, where a config file was vendored to avoid a cross-repo read). Vendoring is not an option here: a vendored copy would itself go stale, which is the bug.

To make the guard live, add a repo secret:

```
ENGINE_REPO_TOKEN - fine-grained PAT, Contents: Read on the upstream repo
```

With the secret present the job runs `--strict`, so a revoked or expired token fails loudly rather than degrading back to a silent skip. Without it the job stays green and prints how to configure it, so outside contributors are never blocked by a credential they cannot have. No secret is invented or referenced anywhere else.

The script also runs locally with no credentials at all, against a checkout:

```
AURACLE_ENGINE_COMPOSE=/path/to/upstream/docker-compose.yml scripts/check-compose-drift.py
```

or through an already-authenticated `gh` CLI, which is how it was verified for this PR.

## Verification

- `docker compose config -q` passes, with and without the opt-in broker profile, using a throwaway env file. Nothing was started.
- Resolved output confirmed: correct image, entrypoint, memory cap, all six variables, `depends_on` on a healthy database, and the relay URL on the control plane.
- Drift script exercised on all paths: passes against the current upstream file; correctly fails with a clear message when the new service is removed from a copy of this compose; skips with instructions when no access is configured; exits non-zero under `--strict` in that same case; reads the private upstream file successfully through `gh`.
- `checksums.txt` regenerated with the same command the publishing workflow uses. Only the compose line changed. The install script and its sidecar hash are untouched (no changes were needed there), and `shasum -c` verifies clean. **This mattered:** the install path verifies the downloaded compose file against this list when verification is enabled, so shipping the edit without refreshing the hash would have broken fresh verified installs in the window before the workflow caught up.
- The smoke workflow's container status/log lists now include the new container, so it is visible in CI output rather than invisible.

## Deliberately not in this PR

- **`live-supervisor`** — also default-on upstream and also missing here. It routes live orders for continuously-deployed strategies; enabling that on every customer install is an owner decision, not a sync detail. Recorded in the guard's exclusion list with that reason, so it stays visible and the check does not go red on it.
- **`jupyter`** — kept exactly as-is. It exists only here, not upstream. Worth a separate look: its image is no longer rebuilt, so the published `:latest` for it is frozen well behind the rest of the stack, and it has no build for current release tags — meaning an install that pins a current version tag cannot pull it. That is a decision to make on its own, not to smuggle into a sync PR.
- The opt-in/profiled services and the volumes that only they use.

author: priscaenoch
body:
## Summary

Implements the transactional outbox described in #54: durable `WebhookEvent` rows, a dispatcher with exponential backoff, admin inspection, and payload redaction — preparing partner webhooks without a real HTTP delivery client.

closes #54

- New `webhooks` module: `WebhookEvent` entity + migration (indexed on `status`+`nextAttemptAt`), `WebhooksService` (`emit`/`dispatch`/`retry`/`listEvents`), admin routes under `/api/v1/admin/webhook-events` (list, dispatch, retry — admin RBAC only, `403` for non-admins), and a deep payload redactor stripping passwords/tokens/secrets/emails from nested objects/arrays.
- Wired emitters: `subscription.created` on subscribe (both new subscriptions and reactivating a cancelled one) and `post.published` on post creation — both now write via `dataSource.transaction()` so the outbox row commits atomically with the domain write.
- No cron/scheduler dependency was installed (none exists in this repo); the dispatcher is triggered via `POST /api/v1/admin/webhook-events/dispatch`, which is also how tests and admins run it on demand. It logs to console by default, or POSTs to `WEBHOOK_DEBUG_URL` if configured. Failures back off exponentially (capped at 5 min) and go `dead` after 5 attempts; dead events can be retried via `POST .../:id/retry`.
- `docs/webhooks-outbox.md` documents the data model, emitters, redaction rules, dispatcher behavior, and admin API, including what's intentionally out of scope (signed partner delivery, per-creator webhook management UI).
- 20 new tests in `src/webhooks/` (service, redaction, admin controller) plus emitter-specific tests added to the existing `subscriptions.service.spec.ts` and `posts.service.spec.ts`.

### Pre-existing baseline breakage (unrelated to #54, fixed to keep CI green)

`main` currently fails `npm run build`/`test:e2e`, apparently from a bad merge of a `post-soft-delete-archive-restore` feature where the controller/tests/migration landed but the service implementation didn't:

- Duplicate `AuditAction.USER_SELF_DELETED` enum member (build-breaking).
- `AuditAction` missing several `BILLING_WEBHOOK_*` members that `billing-webhooks.service.ts` already referenced.
- `FeedService`'s post mapping was missing the now-required `deletedAt` field.
- `PostsService` was missing `getArchivedPosts`/`restorePost` (and `Post` was missing `deletedById`) even though `posts.controller.ts`, `posts.service.spec.ts`, and `test/posts.e2e-spec.ts` already called them — reconstructed faithfully against those existing call sites and the already-present `AddPostSoftDelete` migration.
- One e2e assertion (`test/posts.e2e-spec.ts`) used a numeric user id where every other public-route assertion in that file uses the creator's `handle` — fixed to match the surrounding pattern.
- 3 files with pre-existing Prettier violations, reformatted.

I confirmed with the requester before making these fixes, since they're outside #54's scope but were blocking `build`/`test`/`format:check` regardless of this PR's contents.

## Testing / validation performed

- `npm run build` — clean.
- `npm run format:check` — clean.
- `npm test` — 49 suites / 380 tests pass.
- `npm run test:e2e` (against a local Postgres via Docker, since no DB is available by default) — `test/posts.e2e-spec.ts` (43 tests) passes in full, including the reconstructed archive/restore endpoints. Did not run the entire e2e/integration suite end-to-end locally; CI's Postgres service should cover the rest.

author: johnitvn
body:
## Description

Two least-privilege fixes in `.github/workflows/`, both of which OpenSSF Scorecard was scoring against the repository. Published score at the time of writing: **4.8/10** (scan of `d8e142f`).

**`translate-pr.yml` — Dangerous-Workflow 0 → 10.** The job named its checkout ref explicitly:

```yaml
ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.ref }}
```

That is the *base* commit and the job was never unsafe. But under `pull_request_target`, Scorecard's dangerous-workflow check flags any `ref` mentioning `github.event.pull_request` without distinguishing `.base.sha` from `.head.sha`, so the spelling alone scored the repo as an untrusted code checkout — on the single heaviest-weighted check in the set (Critical). The comparison that makes this concrete is in-repo: `pr-practice-review.yml` uses the same `base.sha` expression and is *not* flagged, because its trigger is `pull_request`.

Removing the input keeps the identical guarantee — `pull_request_target` already checks out the base branch — and is marginally tighter, since it tracks the base branch tip rather than the sha recorded when the PR opened, i.e. the newest trusted `repo-care`. The `workflow_dispatch` path is unchanged: with no pull_request event the old expression already fell through to `github.ref`, which is also what the default resolves to.

**`codeql.yml` — Token-Permissions 9 → 10.** `security-events: write` sat at the workflow level, where any job added later would inherit it; only `analyze` uploads SARIF. Moved to the job. Note that job-level `permissions` *replaces* the workflow-level block rather than merging with it, so `contents: read` is restated alongside it — omitting it would leave `actions/checkout` without read access. This matches the shape `scorecard.yml` already uses.

No behaviour change to what either workflow runs.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change fixing an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change adding functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature causing existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Design system / component update
- [ ] Refactor / performance improvement

None of the listed categories fit a CI-configuration change; `dev-cli pr-facts` returns an empty `typeOfChange` for this diff. Left unchecked deliberately rather than approximated.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [ ] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing completed
- [ ] UI tested (if applicable)
- [ ] Accessibility checked (if applicable)

Verified with the `ossf/scorecard` CLI run against the working tree rather than by reasoning about the checks, and confirmed in both directions so the delta is attributable to this diff:

**Test Steps:**

1. `go install github.com/ossf/scorecard/v5@latest`
2. `scorecard --local . --checks Dangerous-Workflow,Token-Permissions` on this branch → `Dangerous-Workflow 10`, `Token-Permissions 10`.
3. `git stash push -- .github/workflows/codeql.yml .github/workflows/translate-pr.yml`, re-run → `Dangerous-Workflow 0`, `Token-Permissions 9` — reproducing the published report exactly, which confirms the local tool agrees with the hosted scan.
4. `git stash pop`.
5. Parsed both files with a YAML loader to confirm the resulting permission blocks are `{contents: read}` at workflow level and `{contents: read, security-events: write}` on `analyze`, and that no checkout step carries a `with:` any more.
6. `pnpm nx affected -t lint test typecheck build e2e` green (no Nx target consumes workflow YAML, so this is unchanged-by-construction; run for completeness).

## Screenshots (if applicable)

N/A — no UI surface.

## AI-Assisted Development

- [x] This PR is AI-assisted (drafted or substantially written by an AI coding agent)

Claude Code, opus tier.

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have commented complex logic (where necessary)
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] Tests pass locally: `pnpm nx affected -t lint test typecheck build e2e`
- [x] No unrelated code changes included
- [ ] `CLA.md` clauses 4–6 are accurate for **this** pull request

The CLA box is left for the human author to check — it is a first-person assertion about authorship and rights that an agent cannot make on someone's behalf. Flagging rather than silently ticking it.

## Additional Notes

Both `ref:` removal and the permission move are comment-heavy on purpose: each encodes a non-obvious reason (a scanner limitation, and GitHub's replace-not-merge semantics for job-level `permissions`) that the next person to "tidy" these files would otherwise undo.

Scope note: this PR is one of two covering the code-fixable Scorecard findings. The dependency-vulnerability half is separate and touches disjoint files. The remaining findings need repository settings rather than code — chiefly Branch-Protection (3/10) and Code-Review (0/10), which are the same action: requiring approvals on `main`. `Maintained` (0/10, repo under 90 days old) and `SAST` (9/10, commits predating `codeql.yml`) resolve on their own with time. `License` (9/10) is scored down for not being an OSI/FSF licence, which is a deliberate fair-code decision and should stay as-is.

body:
fix: stamp the descriptive pod name on every Task mint path

#517 shipped the `<type>-<project>-<repo>-<i|p><id>` pod-naming scheme, but wired `agent.StampPodName` into exactly ONE Task-creation path: `internal/queue/enqueue.go:482`. `agent.PodName` prefers the stamped `PodNameAnnotation` and otherwise falls back to legacy `"wrapper-" + task.Name`, so every Task minted anywhere else silently kept the old name.

Live evidence from the cluster, all created well after the operator was already running v1.42.0 (so this is a code gap, not a stale image):

| Task | Kind | Annotation | Pod |
|---|---|---|---|
| `incident-qe-d402f92…` | incident (queue path) | `inc-tatara-529b4f14…` | new scheme |
| `mt-r-tatara-chat-59-…` | review (intake path) | `<NONE>` | `wrapper-mt-r-tatara-chat-59-…` |

All six review Tasks minted that day had no annotation.

Grepping every non-test `&tatarav1alpha1.Task{` literal found five unstamped mint paths, not three:

- `internal/controller/intake.go` `MintIssueTask`
- `internal/controller/intake.go` `MintReviewTask`
- `internal/controller/docbatch.go` `MintDocBatch`
- `internal/controller/takeover_mint.go` `MintOrUnparkTakeoverTask`
- `internal/restapi/outcome.go` `mintClarifyTask`

All five now stamp; with `enqueue.go` that is all six creation sites.

`repoRef`: `enqueue.go` passes `p.PodRepo`, whose only non-empty producer sets it to the Repository CR name, and both intake mints already key `IntakeTaskName` on `repo.Name` - so `repo.Name` keeps naming consistent across paths. The doc batch is genuinely repo-bound (`Spec.RepositoryRef = docsRepo.Name`) so it stamps that rather than `""`.

Verified, not assumed:
- **Adoption cannot clobber.** `createTaskRaceSafe` never writes the local literal on the adopt path, and both intake mints return the local task. A pre-#517 Task adopted here keeps no annotation and keeps working through the fallback. Pinned by `TestMintIssueTask_AdoptedLegacyTwin_KeepsFallbackPodName`.
- **Stable across reconciles.** The annotation is written once at creation, never recomputed. This matters because `agent.AgentKind` prefers `status.agentKind` over `spec.kind`, so recomputation would drift as the Task advances. Pinned by `TestMintIssueTask_StampedPodNameStableAcrossStageChange`.
- **63-char DNS-1123 budget.** Worst realistic review case (`tatara` + `tatara-memory-repo-ingester` + PR 34) yields `rev-tatara-tatara-memory-repo-ingester-p34`, 42 chars, no trimming. The takeover test exercises the trim path for real and shows the `tko-` and `-p11` segments surviving intact.

Gates: `mise run test` all packages ok (controller 78s, restapi 7s), `mise run lint` 0 issues, `make generate manifests build` clean. New tests were confirmed to FAIL with the stamp calls removed and PASS with them restored, run through the envtest harness.

The CRD chart diff is a description-string-only regeneration of pre-existing drift from ad420b5 (#517 edited the `PodRepo` doc comment without running `make manifests`). Zero behavior change.

## One thing worth a separate look, not touched here

`ensureStagePod` (`internal/controller/task_stage.go:1281`) reuses a pod found by name when `annPodStage` matches, with no `LabelTaskUID` check - the reaper has one (`reaper.go:163`), this does not. Doc-batch pods were previously `wrapper-<name>` with a date+rand5 suffix, so each nightly batch had a unique name; they now collapse to `doc-<project>-<docs-repo>`. In practice `docBatchInFlight` prevents two concurrent batches and `DeleteWrapper` runs on the terminal transition, and #517 already introduced the same collapse for the queue path (`brs-<project>` / `ref-<project>`), so this is inherent to the naming scheme rather than new here. Flagging rather than dropping it.

## 요약

"릴스 노출이 적다 / 배경이 밋밋하다 / 영어 점검 / SEO·홍보" 요청에 대한 작업. 멀티에이전트 감사(원어민 카피 에디터 + 기술 SEO + IG 그로스 + 라이선스 리서치, 12 에이전트)로 문제를 찾고 코드로 반영했습니다.

### 1. 실사 사진 배경 — 밋밋함의 근본 원인 해결

**이 개발 환경은 외부 이미지/영상 소스가 전부 차단(403)** 되어 있어 제가 직접 받을 수 없습니다. 하지만 **Vercel 런타임은 프록시 밖**이라 거기서는 받을 수 있습니다. 그 구조로 만들었습니다:

```
운영자가 사진 URL POST → Vercel이 다운로드 → 1512×2688 정규화
→ Supabase Storage 저장 → 릴스가 그 위에 켄번즈 카메라 무브
```

- **기차 사진 한 장이면 20초 동안 진짜로 다가오는 기차**가 됩니다 (씬별 무브: rails/road는 강한 push-in, 칠판은 측면 드리프트)
- 사진 없는 씬은 기존 코드 배경으로 **자동 폴백** → 하나씩 채워도 발행 안 끊김
- 최악 조건(밝고 복잡한 사진)에서 텍스트 가독성 실측 확인 — 스크림이 버팁니다
- **사진 경로가 오히려 더 빠름**: 111ms/프레임 vs SVG 144ms
- 켄번즈 기하 유닛 테스트 6건 (프레임 이탈·비율 왜곡·업스케일 방지)

**뉴스·다큐 영상은 넣지 않았습니다.** 라이선스 리서치 결과 AP/Reuters/방송사 영상은 rights-managed이고 IG 저작권 클레임 → 계정 정지 위험이 실제로 큽니다. 안전한 대안 소스와 검색어를 문서로 정리했습니다.

### 2. 영어 카피 — 정답이 카드에 인쇄되고 있었습니다

원어민 감수 29건 중 확정 결함:

| 결함 | 실제 영향 |
|---|---|
| **정답 유출 3건** | `spell-embarrassed` 훅이 카드 배지로 승격돼 **정답 "Embarrassed"를 문제 바로 위에 인쇄**. `spell-occurrence`, `pct-reverse`도 동일 |
| **수열 10문항 캡션이 풀 수 없음** | 숫자가 이미지에만 있고 캡션엔 "What comes next?"만 — 베이트 풀의 1/3이 텍스트로는 무의미 |
| **물음표 삭제 버그** | `hookBadge`가 `?`를 지워 질문을 단정문으로: "HALVE THE DAYS"는 정답 진술, "BACK TO EVEN"은 **오답을 사실로 진술** |
| **곡선 아포스트로피 5건** | ASCII 필터가 삭제 → 카드에 **DONT / ISNT / NATURES**가 27px 대문자로 인쇄. 지능을 파는 브랜드에 치명적 |
| **자기모순 CTA 3건** | 광고는 "곧 정답 공개", 다음 화면은 "내일 공개" |
| 영국식 철자·`2 h 30` 표기·`trick-cats` 중의성 | 미국식 통일 + "exactly" 추가 |

재발 방지 회귀 테스트 4건 추가.

### 3. SEO — 코드로 검증된 지적만 반영

| 수정 | 규모 |
|---|---|
| **canonical 누락** — Next가 `alternates`를 얕게 병합해 자식의 `languages`가 부모 canonical을 덮어씀 | 허브·tests·about + **유형 페이지 108개 = 사이트맵의 77%** |
| 러너 페이지 10개가 **홈페이지를 canonical로 주장** | noindex,follow + 사이트맵 제외 |
| privacy·terms가 홈페이지 canonical 상속 | 자체 canonical·타이틀·설명 |
| **오리진 4종 난립** (localhost / 7iq.vercel.app / 빈문자열) | `getSiteUrl()`로 통일, 프로덕션 도메인 우선 |
| **IQ 랜딩 meta description 18자** (유일한 수익 페이지) | FAQ 5쌍 신설 → 실제 설명 + FAQPage 스키마 확보 |
| FAQ 답변이 DOM에 없는데 JSON-LD는 있다고 주장 (**구조화 데이터 정책 위반**) | 항상 렌더 후 `hidden`으로 접기 |

로컬 실측 검증: `/ko`·`/ko/mbti/types/intj`·`/ko/privacy` 모두 canonical 출력, `/ko/test`는 noindex, IQ 설명은 실제 문장, FAQ 본문이 HTML에 존재.

## 테스트

`tsc`/`lint`/`build` 통과, 유닛 **109/109** (신규 10건: 켄번즈 6 + 카피 안전 4)

author: rakshitkaintura
body:
Fixes #1391.

## Why
On macOS, users with multiple virtual desktops (Spaces) noticed that if they started recording on one desktop and switched to another, the recording UI (and other floating overlay windows) did not follow them to the active screen.

## What
This PR fixes the macOS window persistence issue across spaces. 

In Electron, defining `visibleOnAllWorkspaces: true` as a boolean inside the initial `BrowserWindow` config can cause a bug where macOS ignores subsequent calls to `.setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces(true, { visibleOnFullScreen: true })` because it caches the state.

- Removed the boolean `visibleOnAllWorkspaces: process.platform !== "win32"` from the configuration objects (`MAIN_WINDOW_CONFIG`, `TRANSCRIPTION_PREVIEW_CONFIG`, etc.) in `windowConfig.js`.
- Enforced the property explicitly inside `WindowPositionUtil.setupAlwaysOnTop()` exactly when `window.isVisible()` is true.
- By cleanly relying on the native method call with `{ visibleOnFullScreen: true, skipTransformProcessType: true }`, the overlays now properly hook into the macOS Space system and follow the active virtual desktop seamlessly.

author: theexxby-prog
body:
The two items left open from #27.

## Period control is back on Campaigns

Day / Week / Month / Year returns to the KPI strip — but as **one control for the whole strip**, not the previous per-card switchers. The old dashboard gave each of three cards its own identical switcher, which both cluttered the header and let the cards disagree about which period they were showing.

Only the volume metrics scale with the window. The acceptance rate is a ratio and the campaign count is a live total, so neither is multiplied — picking "Year" shouldn't claim you have twelve times as many campaigns.

## Clients can no longer initiate payment

Per the build-plan direction, clients view and download invoices but don't pay. Removed:

- **Pay Now** from the invoice list, the client invoice card, and the preview modal
- the `handlePay` handler and the stubbed `initiatePayment` / `syncPaymentToTally` calls behind it
- the page subtitle that promised paying "securely"
- the overdue-invoice nudge on the home page, which had a **Pay Now** call-to-action
- the entry in the feature list documenting a button that no longer exists

The `/payment` route is **untouched**. It isn't linked from any navigation, so whether that page should exist at all is a separate decision from this one.

## Verification

Typecheck and build clean. Drove the period control through Day / Month / Year in both themes — Day shows 14 leads and "Billable today", Year shows 4,968 and "Billable this year", with acceptance and campaign count correctly unchanged. Confirmed zero "Pay Now" occurrences on the invoices page in light and dark. No console or page errors.

author: jonahgabriel
body:
Follow-up to #2559 (merged 2026-07-30T05:48:14Z as `276017d1`). Ticket: **OMN-15466**.

An independent verifier found that the equivalence test #2559 shipped is weaker than it claims to be. This PR closes that gap. Test-only — no production behavior changes.

## What was wrong

`tests/unit/scripts/test_lane_census_inventory.py` asserted only that the API path's labels are a **subset** of the CLI path's:

```python
# The CLI carries strictly more labels (compose internals); every label
# the API reports must match the CLI's value exactly.
for key, value in api_row["Labels"].items():
    assert cli_row["Labels"][key] == value, key
```

The justifying docstring claim — "the CLI carries strictly more labels" — is **false against the test's own recorded fixtures**. Measured on the four fixture containers:

| Container | API labels | CLI labels | Key sets identical | Values identical |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `omnibase-infra-forward-migration` | 15 | 15 | yes | yes |
| `omnibase-infra-intelligence-migration` | 14 | 14 | yes | yes |
| `omninode-stability-test-runtime-effects` | 32 | 32 | yes | yes |
| `omninode-stability-test-runtime-worker` | 32 | 32 | yes | yes |

Because the assertion only iterates the API side, a **spurious CLI-only key passes unnoticed** — exactly the primary/fallback divergence the test exists to catch. The two paths are meant to be interchangeable, so nothing weaker than equality is correct.

## The fix

Assert full row equality, driven off the collector's own `_CLI_FIELDS` so a newly consumed field is covered automatically, plus a whole-row `==`:

```python
for field in inventory._CLI_FIELDS:
    assert api_row[field] == cli_row[field], field
assert api_row == cli_row
```

## Proof the strengthened assertion is not vacuous

Injecting **one** spurious CLI-only label (`com.spurious.cli_only=1`) into the recorded CLI fixture, on `.200`, against merged `dev` `276017d1`:

| Assertion | Same mutated fixture | Result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **Old** (subset, as merged in #2559) | `,com.spurious.cli_only=1` | **1 passed** — defect missed |
| **New** (this PR) | `,com.spurious.cli_only=1` | **1 failed** — `Right contains 1 more item: {'com.spurious.cli_only': '1'}` |

That is the "exists but wrong" case, not a "does not exist" case: the test ran green before and still detected nothing. Fixture restored after both runs (`git status` clean, verified).

## Corroboration at host scale

Equality is the right bar empirically, not just in principle. Both collector paths were run back-to-back on `.201` (`omninode-pc`) at 2026-07-30T05:45Z, read-only, over the **full live host inventory** of 91 containers:

```
api=91 cli=91 common=91
label-dict mismatches: 0
State mismatches: 0
Image mismatches: 0
Status mismatches: 0
```

## Gates on `.200` (`stickybeatz-studio`) via patch-transfer

Per rule 11a. Edited locally, `git diff` piped over ssh to `git apply`, then **verified byte-identical before gating** — `sha256(tests/unit/scripts/test_lane_census_inventory.py)` = `cf4a130255c29fdeac34fb1a9ff627fcb87eb9a3e706d643db4ffc9b75e07cd7` on both this Mac and `.200`. The commit was authored and pushed on `.200`.

- Governed selector on the real changed-file set: `{"selected_paths":["tests/unit/scripts/"],"is_full_suite":false}` — no full-suite escalation.
- That selected suite on this branch's base (`origin/dev` `276017d1`): **899 passed, 0 failed**.
- `ruff format --check` clean; `ruff check` clean; `mypy` clean.
- `pre-commit run --files`: **43 Passed, 46 Skipped, 0 Failed, rc=0** — including `Shell hygiene (shellcheck, OMN-14761)`.

One pre-existing `PytestUnhandledThreadExceptionWarning` from `test_monitor_logs_file_tailer.py` is unrelated to this diff and reproduces on `dev`.

## Corrections to the #2559 record

Three evidence claims in #2559's body and squash commit message were wrong. They are corrected in the OMN-15466 ticket body; the squash message on `dev` cannot be rewritten, so this PR is the durable correction record. **None of them affect D1 or D2, which were reproduced directly by the timing table.**

1. **"the only two such runs in the log's history"** — false. `~/.local/log/onex/lane-census.log` holds 19 `Starting` lines and 14 `DRIFT detected:` lines; **five** runs logged `Starting` with no terminal line (log lines 10, 14, 42, 46, 47 = 2026-07-01T23:00:52Z, 2026-07-01T23:41:46Z, 2026-07-22T21:44:15Z, 2026-07-29T22:21:57Z, 2026-07-29T22:22:24Z). What actually distinguishes the Jul-29 pair is that they are the file's final two lines with no completing run after them. The corroboration is in fact **stronger** than claimed: 4 of the 5 unterminated runs have a matching `Canceled: context canceled` in the docker journal within minutes (line 14 → +90 s, line 42 → +5.5 min, lines 46/47 → the 22:23–22:26Z cluster).
2. **The `lstat` hard-failure variant was misdated.** `journalctl` on `omninode-pc` emits local time at `-04:00` (`timedatectl`: `America/New_York (EDT, -0400)`). The record reads `time="2026-07-29T22:01:27.618939458-04:00"` = **2026-07-30T02:01:27Z**, i.e. **3 h 59 m after** the census hang on the next UTC day — not `22:01:27Z`, ~20 min before it, inside the incident bracket. The four cancellation timestamps in the same paragraph were converted correctly, so the handling was inconsistent.
3. **"93 occurrences across 23 distinct days in July"** conflated two error kinds. The whole retained journal (2026-06-28 → 2026-07-30) holds **197** `snapshotter.Usage`-on-`containers/json` errors over 27 distinct local days: **93** `Canceled: context canceled` on **6** distinct local days, **103** `lstat …: no such file or directory` (HTTP 500) on **27** distinct local days, and 1 `readdirent`. The 27-day figure belongs to the `lstat` kind, not the cancellations.

Additionally, OMN-15466 acceptance criterion 7 was unproven at merge time — the 0.15 s figure was a raw `curl`, not the shipped artifact. `scripts/lane_census_inventory.py` has now been executed on `.201`: **0.120 s / 0.157 s / 0.133 s** (rc=0, `inventory_source=engine_api`), CLI fallback **0.132 s**, and both-paths-dead → **rc=4** with empty stdout. Container count is point-in-time (111 at 04:38Z, 92 at 05:44Z, 91 at 05:45Z), so the criterion is a wall-clock bound at ~100-container scale, not a fixed 111 denominator.

`.201` was **read-only** throughout: no daemon restart, no container mutation, no compose action.

Refs OMN-15466

Evidence-Ticket: OMN-15466


Evidence-Source: OCC#5578

author: aayambansal
body:
Adds the branch that answers **"if I change this file, what breaks?"**

Every existing branch answers that with similarity, and similarity cannot see a
caller/callee edge. Nothing about a caller looks like the function it calls, so
vector search misses it and BM25 only catches it when names happen to collide.

There is no import graph in the index, but `symbols` records what each file
defines, and files mentioning the anchor's symbols are in practice the files
that depend on it — callers, tests, re-exports. Scoring by *distinct* anchor
symbols referenced keeps a file that touches the whole API above one that
shares a single common word.

## It works on the query shape it targets

ARB development split, `edit2ripple` (the change-impact workflow):

| weight | edit2ripple Recall@5 |
| ---: | ---: |
| 0.00 | 0.238 |
| 0.15 | 0.310 |
| 0.30 | **0.381** |

Validated by hand first: for anchor `binding/form_mapping.go`, the gold ripple
target `binding/form_mapping_test.go` ranks **#1** with 6 distinct symbol
references.

## Why it is off by default

A standing weight is the wrong mechanism. The gain is paid for by the three
workflows whose answer is not a dependent:

| weight | edit2ripple R@5 | overall MRR | overall R@20 |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0.00 | 0.238 | **0.193** | **0.544** |
| 0.15 | 0.310 | 0.182 | 0.527 |
| 0.30 | 0.381 | 0.163 | 0.493 |

So it ships inert. What it needs is intent gating on the query shape — "here is
a diff, what else is affected" — rather than a global weight. Draft until that
exists.

Opt in per deployment with `SYNSC_FUSION_WEIGHTS=reverse_dep=0.3`.

965 tests pass, ruff and mypy clean.
