author: alexandrosang21
body:
## Pre-flight checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines on pull requests](https://github.com/facebook/docusaurus/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests).
- [x] **If this is a code change**: I have written unit tests and/or added dogfooding pages to fully verify the new behavior.
- [ ] **If this is a new API or substantial change**: the PR has an accompanying issue (closes #12322) and the maintainers have approved on my working plan.

> Left unchecked deliberately: this is a small bug fix rather than a new API or substantial
> change, so no working plan was agreed beforehand. It does close #12322.

## Motivation

Fixes #12322. With `future.experimental_vcs: 'default-v2'`, `sitemap.xml` is generated without
any `<lastmod>` values, while `'git-ad-hoc'` and `'default-v1'` produce them correctly for the
same site and Git history.

`default-v2` selects the eager Git strategy in production. `vcsGitEager` keys its file map by
absolute paths:

```ts
// The Map keys should be absolute file paths, not relative Git paths
return [resolve(repoRoot, entry[0]), entry[1]];
```

but the lookup uses whatever path it is handed:

```ts
return init.filesMap.get(filePath) ?? null;
```

The sitemap plugin passes `route.metadata.sourceFilePath`, which `RouteMetadata` documents as
"expected to be relative to the site directory". So the lookup misses and returns `null`, and
`getRouteLastmod` drops `<lastmod>` for that route without any warning.

`git-ad-hoc` and `default-v1` are unaffected because they shell out to `git log -- <path>`, which
resolves a relative path itself.

This resolves the path against the site dir when it is not already absolute. Absolute paths keep
working unchanged, so `getFileCreationInfo` and existing callers are unaffected.

## Test Plan

**Unit test.** Added `can read repo file info from a site-relative path` to the existing
`VSC Git Eager Strategy` block. It fails on `main` and passes with this change. Every existing
eager test passes an absolute path via `path.join(repoDir, ...)`, which is why this gap was not
covered.

```
pnpm vitest run packages/docusaurus-utils/src/vcs packages/docusaurus-plugin-sitemap
Test Files  5 passed (5)
     Tests  94 passed (94)
```

`eslint`, `tsc --noEmit`, `oxfmt --list-different` and `cspell` are all clean on the two changed
files.

**End to end**, using the reproduction repository from the issue
([eMUQI/docusaurus-vcs-sitemap-repro](https://github.com/eMUQI/docusaurus-vcs-sitemap-repro)),
building the same site twice with only this patch differing:

| `@docusaurus/utils` | `<url>` | `<lastmod>` |
|---|---|---|
| unmodified | 1 | 0 |
| with this change | 1 | 1 |

Its `npm run verify:repro` asserts that `default-v2` produces zero `<lastmod>`, so with the fix
applied that assertion now fails, which is the intended outcome.

### Test links

Not applicable: this changes build-time sitemap metadata rather than anything rendered, so there
is no UI to preview.

## Disclosure

This change was written with AI assistance (Claude), per the AI policy in CONTRIBUTING.md. I have
reviewed every line, verified the root cause against the reproduction repository above, and can
explain and defend the change in review.

author: wombat164
body:
Closes #37. Built to your settled decisions - nothing here was guessed.

## The ordering

`recorded_at` on all thirteen datasets, ISO 8601 with an explicit offset, machine-set on append. Resolution orders by `(date, recorded_at)`, absent before present.

The migration is a **read no-op**, and that is asserted rather than asserted-at: with the key constant across every unstamped row, a stable sort preserves file order exactly, so `last line wins` still holds on a legacy file. `test_an_unstamped_file_keeps_exactly_its_old_behaviour` pins it.

The bug itself is pinned by `test_rewriting_the_file_cannot_change_what_the_record_asserts` - the same two rows in file order, reversed, and sorted by target all resolve to the same goal.

## Where each guarantee is enforced

You said an author-supplied value must be a validation error. I have implemented that as strictly as each layer can actually see:

| Property | Layer | Why there |
|---|---|---|
| ISO 8601 + explicit offset | `validate_record`, per line | all a single line can show |
| **monotonic** | `vitai validate`, per file | not a property of any line - and this is the check that actually catches a hand-written stamp, since a plausible-looking value rarely lands in the right place in the sequence |
| never authored | `append`, at the boundary | the only place that can refuse it outright |

**One thing I did not implement as specified, and want to flag.** I dropped the "is it in the future" check. Every fixture in the repo and the whole demo are dated 2030, deliberately, so a synthetic record can never be mistaken for a real one - a wall-clock comparison rejects the repo's own corpus while catching nothing that monotonicity does not. If you want a future check anyway, it needs an injectable `now` and the 2030 convention has to change with it.

## The append helper

You were right that this decides whether the field is worth anything. It is the API, not a convention:

```
$ echo '{"date":"2030-05-01","kg":79.4,"source":"scale","measured_at":"07:10"}' \
    | vitai append weight
{"date": "2030-05-01", "kg": 79.4, ..., "measured_at": "07:10",
 "recorded_at": "2026-07-30T11:20:11+00:00", "_gen": 3}

$ echo '{"date":"2030-05-02","kg":79.2,"recorded_at":"..."}' | vitai append weight
recorded_at is machine-set and must not be supplied - it is the one clock in
the record that cannot be authored. Remove it and let append stamp it.

$ echo '{"date":"not-a-date","kg":79.2,"source":"scale"}' | vitai append weight
refusing to append an invalid weight line: bad date 'not-a-date'
```

It also fills absent keys with null, stamps `_gen` (the convention documented since G25 that nothing enforced), rejects unknown keys, and refuses a stamp older than the last one in the file. Validating *before* writing matters more than it looks: an append-only file cannot be un-appended, so the alternative to refusing at the door is a superseding line that should never have been needed.

`Vitai.append()` is the same thing for the scripts that actually write this record.

## measured_at

HH:MM local, as decided. It is **not** `start_time`'s format and I want that to be a visible choice rather than an inconsistency: a session has a duration and can cross a timezone, so it needs the offset to be comparable across platforms; a weigh-in is a point on a day the row already names, the useful question is only ever "morning or evening", and HH:MM is what someone can answer from memory. A format nobody can fill in accurately is a field that stays null.

Absent stays absent - the engine never infers a probable weigh-in time.

## The rate caveat, and something it turned up

The demo now carries the artifact: a settled 07:00 routine that falls apart after the travel week, giving a window spanning 12.4 h.

```
**Rate:** losing 0.02 kg/week (target: losing 0.35 kg/week) - **NOT READABLE - weigh-in times vary too much**

> Weigh-ins span 12.4 h, which alone can account for about 1.04 kg - as much
> as the 0.02 kg/week this line reports, so the trend is not yet separable
> from weigh-in timing. Weigh at a consistent time before reading it as progress.
```

**That `NOT READABLE` is a deviation beyond what you asked for, and it is the part I would push back on if you disagree.** Before it, that line read `SLOW - check logging` - and beneath it, a caveat saying the number was noise. Contradictory advice, and the actionable half of it tells an athlete to cut harder off a figure the clock could have produced entirely. `verdicts` emits `nodata` for the same case, since a consumer reading `BEHIND` renders it as fact. It is the same shape as the existing medical carve-out: the engine already knows how to decline to score something.

**No invented threshold.** After two hand-rolled cutoffs with no published basis, `weigh_in_timing` reports the observed spread and the kilograms it could account for, and the caller compares that against the rate actually being claimed. The one constant is the ~1 kg/day diurnal swing, labelled in the source as an order-of-magnitude anchor rather than a personal calibration. The advice clause only appears above a 2 h spread - telling someone who already weighs within half an hour to be more consistent blames the wrong thing when what makes the rate unreadable is that the rate is tiny.

## G25, the regression you flagged

The generation is **derived**, not transcribed: `one past whatever each dataset was already at`. Thirteen hand-written numbers is thirteen chances to typo one, and a wrong generation here does not fail loudly - it silently starts *requiring* a field on lines that predate it, which is the exact time bomb the mechanism exists to defuse.

Three tests: the invariant per dataset, `recorded_at` present in every key list, and a full re-validation of the committed demo corpus - 300+ real gen-1, gen-2 and gen-3 lines across thirteen datasets, every one of which predates this change.

## Also

Contract **7**. Two things a consumer must act on, in `db.py` and the README: order by both clocks or a same-date correction resolves by luck, and `weight_rate` may now be `nodata` for a reason that is not missing data.

`vitai-ingest` is told to write through `append`, never to author `recorded_at`, and to capture the weigh-in time when a screenshot shows one - and to leave it null when it does not, rather than inferring a probable one. The content-repo `CLAUDE.md` template says the same.

## Gates

373 tests (was 345), new `tests/test_clocks.py` has 28. Ruff, personal gate, `generate_demo --check`, `vitai validate` and a dated `vitai build` all clean.

## Queue

Per your sequencing this was taken before #33 and #35. Next: #36, then #32, #23, #28, then #35 → #33.

author: lennystepn-hue
body: Part of #12. ## The file `AnonLanding.vue` was **979 lines**: eleven sections, five unrelated data arrays, a count-up animation and a fetch, all sharing one 200-line preamble. Editing the pricing teaser meant scrolling past the MCP catalogue. 138 of the repo's 267 hardcoded colour literals lived here — the most important page in the product was also the least maintainable one. Now **97 lines** composing eleven section components, each owning its own markup and its own data. `mcpGroups` belongs to the MCP catalogue, not to a preamble shared by ten sections that never mention it. | | lines | |---|---| | `AnonLanding.vue` | 979 → **97** | | `HeroSection` · `McpCatalogSection` · `OrbShowcaseSection` | 147 · 165 · 198 | | `PricingTeaserSection` · `SessionMockupSection` · `HowItWorksSection` | 141 · 106 · 68 | | `WorksWithStrip` · `StatsStrip` · `FinalCtaSection` · `LandingFooter` · `DashboardPreviewSection` | 55 · 51 · 46 · 23 · 20 | The template was **sliced mechanically, not retyped**. It carries a lot of hard-won detail — why the orb hides below `lg`, why `pb-0` on mobile, why the logo strip sits at `-mt-8` — and paraphrasing would have quietly lost some of it. ## The copy was lying about the product Step 02 of "how it works": > *"Copy one config line into your `claude_desktop_config.json`. Vibecell appears as a tool server instantly."* True of the old manual path. Wrong the day `hangar setup` shipped — nobody edits that file by hand now, and the one-liner configures **every** MCP client on the machine rather than one. The hero's shortcut said *"Paste one prompt — AI installs itself"*, also the superseded path. Both now describe what actually happens. A landing page that misdescribes its own product is a worse problem than its line count. ## The tool count was a manual sync that had already failed `49` appeared in the hero stat strip, the catalogue heading, a body paragraph and an orb blurb — above this comment: ```js // MCP tool buckets — counts must sum to the live total (49 as of f82141c). // Re-bucket carefully when adding new tools so the hero stat strip // (49 above) and these per-category counts stay consistent. ``` It went stale the first time a tool was added, which was this session, at 50. **A number a human has to remember to update is a number that will be wrong.** `/api/v1/status` already reports it as the MCP component's message (`"50 tools registered"`), so `useMcpToolCount` reads it from there and per-category counts became shares of the live total. Falls back to a constant when the API is unreachable — a marketing page must render when the backend is down, and a slightly stale number beats an empty one. Six tests cover the parse, all three fallback paths, and singular phrasing. ## Caught by the build, not by the types Slicing the footer took the page wrapper's closing `` with it. `vue-tsc` was clean and all 50 tests passed against a template that **could not compile**. Only `vite build` objected: ``` [vite:vue] LandingFooter.vue (23:3): Invalid end tag. ``` Worth remembering when judging what "green" means here. ## Verification | Check | Result | |---|---| | `vue-tsc` | clean | | `vitest run` | 56 passed, 4 skipped (6 new) | | `vite build` | succeeds, 510 modules | | both design guards | green | ## Not in this PR The visual-signature half of #12 — one recurring signature element across the app, motion as language. The decomposition is the prerequisite: it is now possible to change the hero without touching the footer. Keeping them separate so the diff of a mechanical slice stays reviewable. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01LU8ijNQoKnZvQKKDbU8ZfE

author: adityakumarsingh2
body:
This PR improves the **Microcosm AI Companion** experience with a redesigned interface, contextual query scopes, and new actions that integrate AI responses directly into the note-taking workflow.

## Changes

### 1. AI Scope Selector

* Added **Workspace**, **Notebook**, and **Page** query scopes.
* **Workspace** remains the default scope.
* **Notebook** limits AI context to the active notebook.
* **Page** limits AI context to the currently open page.
* Page scope is disabled when no page is open.
* Chat requests dynamically include the selected scope and relevant `notebookId` / `pageId`.

### 2. Companion Actions

* Added **Copy** action for AI responses.
* Added **Insert into Page** to append AI-generated content directly to the active Tiptap editor.
* Added **Clear Conversation** to reset chat history.
* Added context-aware suggestion prompts based on the selected scope.

### 3. UI/UX Overhaul

* Redesigned the AI Companion sidebar with a modern dark interface.
* Added glassmorphism styling to the header and input area.
* Added segmented scope controls with smooth transitions.
* Improved user and assistant message styling.
* Added hover states and micro-interactions for message actions.
* Added a custom scrollbar for the conversation area.
* Improved inline and block code styling for Markdown responses.

author: wlaur
body:
## Problem

An Arrow ingest destroys any `ON COMMIT DROP` temporary table on the connection, **even when ingesting into an unrelated table**. The table is silently gone afterwards:

```python
with dbapi.connect(uri) as conn, conn.cursor() as cur:
    cur.execute("CREATE LOCAL TEMPORARY TABLE scratch(value INT) ON COMMIT DROP")
    cur.adbc_ingest("some_other_table", batch, mode="append")
    cur.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM scratch")
    # NOT_FOUND: 42S02!SELECT: no such table 'scratch'
```

This reproduces at the raw DBAPI level with `autocommit=False`, so it is not a `sqlalchemy-monetdb-adbc` issue. It is not a stray commit either — a `rollback()` after the ingest still correctly undoes both the ingested rows and any prior pending work.

## Cause

`begin_atomic` takes a savepoint for the ingest and releases it on success. Releasing the savepoint ends the temporary table's lifetime.

That case is already handled: `retain_until_transaction_end` keeps the savepoint until the caller's transaction ends when a transaction-scoped temporary table exists. But the detection query only matched `sys.tables.commit_action = 1`.

MonetDB encodes the commit action as:

| value | meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | `ON COMMIT DELETE ROWS` |
| 2 | `ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS` |
| 3 | `ON COMMIT DROP` |

Verified against Dec2025-SP3:

```
_ca_delete       commit_action = 1
_ca_preserve     commit_action = 2
_ca_drop         commit_action = 3
```

So `ON COMMIT DROP` was never detected, `retain_until_transaction_end` stayed `false`, the savepoint was released, and the table went away.

## Fix

Match both transaction-scoped commit actions and rename the helper, which is no longer specific to `DELETE ROWS`.

The autocommit guard shares the helper but is unaffected in practice: under autocommit the `CREATE` statement's own commit drops an `ON COMMIT DROP` table immediately, so one can never reach an ingest. Its error message is left as-is because only `DELETE ROWS` can reach it.

## Tests

Adds `test_ingest_preserves_drop_on_commit_temporary_table`, which fails on `main` and passes here.

Gates run locally against a Dec2025-SP3 server: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` (131 passed), `pytest` (460 passed, 13 skipped, 5 xfailed), `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `pyright` (0 errors).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: aleadag
body:
## Summary

- classify every executed split field against trusted `HOME` and its lexical ancestors before model inference
- normalize pathname components and conservatively account for `globstar`, `nocaseglob`, repeated separators, and relative pattern reachability
- reject empty or relative trusted `HOME` before isolated helper construction
- add evaluator and Codex, Claude, and Antigravity regressions with safe model-backed controls

## Root cause

The previous exact-HOME guard classified the unsplit resolved value. Shell field splitting and pathname expansion could instead produce relative targets that resolve to `HOME` or one of its ancestors, especially from `/`, `HOME`'s parent, or after shell option changes. Several pattern paths were also compared with inconsistent lexical normalization.

## Impact

Unsafe recursive deletes now deny deterministically before model inference across all supported providers. Quoted HOME descendants and unrelated split patterns retain their existing model-backed behavior. Provider payloads, helper protocol, configuration, and public APIs are unchanged.

## Validation

- `nix develop path:. --command cargo test brain::safety::tests::home_alias_classification_respects_field_splitting -- --exact --nocapture --test-threads=1`
- `nix develop path:. --command cargo test --test hook_activity home_alias_field_splitting_is_denied_before_model_inference_for_every_provider -- --exact --nocapture --test-threads=1`
- `nix develop path:. --command cargo test safety -- --test-threads=1`
- `nix develop path:. --command cargo test --quiet -- --test-threads=1`
- `nix develop path:. --command cargo fmt --all --check`
- `nix develop path:. --command cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `nix develop path:. --command cargo build`
- `git -c core.whitespace=trailing-space diff --check`

Final independent static review approved the complete change with no Critical, Important, or Minor findings.

author: zayokami
body:
## Summary

Six security / robustness fixes, every one with a regression test, plus one CI reliability fix:

1. **`usage_script.rs` — cap untrusted JS execution** (security fix)
2. **`session_usage_grokbuild.rs` — skip oversized session log files** (robustness hardening)
3. **`session_usage_grokbuild.rs` — bound directory traversal, don't follow symlinks** (robustness hardening)
4. **`DeepLinkImportDialog.tsx` — show hidden usage access token / user id** (transparency fix)
5. **`codex_config.rs` — `model_catalog_json` arbitrary file read** (security fix)
6. **Proxy — unbounded response bodies / decompression bombs** (security fix)
7. **CI — set up pnpm via Corepack instead of `pnpm/action-setup` v6** (CI reliability fix)

Each code fix was verified against the vulnerable behavior first: reverting the guard makes the corresponding test fail. The CI change has no unit test; it is exercised by this PR's own workflow run.

---

## 1. Usage script: prevent infinite-loop DoS

`execute_usage_script` creates a QuickJS `Runtime` to run scripts that configure how to query a provider's remaining quota. These scripts can arrive from **untrusted input**:

- a `ccswitch://` deeplink can carry a Base64 `usageScript` parameter
- a WebDAV/S3 sync snapshot can import a provider row whose `usage_script` is enabled

The old code used a plain `Runtime::new()` with **no execution time limit, no memory limit, and no stack limit**. A malicious or simply buggy script containing `while (true) {}` would hang the backend thread until the process was killed.

### Fix

Add `create_script_runtime()` that configures the runtime **before** any `eval`:

- `set_interrupt_handler` with a 5-second deadline — QuickJS raises an uncatchable exception when time is up
- `set_memory_limit(16 * 1024 * 1024)` — caps JS heap growth
- `set_max_stack_size(256 * 1024)` — explicit stack budget

### Verification

Regression test `infinite_loop_usage_script_is_interrupted_before_blocking_the_backend` runs a `while(true)` script through the real `execute_usage_script` and asserts it returns an error in well under 15 seconds. A standalone repro using the original `Runtime::new()` pattern ran until killed by `timeout -s KILL 12` (exit code 137), confirming the issue is real and the test is not a tautology.

---

## 2. Grok session log: skip oversized files

`sync_single_grok_file` read the entire `updates.jsonl` with `fs::read_to_string` and had no size limit. A runaway CLI or a maliciously planted multi-gigabyte file under `~/.grok/sessions` could exhaust process memory during the periodic sync.

### Fix

Check `metadata.len()` before reading; skip files larger than 50 MiB with a warning. 50 MiB is far above normal usage (a single line is a few KiB) while still being safe to read as a string.

### Verification

Regression test `oversized_updates_jsonl_is_skipped_without_reading_into_memory` creates a file of `MAX_GROK_FILE_BYTES + 1` and asserts `sync_single_grok_file` returns zero imported rows without failing.

---

## 3. Grok session log: bound directory traversal

`collect_files_named` recursed with `path.is_dir()` and no depth limit. `is_dir()` follows symlinks, so a symlink cycle under `~/.grok/sessions` caused unbounded recursion and a stack-overflow abort.

### Fix

- Add a 16-level depth limit
- Use `entry.metadata()` and skip symlinks entirely instead of following them

### Verification

Regression test `symlink_cycle_does_not_cause_stack_overflow` creates `sessions/enc-project/sub/cycle -> ../..` and asserts the collector returns only the real `updates.jsonl` without crashing. A standalone repro using the original recursive logic produced `thread 'main' has overflowed its stack`.

---

## 4. Deeplink provider import: show hidden usage fields

The provider import confirmation dialog parsed `usageAccessToken` and `usageUserId` from `ccswitch://` URLs and persisted them into `ProviderMeta.usage_script`, but never rendered them. A malicious or overbroad deeplink could smuggle credentials into the imported provider without the user seeing them before clicking **Import**.

### Fix

- Add both fields to the usage-script section of `DeepLinkImportDialog`:
  - `usageAccessToken` is masked (first 4 chars + `************`), consistent with `usageApiKey`.
  - `usageUserId` is shown in full with `break-all` so long identifiers are not truncated by CSS.
- New i18n keys added for `en`, `zh`, `zh-TW`, and `ja`.

### Verification

Regression test `renders masked usage access token and user id for provider imports` emits a `deeplink-import` event and asserts the dialog displays the masked token and the user id.

---

## 5. Codex `model_catalog_json` arbitrary file read

`resolve_cc_switch_catalog_path` in `src-tauri/src/codex_config.rs` resolved the `model_catalog_json` pointer from the live `~/.codex/config.toml`. It only verified that the file name equals `cc-switch-model-catalog.json`; if the value was an absolute path, it was returned verbatim without checking it lives under `~/.codex`.

That meant a user (or a malicious sync/profile import) could set:

```toml
model_catalog_json = "/tmp/secret/cc-switch-model-catalog.json"
```

and CC Switch would read the file during live-settings backfill and, when the proxy is running, serve it from `/v1/models`. Pointing it at a huge file also exhausted memory because both readers used `read_to_string` without a size cap.

### Fix

- Add `path_is_within(base, path)` in `config.rs` — a lexical containment check that normalizes paths without hitting the filesystem, so it is safe for non-existent paths and avoids symlink tricks.
- Treat Unix-style absolute paths (`/…`) as absolute even on Windows.
- Resolve relative paths under the Codex config directory, not directly to the generated filename.
- Cap catalog reads at **32 MiB** (`read_codex_model_catalog_text`).

### Verification

New regression tests:

- `resolve_catalog_rejects_absolute_path_outside_config_dir`
- `resolve_catalog_accepts_absolute_path_inside_config_dir`
- `resolve_catalog_rejects_traversal_to_parent_directory`
- `read_limited_string_rejects_oversized_file`

Reverting the containment check makes the first test fail.

---

## 6. Unbounded proxy response bodies / decompression bombs

The proxy's non-streaming and error paths collected upstream response bodies with `response.bytes().await` and, when `content-encoding` was present, fully decompressed them with no output limit. A malicious or misbehaving upstream could therefore send an arbitrarily large body, or a tiny gzip/zstd/br body that expands to gigabytes, and exhaust the backend's memory.

### Fix

- Add `ProxyResponse::bytes_with_limit(max_bytes)` that aborts collection when the accumulated body exceeds **128 MiB**.
- Use it in `read_decoded_body` for every non-streaming path.
- After decompression, reject payloads that exceed the same ceiling with the new `ProxyError::ResponseBodyTooLarge` variant.
- Map the new error into the Codex proxy error response builder so it is surfaced correctly to clients.

### Verification

New regression tests:

- `bytes_with_limit_rejects_oversized_buffered_response`
- `bytes_with_limit_rejects_oversized_streamed_response`

Reverting the limit makes both tests fail.

---

## 7. CI: replace `pnpm/action-setup` v6 with Corepack

`pnpm/action-setup` v6 no longer downloads the requested pnpm directly. It bootstraps the *latest* pnpm (11.7.0 at the time of writing) through an npm-driven self-installer, and only then downloads the pinned version (10.12.3) from the npm registry to "switch". That is three registry round-trips before any build step runs, and the second one is fragile: when the `@pnpm/linux-x64-10.12.3.tgz` fetch failed on a degraded runner network (`error (23)`, two retries), the self-installer still reported `done`, then crashed with `ENOENT ... @pnpm/linux-x64/packag

author: mgilbir
body:
Sweeps tension **T2 ("mutation-not-flagged")** across `xlsx/` in both
directions, fixes what it found, and leaves behind guards that fail on a *new*
omission rather than pinning today's set.

## Direction 1 — mutation without a flag

A full AST sweep of every exported pointer-receiver method in the package found
**no unflagged mutator beyond the documented exemptions**. C423's set (the
thirteen opaque-sheet feature mutators, `AddImage`/`AddChart`, plus `AddNote`,
`AddNoteRichText` and `SetPageMargins`) is genuinely closed by #237, and the
handle types (`Table`, `PivotTable`, `Slicer`, `Image`, `Hyperlink`,
`SparklineGroup`, `Comment`) all flag correctly. That is a finding, not a
silence: the guard below is what makes it checkable.

Three writers still assigned `Sheet.dirty` **directly** instead of going through
`markDirty`, bypassing the guard that keeps an opaque
(chartsheet/dialogsheet/macrosheet) sheet from ever being flagged — the exact
shape `AddImage`'s two raw assignments had:

- **`markCommentsDirty` (reachable, real)** — `Sheet.Comments` loads whatever
  comment parts the sheet's relationships name without an opaque check, so a
  `*Comment` handle from a chartsheet reaches `SetRichText`/`Reply`/`SetResolved`
  → `s.dirty = true`. The save path's sheet loops that decide whether to drop
  `calcChain.xml` and rebuild the workbook relationships do **not** re-check
  opaque, so `xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels` was rewritten for an edit that
  `saveOpenedSheetAttachments` then discards.
- **`saveOpenedSheetAttachments`** and **`copySheetImages`** — both already
  unreachable for an opaque sheet, but routed through `markDirty` so the
  invariant is absolute rather than "true by inspection of the caller".

## Direction 2 — flagging when nothing changed

- **`Workbook.Styles()`** marked styles dirty just to materialize the in-memory
  default stylesheet for a package that carries **no** styles part. A plain
  `wb.Styles().NamedStyles()` — a read — therefore grew `xl/styles.xml`, a
  content-type override and a workbook relationship in the saved file. Its own
  godoc promised "merely reading styles does not mark them dirty"; that only held
  when a styles part existed. Created workbooks are unaffected: `saveNew` writes
  `styles.xml` whenever `w.stylesheet` is non-nil, without consulting the flag.
- **`Cell.SetStyle`** and **`Cell.SetNamedStyle`** called `markSheetDirty()` on
  their *first line*, before validating. A rejected call (out-of-range text
  rotation or indent, negative number-format id, unknown style name) changed
  nothing yet dirtied the sheet, regenerating an untouched worksheet — and, once
  `dcterms:modified` is derived from these flags, stamping the file as edited.
  Both now flag through `SetStyleIndex` on the success path only.

## Guards

The strongest deliverable here is structural, not a table:

| Guard | Kind | Catches |
|---|---|---|
| `TestExportedMutatorsFlagState` | AST | an exported method that mutates durable state without reaching a regeneration flag |
| `TestSheetDirtyIsOnlySetByMarkDirty` | AST | any assignment to `.dirty` outside `markDirty` |
| `TestReadOnlyAccessorsPreserveEveryPart` | runtime, reflective | a read-shaped accessor that dirties anything |
| `TestSheetMutatorsPersistThroughSaveReopen` | runtime, table | a mutator whose edit is discarded at save |

`TestExportedMutatorsFlagState` builds the package call graph, taints locals
derived from `ws()`/`ensureWS()`/`ensureSheetView()`, and computes transitive
mutation and transitive flag reachability. Exceptions live in
`mutationFlagExempt` **with the reason each is correct** — the way
`captureExemptAttrs` does in `pptx/internal/oxml` — and a **stale** entry fails
the test too, so the list cannot rot:

- `Sheet.Cell` / `Sheet.CellByRowCol` — materializing accessors by design (C425);
  the phantom entries are dropped by the marshaler, and flagging would dirty a
  sheet that was only read.
- `Sheet.SetName` (C545), `SetVisibility`/`SetVisible`,
  `SetPrintArea`/`SetPrintTitles`/`ClearPrintArea`/`ClearPrintTitles`, and the
  `Workbook` defined-name / protection / `SetActiveSheet` / `SetForceFullCalc`
  setters — all write `workbook.xml`, which is regenerated from the model on
  every save. This is also why print areas legitimately persist on an opaque
  sheet, which `markDirty` refuses.
- `Workbook.SetCustomProperty` — `docProps/custom.xml` regeneration is derived by
  a snapshot diff, not a set flag.
- `Workbook.Styles` / `Workbook.Theme` — lazy materialization of a default model
  is a read; the theme editor carries its own `Modified()`.

`TestReadOnlyAccessorsPreserveEveryPart` invokes every exported read-shaped
method reflectively, so a newly added accessor is covered without anyone
extending a table. It is what reproduced the `Workbook.Styles` defect.

`TestSheetMutatorsPersistThroughSaveReopen` runs 21 mutators against an
**opened** workbook — the case where an unflagged mutator is silently discarded,
because a clean sheet round-trips from its preserved bytes — then saves,
reopens and asserts.

## Verification

Every fix has a test that fails before it and passes after, checked by copying
the pre-fix file in from `git show main:<path>` (no `git stash`: `refs/stash` is
shared across worktrees). Both AST guards were also proven against a temporary
newly-added mutator that forgets to flag, and against removing `markDirty` from
the existing `Sheet.SetTabColor` — which fails the AST guard *and* the runtime
persistence table, so neither is vacuous.

Byte-identity: both fixture packages round-trip part-identically as a baseline
assertion inside the new tests, and every new assertion is "the saved package is
unchanged". The net effect of this PR is strictly *less* flagging, so no
previously-preserved part starts regenerating.

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./... -count=1` and `make lint`
(0 issues) all pass. `xlsx` round-trip/fidelity suites and `spec/spectest` pass.

author: yc-0210
body:
Closes #5.

Completes the visitor interaction loop: selecting an Atom opens its detail panel, Connections are routes you can take — from the panel or by clicking the lit line in 3D — and an explicit exit returns the Sphere to its idle drift.

## Store (test-driven per ADR-0005)

- `selectViaConnection(connectionId)` follows a Connection out of the current selection to the Atom at its far end. Connections are undirected, so it arrives from either end. Unknown ids, Connections that don't touch the selection, and navigating with nothing selected are all no-ops.
- `selectedDetail()` gives the panel everything it renders: the selected Atom, plus each of its Connections paired with the Atom it leads to.
- Exit stays `clearSelection()` — camera framing is derived from the selection, not stored beside it.

Ten new tests at the store seam against the fake repository, driven red first. Mutation-checked: eight mutants across the far-end lookup, reachability guard, emphasis refresh and detail pairing — all killed, no survivors.

## Rendering (ADR-0004 → Owner-chosen directions)

Per ADR-0004, the panel/camera direction was chosen from three interactive prototypes (Dossier), and the Atom treatment from six (Lattice), before any of this production code was written.

- **`AtomDetailPanel`** — the Dossier: slides in from the right with label, hours, description and Connection rows (each with its own description and a Strength bar). DESIGN.md tokens throughout; bottom sheet on mobile. Rows call `selectViaConnection`; ✕ and Escape clear the selection.
- **Lattice Atoms** — solid core inside a slowly turning wireframe shell; the shell's curvature keeps Atoms reading as 3D at any zoom. Each shell turns at its own phase and tilt; `prefers-reduced-motion` parks them.
- **Clickable lit Connections** — highlighted lines get an invisible hit cylinder; dimmed lines get none, so stray clicks still clear the selection.
- **Camera rig** — each selection swings the Atom to face the visitor, shifted left to clear the panel, then *releases* on arrival or the moment the visitor grabs the controls — zooming and orbiting are never fought. Exit eases back to idle framing and auto-rotate resumes. Reduced motion cuts instead of sweeping.

## Verification

- 56 tests green; typecheck, lint and `next build` clean.
- Rendering layer (ADR-0005's manual-verification exemption) driven in a real browser against the production build with PostgREST mocked: select → panel contents → row navigation (Writing → Testing) → genuine 3D line click (Testing → Postgres) → exit via ✕ and via Escape, no console errors.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Selecting an Atom opens an overlay panel with label, description, time spent and Connections list (each row shows its own description)
- [x] Panel styled per DESIGN.md (surface, radius, typography tokens)
- [x] Clicking a highlighted Connection line in the 3D scene animates the camera to the linked Atom and selects it
- [x] Clicking a Connection row in the panel does the same
- [x] Explicit exit control clears the selection and returns the camera to the default idle auto-rotate state
- [x] Store tests cover select-via-connection and exit-clears-selection against the fake repository

body:
## What changed

- reject ambiguous update and delete operations when duplicate journal IDs exist
- reject stale edit snapshots and advance `savedAt` on successful edits
- preserve provenance on untouched structured fields
- distinguish same-kind edit actions and reset forms when another entry is selected
- correct historical-date wording

## Why

PR #148 restored the past-entry revisit flow, but post-merge Sol ultra review found
three data-integrity gaps: duplicate IDs could target or delete the wrong record,
an older open form could overwrite a newer edit, and an unrelated edit could promote
derived or unknown values to explicit analytical authority.

The previous `savedAt` preservation also contradicted the merged account release
gate. Sync uses `savedAt` for last-write-wins, so every successful edit must receive
a strictly newer value.

## User impact

Past entries still edit in place and return to the same date. The follow-up prevents
silent wrong-record mutation, stale overwrite, and provenance escalation. It does
not enable account sync, D9 authority, memo analysis, or training-plan authority.

author: fmeum
body:
`IgnoredSubdirectories#filterForDirectory` computed the directory's segments by splitting its path string on `"/"`. For the root directory the path string is empty, and `Splitter` yields a single empty string rather than no segments at all. `UnixGlob#canMatchChild` then matched that phantom empty segment against the first segment of each pattern, so every pattern whose first segment is not a wildcard was dropped.

Use `PathFragment#segments()` instead, matching what `matchingEntry()` already does.

Fixes #30526

author: phophaliakhushdeep0291-ux
body:
The dashboard showed "Value of gaps found: Rs 0" beside a CRITICAL 100 finding. The gap extractor only understood rules that state a `differenceRupees`-style number, but the rules that actually fire on real shops state theirs differently: "purchase did not increase stock" reports `amountRupees`, "cancelled sale did not restore stock" reports base-unit quantities. Neither was read, so both fell through to "not quantified" and the total collapsed to zero.

Teach DISCREPANCY_BY_RULE twelve more shapes, and draw an explicit line between money that went MISSING (counted) and paperwork that is missing (not counted). Folding unvouched-but-probably-fine spend into the headline would tell a shopkeeper that ordinary undocumented purchases had vanished; the evidence queue already tracks those, and the tile states how many findings carry no figure so the total never reads as "all of it".

Stock gaps are valued at cost, never selling price. Where a purchase states its own per-unit cost, that line wins over the product's running average: it needs no unit conversion and is what the shop actually paid.

Also fixed, found while verifying:

- `makeBill` never set `businessDate`, which defaults to now(). Any test bill built with a past `createdAt` therefore claimed to belong to today, so every rule that looks up "that day's closing" searched the wrong day and stayed silent. This was masking BILL_BACKDATED_INTO_LOCKED_DAY.
- The SQLite migration for `discrepancyPaise` was missing entirely. The schema declared a column no migration created, so a fresh dev clone would break. Verified by applying it to a database built from the pre-fix schema.

Verified against real accumulated shop data, where clean-shop fixtures had hidden the bug completely: the tile now reads Rs 408 (Rs 368 critical + Rs 40 high), nothing is left unquantified, no figure is negative, and the total stays below lifetime sales. A new regression test fails if any CRITICAL finding is ever persisted without a figure.

216 tests, 215 pass, 0 fail (1 pre-existing SQLite-concurrency skip).

author: jovinull
body:
Removes `/configure.py` from `.github/CODEOWNERS`, leaving `/.github/` and `/tools/`.

## Why

Every new translation unit adds an `Object` entry to `configure.py`. All seven pull requests in the #154 batch touched it, and so did both of #155 and #156. Owning the file therefore covered every decompilation pull request, which meant a contributor with write access could not merge any reconstruction without the package owner — the opposite of what granting write access is for.

## What is still owned

`/.github/` and `/tools/` remain owned, and that is where the exfiltration surface actually is: workflow files and the build post-processors that run inside the container holding the original game files. #155 adding `tools/fix_game_movie_object.py` is exactly the case the rule is meant to catch.

## The tradeoff, stated plainly

`configure.py` does execute in the build container, so a malicious change to it could read `/orig`. That risk is accepted rather than eliminated: in a decompilation pull request its diff is a few lines of build configuration, so an unexpected change there is visible to any reviewer reading it. `CONTRIBUTING.md` now says to read a `configure.py` change as build configuration rather than skim it as data.

The alternative — keeping the file owned — traded that residual risk for a review bottleneck on every unit, and made the write role effectively unable to close a decompilation pull request.

body:
## Diagnóstico

Investiguei o relato de itens que "não salvam" ao clicar em Salvar/Urgência/Finalizar Pedido no app Lojas, aba Pedido. Achei o bug real:

Ao sincronizar o pedido pro app Estoque (`_sincronizarComPedidos`), o código casava cada produto com a tabela `gn_catalogo` **só pelo nome em maiúsculas**. Qualquer diferença de texto — acento diferente, espaço a mais, uma quantidade editada no nome do produto — faz o item ser **descartado em silêncio**: ele fica salvo aqui no app Lojas (contagem, confirmação), mas nunca chega ao `gn_pedido_itens`/`gn_contagens_pedido` que o app Estoque lê. Nenhum erro aparece pro usuário — só se percebe quando falta mercadoria.

Confirmei isso comparando ao vivo os 332 produtos do Pedido com o catálogo: hoje já existem **2 itens fora de sincronia**:
- `Banana d´água` (Pedido) vs `Banana d'água` (catálogo) — apóstrofo diferente (´ vs ')
- `Cai-Cai cx c/ 32 pcts...` (Pedido) vs `Cai-Cai cx c/ 16 pcts...` (catálogo) — quantidade divergente

Esses itens especificamente estavam sendo perdidos toda vez que alguém pedia.

## Correção

- `gn_catalogo` já tem uma coluna `item_id` (o mesmo id numérico usado em `PRODUTOS_PEDIDO`) que **não estava sendo usada**. Passei o vínculo principal a usar esse id — imune a qualquer diferença de texto no nome. O nome continua como fallback só pra produtos que por acaso não tenham `item_id` preenchido no catálogo.
- **Segurança adicional**, pro caso de ainda assim aparecer um produto sem vínculo (ex.: produto novo cadastrado no Pedido mas esquecido no catálogo): agora isso **não passa mais em silêncio**.
  - Alerta bloqueante (precisa clicar OK) avisando exatamente quais itens não chegaram ao Estoque, pedindo pra avisar o financeiro/TI.
  - Registro em nova tabela `gn_pedido_sync_erros` (loja, itens, quem confirmou, quando) — dá pra consultar direto no banco quais lojas tiveram esse problema, sem depender de alguém reportar.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --check` no bloco `<script>` de `gn-lojas.html` — sem erros de sintaxe.
- [x] Comparei ao vivo os 332 produtos de `PRODUTOS_PEDIDO` com `gn_catalogo` (por nome) — achei e confirmei os 2 casos reais de divergência citados acima.
- [x] Confirmei que `gn_catalogo.item_id` bate exatamente com `PRODUTOS_PEDIDO[].item` nos casos testados (89, 90, 141, 297).
- [x] Migration aplicada: nova tabela `gn_pedido_sync_erros`.

author: njbrake
body:
## Description

Picks up the review follow-ups on #445 (the histogram-as-time-range-selector work) from @khaledosman and Copilot that landed unaddressed at merge. All are dashboard-only; no gateway API contract change.

### Khaled's comments

- **Activity "All" reintroduced the invisible-default bug.** With `range=all` the histogram sent no `start_date`, so the summary endpoint applied its 30-day default: the bars silently showed a rolling month while the caption read "All time", and you could not drag older. A new `resolveExtentWindow` now gives the histogram an explicit year-long start (deterministic, and the axis shows exactly what it covers), while the list stays genuinely all-time. This is Khaled's first suggested fix (explicit start for the histogram, list window captioned separately); "All" keeps its unbounded list.
- **Empty state counted the default window as a filter.** `anyFilter` used `hasWindow`, so a brand-new gateway on the 24h default read "No requests match these filters." It now mirrors UsagePage's `timeFiltered` (the default preset is not itself a filter), so an empty first load reads "No requests recorded yet."
- **`12mo` was exactly the server cap.** `366 * DAY_S` always exceeds `_MAX_SUMMARY_SPAN` by the client/server round-trip delta and gets pulled forward, so the preset never spanned a year. It now requests `365 * DAY_S`, which leaves headroom and never trips the clamp.
- **Thumb resync missed a rolling series.** The resync keyed on `[windowStart, windowEnd, n]`; it now also keys on the extent's first and last bucket, so a series that rolls forward with identical bounds and length no longer strands the thumbs.
- **Panning had no keyboard path.** The pan strip is now a single-value slider (the window's left edge) operable with arrows, Page Up/Down, Home, and End, so a keyboard user can reach a mid-extent window without stepping both edges in turn.

### Copilot's comments

- **Overview refresh state.** `refresh()` triggers `previous.refetch()`, but `isRefreshing` omitted `previous.isFetching`; it is now included, so the button cannot re-enable (and the spinner cannot stop) while that refetch is in flight.
- **Pan strip pointer-cancel.** `onPointerCancel` now releases pointer capture (when held), mirroring `onPointerUp`.
- **Filter-chip focus ring.** The remove control gets a `focus-visible` ring (also raised by CodeRabbit).
- **Locale-sensitive tests.** The timeline caption tests asserted on `"Jul"`, but the UI formats with `toLocaleDateString(undefined, ...)`. They now assert on day numbers and the UTC marker.

### Deliberately not changed

- **`useDisplayClock` `setInterval` (Copilot).** Kept. The frontend-standards rule targets manual data *polling* (use `refetchInterval`); this is a display-only clock that fetches nothing, already pauses while the tab is hidden, and only exists to keep the "updated Ns ago" label truthful. Removing it would freeze the label between refetches, making it misleading. Happy to revisit if reviewers disagree.

body: Industry artwork is now photographic wherever a photograph exists. The files themselves are **not in this branch and were not downloaded** — Unsplash and Pexels are blocked by this environment's egress policy. Ten photographs have been selected and the site is wired to use them; the owner downloads them by hand into `assets/images/stock/`. `STOCK-IMAGE-DOWNLOADS.md` has the source page, exact filename, dimensions, alt text, framing note and current status for each. ## How the fallback works `resolveImage()` in `src/lib/media.mjs` checks the filesystem at build time and picks the photograph if the `.webp` is there, the generated SVG illustration otherwise. A half-filled photo library renders as a mix; an empty one renders exactly as the site did before. **There is never a broken ``.** As of this branch all ten are missing, so every page currently renders its illustration — the diff to the generated HTML is almost entirely attribute reordering. Optional renditions follow the same rule: an `.avif` sibling gets a `` source and a `-900.webp` gets a `srcset` entry, but only once the file exists. Nothing references a file that is not on disk. ## Changes **Data** — each industry in `src/data/industries.mjs` gains `stockImage`, `stockImageAlt` and `stockSourceUrl` alongside its existing `art`/`artAlt`, which serves as the fallback illustration. The source URL is a licence record and is never rendered on the site. **Components** — new `picture()` primitive; `figure()` takes a resolved media object. `pageHero` accepts either a path or a media object, so all existing callers are unchanged. **Homepage** — the four flagship niches (tree, concrete, fence, landscaping) carry photography; the other six are compact text cards. A `--photo-filter` custom property is defined and left at `none`; the suggested `saturate(0.92) contrast(1.02)` is a one-line change once the real photographs can be seen. ## Testing - `npm run build`, `npm run check`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` — all pass. - Rendered in Chromium at 320, 390, 768, 820, 1280 and 1440 px, both with the photographs present (stand-in files, since deleted) and absent: no horizontal overflow, no broken images, no missing `alt` at any width. - No stock webpage URL appears as an image source; the checker now enforces this. ## Still required from the owner Download the ten photographs listed in `STOCK-IMAGE-DOWNLOADS.md` into `assets/images/stock/`, then run `npm run build`. author: junjosick
body:
An audit of the deterministic validators for language assumptions, prompted by the discovery that glossary extraction is English-only. Three of five validator families turned out language-neutral; two did not.

## Measured result

Replayed over the real store, **protected-span flags fall 265 → 172** — 93 fewer flagged pairs.

All 93 are cases where the numeric *value* was preserved and only the English suffix or surrounding prose was translated: `4th` → `4°`, `19-August` → `19 agosto`. Those were false positives.

That continues the recorded series **600 → 371 → 348 → 265 → 172**. Unlike the earlier rounds — which `validator-tooling.md` notes cut *volume* without improving precision — this one removes genuine false positives. Source-copy and marker counts are unchanged.

## Verdicts

| validator family | verdict |
| --- | --- |
| protected identity spans (URL, email, filename, anchor, citation, code) | language-neutral |
| inline marker structure | language-neutral |
| `target_language_gate` | language-dependent **and correct** |
| **protected numbers** | **broken — fixed** |
| source-copy / `translation_unchanged` | broken at boundaries — see below |

Month recognition now covers English, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, Danish, Norwegian, French and German. Numeric *value* equivalence still requires ASCII digits; that limitation is now documented rather than silent. A reference-text classifier that assumed ASCII numerals is also fixed.

## Two suppositions in the brief were wrong

Recorded so nobody re-derives them:

- **`target_language_gate` is not a general language gate.** It is exclusively the closed-vocabulary Toki Pona check. The `translation retains 99% of the source-language words` messages seen in replay output actually come from source-copy overlap, and **`replay_validation` misclassifies them as `other`** — a taxonomy bug in the example, left alone because examples were out of scope for this branch.
- **The Italian→Italian identity job is not close-pair evidence.** Its source and target languages match *and* its provider is `mock`, either of which disables source-copy validation entirely. The probe I suggested would have measured nothing.

## Deliberately unchanged

- **The 92% source-copy near-copy threshold.** Exact equality has no size threshold and near-copy detection is pair-blind, so a close pair (IT–ES, PT–ES, DA–NO) could plausibly misfire — but no such corpus exists here, and guessing a new threshold would be worse than the current behaviour. Documented as a known boundary instead.
- The Toki Pona gate, and the structural marker checks.

## Verification

`fmt` clean, `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` clean, **919 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored** over two runs. Replay is free — zero API calls.

author: sionic-khope
body:
## Feature Report

### What Changed

- Adds a receipt-bound memory lifecycle on top of Hermes: review-first capture, volatile/durable retention labels with expiry, report-first `prune`/`restore`/`correct` commands whose `--apply` now runs through a single store-owned transaction executor, and Hermes replay that injects only approved, fresh, metadata-only context.
- Ships **new**: `memory capture`, `memory evaluate`, `memory apply --batch`, `memory prune|restore|correct --apply`, `memory dream`, migration inventory/reactivate, batch stage/review/apply, dreaming reminders, and provider replay gating (`omh` provider 136 tests green).
- Introduces durable operation records (`memory_operation/v1`) with cumulative receipts, tombstones (`memory_tombstone/v1`), bounded metadata-only journals, and exact target-set receipts for every lifecycle mutation.
- Fixes the structural-key index collision so `record_id="records"` no longer drops unrelated index entries.

### Why This Exists

- Unreviewed, stale, or externally sourced memories must never silently enter later Hermes runs; destructive/local lifecycle operations need durable, resumable, receipt-bound semantics instead of prepared-only claims.
- Previously `memory restore|prune|correct` existed only as report-first surfaces; operators had no way to actually apply them with durable evidence.

### User / Operator Impact

- **Before:** memories entered silently, no retention labels, no receipts, prune not applyable, no working restore/correct CLI. **After:** `omh memory capture` lands in review only; `omh memory prune` shows a report and requires `--confirm-hard-delete-local`; every apply returns a receipt bounded to the exact target set; interrupted operations report truthfully (`operation_interrupted`) and resume exactly once; dreaming reminds but never consolidates.

### How It Works

- `src/commands/memory.py` parses and exposes the lifecycle CLI; `_cmd_memory_lifecycle` keeps report-first defaults and confirmation gates, then calls `execute_memory_lifecycle` on eligible plans.
- `src/workflows/memory_lifecycle_executor.py` translates every lifecycle mutation into `run_memory_operation` steps (`write_json`, `delete`, `rewrite_jsonl`, `move`) under the single store lock; no second lock engine, no model calls.
- `src/workflows/memory_store.py` enforces receipt shape, cumulative resume, terminal `failed` vs `interrupted` separation, and path/symlink/safe-token validation.
- Provider replay (`memory_provider.py` + `memory_block_replay.py`) injects only approved blocks, emits reminder-only dream reasons, and never mutates or issues network calls.

### Files And Contracts Touched

- 85 files (9,683 insertions, 1,226 deletions): new lifecycle/executor/store/governance/evaluation blocks, CLI parser + subcommands, replay/provider, docs, memory skill guidance, fixtures, and 10 new test modules.
- Key contracts: `project_memory_record/v2`, `project_memory_capture/v1`, `project_memory_review/v2`, `memory_operation/v1`, `memory_tombstone/v1`, `memory_lifecycle_receipt/v1`, dreaming reminder schemas.

## Validation

- [x] `uv run --group lint ruff check src tests`
- [x] `PYTHONPATH=tests uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests` (2577 tests OK, 1 skip)
- [x] `uv run python -m compileall src`
- [x] `uv run python -m omh.cli docs workflows --check`
- [ ] `python3 -m omh.cli harness validate` (not run — gate not in the standard suite path used for this work)
- [ ] `python3 -m omh.cli release checklist --json` (not run — release checklist not driven for this feature PR)
- [ ] `python3 -m omh.cli release hermes-smoke` (not run — live Hermes smoke is manual/operator-owned)
- [x] `omh --help` implicitly exercised through CLI subprocess coverage
- [ ] `omh ... release hermes-smoke --install-path setup ...` (not run — same reason as above)
- [x] Relevant workflow-learning review queue smoke (wrapper contract tests extended, 109 sessions tests green)
- [x] Relevant dry-run or smoke command: manual E2E CLI QA (prune confirm gate, restore tombstone block, interrupted truth, external-class rejection, 8-day volatile gate, dream report-only) run against isolated `/tmp` OMH_HOME/HERMES_HOME
- [x] Manual Hermes/TUI check: not run — provider is tested through the orchestration boundary (136 provider + 34 bridge unit/integration tests), not via a live Hermes TUI; verified through deterministic replay tests instead
- Plus: independent final verifier (`st_019fb270`) closed prior blockers live; digest/mount/AVB-style hash binding held across executor and store files (sha256 matched artifact, no drift)

## Risk

- **Broad blast radius:** 85 files, introduces durable operation state under `.omh/memory/` — operators with existing `.omh` state will see new `operations/`, `tombstones/`, `journals` directories appear on first lifecycle use.
- **Receipt semantics:** receipts prove OMH-local metadata outcomes only; they do not prove deletion, erasure, or provider/native changes outside the named target set. Callers must not present them as merge-readiness or deletion evidence beyond the scope recorded.
- **Interrupted operations:** transient vs permanent failures now split (`failed` vs `interrupted`); operators who relied on automatic resume for buggy manifest data will now see terminal `failed` instead and must fix input.

## Compatibility / Rollout

- Report-first CLI surface is additive; existing `memory sync|recall|dream` behavior is preserved and now has deterministic receipts for mutating paths.
- Existing `.omh` state is not migrated destructively; new store layout lands alongside old files.

## Release / Claims

- [x] Release-channel impact considered (`stable`, `preview`, or `local`) — introduces local durable state; no external first-class release channel behavior changed
- [x] Runtime/native capability claims are backed by evidence or marked as not observed — ALL lifecycle claims here are live-verified through subprocess CLI execution / independent verifier, not `prepared_not_observed`
- [x] Known manual Hermes checks are listed — live `omh release hermes-smoke --live` TUI checks not performed; replay behavior verified via deterministic provider tests instead

## Follow-Up

- Optional: add a runtime-lived smoke that ties `memory dream` output to a real Hermes session so reminder reasons can be observed end-to-end in a TUI soak.

The combined SDK only ever existed as an Actions artifact: it expires, and downloading it requires being logged in to GitHub. That is no way to ship an SDK people are meant to `swift sdk install`.

The `combined-swift-sdk` job now also publishes the tarball to a rolling **`swift-sdk-latest`** release, mirroring how `build-toolchain.yml` publishes its toolchain trees, so anyone can:

```sh
gh release download swift-sdk-latest --pattern 'swift-linux-swift-sdk.tar.gz.part*'
cat swift-linux-swift-sdk.tar.gz.part* | tar xzf -
swift sdk install swift-linux.artifactbundle
```

Details:

- **Split into parts** like the toolchain assets, because release assets cap at 2 GiB. This bundle compresses well below that today, so the split normally yields a single `.part00`; consumers concatenate either way, which keeps one documented command rather than two spellings of the same asset depending on size.
- **Old parts are deleted before upload**, so the release does not accumulate stale assets across nightly runs — same approach as the toolchain workflow.
- **Skipped on pull requests** (`if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'`), and the job gains `permissions: contents: write`.
- The **per-arch bundles stay Actions artifacts** — the combined one is what `swift sdk install` consumes, so it is the one worth publishing.

`docs/swift-sdk.md` gains the download recipe; it previously documented no way to obtain the bundle at all.

Verified locally that `split -b 1900M` followed by the documented `cat …part* | tar xzf -` restores the bundle intact, including the single-part case.

⚠️ **This workflow cannot currently run to completion**, for an unrelated reason: all four `App SDK` jobs fail at `Check out the ports external`. Master pins `ports` at `0e4feb9`, but `buildroot-ports`' master was force-pushed to `b968bb7`, orphaning that commit (`git fetch --dry-run` reports `+ 0e4feb9...b968bb7 master -> origin/master (forced update)`). Local checkouts still have it, so local builds are fine; CI cannot fetch an orphaned sha. Either push `0e4feb9` back to `buildroot-ports` or bump the submodule pointer to `b968bb7` — then this publishing step gets its first real exercise.

Adds CVEDIA-RT as an opt-in component.

## The wrinkle
CVEDIA's bootstrap (`get.cvedia.com`) presents **its own menu the tech steps through**. That can't run inside our non-interactive full-screen dashboard — the prompts would be hidden and it would hang.

## How it's wired in
- New `INSTALL_CVEDIA` env var (default `false`) and a menu prompt; shown in the plan card and one-line plan.
- After the dashboard phases finish, the installer **restores the screen and runs CVEDIA's bootstrap on the visible terminal**, with stdin wired to `/dev/tty` and our forced `DEBIAN_FRONTEND`/`needrestart` settings removed (via `env -u`), so its menu behaves exactly like the vendor's own `curl … | sudo bash`. Then it installs the `cvedia-rt` package non-interactively (`apt-get -y`, captured to the log).
- Reported in the summary; failures **warn, they don't abort**. In a no-terminal run it falls back to non-interactive and warns.

Runs the vendor's documented commands:
```bash
curl -fsSLo - http://get.cvedia.com | sudo bash
sudo apt install cvedia-rt -y
```

## Testing
`bash -n` passes. With stubs (a fake vendor bootstrap that reads a menu choice from the terminal + stubbed `apt-get`), verified the bootstrap runs interactively with `DEBIAN_FRONTEND` correctly unset, the package install is captured to the log, and the summary reports it. body: ## Was dieser PR macht Baut ein vollautonomes Multi-Agent-Content-System in FlowForge ein, das den neuen „Daily Channel“ der App selbstständig mit täglich frischem Trainings-Content versorgt, pflegt und aktualisiert – nach dem Vorbild produktiver Content-Ops-Systeme (spezialisierte Agents, strukturierte Übergaben, harte Qualitätsgates vor dem Publishing, Scheduler als Orchestrator). Zusätzlich enthält er einen **YouTube-Autopiloten**, der jede Edition als automatisch gerendertes Daily-Video hochlädt, sobald die API-Secrets hinterlegt sind. ## Architektur ``` GitHub Actions (Cron, täglich 05:17 UTC) │ Research → Draft → Editor (6 Qualitätsgates, sonst neuer Versuch, max. 5) │ freigegeben Maintenance (Archiv & Health) → Publisher (channel.json, Archiv, Log) │ YouTube-Publisher (optional, eigene Gates) ``` - **ResearchAgent:** Thema (5-Tage-Cooldown), Trend-Wörter, Flow-Technik, Beat-Richtung - **DraftAgent:** Tages-Challenge, 3 Wortpakete, Reimpaare, Starter-Bars, Zitat, Beat-Preset - **EditorAgent:** Gates für Vollständigkeit, Frische (Dedupe gegen Archiv), Lexikon, Silbendichte, Reimpaare, Wortpakete - **MaintenanceAgent:** Rolling-Window-Archiv (30 Editionen), Health-Report - **PublisherAgent:** einzige Schreibstelle; idempotent per Content-Hash, führt Lauf-Protokoll ## YouTube-Autopilot - **Beat-Synthese:** Rendert den Übungs-Beat der Edition als WAV (Kick-Sweep, Bandpass-Snare, Hi-Hat – gleiche Drum-Logik wie die WebAudio-Engine der App), deterministisch geseedet. - **Video-Render:** ffmpeg baut daraus ein 1080p-Video im FlowForge-Look mit Challenge, Zusatzregel und Beat-Infos (visuell verifiziert). - **Metadaten-Gate:** Titel-/Beschreibungs-/Tag-Limits und Lexikon-Check vor jedem Upload. - **Upload:** OAuth-Refresh + Resumable Upload über die YouTube Data API; idempotent über `content/youtube-log.json`. - **Graceful Skip:** Ohne Secrets wird der Schritt sauber übersprungen; `YOUTUBE_DRY_RUN=1` rendert alles ohne Upload. - **Einmal-Setup:** `deno task setup:youtube` führt durch den Google-Login und gibt die drei Secret-Werte fertig zum Kopieren aus (Anleitung im README). ## Frontend - Neues Panel **„3) Daily Channel“** in `index.html`: Challenge, Wortpakete (per Klick in den Trainer übernehmbar), Reimpaare, Starter-Bars, Flow-Tipp, Zitat, BPM-Übernahme. - Neues **Agent-Dashboard** (`agents.html`): Pipeline-Visualisierung, Channel-Health, Qualitätsgates, Lauf-Protokoll und YouTube-Upload-Liste. ## Automatisierung - `.github/workflows/content-agent.yml`: täglicher Cron (05:17 UTC) + `workflow_dispatch`, committet neue Editionen als `chore(agent): Channel-Edition YYYY-MM-DD` auf `main`; YouTube-Upload-Schritt nutzt die Secrets automatisch, sobald vorhanden. - Bestehende Deno-CI auf `setup-deno@v2` / Deno v2 aktualisiert. ## Verifikation - `deno lint`: sauber (19 Dateien) - `deno test -A`: 13/13 Tests grün (Gates, Pipeline-Idempotenz, Themen-Frische, WAV-Renderer, YouTube-Metadaten-Limits) - Pipeline lokal ausgeführt: Edition 2026-07-30 mit Score 99/100 veröffentlicht (liegt im PR) - YouTube-Publisher E2E im Dry-Run: 65,7 s Video (1080p, H.264 + AAC) gerendert, alle 4 Metadaten-Gates grün, Frame visuell geprüft - Skip-Pfad ohne Secrets verifiziert (Exit 0, klare Anleitung im Log) - Smoke-Test über lokalen File-Server: alle Seiten und JSON-Feeds liefern HTTP 200 [Frame des automatisch gerenderten Daily-Videos](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-4d1aa7f7-2727-4d24-b1e6-29d5b8cb11ad/artifacts?path=%2Ftmp%2Fframe.png) To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

author: qnox
body:
Stacked on #404 (base is that branch, so this PR shows only its own two commits).

A bridge is not a Kotlin declaration. It exists because the JVM dispatches on an
ERASED descriptor, so an override whose descriptor differs from the supertype's
is invisible through a supertype reference without a synthetic `ACC_BRIDGE`
method. Descriptors, erasure, accessor names and `@JvmName` mangling are JVM
realizations of a declaration — none of them belong in `ir_lower`, which is
shared with the JS backend and had grown to call `type_descriptor` and build
`getX`/`setX` names to decide what to emit.

All four bridge families now derive in a new `jvm::bridges` pass, step 2 of the
backend pass pipeline:

- superclass method bridges (a generic or covariant override),
- property accessor bridges, against a source and against a classpath supertype,
- mapped-interface bridges (a Kotlin member whose physical JVM name differs),
- interface bridges (an obligation from an implemented interface).

The whole bridge vocabulary moves with them: `bridge_erasure`,
`resolve_bridge_method`, `resolve_default_bridge_method`, `bridge_types_match`,
`bridge_param_narrows`, `bridge_return_admits`, `bridge_post_value_erasure`,
`collect_iface_methods`, `iface_method_is_default` and
`method_is_override_or_synthesized`. `ir_lower` shrinks by ~290 lines and no
longer mentions bridges at all.

Two things had to be added rather than relocated:

- `IrFile::fresh_method_decls` — a method declared WITHOUT `override`. The one
  language fact the IR was missing; a supertype's descriptor must not be pointed
  at a fresh same-named declaration, and lowering used to answer that by
  re-reading the AST. A synthesized method is deliberately absent from the set
  (matching the old predicate): both an override and a synthetic member can
  legitimately be a bridge target.
- `SkipReason::Bridges` — the two file-level bails these families carried are
  now JVM decisions and report through the existing pass-pipeline skip path: a
  bounded type-param erasure krusty cannot yet reproduce, and a `suspend`
  override whose bridge the coroutine pass would rewrite out from under.

Deriving after lowering also removes a declaration-order dependence: lowering
could only see a superclass whose own lowering had already run, while the pass
sees every class in the file.

### Verification

Full harness green. The box corpus passes — and earned its keep here:
`bridges/kt318.kt` and `bridges/test14.kt` caught a mis-transcribed erasure in
the first cut (`Unit` erased to `Lkotlin/Unit;` instead of `V`, so the bridge
silently failed to override the interface method and dispatch fell through to
the interface default). Neither the gate nor a type-check would have seen it;
only running the box did.

### Not in this PR

`Bridge` itself still lives in `src/ir.rs` as `IrClass::bridges`. Removing the
field means threading a side table from the pass through `value_classes` (which
retargets bridges once mangled names are known) to `ir_emit`, across every
caller of the shared pass pipeline, and deciding what to do with
`plugins::serialization`, which assigns `ser.bridges` directly for the
`KSerializer<Foo>` interface from shared (non-JVM) plugin code. That is a
mechanical but wide change and lands separately.

author: whitphx
body:
## Motivation

The `release` job has been failing on every push to `main` — most recently [run 30535460404](https://github.com/whitphx/anipres/actions/runs/30535460404/job/90848295356):

```
🦋  info anipres is being published because our local version (0.13.0) has not been published on npm
🦋  error 403 Forbidden - PUT https://registry.npmjs.org/anipres - You cannot publish over the previously published versions: 0.13.0.
🦋  error 403 Forbidden - PUT https://registry.npmjs.org/slidev-addon-anipres - ... 0.8.11.
```

Both versions have been on npm since 2026-05-11, so `changeset publish` should have skipped them entirely.

### Root cause

This is **not** caused by #485 — that PR left the `release` job byte-for-byte unchanged. It is a coincidence of timing: this was the first push to `main` since 2026-05-26, and the breakage landed in between.

[npm 12](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/using-npm/changelog) (released 2026-07-08) changed `npm info --json` to always return an array, even for a single package spec:

```console
$ npx -y npm@11 info anipres --json | jq type
"object"
$ npx -y npm@12 info anipres --json | jq type
"array"
```

The release job runs `npm install -g npm@latest` — required for npm trusted publishing (needs >= 11.5.1) — which now resolves to 12.x.

`@changesets/cli` 2.29.7 reads `pkgInfo.versions` straight off the parsed JSON. On an array that is `undefined`, so `publishedVersions` falls back to `[]`, every package is treated as unpublished, and `changeset publish` attempts to republish already-released versions.

For contrast, the last green release run (2026-05-26, same changesets version, npm 11) correctly logged:

```
🦋  warn anipres is not being published because version 0.13.0 is already published on npm
🦋  warn No unpublished projects to publish
```

Upstream: changesets/changesets#2164, fixed by changesets/changesets#2159, shipped in `@changesets/cli` 2.31.1.

## Key changes

- Bump `@changesets/cli` `^2.29.7` → `^2.31.1`. 2.31.1 adds `normalizeInfoJson()` (`Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed[0] : parsed`), which works under both npm 11 and npm 12.

No changeset is included — this is release tooling only, with no user-facing or API change.

### Note on lockfile size

The lockfile diff is larger than a one-line dep bump suggests. Two legitimate causes:

- pnpm 11 records `libc:` fields that the previously-committed (pnpm 10-era) lockfile lacks;
- the new subtree causes `debug`'s optional `supports-color` peer to resolve tree-wide, adding `(supports-color@10.2.2)` peer suffixes.

`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes and the supply-chain policy check is clean (1631 entries).

## Testing done

Verified the exact predicate that fails in CI, against real npm 12 output:

```
anipres@0.13.0              json=array  2.29.7 sees published=false  2.31.1 sees published=true
slidev-addon-anipres@0.8.11 json=array  2.29.7 sees published=false  2.31.1 sees published=true
```

Also run locally:

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` — clean, lockfile unmodified by install
- `pnpm --filter anipres test` — 21 passed (4 files)
- `pnpm --filter anipres lint` — clean
- `pnpm --filter anipres build` — succeeds

The release job itself only runs on pushes to `main`, so it cannot be exercised by this PR's CI; it will be validated when this merges.

author: matze4u
body:
## Scope changed — the guarded rules came out

This PR was a four-rule kernel-budget bundle. `check_safety_floor_untouched`
(CI, `rule-backstops`) forbids modifying `non-destructive-by-default`,
`commit-policy`, `scope-control`, and `verify-before-complete` per the Q3=A
locked decision (council Round 3, 2026-05-03). Three of them were in the bundle.

Lifting that lock is a maintainer decision, and editing the guard so its own PR
passes would be the worst available option. **The guarded edits are preserved
intact on `chore/kernel-floor-rules-parked` at `5fc0e278e`** and restore in one
merge if the lock is lifted.

## What this PR does now

| Rule | before | after | why it stands alone |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `no-cheap-questions` | 3,754 | **3,663** | was 35 chars over its recorded concentration ceiling (3,719) |
| `ask-when-uncertain` | 2,594 | **2,327** | `## Examples` pointer block; both targets stay reachable via `docs/catalog.md` |

Neither file is guarded. Both changes are telegraph-only or pointer-only —
every paragraph, list item, and fenced block retained.

### The concentration finding

`no-cheap-questions` had drifted 35 chars past its ceiling in
`KNOWN_CONCENTRATION_BREACHES`, and the drift was invisible: the check
short-circuits on the 12%-of-used-budget cap first, and at the then-current
budget of 31,496 that line sat at 3,779 — above the rule — so the ceiling test
was never reached. Shrinking the kernel bucket lowered the line to 3,542 and
exposed it. Worth noting as a property, not an incident: **bucket cuts and the
concentration cap pull against each other** — every reduction shrinks the
denominator and tightens each per-rule percentage line.

## What this PR no longer does

It does not close the kernel bucket. That stays at **27,521 / 26,000**, with
`non-destructive-by-default` (4,770 / 4,000) and `verify-before-complete`
(2,865 / 2,500) over their per-rule caps. Both are guarded files, so no edit
outside the guard's scope can fix them.

Context for whoever picks this up: `lint-rule-budget` runs **only in local
`task ci`, in no workflow**, while `check_safety_floor_untouched` is
CI-enforced. The original bundle therefore traded a CI-enforced safety lock for
a local-only gate. The open decision is a cap revision or a lock lift — both
decisions, not edits.

## Verification

`check-always-budget` · `check-condensation` · `check-refs` ·
`check_iron_law_prominence` · `check_safety_floor_untouched` — all pass locally.

author: nuna
body:
M5 H6 の Step 143〜151。コーパス拡張と gem 検証を道具化し、その道具が見つけた
rubycc 側のギャップを 5 つ潰して、**nkf 0.3.0 を新規に検証済みとして記録**しました。

## 道具づくり(Step 143〜145)

- **`tools/scan_popular_gems.rb`**(Step 143) — 人気ランキングから C 拡張を持つ gem を
  機械的に洗い出す。R10 の判定は `test/corpus/census.rb` に委譲して再実装しない。
  R10 が原理的に見ない**アセンブラ要否**だけスキャナ側で 2 系統検査し(`.S`/`.s` 走査 +
  `$objs` の未対応エントリ)、`[1b]`「要確認」に分類する。実走で bcrypt が
  「追加候補」として報告されたのがこの検査を足した理由。
- **`tools/verify_gem_tests.rb`**(Step 144) — `RUBYCC=1 gem install` → rubycc が
  使われた痕跡の確認 → 上流タグの取得と `.so` 差し込み → gem 自身のテスト実走 →
  `--update` で `data/verified_gems.json` へ。
  **`sanity` 式が必須**で、これがこのツールの本体。racc の `cparse.so` を壊しても
  スイートは 71 tests / 0 failures / 100% passed になることを実測しており、
  sanity が無ければ虚偽の「検証済み」記録が書かれる。
  既存 6 件を全て再現して自身を検証済み。
- **スキル `corpus-expansion`**(Step 145) — 道具の使い方ではなく道具の間をつなぐ判断
  (ヘッダギャップの仕分け、(d) レベルの証拠の水準、sanity 式の選び方、横断規約)。

## ギャップの特定と修正(Step 146〜150)

stackprof / nkf の検証は両方 FAIL したが、**先にホスト gcc で対照を取って環境要因を
否定**し(stackprof 31 runs、nkf 8 tests がどちらも完走)、原因を rubycc 側の
6 ギャップに確定させた。うち 5 つを修正:

| # | ギャップ | 対応 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `sigset_t` を `signal.h` と `sys/select.h` が別ガード・別型で二重定義 | Step 147。**ruby.h と `<signal.h>` を併用する任意の gem** が踏む |
| 2 | `sizeof(式)` が enumerator・ビットフィールド幅・case ラベル・配列デシグネータで整数定数式に畳めない | Step 148。機能の欠落ではなく**配線漏れ**(リゾルバは既に存在) |
| 3 | `pthread_kill` / `pthread_atfork` 未宣言 | Step 149 |
| 4 | `_POSIX_MONOTONIC_CLOCK` 不在 | Step 149。**実測値は 0** |
| 5 | 不完全配列型の補完が `conflicting types` | Step 150。`Type.composite`(C11 6.2.7p3)を新設 |
| 6 | `__dso_handle` を供給できない(`libc_nonshared.a` 経由の text relocation) | **未着手**。リンカの構造的な穴で別途設計が必要 |

## 結果(Step 151)

**nkf 0.3.0 が PASS し、`data/verified_gems.json` が 6 → 7 件**。
この経路で初めて新規に検証・記録された gem で、手編集は 1 文字もしていない
(`--update --step 151` のみ)。差分は nkf のエントリ 8 行だけで、
既存 6 件の行は 1 行も動いていない。

stackprof はギャップ 6 番だけが残り、失敗は**コンパイル段階からリンク段階へ移った**。

## テスト

`2,564 → 2,585 runs / 7,171 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors / 47 skips`

追加した検証の性格:
- ABI ハーネスに `also:` を使って**両方の include 順**のケースを追加(1 Spec = 1 ヘッダ
  では通ってしまう種類の欠陥だったため)
- Step 147・148・150 はいずれも `git stash` で**修正前に落ちることの対照**を取っている
  (テストが元の欠陥を捉えていることの確認)
- 実行オラクルは gcc 差分。Step 150 は `sizeof` を印字させて、合成型が完全なほうに
  なっていることを実際に確かめている

## 記録した既知の負債

- `test/corpus/gems.rb` の 4 エントリ(bigdecimal・date・racc・redcarpet)が
  `version: nil` = 最新追従で、上流のリリースだけで週次 CI の census ジョブが赤くなる。
  `verified_gems.json` 側は厳密に固定しているため食い違いうる
- racc の assertions が既存記録の 319 に対して実測 320。仮説を 5 つ潰したが原因未特定の
  ため DB は書き換えず、次回 `--update` で両測定が日付付きで並ぶのに任せている
- `extern int tbl[3]; int tbl[] = {1,2};` は gcc が受理するが rubycc は
  `conflicting types` のまま(nkf は逆順を使うため今回は未対応)
