author: ivantit66
body:
Три проблемы, о которых сообщил пользователь: exe не смог скачать ни GigaAM, ни Whisper («хотя huggingface доступен»), а после запуска из исходников транскрибация двухчасового видео шла полтора часа при 20% загрузки 12-ядерного процессора.

## 1. Whisper использовал 4 потока на любом железе

`WhisperModel` создавался без `cpu_threads`, а дефолт CTranslate2 при `cpu_threads=0` — ровно 4 потока независимо от числа ядер (`faster_whisper/transcribe.py:652`, дальше уходит в `intra_threads`). Отсюда и 20% на 12 ядрах, и время транскрибации втрое больше необходимого.

Теперь по числу ядер, с ручным потолком через `asr.whisper.cpu_threads` (`0` = авто). Смена значения сбрасывает загруженную модель — как `set_model_size`, потому что это тоже параметр конструктора.

## 2. Модели не скачивались за корпоративным TLS-прокси

`huggingface_hub` 1.x работает через httpx, а httpx по умолчанию доверяет только certifi и игнорирует хранилище сертификатов ОС. На машине с прокси, подменяющим сертификаты, корневой сертификат лежит в хранилище Windows — браузер HuggingFace открывает, а приложение падает на скачивании.

Добавлен `truststore`, инжектится в самом начале `main.py` (и в `backend/__main__.py` для запуска без окна) — до создания любых SSL-контекстов. Прежняя ветка с certifi для macOS осталась запасным путём.

Побочно это выравнивает поведение двух движков: GigaAM качается через `urllib`, который на Windows системное хранилище и так использовал, а HF-загрузки — нет.

## 3. В UI улетал голый `str(exc)`

По такому тексту невозможно отличить «нет интернета» от «заблокирован конкретный хост», особенно удалённо, в переписке с пользователем. Теперь ошибка называет хост и причину: блокировка, таймаут, HTTP-код, подмена сертификата.

Существенно, что **хостов два**, и они не связаны:

| Что | Откуда |
|---|---|
| веса GigaAM | `cdn.chatwm.opensmodel.sberdevices.ru` |
| KenLM (T-one), Whisper | `huggingface.co` |

Веса GigaAM лежат на CDN Сбера (`gigaam/__init__.py`, `_URL_DIR`), поэтому «huggingface доступен» про них не говорит ничего — раньше из текста ошибки это было не видно.

Несетевые сбои (нехватка памяти, битые веса) намеренно **не** переклассифицируются: `describe_download_error` возвращает `None`, и наверх уходит исходное сообщение.

## Проверено

- `tests/test_asr_errors.py` — 7 тестов на классификацию, включая обёрнутые исключения, httpx-стиль с кодом в `.response` и отказ выдавать `MemoryError` за сетевую ошибку. `tests/test_tts.py` — без регрессий.
- `truststore.inject_into_ssl()` не ломает существующие пути: httpx к HF, `urllib` к CDN Сбера и `HfApi` после инжекта отвечают как раньше.
- Настройки читаются, `cpu_threads` доезжает до движка, `backend.main` импортируется.
- Полная загрузка модели Whisper на живом железе не проверялась — канал на машине сборки даёт 0.1 МиБ/с. Передача `cpu_threads` в CTranslate2 подтверждена по исходникам faster-whisper, не прогоном.
- В `build.ps1` добавлен `truststore` в `hiddenimports`; exe после этих правок не пересобирался.

author: ozykhan
body:
## Description

Adds an `AGENTS.md` at the repository root — a short, machine-readable entry point for coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex, Aider) — and cross-references its central rule from `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

The primary rule, stated first in the file: commits and pull request descriptions must not carry AI generated or co-authored trailers. Such tags create legal and licensing gray areas, and `Signed-off-by` is a DCO certification that only a person can make.

**Component:** Build/CI (documentation)

**Type of Change:**
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Performance optimization (no change in behavior, improved speed/memory)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, code cleanup)
- [x] Build / CI / Documentation

---

## Related Issue

Closes #19

---

## Technical Deep Dive & Context

No code is touched. Two files change: a new `AGENTS.md` (156 lines) and three added lines in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

**Why a separate file rather than more of `CONTRIBUTING.md`.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` is written for humans and runs 238 lines. The failures this addresses — unsigned commits, AI trailers, wrong commit scopes, hot-path allocations, missing file block headers, speculative scope — happen precisely because that information is one hop away from where an agent is working. A pointer to a long document does not fix a problem caused by agents not reading a long document.

**What is duplicated, and why that is bounded.** `AGENTS.md` restates only rules that are short, mechanical, and checkable: `git commit -s`, the Conventional Commits format and scope list, `task check` before committing, the block-header shape. Everything narrative — architecture reasoning, benchmark methodology, the PR process — is linked, not copied. The duplicated facts change rarely, and the new `CONTRIBUTING.md` pointer means anyone editing either file learns the other exists.

**Alternatives considered.** A thin pointer file with no duplication was rejected: zero drift risk, but it documents a policy without changing behaviour. Inverting the relationship — making `AGENTS.md` canonical and having `CONTRIBUTING.md` link to it — was rejected as restructuring a maintainer-owned document well beyond the scope of issue #19. Per-tool files (`CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules`) were rejected because N copies of the same rules drift apart immediately; `AGENTS.md` is the cross-tool convention and one file serves all of them.

**Section order is deliberate.** Agents skim top-down, so the most-violated rules come first and the reasoning last: attribution and commits, then pre-commit checks, then codebase rules, then the coding principles, then a table of where to look.

**One inconsistency surfaced but not fixed.** `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s block-header template shows line 2 as the literal string `Tellstone Cloud-Native In-Memory Database`, while every real file uses a component title (`Tellstone Request Router`, `Tellstone Redis-Compatible Wire Protocol`). `AGENTS.md` tells agents to copy a neighbouring file in the same package rather than the template. I have left the `CONTRIBUTING.md` template alone — it is outside the scope of this issue, and I would rather flag it than change it unasked. Happy to fix it here or in a separate PR, whichever you prefer.

`internal/protocol` is deliberately absent from the list of allocation-free packages, since `ARCHITECTURE.md` describes it as the experimental frontend path rather than the hot path. Say the word if it belongs there.

---

## Performance & Benchmarks (If Applicable)

No measurable change — documentation only, no code paths touched.

---

## How Has This Been Tested?

No tests were added: the change is two Markdown files and adds no code to test. Verification focused on the failure modes that actually apply to a docs change — factual accuracy and self-consistency.

- `go vet ./...` — exit 0.
- `go test -race ./...` — exit 0, 14 packages ok, no FAIL, panic, or DATA RACE.
- Every path, file, and `task` target referenced in `AGENTS.md` was checked to exist mechanically rather than by eye: the five `internal/` packages, the five linked documents, and `task check` / `task fmt`. The stated non-`task` equivalents were read out of `Taskfile.yml` (`check` is `deps: [vet, test:race]`, `fmt` is `go fmt ./...`) rather than assumed.
- Prose is hard-wrapped to match the surrounding docs; no line exceeds 95 columns.
- The commit for this PR complies with the rules the PR adds: 37-character Conventional Commits subject, `Signed-off-by` present, no AI trailer. A commit that violated `AGENTS.md` while adding `AGENTS.md` would be self-refuting.

---

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the existing code style of this project
- [ ] I have added tests that prove my fix/feature works — not applicable, documentation only
- [x] New and existing tests pass locally (`go test ./...` and `go test -race ./...`)
- [x] I have updated the documentation (README, comments, or any relevant docs)
- [x] My changes generate no new `go vet` warnings
- [x] Any breaking changes are documented and communicated — none

author: lsjfy-open-com
body:
## What changed

- add a continuous namespace-scoped supervisor that correlates InferNexService status, managed workloads, Pods, and related Kubernetes Events
- add optional cached advisory analysis through an internal OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint
- add a self-contained read-only Web dashboard and JSON snapshot API on port 8081
- add a control-plane/master-node Helm profile that exposes only the dashboard through NodePort 30081
- add deterministic double-opt-in recovery that creates only a distinct InferNexService from an operator-approved InferNexServiceConfig after consecutive critical scans
- add a container/Helm offline Bundle with content checksums, image import, idempotent installation, and post-install verification
- add a static-binary host Bundle for openEuler amd64/arm64 management and bootstrap nodes
- add a dedicated least-privilege kubeconfig bootstrap, hardened non-root systemd install, health/RBAC verification, update rollback copy, and guarded uninstall
- add CI packaging plus manual/PR multi-architecture amd64/arm64 bundle workflows

## Host and existing-cluster impact

The Agent already supported an explicit external kubeconfig. The new host mode productionizes that path: the Agent runs outside Kubernetes on a fixed master/bootstrap server while using the same observer, supervisor, catalog and recovery boundaries against the apiserver. It does not gain SSH, shell, raw YAML, direct node access, CANN/NPU access, or a second serving reconciler.

A one-time administrator action creates a dedicated ServiceAccount and namespace Roles. The long-running systemd service never uses `admin.conf`; it receives a self-contained, 0600 kubeconfig with only the required namespace verbs. The service runs as an unprivileged user with no capabilities, NoNewPrivileges, protected kernel/system paths, and loopback-only MCP/dashboard defaults. Optional model API keys are read from a separate 0600 credential file, not the unit or process environment.

The host binary is CGO-disabled and statically linked, so openEuler compatibility is determined by CPU architecture (`x86_64` -> amd64, `aarch64` -> arm64), not by the A2 accelerator model or glibc version.

## Offline boundary

The container bundle contains only the Agent image, Agent chart, scripts, checksums, and secret-free values. The host bundle contains only the static binary, systemd/bootstrap tools, checksums, documentation, and license. Neither bundle reinstalls InferNex Bridge, gateways, NPU drivers/firmware, model weights, or inference workloads.

## Safety

The default remains namespace-scoped and observation-only. MCP is not externally exposed by default. Auto-recovery is disabled by default and requires controller, source-service, exact profile, approval-label and repeated-evidence gates. It does not overwrite/delete the source, switch traffic, create configs, or accept model-generated YAML.

## Validation

Local:

- `go test ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- Bash syntax for every container and host offline script
- Helm 4.2 lint/render
- native linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 static cross-compilation
- host Bundle assembly, extraction, internal SHA256 verification, and amd64 execution

GitHub CI:

- Linux race tests and Helm render matrices
- real Kind MCP/dashboard smoke test and tiny-model chat completion
- container Bundle creation and reinstall using only that Bundle
- dedicated ServiceAccount/kubeconfig creation
- real host systemd install outside Kind, Kubernetes API/RBAC checks against Kind, MCP/dashboard checks, unit verification, and uninstall
- independent amd64/arm64 container and host Bundle builds and checksums

Successful runs upload both container and host bundles. A prerelease is created only by an explicit workflow-dispatch choice.
## Product operations

Model analysis is now an optional managed lifecycle instead of an install-only argument set. Host installs use `/etc/infernex-agent/agent.conf` for non-secret effective arguments and a separate `0600` API-key file. The installed `configure-model.sh` command can show, test, enable, replace, rotate, or disable the model without reinstalling. Re-running the binary installer preserves model configuration when no replacement model flags are provided, restarts an existing service, and retains the previous binary for rollback.

The systemd CI contract covers no-model startup, a real OpenAI-compatible chat-completions test, API-key isolation, service restart, upgrade preservation, disabling the model, and continued health/RBAC access.

## Product documentation

The repository and both offline bundle types now include a product guide, product design and failure semantics, a model configuration manual, security/capability boundaries, and an operations runbook. The guides distinguish required bootstrap configuration from optional post-install model configuration and provide an `aarch64`/`linux-arm64` acceptance path.
## Transactional change safety

- persist a change journal before every Agent-created deployment or recovery resource
- assign a unique `agent.infernex.io/change-id`, expose redacted status through MCP/dashboard, and resume unfinished monitoring after process restart
- require `Ready` with the current `observedGeneration`; automatically roll back exact Agent-owned resources on `Degraded` or readiness timeout without overwriting unrelated operator drift
- capture SHA256-protected pre-install cluster and host recovery points before host installation, preserve them under `/var/lib/infernex-agent/backups`, and restore files, credentials, unit state and Agent-managed cluster source objects on install failure
- provide `cluster-state backup|verify|restore` and an explicit `restore-host-install.sh --confirm` recovery path
- preserve state on normal uninstall unless `--purge-state` is explicitly supplied; support optional persistent Agent state in Helm

## Rollback validation

The latest CI executes the safety contract rather than only rendering manifests: it deploys a real tiny OpenAI-compatible model, confirms inference, injects a `Degraded` status into a new deployment, verifies automatic rollback to pre-create absence, reinstalls from the offline bundle, then restores a previous host/model/systemd state from the pre-install recovery point.

Latest successful validation:

- [Kind, tiny model, injected failure rollback, offline reinstall and full host restore](https://github.com/lsjfy-open-com/infernex-agent/actions/runs/30603192847)
- [amd64 and arm64 offline product bundles](https://github.com/lsjfy-open-com/infernex-agent/actions/runs/30603192846)
- [RC4 rollback-safe product bundles](https://github.com/lsjfy-open-com/infernex-agent/releases/tag/infernex-agent-offline-v0.3.0-rc.4)

author: agentfleets
body:
## Motivation

User-approved redesign: **the dock IS the companion.** The app-level assistant dock (kimi web) and the per-surface `AgentCompanion` panels (Read's aside + reader tab, Author's aside) were two homes for "talk to an agent" — the companion even duplicated the dock's panel shape. This unifies them: the assistant dock becomes a **tabbed** panel — `kimi web` | `Companion` — hosting the ONE `AgentCompanion`, and the per-surface mounts retire. The kimi-web lifecycle (daemon hold, detach/attach, confirmed close) is untouched and stays scoped to the kimi tab.

This is also the `SurfaceContext` contract the design review asked for (`docs/discussions/desktop-design-review.md` §4): surfaces declare "what am I looking at" + "what can you insert" through a small registry instead of hand-rolled per-mount props.

## Design

**1. Tabbed dock.** `state/assistant.ts` gains `view: 'kimi' | 'companion'`, persisted like `dockSide` (`termipod.assistant.view`). `AssistantDock.tsx`'s header leads with a segmented tab strip (the existing `.seg`/`.seg-btn` idiom). The body renders BOTH the kimi `WebPanel` and one `AgentCompanion`, each CSS-hidden by `view` (visibility, never unmounted once `started` — the webview white-screen hazard applies, so no `display:none`). Detach/attach, the placeholder, and the confirmed close behave exactly as before, on the kimi tab only; the Companion tab stays usable while kimi is detached.

**2. Context-provider registry** — new `state/companionContext.ts` (zustand). Surfaces register `{ label, build, insert? }` keyed by job; registration marks the job most-recently-focused (a simple focus-order stack), unregistration removes it. The dock companion reads the ACTIVE provider for its context chip + `onInsert`.
- **ReadSurface** registers the selected paper: label = title, build = the Paper/Authors/Year/Abstract block the aside passed, insert = append to the ref's notes.
- **AuthorSurface** registers the active document: the exact three-branch build() the aside passed (markdown draft / figure spec / other-kind one-liner), insert = append into the markdown draft, or replace the figure body with the unfenced reply (today's semantics preserved for both kinds; structured bodies register no insert).
- Focus-tracking approximation (sanctioned by the design): Read/Author have no focus event, so a surface registers on mount + selection/active-document change and unregisters on unmount/no-context. `build`/`insert` read their stores LIVE at call time, so registration only refires on label-affecting changes, not per keystroke.

**3. Dock companion instance.** `storageKey: 'termipod.dock.agent'` with a one-time, read-only fallback to the retired mounts' keys (`termipod.read.agent`, then `termipod.author.agent`) so existing agent bindings survive — `state/companionBinding.ts`. Everything else the component already does (agent picker, hub/local toggle, @-mention, annotate button, D2.1 annotationTargets self-registration, image handoff) is unchanged.

**4. Retired.** The Read aside + embedded reader `assistant` tab, the Author aside, both "✦ Assistant" toolbar buttons, `showAgent`/`agentW` state + resize handles, dead CSS (`.read-agent`, `.author-agent`, `.ref-assistant-body`), and the `author.assistant` / `author.assistantHint` / `read.tabAssistant` i18n keys (en+zh). New keys: `assistant.tabKimi`, `assistant.tabCompanion` (en+zh).

**5. Amendment — kimi attach availability + reveal.** The annotation target row's kimi availability moves from `open && !detached` to `started && !detached` (guest mounted = attachable — a hidden dock's guest never unmounts). On a successful kimi attach — injected OR clipboard fallback — the dock auto-opens on the kimi tab (`reveal('kimi')`) so the user lands in kimi's composer to review and send.

**6. Amendment — dock steps aside during selection.** While the overlay is armed (any origin: companion compose button, status-bar chip, palette, hotkey — all funnel through `arm()`), the dock hides via an `annotating` CSS class driven by `dockHiddenForPhase(phase)` — `open` is never flipped, so Esc/cancel restores it exactly as it was, and it stays out of the captured pixels. On target pick the dock returns revealed: kimi tab after a kimi attach, Companion tab after a companion handoff — including the compose-box-armed case (the dock companion's own annotate button).

**7. Handoff reveal.** `handOffToCompanion` reveals the dock on the Companion tab when the handoff targets the dock companion's key (`handoffRevealsDock`) — and since `reveal` sets `started`, this also mounts the dock+companion on a never-opened dock, so the crop chip has somewhere to land.

The pure decisions (dock-hide flag, handoff routing, reveal predicate) live in bridge-free `state/annotationTargets.ts` per the established pattern (the store imports the shell bridge, which node ESM can't resolve).

## Tests

- New unit (`node --test`, desktop): `assistant.test.ts` (view persistence/switching, `reveal`, `kimiAttachable` truth table), `companionContext.test.ts` (register/replace/focus-order/unregister/insert passthrough), `companionBinding.test.ts` (the dock-key fallback migration incl. priority + non-dock no-fallback), `annotation.test.ts` (annotating-hide flag, handoff routing/reveal contract). `annotationTargets.test.ts` fixtures moved off the retired storage keys.
- E2E (`desktop/electron/e2e/annotation.spec.ts`): the D2 test now opens the dock from the status-bar chip and drives the Companion tab (the old flow clicked the retired "✦ Assistant" button); both tests additionally assert the dock hides while armed and reveals on the Companion tab after the handoff. CI is the e2e gate; the spec stays hermetic (TERMIPOD_E2E, throwaway user-data-dir + workspace).

author: olebhansen
body:
Denne endringen ble pushet til `docker/enkeltcontainer` etter at #3 allerede var merget, så den ble aldri med i master. Master har derfor fortsatt Debian-varianten med **323 kjente sårbarheter**. Dette er samme commit, cherry-picket rent på gjeldende master.

## Hvorfor

Trivy-skanning av Debian-varianten ga 323 sårbarheter (18 kritiske, 43 høye), og **ingen av dem hadde en tilgjengelig fiks** — Debian har merket dem `will_not_fix`/`fix_deferred`, så `apt-get upgrade` gjør ingenting. Eneste virkemiddel er å ha mindre i imaget.

Det aller meste kom fra **perl** (32 høye/kritiske fordelt på fire pakker, dratt inn som avhengighet av `postgresql-15`) og **curl/libcurl** (10). Alpine trenger ingen av dem: postgres har ingen perl-avhengighet der, og busybox' `wget` dekker helsesjekken.

| Base | Kritisk | Høy | Totalt | Størrelse |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aspnet:8.0-bookworm-slim` (master i dag) | 18 | 43 | 323 | 816 MB |
| `aspnet:8.0-alpine` | 0 | 0 | **0** | **339 MB** |

Målt på nytt mot gjeldende master: **null funn**. Da jeg målte første gang gjensto ett — `CVE-2026-54570`, mXSS i AngleSharp 0.17.1 via HtmlSanitizer — og den er borte nå fordi #1 er merget og bumper HtmlSanitizer til 9.1.973 (AngleSharp 1.6.0).

Alpine er dessuten samme base som Altinn-app-malen bruker.

## Følgeendringer

- **postgresql16** i stedet for 15 (eldste major i Alpine 3.23). Compose og testene står fortsatt på 15; skjemaet bruker ingenting som skiller de to, og jsonb, GIN-fulltekst, partial unique index og check-constraints er verifisert kjørende på 16.
- **su-exec** i stedet for `setpriv`, som ikke finnes på Alpine. `start.sh` velger nå automatisk mellom de to, så skriptet virker på begge baser.
- **icu-libs** + `DOTNET_SYSTEM_GLOBALIZATION_INVARIANT=false` — uten dette faller .NET tilbake til invariant kultur på Alpine, som gir feil sortering og formatering av norsk tekst.

## Verifisert

Bygget og kjørt fra Dockerfilen i denne branchen: healthy etter ~20 s, `/helse` OK, SPA-fallback 200 `text/html`, 1087 rader i `rettskilde_noder`, tom `listen_addresses`, dotnet som uid 10001, `docker stop` på 0,9 s med exit 0.

author: rengo
body:
Slice 5a of sixteen — plan #17, slices so far #18–#26. **543 review lines, `size:exception`** — the
chain's first, argued below.

Four ordered steps: an explicit path, `$NOOMA_VAULT`, an **upward search** from the working directory,
and `~/.nooma`.

## The ascent took three revisions, and the last two both looked correct

**Inherited from doc 01**: "a vault next to the executable". No conventional CLI resolves *data*
relative to `argv[0]`, and `os.Executable` returns the **resolved** path — so a symlinked install would
search a directory the user never typed. Also a silent-wrong-vault generator: a contributor's throwaway
vault beside the `go build` output becomes the default during development.

**First replacement**: check the working directory and its immediate children. Perfectly
self-consistent. Then an ordinary action broke it — `cd pablo.nooma/attachments && nooma status` finds
nothing there, falls through to `~/.nooma`, and **opens a different vault in silence**.

**Now**: ascend to the filesystem root, git-style. `TestResolveAscendsFromTheWorkingDirectory` drives
the vault itself, one level in, two levels in, and the parent — all resolving to the same vault, with a
different one sitting in `~/.nooma` to catch a fall-through.

## `environment` has no `executable` member, on purpose

R6.6 forbids consulting the binary's directory. The surest way to guarantee that is to leave the
resolver no way to ask.

## The binary never chooses

| Candidates | Behavior |
|---|---|
| one | it is the vault |
| none | error naming the directory searched, pointing at `nooma init` |
| two or more | error listing every one, showing the disambiguating command |

Opening the wrong brain is the worst failure this component can produce, and picking the alphabetically
first match would make it silent.

## Two exclusions, both narrower than they look

**Only directories count.** A stray file named `decoy.nooma` is not an ambiguity a user should have to
resolve.

**The literal name `.nooma` is never a candidate.** The glob matches it — `*` also matches the empty
string — so `~/.nooma`, the *container* that holds vaults, looks like one by name. It has no config
inside, so the predicate rejects it anyway; the requirement is that it must never be **reported** as a
broken vault, because it is doing exactly its job and sending the user to repair it would be a bug in
the message.

The test also proves a legitimately hidden `.work.nooma` **is** still a candidate — so the exclusion is
the literal name, not any dotfile.

## The `size:exception`, and why this one and not the eight before it

543 against 400. Unlike slices 3a–3e, there was no clean cut. A resolver that handles two of its four
steps is not shippable, and splitting would have published a function whose documented contract was
**false for one PR**, with a test asserting that lie to stay green.

The precedent this sets is *"split unless splitting makes the result worse"* — not *"the ceiling is
optional"*. Eight earlier slices were split rather than excepted, including one left 14 lines over
rather than deleting the record of why the chain grew. Recorded in `tasks.md` with the argument, not
just the number.

## Test plan

- [x] `make check-all` — exits 0
- [x] Watched failing first: `undefined: environment`, `undefined: resolveVault`
- [x] 99 tests and subtests, `-race`, all `t.Parallel()`
- [x] Real directory trees via `t.TempDir()` — the cheapest honest fake of a filesystem is a
      filesystem, and it stays L1: no database, no network, no subprocess
- [x] Precedence driven against one tree where **every** step could succeed, asserting the earlier wins
- [x] `golangci-lint` — 0 issues
- [x] Conventional commits, no `Co-Authored-By` trailers

## Summary
Implements the Class/Section Assignment sub-flow for assigning students to sections within a grade.

## Changes
- **Section model**: New prisma model with name, year, capacity, FKs to Grade/Branch/Tenant. StudentGrade.section (string) replaced by sectionId (FK to Section).
- **Manual assign**: Registrar assigns students to a section. Blocks with 409 if section capacity is exceeded.
- **Auto-balance**: Two modes — count (even distribution) and gender_ratio (balance male/female across sections). Returns a preview plan; registrar confirms via a separate endpoint before records are created.
- **Section CRUD**: Create, list, get, update, delete sections. Delete blocked if students are assigned.

## Endpoints
| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| POST | /registration/sections | Create section |
| GET | /registration/sections | List sections (filter by gradeId/branchId/year) |
| GET | /registration/sections/:id | Get section details |
| GET | /registration/sections/:id/students | List assigned students |

body:
Follow-up to #10 and #11, which restored `[logs].status_jsonl` — the one setting whose loss broke systemd's `ConditionPathExists` loudly enough to notice. This restores the other six, which stayed silently wrong.

## What happened

`config/validator-mainnet-sn39.toml` is a declared divergence. Reconciling it during the `dabf10b` re-sync (#6), I found one conflicting comment hunk (about `controlled_dir`), resolved it correctly with `git merge-file` — then discarded that merge result entirely and overwrote the whole file with raw upstream bytes, on the mistaken belief that one resolved conflict meant the whole file had been superseded upstream. It hadn't.

## What was silently wrong on `main` until now

```
mode = "authority"                              -> silently became "shadow"
registry_keys/report_keys/index_keys             -> /etc/cathedral-validator/provenance/*
                                                     became repo-relative config/provenance/*
max_anchor_lag_blocks = 600                       -> dropped entirely
min_assurance = "rewarded_set_proven"             -> dropped entirely
beta_skip_launch_ceremony = true                  -> dropped entirely
require_completed_launch_for_broadcast = false    -> flipped to true
```

All six are read by `scaffold/cli.py` and `scaffold/validator_thin.py`; `mode` gates the authority provenance path.

## The fix

Diffed line-by-line against `873621a` (the last commit before the regression) and restored everything, keeping only the two changes that are genuinely later and correct: `#407`'s path/wording fix for the recurring-write-authorization comment (`/etc/cathedral` → `/etc/cathedral-validator`, confirmed present in upstream at `dabf10b`), and #10/#11's improved `status_jsonl` comment. Confirmed the result matches `873621a` byte-for-byte outside those two hunks.

## Verification

- `tools/manifest.sh verify` — VERIFY OK, 13 declared divergences confirmed different including this file
- Both selftests (`manifest.sh selftest`, `sync-from-upstream.sh selftest`) pass
- `tests/thin` + `tests/boundary`: 418 passed
- Scanned every other file touched by the same re-sync for the same "wholesale overwrite" pattern (`git diff 873621a origin/main` line-removal counts per file) — only this file and `scripts/build_sn39_release_manifest.py` got that treatment, and the latter was already correctly reconciled at the time (its narrowing re-applied on top of upstream's hardening, verified by its own test).

author: cplieger
body:
envx v1.5.0 returns a KEY_FILE value with at most one trailing line
ending removed and every other byte as written, because a secret may
legitimately contain whitespace and a generic getter cannot guess which.
Both values this app reads that way are values where whitespace is
meaningless, so passing it through produced a malformed URL or a token
Plex answers 401 to.

requireEnv now trims at that boundary, which also means KEY and KEY_FILE
cannot resolve to different secrets for the same key, and treats a
blank result as fatal alongside missing and unreadable. envx already
rejects a blank secret FILE, but a padded KEY would otherwise trim down
to an empty string and start the app with no URL or token at all.

author: williaby
body:
## Summary

Stage A of the approved moderation review redesign: stop the fail-safe flag
flood at its source and stop mock verdicts from masquerading as review.

Root cause (proven against live data): 5,048 of 5,056 `llm_safety` FLAGs carry
"unknown verdict; defaulted to fail-safe". The mock reviewer returns `{}`,
which parses as JSON but has no verdict key, so the unknown-verdict branch
emitted Stage 1's fail-safe FLAG once per node. 22 of 29 live books were
mock-moderated; only 8 genuine safety flags exist in the corpus.

Changes:

- **Flood collapse**: per-node fail-safe verdicts collapse into a single
  story-level `reviewer_unavailable` finding instead of one FLAG per node.
- **Mock guard**: outside local environments the mock reviewer now requires an
  explicit escape hatch (`CYO_ADVENTURE_ALLOW_MOCK_REVIEW=1`); reports are
  stamped when the hatch is used, so mock-reviewed output is identifiable.
- **Stage-0 fail-open fix** (gap G11): a malformed reviewer response now
  produces a structural finding instead of passing silently.
- **Threshold-evidence hygiene**: structural fail-safes are excluded from
  threshold-suggestion evidence, including legacy rows matched by their exact
  fail-safe message strings, so the flood can never arm a FLAG-to-BLOCK
  threshold (the G2a measurement showed (16+, safety) one release from
  arming on flood evidence alone).
- New `counts.structural` event field and a structural split in insights;
  fenced-JSON parsing covered by test.

## Deploy prerequisite (before this reaches production)

Production currently runs `review_provider=mock`. The new boot guard will
refuse to start there unless either a real reviewer is configured or
`CYO_ADVENTURE_ALLOW_MOCK_REVIEW=1` is set. Merging is safe; deploying
requires one of those two changes first.

## Verification

All commits signed; pre-commit and the full quality gate pass on the branch.

author: raphyduck
body:
## Problème

Dernière couche du debug L'Âme Idéale, découverte après le déploiement de la PR #874 (throttle) : le job watchlist reçoit désormais les **6 releases c411** (10-370 seeders, elles passent les filtres seeders/qualité/taille)… mais chaque release meurt ensuite sur `File 'L.Ame.Ideale...' not identified, skipping`.

Diagnostic en live sur le serveur :
- `Tmdb::Movie.find('L Ame Ideale')` **trouve le film** (tmdb 1166170, « L'Âme Idéale (2025) », imdb tt35526093) ✔
- mais `media_chose` rejette le match : le titre provider porte une **apostrophe typographique** (`L'Âme` avec `’` U+2019) que `regularise_media_filename` laisse passer alors que l'apostrophe ASCII `'` est supprimée. `clean_search` produit donc `L'Ame Ideale` (avec ’) vs `L Ame Ideale`, et `Metadata.match_titles` échoue dans les deux sens — vérifié en isolation : `false/false` avant le fix, `true/true` après.

## Fix

`’` et `‘` sont désormais supprimées comme `'` dans `StringUtils.regularise_media_filename`, si bien que les deux côtés de `match_titles` se normalisent identiquement (le hack `^l(\w)` de `regexify` fait ensuite matcher `LAme` ↔ `L Ame` comme pour les titres ASCII).

## Tests

- Nouveau test de régression dans `metadata_match_titles_test.rb` : `L'Âme Idéale (2025)` (apostrophe typographique) ↔ `L Ame Ideale 2025`, dans les deux sens.
- `metadata_match_titles_test.rb` (13 runs), `string_utils_test.rb`, `torrent_search_test.rb`, `tracker_query_service_test.rb` verts. (`metadata_test.rb` : 1 failure préexistante sur master, inchangée ; les 2 erreurs standalone du fichier service préexistent aussi.)

Avec les PR #873 (élision) + #874 (throttle) + celle-ci, la chaîne complète est réparée : requête correcte → c411 répond → releases filtrées → identifiées → stockées avec timeframe.

## Summary

- **Appends two data points to `#146`** (`ui-phone-scroll` Services result anchor jumps on viewport shrink under CI load) rather than opening a duplicate. The test failed once more on #1457 head `c739340` (`anchorTop` expected `-138`, received `-7`, `120 passed`) and then passed on heads `9da02d9` and `a6f2281` across all three shards with the spec byte-identical. That takes the row to six data points, two failures, shard 1 only — and both failures landed on a PR touching nothing but `src/app/mockups/**` plus one mockup test, which strengthens the row's existing unchanged-code reading. Also records that the 131px delta is roughly 2× the 64px viewport shrink rather than sub-pixel drift, which is a constraint for the element attribution `#146` already asks for.
- **Records the `prlanded` verification for #1457** in `docs/branch-review-ledger.md` via `npm run ledger:append`: squash `e79e499`, content diff against the branch tip empty, and the late `aria-live` commit confirmed present on `main` rather than orphaned by the squash race.

Two ledger files, no new IDs allocated. No source, test, config or workflow file is touched.

### What this PR no longer contains

It originally filed a new row claiming `search-results-header-band.tsx` announces a failed clinical search to nobody, because its count span sets `aria-live={faulted ? "off" : "polite"}`.

**That claim was false and has been dropped entirely.** The band *does* announce the failure — it mounts a fault panel with `role="alert"` carrying the title, body and Retry (`search-results-header-band.tsx:407-414`), the mute is deliberate and documented in place (*"the freshly-mounted fault `role="alert"` below makes the single announcement, rather than both speaking"*), and `tests/search-results-header-band.dom.test.tsx` already pins it with singular role queries that throw on duplicates. The proposed fix would have added a second alert — a duplicate announcement and a red test.

Credit to the Codex review on this PR for catching it. It is dropped rather than filed-and-withdrawn because **the row never reached `main`**: there is no false claim in the durable record to correct, so a withdrawal entry would be noise. The reasoning is preserved in the resolved review thread on this PR. Removing it also retires the ID allocation, so `issues:next-id` is untouched at `149` and this PR can no longer collide with concurrent sessions over IDs — which was the cause of every conflict it hit.

`npm run verify:pr-local` not run: this diff is two markdown ledgers, so the build, client-bundle scan and RAG fixture stages it adds over `verify:cheap` have no reachable surface here. UI verification not applicable — no component, route or style changed.

RAG impact: no retrieval behaviour change — documentation only, touching nothing under `src/lib/rag/**`, clinical-search, retrieval-selection, ranking-config, answer-ranking, the eval harness or the golden fixture.

## Risk and rollout

- Risk: None. Both files are append-oriented records with no runtime effect, and this PR now recommends no production change.
- Rollback: Revert the merge commit.
- Provider or production effects: None.

## Notes

- Every conflict on this branch was resolved by rebuilding `docs/outstanding-issues.md` from `origin/main` and re-applying only this branch's edit — never taking one side wholesale — so no concurrent session's rows were dropped. `npm run check:outstanding-issues` passes on the result.

author: cplieger
body:
The hand-rolled base-dir preflight is replaced by
atomicfile.ProbeWritable, whose stage set covers every stage this probe
distinguishes (mkdir, create, write, sync, close, remove) with the same
first-failure-wins precedence. Each stage's error keeps its previous
wording, so every failure stays as distinguishable in the log as before,
including the actionable "not writable" line the startup hint is written
against.

A non-nil error return now means the probe was never attempted (an empty
dir, an already-cancelled context) and is reported as such: a cancelled
preflight is not a read-only volume, and it must not borrow any stage
diagnosis.

The probe file carries atomicfile's own temp-name shape instead of an
app-invented ".write_test-*", so a leftover reads as a package temp
rather than a name nothing in the fleet recognises.

body:
Windows reserves device names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9) at the OS level. git stash push --include-untracked fails when trying to stage files with these basenames on Windows.

Instead of silently deleting untracked reserved-name files (which could lose user data), we temporarily rename them before stash and restore the original names after stash apply.

- Add _rename_reserved_untracked() to detect and rename matching files
- Add _restore_reserved_renames() to undo the temporary renames  
- Hook into _stash_local_changes_if_needed (before stash push)
- Hook into _restore_stashed_changes (after stash apply)
- Add 7 tests covering detection, renaming, restore, non-Windows noop, and full E2E round-trip with real git

Fixes review feedback on PR #71841.

author: kourchenko
body:
## Summary

Ships the two commands issue Kourchenko/kovalent#51 asks for, the core of Knaix CLI Phase 5.

**`knaix doctor`** — every other command stops at the first thing that is wrong, so diagnosing a setup meant running four commands and assembling the answer by hand. This runs every check, reports all of them, and prints the command that fixes each one it did not like: CLI version, `.knaix.toml`, API URL, control plane, session, Docker, local node, and finally whether the node your commands address can actually answer.

One rule decides the exit code: **doctor fails when something on the path to your node is broken, and warns about anything that is not on it.** The path is everything a command traverses to reach its node: the project file and API URL that decide where it goes, the control plane and session that authorize it, and the node itself.

- No Docker is fine if your default node is hosted. An unreachable control plane is fine if your default node is `local`. Neither is reported as a failure to someone it does not affect — otherwise the command is useless to half its audience.
- A run that only warns exits 0, so it can gate a CI step.
- An unconfigured machine is not broken, it is unconfigured. The single finding is that, with both ways out of it, rather than an auth failure for an account the user may never want.
- It is one of only two commands that survive a `.knaix.toml` they cannot parse — the other is `knaix init`, which is how a broken one gets replaced. Every other command reads that file before it runs, so a broken one breaks all of them, including the one whose job is to find out why. `main` skips the pre-parse for both so the failure arrives as a finding instead.

**`knaix bench`** — `selftest` answers whether a node answers correctly; this answers how long it takes. Three phases, because they slow down for different reasons and one end-to-end number hides which one moved:

| Phase | What it measures |
| :--- | :--- |
| Reach | A bare health round trip: the floor everything else sits on. |
| Ingest | One generated document parsed, chunked, embedded and written: the write side of the vector store. |
| Answer | A question, split into time to first token and total. |

The answer split is the useful one. Retrieval, reranking and prompt assembly all happen before the first token, so a high first-token time with a small gap to the total means the knowledge base is slow, and the reverse means the model is. Getting it required the streaming readers to record when the first token landed, so `ChatAnswer` now carries `first_token_ms`; the pre-streaming local path leaves it absent rather than reporting the whole wait, which would read as an instant answer that then took seconds to finish.

Reachability is measured first, so an unreachable node is reported as one rather than as a confusing ingest failure — and nothing is written to a node that was never going to answer. `--runs` is capped at 100: past that this stops being a measurement and starts being a load test against someone's node. A node answering with the deterministic mock is labelled, because those timings measure the mock rather than a model.

The document `bench` ingests is part of the corpus while it is on the node, so the command is careful about it: a normal run deletes it, `--sweep` clears what an interrupted run left on a hosted node, and the two cases that cannot delete it warn instead of exiting quietly. See the review round below.

Both take `--json` and a documented exit code, and neither needs an account: the `knaix local` path keeps full parity.

Single-document ingest, delete, and the percentile helper are now shared with `selftest` rather than copied.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
| :--- | :--- |
| `src/doctor.rs` | New. Eight checks, the pass/warn/fail model, the exit-code rule, text and JSON reports. |
| `src/bench.rs` | New. The three phases, percentile summaries, the generated corpus document, cleanup. |
| `tests/doctor_and_bench.rs` | New. Seven end-to-end tests: none of these cases can be proved from inside the process. |
| `src/main.rs` | Both subcommands, and the `doctor` exemption from the project-file pre-parse. |
| `src/nodes.rs` | `ChatAnswer.first_token_ms`; both stream readers record when the first token landed. |
| `src/selftest.rs` | `ingest_text`, `delete_document` and `percentile` made shareable; `ingest_corpus` now calls `ingest_text`. |
| `src/update.rs` | `newer_version_available()` extracted from the banner, so `doctor` reads the cached result rather than making a network call. Version comparison now has tests, and correctly ranks `0.10.0` under `1.2.0`. |
| `src/local.rs` | `docker_version()`, so `doctor` can report the daemon without failing on its absence. |
| `README.md` | Both commands in the reference table, plus a section each. |

`CHANGELOG.md` is untouched: this repository compiles it in the release PR.

## Validation

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, and `cargo test --locked` all pass. 181 tests, 24 of them new.

Verified end to end against a real local node (`ghcr.io/kovalentai/node-runtime:latest`, answering with `gemma4:latest` through Ollama), not only in tests.

**Healthy machine, `doctor` exits 0:**

```
Diagnosis:
╭──────┬───────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│      ┆ Check         ┆ Detail                                                                           │
╞══════╪═══════════════╪══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╡
│ ok   ┆ cli           ┆ v0.4.5                                                                           │
│ ok   ┆ project file  ┆ none in this directory or above                                                  │
│ ok   ┆ api url       ┆ https://api.kovalentai.com                                                       │
│ warn ┆ control plane ┆ could not reach https://api.kovalentai.com (not needed for the local node)       │
│ warn ┆ auth          ┆ a session is stored, but the control plane could not be asked to honour it       │
│ ok   ┆ docker        ┆ server 24.0.2                                                                    │
│ ok   ┆ local node    ┆ ready on http://127.0.0.1:8090, answering with a model at http://localhost:11434 │
│ ok   ┆ target node   ┆ local, ready on http://127.0.0.1:8090                                            │
╰──────┴───────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

✓ Everything a command needs is in place.
```

**Fresh machine with nothing set up, exits 7 (Precondition):**

```
│ warn ┆ control plane ┆ could not reach http://127.0.0.1:9 (not needed for the local node) │
│ warn ┆ auth          ┆ not logged in (the local node needs no account)                    │
│ fail ┆ target node   ┆ no node is configured, so commands have nothing to address         │

What to do:
  target node: knaix local up for a free local node, or knaix up for a hosted one
```

**`bench` against that local node:**

```
╭─────────────────────┬─────────┬─────────┬─────────┬─────────╮
│ Phase               ┆ p50     ┆ p95     ┆ min     ┆ max     │
╞═════════════════════╪═════════╪═════════╪═════════╪═════════╡
│ Reach               ┆ 2ms     ┆ 31ms    ┆ 2ms     ┆ 31ms    │
│ Ingest              ┆ 656ms   ┆ -       ┆ -       ┆ -       │
│ Answer, first token ┆ 17033ms ┆ 33543ms ┆ 14286ms ┆ 33543ms │
│ Answer, total       ┆ 19775ms ┆ 36990ms ┆ 16951ms ┆ 36990ms │
╰─────────────────────┴─────────┴─────────┴─────────┴─────────╯

  Answered by: local:gemma4:latest
  Split: 17033ms to the first token (retrieval, reranking, prompt), then 2742ms generating.
```

Cleanup verified rather than assumed — the node's own count after the run:

```
$ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/kb/count -d '{"instance_id":"...","by_document":true}'
```

author: amroksaleh
body:
## WC-notifications — user preferences (task c56a6455)

Slice 5: per-user notification preferences, wired into the dispatcher's channel-resolution seam (#652). Backend + API; the notifications Settings UI consumes the typed client generated here.

### What's in it
- **Migration 071** — `user_notification_preferences` (tenant-owned): one `(tenant, profile, type, channel)` toggle; `UNIQUE(tenant_id, profile_id, type, channel)` for idempotent upsert; `type = '*'` is a channel-wide toggle. Registered in `TenantOwnedTables` + proven in `CrossTenantRejectionRealEngineTest`.
- **`NotificationPreferenceRepository`** — `(tenant, profile)`-scoped `listForProfile` / `set` (upsert via `ON CONFLICT`) / `delete`; `tenant_id` in the SQL literal (guard-visible).
- **`NotificationPreferenceResolver`** — **opt-OUT** model: a channel is delivered unless an explicit pref disables it; an exact `(type, channel)` row wins over a `('*', channel)` channel-wide row. **Transactional** types (`security.` / `account.` / `auth.` / `password.` / `billing.` — an overridable preset) and a **null recipient** bypass filtering entirely (always deliver).
- **`NotificationDispatcher`** — filters a recipient's channels through the resolver before recording deliveries (nullable dep — permissive when absent, so existing behavior is unchanged). The notification row is still persisted, so the **in-app inbox stays the complete record** even when outbound channels are opted out.
- **`NotificationPreferencesApiHandler`** + `GET`/`PUT /api/me/notification-preferences` (self-scoped, session-gated, no RBAC permission — like `/api/me/notifications`). `PUT` validates the whole batch first (no partial writes) and **rejects a disable on a transactional type** (422).
- **Typed OpenAPI** — routes + `NotificationPreferenceEntry` / `NotificationPreferencesResponse` / `NotificationPreferencesUpdateRequest` components; `public/openapi.json` + `web/lib/api/schema.d.ts` regenerated.

### Verification
- **phpunit**: **242/242 (SQLite)** incl. migration/tenant/cross-tenant gates; prefs + dispatcher **21/21 (real Postgres, isolated schema)** — proves `ON CONFLICT` upsert + boolean handling on PG; OpenAPI drift + route-catalogue gates green.
- **phpstan L8** (changed scope): clean.
- **tenant-predicate guard script**: clean.
- **Real-stack boot** (worktree on dev Postgres): migration 071 applies + both prefs routes return **401 unauthenticated** (wired + the dispatcher-with-resolver wiring boots).

### Design notes
Opt-out default (absent row → enabled) so notifications work out of the box. Transactional enforcement is centralized in the resolver (a stored disable on a transactional type is also ineffective), and the API rejects setting one so the UI stays honest. In-app is the always-present inbox record; preferences meaningfully gate the outbound channels.

author: zahirinatzuke
body:
## El fallo

`local-delegate --help` **no imprimia nada** y se quedaba colgado hasta un Ctrl+C, que escupia sesenta lineas de traceback de `anyio`. Reportado por el usuario desde su terminal, con el CLI instalado por `uv tool install`.

Reproducido antes de tocar nada:

```
$ LOCAL_DELEGATE_AUTOSTART=0 uv run python -m local_delegate --help < /dev/null
EXIT=0
--- stdout ---   (vacio)
--- stderr ---   (vacio)
```

Exit 0 y cero bytes de ayuda: **nunca se llamo a argparse**. El despacho comparaba `sys.argv[1]` contra una lista literal de siete subcomandos, y todo lo que no estuviera en ella caia al servidor MCP stdio a esperar mensajes JSON-RPC. Le pasaba igual a `-h` y a cualquier subcomando mal escrito — `local-delegate doctro` se clavaba en vez de decir «invalid choice».

## El agravante

La lista de subcomandos estaba escrita **tres veces**: la que decidia el despacho (`server._CLI_COMMANDS`), una copia muerta sin un solo lector en todo el repo (`cli.KNOWN_COMMANDS`) y las llamadas reales a `sub.add_parser(...)`. Hoy coincidian por casualidad. El change B anade `update`, que con ese diseno habria que dar de alta en dos sitios — y olvidando uno, se colgaria exactamente igual.

## El arreglo

Una sola frontera: **con argumentos es un CLI, sin argumentos es un servidor MCP stdio**. De los argumentos responde el parser, que es quien sabe que subcomandos existen. Las dos copias de la lista desaparecen.

Lo que **no** cambia es la invocacion sin argumentos, que es como lanzan el binario Claude Code y Codex; romperla los dejaria sin MCP. Tiene test dedicado y se verifico con una tuberia real.

Extras:

- Aviso por **stderr** cuando alguien escribe `local-delegate` a secas en una terminal (solo con stdin en TTY). El servidor arranca igual en los dos casos.
- La descripcion de `--help` ya no dice que el CLI sea solo para los groups de llama-swap.

## Verificacion

Los cuatro casos por ejecucion real, no solo por tests:

| Caso | Antes | Ahora |
|---|---|---|
| `--help` | cuelgue / exit 0 mudo | `usage: ...`, exit 0, stderr vacio |
| `doctro` | cuelgue | `invalid choice`, exit 2 |
| `doctor --home <vacio>` | OK | OK |
| sin argumentos, stdin por tuberia | arranca MCP | arranca MCP, stderr vacio |

**Tests verificados al reves:** reintroduciendo el filtro por lista fallan 4. El de `--help` falla con su propia asercion, no reventando al arrancar un servidor de verdad.

**Hallazgo que conviene no perder:** `/dev/null` en Git Bash es `NUL`, un dispositivo de caracter, y ahi `isatty()` devuelve `True`. La primera prueba del caso «host MCP» dio el resultado contrario al esperado por eso. Para probarlo hace falta una **tuberia** de verdad. Queda escrito en el docstring.

Los cuatro pasos del CI en verde en local: `ruff check` · `ruff format --check` · **322 passed, 1 skipped** (antes 316) · `extract_dashboard_js.py` + `node --check`.

Traza SDD completa en `.sdd/changes/cli-help-arranca-el-mcp/`.

author: arnozhang
body:
## Why

`parse_table_name_parts` right-aligns a dotted identifier onto a dialect-specific field order (`[catalog, database, table]` for StarRocks, `[database, schema, table]` for the Postgres family, `[database, table]` for SQLite, …). That order lived in a closure inside the function, so every caller that needs to **emit** an identifier with a matching segment count — scope tokens for `SubAgentConfig.scoped_context.tables`, `metadata_identifier`, the SaaS catalog tree — had to re-derive the shape from `connector_registry.support_*`.

The two derivations already disagree. For a dialect that declares no namespace capabilities (adapter not installed, or one that reports none), the parser falls back to the widest `catalog.database.schema.table` shape, while an emitter reading `support_*` sees zero namespaces and produces a two-segment `<db>.*` — whose literal then right-aligns into `schema_name` and matches nothing. SQLite's two-segment shape is likewise hardcoded in the parser only, so an emitter agrees with it by luck rather than by contract.

Downstream symptom this unblocks: Datus-backend builds `ask_report` / `ask_dashboard` scope tokens from `support_*` and needs the parser's own shape to stop emitting tokens the matcher can't match.

## Solution

Lift the closure to a module-level `table_name_field_order(dialect) -> List[str]` returning the same `*_name` keys `parse_table_name_parts` produces, and have the parser consume it.

Key decisions:

- **The order always has >= 2 fields.** A capability-less dialect returns the widest shape explicitly (`_WIDEST_FIELD_ORDER`) instead of `["table_name"]`, which is exactly what the parser's old `len(field_mapping) > 1` fallback branch computed by hand. That branch is now dead code and is removed, so the right-align loop handles every dialect uniformly.
- **Capabilities are still resolved through `parse_dialect`**, keeping the existing `postgresql` -> `postgres` lookup behavior intact.
- **Adapters with a custom `get_identifier_parser` keep short-circuiting** ahead of the field-order path; their shape is expected to follow their declared capabilities, which is now stated in the docstring.

Verified behavior-preserving with a differential harness comparing the new path against the previous implementation across 16 dialects x 9 token shapes (bare, 2/3/4/5-segment, wildcard-bearing): identical output on every combination.

## Test Cases

Unit tests only — this is a pure refactor of a parsing helper with no external dependencies, so it belongs in the CI tier per the testing rules.

`tests/unit_tests/utils/test_sql_utils.py` -> new `TestTableNameFieldOrder`:

- Per-dialect orders: MySQL (no schema level), StarRocks (catalog first), Postgres family (resolves through `parse_dialect`), SQLite (2 segments), DuckDB (keeps its schema level).
- Capability-less and blank dialects fall back to the widest shape rather than collapsing to a bare table name.
- **Cross-component contract** (parametrized over 7 dialects): a token emitted with one segment per declared field parses back with every literal in the field it was emitted for — this is the property emitters depend on.
- The failure mode the contract prevents: a token one segment short right-aligns and shifts every literal left by one field.

Existing `tests/unit_tests/utils/test_sql_utils.py` (202 tests) and `tests/unit_tests/tools/db_tools/` pass unchanged. `ci/audit_tests.py --diff-only` reports P0=0, P1=0.

author: cplieger
body:
The writability preflight discarded both the close and the remove error,
so a directory that accepted a create and then refused to flush or clean
up passed silently. It now runs atomicfile.ProbeWritable — the same
package that stages every dump temp — and rules on each stage:

  - Mkdir, Create, Write, Sync: fatal, as before. Nothing durable was
    written, so the destination cannot take a dump.
  - Close: fatal, and this is the stage that used to be dropped. Close is
    where a filesystem reports a write that never reached disk, and this
    gates a BACKUP run, so a destination that cannot prove it durably
    took one byte must not be called ready. Deliberately stricter than
    ProbeResult.Writable.
  - Remove: a WARN. A dump commits with a rename and never with an
    unlink, so a refused unlink costs leaked temps, not backups. It is
    also not clearable by a restart, and this app keeps
    restart-unclearable states out of the health marker.

The probe file now carries atomicfile's temp-name shape, so a leftover is
reclaimed by the ReclaimOrphans sweep each cycle already runs; the old
".pg-autodump-writable-*" name was reclaimable by nothing.

Guard.WaitIdle no longer misreports a finished dump as a blown drain
budget. webhttp.Run hands the teardown whatever is left of the shutdown
grace after the HTTP drain, so a drain that spent the whole budget called
WaitIdle with an already-expired context, and a select with both cases
ready picks pseudo-randomly: a dump that had finished reported false and
the caller cancelled an idle guard. webhttp.AwaitDone re-checks
completion after the context fires.

DUMP_DIR's ".."-component rule is now pathinside.HasDotDot, which
examines the value as written so a traversal that would normalize away is
still refused. A name that merely contains consecutive dots is still
accepted.

author: gkamradt
body:
## Summary

- Add an `encrypted_replay` state mode for the OpenAI Responses API.
- Keep state client-side by replaying encrypted reasoning and compaction items with `store: false`, without `previous_response_id` or server-managed conversations.
- Prune replay history after automatic compaction while retaining the latest compaction item and subsequent output items.
- Add optional action-level state telemetry for input item counts and compaction events.
- Record model output and available OpenAI reasoning summaries as distinct ARC reasoning fields.
- Add GPT-5.6 encrypted-replay profiles for each supported reasoning effort, using `reasoning.context: auto` and `reasoning.summary: auto`.

## Why

This enables multi-turn reasoning continuity and automatic compaction for long ARC-AGI-3 runs while preserving the client-managed state required for Zero Data Retention workflows.

## Validation

- `uv run pytest -q` — 277 passed, 2 paid live tests skipped
- `uv run ruff check benchmarking tests` — passed
- Opt-in live tests cover two-turn encrypted replay and end-to-end automatic compaction at a small test-local threshold.
- Production ARC-AGI-3 runs were exercised during development to validate long-running replay and repeated compaction.

## ZDR considerations

The new profiles require `store: false`, request encrypted reasoning content, reject server-managed state fields, and retain replay state only in the benchmark process. API credentials remain environment-variable based and are not included in this change.

body:
## Seed imported Claude Code turns as ChatModule recent history (plan C)

Follow-up to the Agent Migration feature (#209). Imported conversation turns were
stored only as `event` memory (search-only), so the imported agent never saw the
conversation as **recent history** — recent history is sourced from ChatModule's
per-instance JSON memory, a separate store.

`applier._seed_chat_history` now ALSO writes the recent turns into the imported
Narrative's ChatModule instance memory (`add_instance_json_format_memory(
"ChatModule", <chat instance>, ...)`), so they load as normal recent history when
the user opens that narrative. Turns still go to `event` memory too (searchable).

**Ordering:** each message's `meta_data.timestamp` is the turn's ORIGINAL time —
a multi-session import writes all narratives at once and ChatModule's unified
timeline sorts by that field, so import-time would collapse the cross-narrative
order; original times keep sessions interleaved by real conversation time. Chat
instance id comes from `narrative.active_instances` (create_narrative already made
it). Best-effort — never breaks import.

Verified live on the sqlite proxy backend: turns persist into ChatModule instance
memory and read back with their original timestamps via the same method
ChatModule uses to load history. Unit test captures the write payload (the table
machinery uses MySQL information_schema, which the direct sqlite test backend
can't run — the real write is ChatModule's prod-proven path).

26 migration tests green; ruff clean. Applies cleanly on dev.

author: imaginethegames
body:
The online-final round (#246) closed with one item carried as UNKNOWN: the ~5 s
after a death in which the `online-feel` telemetry re-charges the same correction,
identical to three decimals, while the ship provably sits still. This measures it,
and corrects the previous round on one point that matters: **the accounting is
sound — the states genuinely disagree.**

## What was measured

`evidence/respawn-tail.live.test.ts` watches the subtraction itself. `prediction.ts`
computes the number this gate is failed on in one place (`reconcile`):

```
this.error = checkpoint && authoritative
  ? Math.hypot(checkpoint.x - authoritative.posX, checkpoint.y - authoritative.posY)
  : 0;
```

Two terms. The probe wraps the SHIPPED `reconcile` and records **both**, per
reconcile, across a real death on the live fleet. Nothing stubbed, nothing modified.
Output committed verbatim as `images/online-feel-respawn-tail.json` (room SWQD,
1 598 reconciles, all applied).

Across the 150 breaching reconciles there is exactly **one** distinct error value,
because there is exactly one distinct value on each side:

| term | value | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `checkpoint` | (1968.841, 1200) | the player's **home** |
| `authoritative` | (744, 1291) | the **death site** |
| `error` | 1228.217 u | the distance between them, charged 150× |

`histHit` true and `resynced` false on every one — each was a real rewind to a real
history entry at the snapshot's own tick. The window spans snapshot ticks 2606 →
2904: 298 ticks, and at `TICK_DT = 1/60` that is 4.97 s — `RESPAWN_S = 5`.

## Root cause: the respawn countdown never crosses the wire

Every link measured or read from shipped source:

1. `killShip` (`src/sim/damage.ts:37-40`) sets `alive = false`, `hull = 0`,
   `respawnTimer = RESPAWN_S` — and **only authority runs it**, because damage is
   the server's word by design.
2. `ShipSnap` (`src/net/snapshot.ts`) carries pos, vel, heading, hull and a
   `SHIP_FLAG.alive` bit — and **no `respawnTimer`**.
3. `applySnapshot` (`src/net/prediction.ts:799-809`) writes pos, hull and `alive`,
   and never writes `respawnTimer`.
4. So the client's ship goes dead with its countdown **already at 0**.
5. `step()` (`src/sim/step.ts:199-202`) does
   `ship.respawnTimer -= dt; if (ship.respawnTimer <= 0) respawn(ship)` — so the
   first replay step after the death snapshot resurrects it at home, full hull,
   **the whole 5 s early**.

Every reconcile until authority catches up then repeats the round trip: authority
writes dead-at-death-site, the replay writes alive-at-home, and the full distance
is charged again.

## Why nobody reported seeing it — and what is actually wrong

`absorb()` measures displacement across the *whole* reconcile — home before, home
after — so no visual snap is counted and this never looked like a teleport. But the
ship the renderer draws is the same `world.ships` entry the probe sampled, and for
those 298 ticks it sits within **±4 u of home while thrust is held down** at 33 ms
intervals. The symptom this implies is not a visual glitch but a dead control
stick: for ~5 s after you die you are drawn at your home planet at full hull,
unable to move, on a ship authority still holds dead in the field.

**Owner: Netcode.** The fix is to give the client authority's remaining countdown
(stream `respawnTimer`, or hold the local ship dead until authority revives it) —
not to change the instrument.

## Also in this PR

- `recheck-online-blockers.mjs` absorbs the finding: an absence in a wire format
  *is* statically checkable, so the fifth question is no longer UNKNOWN but an
  ordinary check. It now reports **BLOCKED on five**, each with a named owner.
- Asked of GitHub at 15:44Z: no lane has a fix in flight for any of them — every
  `Deploy server (Fly.io)` run still red through run 30552080733, `origin/main`
  still `927943a` at the time, #246 the only open PR.

## Verdicts

**Untouched.** `online-reconnect` and `online-feel` both remain `failed` — still the
honest reading, still not QA's to flip. What changed is that the last UNKNOWN is now
a named mechanism with a named owner. `evidence/` only.

author: benjithatfoxguy
body:
Replaces #16, which was opened on the recycled `claude/bdrive-dedup-debug-c2osgc` branch. Same commit, own branch.

## The problem

`upload_id` is a client-computed MD5 sent as a path or body parameter, so the server accepts **any string** for it. `models.Upload` carries a `UserId` column that `UploadsUpload` populates on every insert — and until now nothing read it. The table's primary key is `(part_id, channel_id)`, so there was no scoping at the database level either.

Anyone supplying another user's `upload_id` could:

- `GET /uploads/{id}` — read their part IDs, channel IDs and encryption salts
- `DELETE /uploads/{id}` — destroy their in-progress upload
- `POST /files` / `PATCH /files/{id}` — adopt their uploaded parts into a file of their own

The behaviour predates deduplication. But #14 widened it: `FilesCreate` now loads the upload rows whenever an `uploadId` is present, even alongside an explicit `parts` list, so an adopted session also yields its **block hashes** — and with them the victim's content hash and dedup identity. That's what made it worth closing now rather than leaving to general triage.

Surfaced while explaining the `FilesCreate` panic from #14; deliberately left out of that PR rather than folded in silently, since it touches endpoints beyond the dedup path.

## The change

`user_id` added to all six `upload_id` queries — one pattern, no logic changes:

| File | Site | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pkg/services/file.go` | `FilesCreate` lookup | `userId` already in scope |
| `pkg/services/file.go` | `FilesCreate` delete-after-commit (in tx) | ” |
| `pkg/services/file.go` | `FilesUpdate` lookup | ” |
| `pkg/services/file.go` | `FilesUpdate` delete-after-commit (in tx) | ” |
| `pkg/services/upload.go` | `UploadsDelete` | did not resolve the caller at all; now calls `auth.GetUser(ctx)` |
| `pkg/services/upload.go` | `UploadsPartsById` | ” |

`UploadsPartsById` still returns an **empty list** for an upload id owned by someone else, exactly as it does for one that doesn't exist — so the response never reveals whether an id is in use.

## Compatibility

- **No migration.** `user_id` has been on `teldrive.uploads` since the initial schema (`20231102165658_tables.sql`) and is set on every insert.
- The column is nullable, so a row with `NULL user_id` would become invisible. No code path creates one, and upload rows are transient and retention-bounded, so nothing needs backfilling.
- **No spec change**, so no bdrive-docs PR and no generated-API churn.
- **No client change.** bclone (`prepareUpload`, `createFile`, `Object.Update`) and bdrive-ui (`uploadFile`) all call these endpoints as the user that owns the parts. Resumed uploads still work — bclone's `prepareUpload` calls `GET /uploads/{id}` to find already-uploaded chunks, and the owner still sees them.

## Verification

```
go build ./pkg/... ./internal/...     # clean
go vet ./pkg/services/...             # clean
go test ./pkg/services/ ./internal/hash/ ./internal/cache/
ok  github.com/tgdrive/teldrive/pkg/services
ok  github.com/tgdrive/teldrive/internal/hash
ok  github.com/tgdrive/teldrive/internal/cache
```

Completeness check — `grep -n 'Where("upload_id' pkg/services/*.go` returns six hits, all carrying `user_id`, and `grep 'Where("upload_id = ?"'` returns none.

**Not yet run — needs a live instance with Postgres, which the build environment doesn't have.** Worth doing before merge:

- As user A, upload a part; as user B, confirm `GET /uploads/<idA>` returns `[]`, `DELETE /uploads/<idA>` removes nothing, and `POST /files` with `uploadId: <idA>` does not adopt A's parts
- As user A, confirm the normal flow still works: list the part, commit it, rows gone afterwards

No automated test is included: there's no DB harness in this repo (`file_test.go` is pure unit), and standing up sqlmock or testcontainers for a `WHERE` clause change seemed disproportionate. Happy to add one if you'd rather have the coverage.

Adds the screens the prototype was missing: full judgment text with permalinks and citation copying, legislation amendment history, the rules-of-court and forms corpus, the editorial CMS, and the report batch workflow.

Fixes the layout defects a viewport audit turned up. Two root causes covered most of them. The .page grid track could not shrink below its content, so the scroll wrapper on admin tables never engaged and those screens overflowed the viewport below ~900px. And .form-input is width:100%, which stretched the Draft Studio matter selector across the page and broke its toolbar apart.

The rest were per-screen: metadata stranded against the right edge on wide monitors, a hidden Library delete button reserving height in normal flow, Profile fields that were editable but looked like static text, unlabelled facet groups on Practice, and record IDs wrapping mid-token in admin tables.

author: lisachenko
body:
## Summary

**PR 5/6 of the library refresh stack** (agent docs ✅ → README ✅ → toolchain ✅ → PHPStan max #102 → **PHP 8.4 modernization** → CHANGELOG). Based on `chore/phpstan-level-max` — merge #102 first.

The core of the 4.0 release: a full redesign around PHP 8.4-era language features, in four commits.

### `feat!: introduce backed enums and typed instance hydration`
- **New int-backed enums** replace the `FCGI` class int constants: `RecordType` (all 11 record types, plus `recordClass()` mapping each type to its record class), `Role` (Responder/Authorizer/Filter) and `ProtocolStatus` (RequestComplete/CantMultiplexConnection/Overloaded/UnknownRole). `FCGI` keeps only the structural constants (`HEADER_LEN`, `HEADER_FORMAT`, `VERSION_1`, `NULL_REQUEST_ID`, the `KEEP_CONN` bitmask) and is now `final` with a private constructor.
- **`getType()`, `getRole()`, `getProtocolStatus()` return enums**; `BeginRequest` now requires an explicit `Role` (the old default silently meant role 3 = Filter — a latent quirk).
- **`unpackPayload()` is a protected instance method.** The old protocol — `static function unpackPayload($self, ...)` with an untyped param plus `assert()` in every subclass — existed only to work around parameter contravariance. As an instance method `$this` is naturally the concrete type; this also fixes `UnknownType::unpackPayload()` being `public` while every sibling was `protected`.
- **`ProtocolException` (extends `RuntimeException`)** replaces the mix of bare `RuntimeException`/`DomainException`. Invalid wire values (unknown record type, role, status) fail fast via `Enum::tryFrom() ?? throw`. Existing broad `catch (RuntimeException)` blocks keep working.
- Wire fidelity is preserved: unpacking still bypasses constructors (hydration), so byte-exact round-tripping holds even for non-canonical peer encodings — the untouched Wireshark hex fixtures pin this.
- Modern surface throughout: constructor property promotion, native `static` return types, `Stringable`, `final` record classes (`Params` stays open for `GetValues`/`GetValuesResult`), throw expressions, PHP 8.4 `new X()->method()` chaining.

### `perf: cache reflection and avoid buffer copies in parsing hot paths`
- `Record::unpack()` reuses a cached per-class `ReflectionClass` instead of constructing one per parsed record.
- `FrameParser::hasFrame()` unpacks only the two length fields (offset-based) instead of the whole header.
- `Params::unpackPayload()` now walks the payload with an integer cursor — the old loop made three O(n) `substr()` copies per name-value pair, quadratic on big PARAMS frames.

### `test: cover protocol errors, long name-value pairs and empty params`
New coverage: unknown record type and truncated buffer → `ProtocolException`; >127-byte names/values (4-byte long form) round-trip; empty `FCGI_PARAMS` end-of-stream marker hydrates with `getValues() === []` (this guards the one place where constructor promotion would be a correctness trap — documented in `Params` and AGENTS.md).

### `docs: update README examples and agent guidelines for the enum API`

### Deliberately not used
- `readonly` — hydration writes properties after `newInstanceWithoutConstructor()`, and mutable `setRequestId()` chaining is the documented usage pattern.
- Property hooks / asymmetric visibility — would duplicate the getter API for no gain here.

### Breaking changes (4.0)
`FCGI` type/role/status constants removed; enum-typed getters; `BeginRequest` role required; `unpackPayload()` signature; record classes `final`; `FrameParser` `final`; `ProtocolException` instead of `DomainException` for unknown types.

## Test plan

Verified locally on PHP 8.4.19: `composer test` — 31 tests, 87 assertions green; `composer phpstan` — 0 errors at level max.

author: cplieger
body:
truncateRelease charged the "..." marker OUTSIDE the cap, so a shortened
release name rendered up to 45 bytes in a column budgeted for 42 and the
table's alignment broke on exactly the rows that needed it most. The
marker is now charged inside the budget (runesafe.SanitizeSingleLineCapped),
so a truncated name shows at most 39 bytes plus the marker. Names within
budget render byte-identically to before, pinned by the golden test.

Path traversal checks stop rejecting legitimate names. Three places tested
for ".." with a substring or a hand-rolled component split and refused
directory names whose only sin was two adjacent dots — "/backups/a..b",
"/backups/..archive", "..extras/movie.mkv". They now use pathinside:
HasDotDot where the value is judged as written (backup.path, the static
cache path), so a traversal buried mid-path is still refused, and
RelEscapes where a cleaned relative result is judged (the media-root
containment gate). The os.Root handle remains the authoritative layer;
these are the cheap first gate.

author: marclo101
body:
Follow-up to #37 (merged). **74/74** UX + regression checks and **79/79** simulation-engine checks pass. Four commits, **+467 / −106**.

## The design rate now does real work

Picking a library material used to take whatever rate row happened to be first. It now takes the measurement made **closest to the rate you are designing for** — reversible capacity from the row nearest the operating rate, first-cycle capacity from the row nearest the formation rate — compared in log space, since rates span decades. Change either rate later and every preset-bound electrode **re-picks automatically**. A capacity you typed by hand is never overwritten.

Worked example from the shipped library (Hard Carbon, 0.05→0.5 A/g ladder): at C/10 it selects the 270 mAh/g measurement; raise the target to 1C and it switches itself to 225 mAh/g.

This is also why a library entry is worth building with **every rate you measured** — the tour's closing step now says exactly that.

## Enter the rate either way

`0.05C` and `C/20` are the same number, so both boxes are there and linked as reciprocals — fill either and the other follows. Only the box you are *not* typing in is rewritten, so the caret never jumps, and a half-typed value is ignored rather than corrupting the rate. The equivalent charge time sits below in larger type: `= C/20 · 20 h per charge or discharge`, switching to minutes and seconds as the rate climbs.

## Capacity bars are keyed

The stacked bars were unlabelled — no way to tell active material from salt. Each segment is now named with its value in a key beneath the chart, and the key correctly **drops the salt on the Nth cycle**, where a sacrificial salt contributes nothing.

## Tour reworked around sections

Rebuilt so it moves through *sections* rather than lone elements:

- Entering a section lights the **whole thing** and dims the rest. Sub-steps leave that highlight alone and only **move the message**, so an area is explained as one continuous unit instead of re-darkening on every sentence.
- The lit section sits above the dimming layer, so **it stays usable** — which fixes the step that told users to click a rate chip they could not actually reach.
- **Advanced options** now opens on entry and closes again on the way out.
- The **sacrificial-salt** message sits beside its section, so switching the salt on mid-step expands the panel without burying the text (verified: the panel grows, the message stays clear).
- The **mass** step calls out that *entering neither side compares the two materials per cm²*.
- A closing step opens the **library** and explains adding a multi-rate material.
- Steps are filtered on **visibility**, not mere presence. Walking all of them turned up a real bug: the hero and results tabs live in a panel that stays hidden until the first Calculate, so on a fresh page those steps highlighted a zero-size box. A fresh page now runs 12 steps and a calculated one 15 — and the always-visible Calculate step describes what the results contain, so nothing is lost either way.
- Copy supports emphasis, and arrow-key navigation stands down while you are typing in the lit section.

The tour is now offered **on every load** rather than once ever — dismissing it is one click.
