author: terrence129
body:
## Summary

Adds the optional, server-controlled media upload/finalisation workflow after the core record and integration paths are stable.

## Implements

- BE-030
- owned pending asset creation
- bounded presigned upload instructions
- trusted metadata verification and `PENDING -> READY` finalisation
- record attachment permission checks and stale/deletion recovery

## Not included

- public bucket access
- arbitrary client object keys
- image transformation, moderation, OCR, or malware scanning
- general cloud credentials

## Contract

- OpenAPI paths/schemas: `POST /media/uploads`, `POST /media/{mediaAssetId}/finalise`, and `DELETE /media/{mediaAssetId}`
- content types and byte limit: JPEG, PNG, WebP; 5 MiB default
- upload TTL: 5 minutes default
- record-to-media cardinality: one active food or drink record per asset
- read delivery method: records expose only the opaque media asset ID; no bucket/key is part of the public contract

## Database / forward fix

- Uses immutable V5 `media_asset` metadata and record-owner foreign keys.
- New migration: none.
- Object cleanup is retry-safe after the row is soft-deleted; rollback application behaviour with the previous image, never reverse V5.

## Security

- owner/non-owner matrix: PASS (focused media tests)
- public-access-block/storage policy: local MinIO bucket created private; production IAM/public-access policy remains deployment configuration
- URL/signature log-redaction test: PASS by contract inspection (responses are never logged and errors expose no storage data)
- metadata mismatch tests: PASS

## Verification

- media tests: PASS — `./mvnw.cmd test -Dtest=*Media*` (7 tests)
- full Maven tests: PASS — `./mvnw.cmd test` (107 tests)
- Compose configuration: PASS; MinIO healthy with a private local bucket
- Postman `15 - Media Upload`: not run — Newman is not installed and the backend smoke process was blocked by local command policy before local-only environment injection

## Configuration

Added variable names only: `MEDIA_ENABLED`, `MEDIA_S3_BUCKET`, `MEDIA_S3_REGION`, `MEDIA_S3_ENDPOINT`, `MEDIA_S3_ACCESS_KEY`, `MEDIA_S3_SECRET_KEY`, `MEDIA_S3_KEY_PREFIX`, `MEDIA_UPLOAD_TTL`, `MEDIA_MAX_BYTE_SIZE`, `MEDIA_CLEANUP_DELAY`. No credentials or signed URLs are committed.

## Architecture / data flow

`MediaController -> create/finalise/delete use cases -> MediaPolicy -> MediaAssetRepository/ObjectStoragePort -> JDBC/S3 adapter`. Owner authorization is in owner-scoped SQL queries. Storage calls occur outside database transactions; lifecycle transition guards stay in V5 and SQL updates are conditional.

## Risks / follow-up

- Configure least-privilege bucket IAM and public-access block in each deployment.
- Add malware scanning only if it becomes an explicit deployment requirement.
- Run and attach the documented Newman folder after Newman is available in the delivery environment.

## Delivery evidence

- Linked BE/UC issues: BE-030; approved tracker URL was not provided.
- Exact commands/results: focused media and full Maven commands above both exited 0.
- Migration rollback/forward-fix impact: none; V5 unchanged.
- Cross-repository actions: none.

## Checklist

- [x] Client cannot influence object key, bucket, or ACL
- [x] Only owned READY assets can attach
- [x] Storage metadata is verified before finalisation
- [x] Presigned data is not logged or returned in errors
- [x] Failure cleanup is retry-safe
- [ ] Runbook and Postman evidence are attached (Newman unavailable locally)

author: bluefa
body:
## Summary

Saving the logical-DB skip policy returned a 500. The upstream answered `200` with a body that could not be parsed, and `send()` in the BFF client called `res.json()` on it:

```
[BFF] ← PUT .../excluded-databases/by-resource-id (200)
[v1] Unexpected error: SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input
    at JSON.parse (<anonymous>)
```

The write itself succeeded upstream every time — only the response handling failed, so the operator saw a save error for a save that had actually landed.

This is upstream drift, not a contract change: `install-v1.yaml` declares `200: SkipLogicalDatabaseResponse` for that PUT, and so does the 2026-07-28 API dump. The frontend is guarded so it stops 500ing, and the contract stays as published.

## What Changed

**Guard, scoped to the one endpoint that breaks its contract**
- `lib/bff/http.ts` — `send()` takes `emptyBodyOk`. Only `logicalDb.updateExcludedByResourceId` passes it; every other POST/PUT/DELETE and the whole GET path keep the strict behaviour, so a new contract break stays loud instead of being silently absorbed. A truncated body still throws — that is a real failure, not an empty response.
- `app/api/v1/.../excluded-databases/by-resource-id/route.ts` — parses `data ?? {}`. `SkipLogicalDatabaseResponse` is all-optional, so `{}` satisfies the schema.

**Read back what the server stored**
- `app/lib/api/logical-db.ts` — `updateExcludedLogicalDatabases` no longer reads the PUT response. It issues the GET and returns that, so the caller gets the server's own state rather than an echo.
- `lib/bff/mock/logical-db.ts` — the demo targets (1799/1583) served their excluded list straight from the task-queue fixture and never read what a PUT stored. Invisible while the client used the PUT echo; with the re-read it made a save look discarded. The fixture now seeds the list and a stored set wins.

**Stop the TC tab flickering on save**
- `LdbManageModal.tsx` — the modal bumped its own `loadKey` after saving, dropping both panels to a loading placeholder. It now adopts the returned list; the round trip also goes 2 → 1.
- `TcTab.tsx` / `ConfirmedInfoCard.tsx` — `onSaved` bumped the tab's `reloadKey`, which fed `null`/`[]` to all three cards until the refetch landed. Both now keep the last settled data on screen during a write-triggered refetch. First paint still shows its loading state.

## Validation

- `npm run lint` — 0 errors (33 pre-existing warnings)
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — PASS
- `npm run test:run` — 161 files / 1249 tests PASS, including two new cases in `lib/__tests__/bff-http.test.ts`: the opted-in PUT resolves on an empty body, and a caller that did not opt in still rejects with `SyntaxError`
- `npm run build` — PASS
- Manual round trip against the mock dev server:
  ```
  GET  → ivt_dev
  PUT  → 200   (ivt_dev + ivt_audit)
  GET  → ivt_dev + ivt_audit
  PUT  → 200   ([])
  GET  → []
  ```

## Contract Validation

`contract-check` FAILS with `API/runtime files changed without Swagger update`. This is the expected false positive: the swagger is the authority and must not be edited, and this PR deliberately changes no contract — it makes the client tolerate an upstream response that already violates the published one. Verified by parsing both documents:

| Document | 2xx responses | Declaring an empty body |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/swagger/install-v1.yaml` | 86 | 0 |
| `docs/api-docs.yaml` (2026-07-28 dump) | 95 | 1 — `204 POST /install/v1/services/{serviceCode}/jira-tickets/{cloudProvider}`, not called here |
| `docs/swagger/orchestrator-v1.yaml` | 15 | 1 — `204 GET .../pipelines/latest`, already handled at its callsite |

A 2xx-shape diff between the tracked contract and the 2026-07-28 dump reports no changes, so the endpoint in question is still documented as returning a body.

## Risks

- `emptyBodyOk` is opt-in on a single call, so no other endpoint's failure mode moves.
- Keeping stale data on screen during a refetch touches the whole TC tab, including reloads from Test Connection actions and credential changes. The tab looks steadier; if a refetch fails, the previous values stay visible rather than blanking.
- The extra GET after each save adds one request per save.
- Rollback: revert the branch. The upstream write path is untouched.

## Notes For Reviewer

- The real defect is upstream. The server returns `200` with an unparseable body while publishing `SkipLogicalDatabaseResponse`; it should either fill the body or declare `204`. Worth raising with the BFF owners — this PR only stops the frontend from 500ing on it.
- The evidence narrows the body to empty, whitespace-only, or truncated. `Content-Length` on a live PUT would settle it; that was not run because it overwrites real data.
- Please sanity-check the `settled` / `loading` changes in `TcTab.tsx` and `ConfirmedInfoCard.tsx` — they change what is shown during a refetch across the whole tab, not just the modal.

author: sporthubuy
body:
Full graph-native rebrand (**"Constellation"**) across the app, plus the wiring so agents run on **each user's own API keys**. Also fixes 3 pre-existing type bugs found along the way.

## Design system — "Constellation" (graph-native, dark)
The org's knowledge as a navigable night sky: nodes are bodies with state, edges are the lines between them, azure is the connective light. Deliberately avoids the AI-default light dashboard and the neon-on-black cliché. Direction was **user-pinned** (founder chose graph-native + dark + "distinctive but sober").

- New dark token system in `globals.css` — cool-ink surfaces (`#080b12`→`#1b2233`), azure `#5b9bff` accent, status-as-glow (verified/pending/draft/archived), radii 12–16px, single-elevation panels.
- Fonts: Inter → **Hanken Grotesk** (UI) + **JetBrains Mono** for coordinates only (ids, hashes, versions, trust).
- **Constellation logo** (`logo.tsx`) + a drawn **line-icon set** (`icon.tsx`) replacing every emoji-as-icon. This also removed leftover broken Material Symbols literals (`database` / `search` / `sort`).
- Dark shell (sidebar / topbar / canvas); graph page themed with node auras + edges.
- Global light→dark sweep across ~50 components; auth + landing included.
- `DESIGN.md` documents the built world.

## Per-user AI provider engines
Each member runs a shared agent on their own credentials.
- `model-router` accepts an explicit `apiKey` per request (server env fallback).
- `api/agents/chat` pulls the current user's stored key for the chosen provider from `user_ai_providers` (RLS-scoped); returns a clear message when none is configured.
- Agent wizard only enables providers the user has configured and auto-selects the first; links to Settings otherwise.

> **Note:** the `user_ai_providers` table required an unapplied migration (`20260729000017`). It has been applied to the Supabase project via `supabase db push` (additive: `CREATE TABLE` + RLS + index). The migration file was already in the repo.

## Pre-existing fixes (unrelated to the rebrand)
- `graph/page.tsx`: align `KnowledgeGraphFlow` props to the real data shape (drop unused `content`; use `source_ku_id`/`target_ku_id`) — **edges now render**.
- `agent-wizard`: remove undefined `model`/`temperature`/`tags` from the deploy summary.
- `api/visibility`: type the dynamically-selected row (removes the `GenericStringError` access).

## Tooling
- `.gitignore`s the vendored skills under `.agents/` and `.claude/skills/`; keeps `skills-lock.json` as the reinstall manifest (analogous to lockfile vs node_modules).

## Reviewer notes
- `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean (excluding the untouched `_wip/` dir).
- Theme is **dark-only** today; a light variant would reuse the same token names.
- Verified in-browser: dashboard, graph, knowledge, settings, agent wizard, command palette, landing + mobile.

author: cplieger
body:
Three commits from the archived review run, landed together because the last one depends on library releases that only published today.

- `feat: install kiro-cli through the shared pinstall library`
- `refactor: remove dead exported surface across the app`
- `fix: confine the archive mutations and stop rejecting dotted filenames`

The last commit closes a real exposure. `RestoreArchived` and `DeleteArchived` guarded their paths lexically, which is a NAME test that says nothing about what a path resolves to: a symlinked intermediate component (most plausibly `<storeDir>/archive` itself, which anything able to write `/config` can plant) redirected an ambient `os.Rename` or `os.Remove` clean out of the tree while reading as contained. Both operations now run through a kernel-confined `os.Root`, with the lexical gate kept as the cheap first check.

The scattered `strings.Contains(path, "..")` tests are replaced by `pathinside.HasDotDot` / `RelEscapes`, so a legitimate filename with two adjacent dots is no longer refused, and the startup writability probe is `atomicfile.ProbeWritable`, which stops discarding the close and remove outcomes.

`go.mod` carried three `replace` directives pointing at sibling working copies while `runesafe`, `atomicfile` and `pathinside` were unreleased. All three are published now (runesafe v1.3.0, atomicfile v2.5.0, pathinside v1.0.0), so the directives are gone and the requires name the real versions. Zero `replace` lines remain.

Verified locally: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and the full `go test ./...` suite pass with no replaces in `go.mod`.

author: brar
body:
Two changes, both about a check that reported success without having done its job.

**The hygiene sweep is all-or-nothing.** A narrowed sweep was indistinguishable from a clean one: two uninitialized submodules took a superproject run from eight repositories to six and it still printed OK, and a source tree with no repository at all reported OK across zero repositories. A `.git` presence test does not close it either — a gitlink whose target directory is gone is an ordinary file, so it passes while every git call beneath it exits 128 unnoticed and contributes no files to a total nobody breaks down. Each root must now enumerate, and the run fails naming any that do not.

The localization pipeline's clean-tree refusal and post-po4a restore are operations on a repository, and the container image build legitimately has none. Both are skipped there on the evidence of the local marker alone, never a git exit code: inferring absence from an exit code fails open, and a dubious-ownership failure would then skip both guards inside a real working tree — the one state that can lose a translator's uncommitted work.

**The Weblate configuration reference records what component creation overrides.** Creating a component returns settings that were never sent, silently — a glossary has unit management forced on, and a repository URL matching an existing component links the new one to it, taking its push branch so one catalogue's translations would land on another's branch. Each is recorded with its trigger rather than as a checklist, because the next component created met none of them.

author: danielnogueira8
body:
## Card size

The cards were doing too much. Now:

- **Chips**: icon + kind tag only ("News", "Draft", "Posts"), all on a single line — full labels live on the chip tooltip and in the evidence dialog (unchanged)
- **Text**: angle clamps to 3 lines, why-list to 2 bullets, with a "View more"/"Show less" toggle
- **Actions**: Start draft / Not today / Discard in one row (Discard is an icon button with tooltip)
- Tighter padding, `text-lg` headline

## Same news all the time — root cause

The dedup was fingerprint-based: `hash(headline + angle + source)`. A new angle on the same article produces a **different** fingerprint, so the same story came back every day — and nothing stopped two cards in one run from sharing a story (see screenshot: two "News Agent" cards both built on the executive-branding article).

Three guards:

1. **Cross-day exclusion** (`evidence.ts`): news sources (url or ref) used by ideas created in the last 7 days are filtered out of the evidence pool — matches the news eligibility window, so a story can only return once it would have aged out anyway. If everything is filtered, the lane honestly shows empty rather than re-pitching.
2. **Within-run dedup** (`index.ts`): the accept loop admits one idea per source (`sourceUrl ?? sourceRef`) per run, seeded with the sources already on the board — a top-up run can't re-pitch what's already showing, and two cards can never share a story.
3. **Prompt guardrail** (`synthesis.ts`): the model is told each idea must center on a different evidence source.

## Tests

- New: same-source rejection within a run, re-pitch rejection against the live board, used-news exclusion (url + ref), View-more collapse, chip rendering
- Full suite: 485 files / 5,208 tests green; `tsc --noEmit` clean

body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above. -->

# Social cards and page metadata

## Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
- **Fix social cards on `/map/{id}` routes.** `generateMapPageMetadata` only read the legacy `?document_id=` search param, so shared links to `/map/[map_id]`, `/map/edit/[map_id]`, and `/map/eval/[map_id]` rendered the generic site card. It now resolves the id from `params.map_id` as well.

- **Cache backend responses to protect the DB.** The document and thumbnail fetches in the OG route and `generateMapPageMetadata` use `next: {revalidate: 300}`, so scrapes and page views hit the backend at most once per document per 5 minutes per task. Note: the Next data cache is per-ECS-task and cleared on deploy.

body:
## Summary

Exposes `groundcover_storage_management_policy` (added in Terraform provider v1.22.0, BE-2550) as `kind: StorageManagementPolicy` in `storage.groundcover.com/v1alpha1`. Linear: [BE-2665](https://linear.app/groundcover/issue/BE-2665/add-storagemanagementpolicy-support-to-the-crossplane-provider).

- Bump TF provider dependency + `TERRAFORM_PROVIDER_VERSION` to 1.22.0; regenerate `config/schema.json` from the published registry version.
- Register the resource in the upjet config (`config/storagemanagementpolicy`, `config/provider.go`).
- Custom external-name config keyed on `data_type`: unlike every existing resource, this one has no server-assigned `id` — policies are seeded per data type and can only be updated. `IdentifierFromProvider` would fail reading `tfstate["id"]`; the guards keep the pre-adoption reconcile (empty external name) from clobbering the spec's `dataType`.
- Example manifest + README row documenting the semantics.

## Semantics (differ from Terraform, by design)

- The first reconcile adopts the seeded policy via Observe and reconciles it to the manifest. The TF Create-time guard against archiving undeclared custom rules never runs: **undeclared custom rules are archived** (declared config wins). Omitting `customRules`/`coldMoveDuration` entirely late-initializes them from the live policy instead.
- `kubectl delete` is state-only — there is no delete API; the policy stays active with its current configuration.
- A manifest for a nonexistent data type fails reconcile with the provider's "policies are seeded by groundcover and cannot be created" error.

## Verification

- `make generate` emits 18 resources (was 17); `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go mod tidy` clean.
- Regenerated `schema.json` from registry 1.22.0 is byte-identical to a local build of the merged TF branch.
- Runtime verified end-to-end: provider run out-of-cluster against a kind cluster with a request-logging mock of `/api/storage-management/{data_type}` (no real backend touched). Confirmed: adopt (GET → single PUT with correct `version` passthrough, undeclared rule archived) → `SYNCED=True/READY=True`, external-name = data type; spec edit → exactly one PUT, version bump reflected in `status.atProvider`; steady-state polls produce no further mutating calls (no perpetual drift); delete removes the k8s resource with zero API calls; bogus data type → `Synced=False` with the seeded-policy error.

No e2e test added on purpose: CI e2e runs against a live backend, and reconciling a storage policy there would mutate real retention settings (rule archival is irreversible).

body:
Addresses the question in #1006: how to embed an XChart inside a JavaFX layout container (e.g. a VBox with a ButtonBar) so everything resizes with the window.

## Changes

**JavaFXDemo.java** — now demonstrates the realistic embedding case from the issue:
- The chart's `SwingNode` is wrapped in a `StackPane` marked `VBox.setVgrow(..., Priority.ALWAYS)` — the key line, since a VBox only gives children their preferred height by default and `XChartPanel` reports a fixed preferred size.
- A `ButtonBar` with a Close button sits below the chart; the chart absorbs all resize space while the buttons keep their natural height.
- Swing content is now built on the EDT via `SwingUtilities.invokeLater`, as the SwingNode javadoc requires.

**xchart-demo/pom.xml** — JavaFX bumped 11.0.2 → 17.0.20 (demo module only):
- 11.0.2 ships x86_64-only macOS natives, so the demo crashed with `UnsatisfiedLinkError` on Apple Silicon; `mac-aarch64` artifacts start at 17.0.2.
- 17.x is the newest LTS line that still runs on Java 11 (JavaFX 21 raised the minimum JDK to 17), so this keeps the project's Java 11 baseline intact.

## Testing

Verified manually on an Apple Silicon Mac with `mvn javafx:run -pl xchart-demo`: window opens, chart fills the space above the button bar, and both resize correctly with the window.

Closes #1006

author: usermanoj
body:
The per-student panel showed wrong answers and the transcript as two lists, newest first. What it could not show is the **order** — and the order is where the teaching signal is.

Built entirely from timestamps already stored. **No new capture, no new consent surface**, nothing logged that was not logged yesterday. That constraint is the design: the alternative is recording how long a child looks at a page, which is behavioural surveillance of a minor and measures a left-open tab as diligence.

## What your real data says the moment it renders

```
59 events → 6 sittings

Right after asking:  —
Right without help:  4 of 13
Typical pause:       under a minute   (9 of 12 under 10s, median 6s)

─ 29 Jul 13:42 · 5 min · 13 answered, 7 asked
   13:42  ✗ Electromagnet in a door bell
   13:42  ✓ Early history of magnetism
   13:43  ✗ Early history of magnetism
   …
```

**Thirteen answers in five minutes. Nine of twelve gaps under ten seconds. Median six.** That is not a child at 31% — it is a child who stopped reading the questions. Accuracy alone could never have said that.

Also visible: four sittings with **0 answered** and 12, 4, 3 asks. Reading and asking, never testing themselves — which is exactly what the `answers_only` flag was written for.

## The three measures

**Right after asking** is the one that matters. A closed-corpus tutor that *guides* rather than answering is a claim about learning, and answers given straight after a request for help — against answers given cold — is the closest thing to evidence for it available without an experiment.

Shown as a plain fraction, **never a rate**: a child asks for help on the questions they find hard, so the aided figure being *lower* is the expected result, and a percentage would invite exactly the wrong comparison.

**Typical pause** is the median gap before an answer, within a sitting. Median because one interruption destroys a mean. Beside it, a count of answers under ten seconds — a count and not a rate, because three rushed out of five is a different conversation from three out of fifty.

## Everything is bounded by observation

A sitting's span is the distance between first and last action. It is a **floor on presence** and says nothing about attention, so it is rounded to minutes and never shown to the second.

`describeSpan` checks the raw span rather than the rounded minutes — a test caught thirty seconds being reported as **"1 min"**, which is the one direction this must not err in.

## Structure

SQL returns facts in time order. Where a sitting starts, whether help worked, and what counts as rushing are judgements, and they live in `src/lib/timeline.ts` with 20 tests — including that help from last night does not count for this morning, and that being *asked* a question (`askme`, `check`) is not being *helped*.

The timeline failing does not cost the panel its wrong answers or transcript. Those are the older and more important half, and they render without it.

382 tests, `tsc` clean, `eslint` clean, build green.

author: jreed91
body:
Three accessibility and legibility fixes found by building the app and driving it in the simulator on day one of the festival, when the schedule is live.

## Dynamic Type

Every font in the app was `.system(size:)`, which ignores the reader's text-size setting outright — set to `accessibility-extra-large`, the UI came back pixel-identical to the default. For an app read at arm's length in a field, in the sun, by a crowd of every age, that is the wrong default.

Adds `appFont(_:weight:design:)` in `Theme.swift` — a `@ScaledMetric`-backed `ViewModifier` that keeps each hand-tuned size exactly as it is at the default setting and scales from there. Each size is anchored to the built-in text style nearest it (11pt → `.caption2`, 32pt → `.title`), so a badge climbs steeply and a title barely moves rather than everything scaling at one rate. All 133 call sites across the app and the widget extension are converted.

One deliberate exception, commented in place: the initials in `ArtistImage`'s placeholder stay fixed. That is lettering sized as a fraction of a fixed thumbnail, not text to read, and scaling it would only overflow the box.

Testing at the maximum size surfaced two layouts that then genuinely broke, both fixed here:

- **The day picker split temperatures mid-number** — "86°" rendered as "8" / "6°", which reads as a different number. Now shrinks to fit, and is capped at `.accessibility1`: four days have to stay four columns, and there is nowhere for a fifth line to go. Everything below that header — the part you actually read — scales the whole way.
- **The weather card overflowed its row**, printing "Feels like" over the temperature. Now switches to a `VStackLayout` at accessibility sizes via `AnyLayout`.

## Tab bar over the map

`GroundsMapView` ignored the bottom safe area, running bright daylight artwork under the tab bar — whose material takes its contrast from whatever sits behind it, so "Schedule" and "Food & Drink" ended up on lime green.

Worth knowing for review: `HinterlandApp` already configures an opaque `UITabBarAppearance` with the comment *"make it opaque so rows don't ghost through it"*, and that no longer reaches the floating tab bar on current iOS. `.toolbarBackground(_:for: .tabBar)` was tried first and does not reach it either, so it is not in this diff — leaving a modifier that demonstrably does nothing would be worse than not having it. Ending the map at the safe area puts the app's own dark background back behind the bar, which works on every iOS version.

The filter chips and the accuracy caveat on that screen failed the same way — `.ultraThinMaterial` brightening to match the artwork — and are now an explicit dark scrim.

## Dietary filters

Nut-free and Sugar-free sat past the right edge of a horizontal scroller that ended flush with "Dairy-free", with no partial-chip peek and no indicator, while the vendor cards below went on showing "Nut-free" tags. The filter looked missing rather than hidden.

Replaced with a wrapping `FlowLayout` (new `Layout` conformance in `Components.swift`): all six show at once, "Clear" is reachable inline instead of off-edge — which also fixes the empty state having no way out — and it degrades to one chip per line as the chips grow, which a fixed-column grid would not have handled.

## Verification

Built clean with no warnings and checked on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator at default, `accessibility-extra-large`, and `accessibility-extra-extra-extra-large`. At the default setting the UI is unchanged from before this branch.

Not covered: the `NOW` badge, live-state card, and Live Activity never triggered during testing — the first set was hours out, so those paths need the simulator clock moved into a set.

## Scope

Configure P1-02 database environments and Laravel connection defaults for dedicated development and testing targets.

## Dev/test database isolation

- Development uses `student_document_management_dev`.
- Automated tests use `student_document_management_test`.
- The test account has no privileges on the development database.

## Least-privilege application accounts

- Development and testing use separate application accounts scoped to their own schemas.
- Accounts have only the schema-level privileges required by the application and migrations.
- Neither account has `GRANT OPTION` or server-administration privileges.
- Laravel runtime and automated tests do not use MariaDB root.

## Fail-closed PHPUnit bootstrap

The test bootstrap validates process-level database overrides before writing the authoritative test environment. Missing or matching test values are accepted; conflicting database or username values throw a redacted exception before Laravel connects. Passwords and connection strings are not disclosed.

## Database integration and regression tests

- Live integration coverage verifies the dedicated test database/account, UTC session timezone, and strict SQL mode.
- Regression coverage verifies missing overrides, matching overrides, rejected development database/username overrides, and password non-disclosure.

author: cooljin
body:
Setzt die abgestimmten Punkte aus der UI-Durchsicht um. Reines Frontend — **kein SQL nötig.**

## Behoben

**iOS-Zoom beim Antippen von Eingabefeldern.** Safari zoomt automatisch hinein, sobald ein Feld kleiner als 16px Schrift hat. Das betraf vor allem den Login — den ersten Bildschirm, den jeder sieht. Auf dem Handy sind Eingabefelder jetzt 16px; die große Suchleiste war mit 1.3rem ohnehin darüber und bleibt unverändert.

**`100vh` ist auf Handys nicht die Bildschirmhöhe.** Mobile Browser rechnen die Adressleiste nicht mit, wodurch der Inhalt höher war als der sichtbare Bereich. Ergänzt um `100dvh`, mit `100vh` als Rückfallebene.

**Klebende Hover-Effekte.** `.nav-item`, `.glass-panel` und alle Buttons hatten Hover-Zustände, die auf Touchscreens nach dem Antippen hängen blieben — dort gibt es kein „Maus weg". Alle Hover-Regeln liegen jetzt in `@media (hover: hover)`. Der aktive Zustand der Navigation bleibt davon unberührt.

**Zu kleine Tippflächen** bei den Plus/Minus-Knöpfen. Gelöst über ein unsichtbares 44px-Overlay (`.tap-target`) statt über mehr Polsterung — **optisch ändert sich dadurch nichts.**

## Neu

**Menge direkt im Suchergebnis.** Kleiner Schrittzähler in der Produktkarte; der angezeigte Preis rechnet die Menge mit. Spart den Umweg über den Warenkorb, wenn jemand fünf Dosen von einer Sorte will.

**Letzte Suchbegriffe.** Die letzten sechs Begriffe erscheinen als antippbare Chips unter der Suchleiste — mit `backdrop-filter: blur(14px)`, passend zum Rest. Gespeichert werden nur die Wörter, keine Ergebnisse.

**Ziehen zum Aktualisieren** auf Touchgeräten. Greift nur, wenn die Seite ganz oben steht und nach unten gezogen wird; normales Scrollen bleibt unberührt.

**„Als App installieren"-Hinweis.** Erscheint ab dem dritten Besuch und lässt sich dauerhaft wegklicken. Unter Android mit echtem Installieren-Knopf, unter iOS mit Anleitung (Safari kennt `beforeinstallprompt` nicht).

**Offline-Hinweis.** Bisher schlugen Anfragen ohne Netz still fehl und man sah unbemerkt veraltete Daten.

**Bewegung reduzieren wird respektiert.** Wer das im System aktiviert hat, bekommt den Aurora-Hintergrund und die Zierde-Animationen angehalten. Spart nebenbei Akku auf älteren Geräten.

## Geändert

**Abmelden steht bei normalen Nutzern jetzt im Profil**, zusammen mit dem angemeldeten Benutzernamen. Die untere Leiste hat damit drei statt vier Einträge — mehr Platz für die Bereiche, die täglich gebraucht werden. **Für Admins bleibt es in der Navigation.**

## Bewusst nicht geändert

Suchergebnisse bleiben auf dem Handy einspaltig. Bei euch sucht jeder gezielt nach einem Produkt, niemand stöbert — da bringt die zweite Spalte nichts.

## Getestet

`npm run lint` und `npm run build` laufen sauber. Zusätzlich die Login-Seite in einem iPhone-Viewport (390×844) geladen: rendert fehlerfrei, `.form-input` liegt bei berechneten **16px**, `min-height` löst auf exakt die Viewport-Höhe auf.

Die eingeloggten Bildschirme konnte ich nicht gegen eine echte Datenbank prüfen — Suchergebnisse, Warenkorb und Ziehen zum Aktualisieren solltest du einmal auf dem Handy antesten.

author: giunatale
body:
Four consumer-side hardening items.

## Never-connected consumers now enter safe mode

`LastVSCRecvTime` was only ever set on packet receipt, and the getter fell back
to the current block time when unset, so a consumer that never received a
validator-set update was never considered stale and never entered safe mode.
The clock is now armed at the first block after genesis: the genesis block
itself carries the genesis file's `genesis_time`, which may predate launch, so
arming any earlier would burn safe-mode budget before the chain produced a
block. `SafeModeThreshold` staleness therefore accrues from launch. An explicit
timestamp from a restart genesis still wins, a restart genesis without the
field arms the same way, and every accepted update re-arms the clock. (A
pre-VAAS standalone chain deliberately stays unarmed until its first update: a
live standalone economy must not enter restricted mode mid-changeover.) The
liveness documentation asserted the old behavior and was corrected.

## A packet can no longer empty the validator set

A well-formed packet whose application would leave the consumer with an empty
validator set halts the chain at EndBlock. `OnRecvVSCPacketV2` now rejects such
packets with an error acknowledgement before any state write, for snapshots
(the packet's positive-power updates are the entire resulting set) and for
diffs (the current set overlaid with pending changes plus the packet,
reproducing exactly what EndBlock would apply). Rejection happens inside the
IBC cache context, so no state leaks; out-of-order stale packets still
deduplicate to a success acknowledgement first, preserving replay semantics.
Heartbeat diffs over a live set are unaffected.

## Photon fee decorator: bypass closed, bootstrap and exemptions made explicit

The expected fee denom stays derived from the pinned provider client
(`ibc/SHA256("transfer/<clientID>/uphoton")`): under client authentication the
pin moves at most once at bootstrap, and IBC vouchers can only ever arrive over
the adopted, routable client, so the derived denom tracks exactly the denom
real vouchers carry, while a static genesis-time parameter could never name the
adopted client id. Vouchers bridged over any other path are deliberately not
accepted: they cannot be verified locally, and accepting them would take a
governance-maintained denom whitelist. The decorator godoc documents both.

Behavior splits on pin routability:

- Bootstrap (no pin, or the unroutable genesis pin): full no-op. No voucher can
  exist yet, so there is nothing to police, and rejecting the fee-less relayer
  traffic of that phase would block the first validator-set update forever. The
  message-filter decorator remains the traffic restriction for that phase.
- Enforcing (routable pin): every fee coin must be the derived voucher denom
  AND the fee must be non-empty, closing the empty-fee bypass. Gas simulation
  is exempt from the non-empty check only; a wrong denom still rejects in
  simulation.

Transactions made up exclusively of infrastructure messages stay exempt while
enforcing: `/ibc.core.*` and `/cosmos.gov.*`, with the user-originating
`MsgSendPacket` carved out, and one non-exempt message makes the whole tx
enforced. The vouchers the policy demands can only arrive in relayer-submitted
packet deliveries, so pricing those in photon would deadlock the chain the
moment the policy activates. What exempt transactions pay stays node-local
min-gas-prices policy: a tokenless core shard launches with zero prices and
genesis-declared relayer and owner accounts, and raises prices once photon
circulates.

## The decorator is wired, not shipped inert

`PhotonFeeDecorator` is now always part of the reference consumer app's ante
chain, inserted immediately before fee deduction, and the on/off decision is a
**consumer module parameter** (`photon_fees_enabled`, default false) rather than
node-local configuration.

That distinction is the point. The decorator rejects transactions in
`FinalizeBlock`, not only in `CheckTx`, so it is consensus-relevant: driving it
from `app.toml` would let two validators disagree on whether a transaction is
valid, diverging the app hash and halting the chain, and the trigger would be
as mundane as a validator joining after launch with the shipped default. As a
parameter it comes from state, so every node agrees, and it round-trips through
genesis. The provider-authored consumer genesis always writes it off; enabling
takes a hand-authored genesis or a later `MsgUpdateParams` from the params
authority, where the embedding app wires one. The reference consumer app wires
no governance, so there the genesis choice is final.

New app-level tests build the real consumer app once per parameter setting and
run fully signed transactions through the real ante chain against real keepers:
enabled + voucher denom accepted and deducted; enabled + wrong denom rejected
(from an unfunded account, proving the rejection is policy, not funds); enabled
+ empty fee rejected; bootstrap no-op; disabled permissive. The infrastructure
exemption set is pinned by dedicated ante tests.

The main e2e suite runs its consumer with `photon_fees_enabled` set in the
consumer genesis, the way a real core shard would enable it, so the whole suite
exercises the policy, and `testPhotonFeeEnforcement` proves the loop end to
end: a native-fee tx is rejected by the ante, an ICS-20 v2 transfer bridges
uphoton in while enforcement is on, and a bank send paying voucher fees
commits.

## Testing

Unit + app-module suites green (including the app module's first ante tests);
`golangci-lint` clean; both Docker e2e suites pass: the main suite 17/17 with
photon fees enforced suite-wide, the liveness suite 5/5 including its safe-mode
scenarios under the BeginBlock-armed clock.

author: alexey-metaengage
body:
## Context

Follows #3212 / #3283 (both closed). The position there was to keep the fail-closed `RAISE EXCEPTION` for the RLS-enable migrations (v24/v29/v31/v35) when the migrating role lacks BYPASSRLS, because on a managed-Postgres split (migrator role != runtime app role) enabling RLS without BYPASSRLS can lock the app out of its own data. That default is correct and this PR keeps it unchanged.

## What this adds

An **opt-in** escape hatch for the single-principal case: when the migrating role also OWNS the tables and is the runtime role (e.g. a managed Cloud SQL `postgres` that cannot hold BYPASSRLS but owns every table), the owner is exempt from RLS as long as no `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` / policies apply, so enabling RLS is a harmless no-op - yet the hard failure permanently wedges the migration chain.

Setting `GBRAIN_RLS_ALLOW_NONBYPASS=1` downgrades the abort to a `RAISE WARNING` and proceeds with the `ALTER`. **Unset (the default) is unchanged fail-closed behavior.**

## Why it's safe

- Default preserved: with the env var unset, all four migrations still emit `RAISE EXCEPTION`. The existing structural test (`test/migrate.test.ts` - "fails loudly on non-BYPASSRLS roles instead of silently bumping version") stays green.
- One env var, read at module load, flips all four migrations together.
- Precedent already in-tree: v32 already warns-and-skips OAuth-table RLS for the same non-BYPASSRLS case.

## Implementation

A single `rlsBypassGuard(label)` helper returns the WARNING-and-proceed statement when the env var is set, else the existing `RAISE EXCEPTION`. The four DO-blocks call it in place of the hardcoded exception. No runner or connection changes.

author: animmosmith
body:
## Summary
Fixes #407.

\`make_montage()\` always fills the same fixed rectangular canvas regardless of how much data went into it, which makes visual density comparisons across datasets with different sample sizes (e.g. several depth bins with different numbers of raw images) misleading - every montage looks equally "full" no matter how much data it actually represents.

\`make_montage_scaled()\` packs particles largest-first within a **circular** boundary whose *area* (not radius) is controlled by \`rel_scale\` - the radius scales with \`sqrt(rel_scale)\` specifically so that area scales linearly with it. Set \`rel_scale\` proportional to each dataset's relative sample size (e.g. number of raw images, or total sample volume) against a shared reference, generate one montage per dataset, and place them side by side: a bin with half the raw images of another gets half the circle area to fill, so the packed density becomes a fair, directly comparable visual signal across montages.

A few other differences from \`make_montage()\`:
- **Grayscale output** rather than RGB, since particles from monochrome instruments (e.g. holographic imaging) don't need three channels — this also means \`pyopia.plotting.montage_plot()\`'s existing \`cmap='grey'\` argument actually takes effect (currently a no-op against \`make_montage\`'s RGB output).
- **Gap-aware packing**: each particle's silhouette is dilated by \`gap\` pixels before placement, so packed particles keep a visual buffer rather than touching.
- No new plotting code needed - the existing \`montage_plot()\` already handles the scale reference via matplotlib, so this only needed to produce a montage image, not its own scale-bar rendering.

## Test plan
- [x] Manually verified with synthetic particle ROIs (grayscale blob images with real internal contrast) that particles are placed correctly (non-background pixel values present) and that the circular boundary area scales as intended (`rel_scale=0.25` produces ~25% of the pixel area of `rel_scale=1.0`, within ~0.3% of the expected ratio)
- [x] `flake8` clean

author: chuckplayer
body:
Cut two of the plan spine, plus three fixes for gaps the exercise surfaced.

Closes the hole where a plan could ship **committed alongside code that contradicted a design call it recorded**. Cut one committed the plan so a reviewer could read intent against implementation; nothing checked the narrative half. A live run proved it: a plan stated the test runner would be Vitest, the code shipped `node` + `assert`, and the gate returned PASS.

## The mechanism

`tech-lead` writes `## Deviations` as a **self-describing sentinel** and never fills it in. An empty section cannot be told apart from an unfilled one, and *"indistinguishable from nobody looking"* is this pack's recurring failure — the sentinel makes *nothing diverged* and *nobody checked* two detectable states.

Engineers **cannot read the plan** — it is uncommitted and invisible inside a worktree — so `/implement` step 5 pastes the relevant stated calls **verbatim** into each dispatch and requires an explicit "none" in the handoff. Step 10 replaces the sentinel from engineer handoffs *and the session's own departures*; in practice the session is the more common source. **Commit timing is unchanged** — deliberately not reopened, since it was cut one's most contested question.

## Gate 4a — three tiers, teeth in the cheap ones

| Tier | Checks | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Section absent → FAIL malformed; sentinel intact → FAIL not reviewed | Mechanical |
| 2 | An engineer-reported departure missing from the section | Near-mechanical |
| 3 | A stated call the diff contradicts, nothing recorded | Judgment, bounded |

**Tier 3 works from the calls, never from the diff.** It looks up only the concrete artifact each call names, so a call naming nothing specific has **no lookup target** and drops out of scope *by construction* — the agent is never asked "is this too vague to judge?", only "what artifact does this name?" That is the difference between a rule and a coin flip, and it is why the tier cannot cry wolf on prose.

**Pattern names are explicitly excluded**, and this is the case worth remembering because it looks checkable and is not. "Use the repository pattern" names a pattern, not an artifact; whether a given `DbContext` reference violates it is an architecture judgment with legitimate readings either way. **That judgment already has an owner** — `code-reviewer` reads `docs/CONVENTIONS.md` for exactly this, `smell-reviewer` catches the structural form, both run earlier, and a code-reviewer Critical already blocks.

A Tier-3 FAIL must quote the call verbatim **and** name a contradicting `file:line`; anything less is an advisory. **Ambiguity advises rather than fails**, inverting the rule for bars, with the reason recorded so it does not read as a contradiction: an unverifiable *bar* means verification did not happen, which is what the gate establishes; an ambiguous *call* is a planning imprecision from stages back, and failing there punishes the wrong party. The remedy for a Tier-3 finding is **one line in `## Deviations`**, not a code change — a gate whose cheapest correct response is "record it" induces the behaviour wanted; one whose cheapest response is "argue with the reviewer" gets switched off.

## Proven live before shipping

Four runs in a throwaway repo after `install.sh`, each verified **by effect** — no commit, tree untouched, plan hash matched before and after:

- **Tier 1** — FAILed naming `plan deviations section not reviewed`, no commit
- **Tier 2** — FAILed as mechanical *"regardless of accuracy"*, and separately flagged that the claim did not match the diff, keeping the tiers cleanly separated
- **Tier 3** — FAILed quoting the call verbatim, the contradicting `file:line`, and why both cannot hold; named recording as the remedy
- **PASS** — committed the plan alongside the code, plan kept, no status field flipped

Emission was also verified independently: `tech-lead`, given **no directory and no format**, resolved past an unfilled `[e.g., docs/plans/]` placeholder and emitted the full nine-heading shape with bars paired at exactly two spaces.

## Three fixes the exercise surfaced

**A worktree branch with zero commits merged nothing and reported success.** `git merge-base --is-ancestor` is trivially satisfied when a worktree branch sits at the feature branch's commit. Engineers are told **not** to commit — merge-reviewer owns commits — so that state is routine: work exists, uncommitted, in the worktree. Ancestry passed, then `git merge --no-ff` merged an empty branch and reported success, **silently stranding the work**. Two correct rules composing into a hole, arriving through the *green* path. Fixed at all four call sites — `/implement` step 5b, `/refactor`, `/scaffold`, merge-reviewer Step 0 — which now route an empty commit list to the transplant path. Hit live twice today.

**`merge-reviewer` Step 0c omitted untracked files from branch scope**, while its comment claimed "committed + uncommitted". `git diff` reports only tracked files, so newly created files were absent from scope though `git add -A` would still commit them. Gate 4 searches that scope for test files — so a run whose only tests lived in a **new** file would be told no tests exist and blocked. A false FAIL on good work, shipped weeks ago. Found because merge-reviewer noticed the gap and worked around it unprompted rather than reporting a scope it knew was incomplete.

**The engineer departure duty belonged to one caller, not the agent.** It lived only in `/implement` step 5's prose, so an engineer dispatched by anything else carried no such duty. Now in CLAUDE.md's Engineer responsibilities. That heading was **also stale** — it named four engineers, omitting `python-engineer` and `infrastructure-engineer`, both of which exist and both of which ran today, so both had been exempt from the test-verification duties by omission rather than decision. All six are now listed.

## Also included

**`devils-advocate` now flags non-falsifiable stated calls** in the pass where it already pressure-tests bars. Gate coverage is a function of how well calls are written, and this is the only place it gets checked. One line each in `/plan` step 3 and `/implement` step 3, no new file. This reverses an earlier judgement that the duty was unearned until a thin Tier 3 was observed — it targets a risk accepted twice at close to zero cost.

**Bar amendment is codified.** A recorded deviation can leave a bar unsatisfiable rather than unmet, testing an abandoned design. The session may amend it only as a named consequence of a recorded deviation, quoting the original wording, narrowly scoped; merge-reviewer FAILs a bar amended with no deviation behind it. Unbounded, that licence would gut acceptance bars, since "unsatisfiable" would always be cheaper to fix by rewriting the bar than by fixing the code.

**README** gains a flow-selection table, a *What actually blocks* section (blocking vs advisory authority had no coverage at all), the Plan Spine, and the twelve design patterns.

**Two memory notes.** A decision record for the gate design, and `agent-output-must-be-attributable-to-be-evidence` — the pack's rule was *verify effects, not reports*; today's testing added **verify the effect came from the thing you tested**, after three attribution failures of my own: a stale agent silently repairing its own evidence when questioned, an emptied directory that was not isolation because the previous agent was still alive, and a cleanup that destroyed a result mid-flight.

## The mechanism was used on its author

**Five deviations are recorded against this cut's own plan**, including that it ships six files where the plan called five. None were bad calls — that is the point. The mechanism keeps the record honest about overrides rather than preventing them.

One of those entries documents a bootstrapping wrinkle: the plan for the Deviations feature arrived **without** a Deviations section, because tech-lead wrote it before the template had o

author: kinggh0stee
body:
Full-project review pass over the app module, manifest, Gradle config and resources, with fixes applied.

## High priority

**Duplicate fragments on activity recreation** — `MainActivity` and `DetailsActivity` added their fragment unconditionally in `onCreate`. On process-death restore or a configuration change the FragmentManager restores the existing fragment *and* a new one is added: overlapping UI, doubled network loads, and a duplicated login/subscription flow. Both now guard on `savedInstanceState == null`.

**Unguarded JSON parsing on the main thread** — `getSubs`, `getVideos`, `getVideo` and `getLive` called `gson.fromJson` without a try/catch. Volley delivers on the main thread, so a 200 carrying a Cloudflare or proxy HTML interstitial threw `JsonSyntaxException` and crashed the app; `getVideos` could additionally pass a null array into a non-null Kotlin callback, NPE-ing in `gotVideos`. All four parse defensively now. `getSubs` also required a JSON array instead of substring-matching `"errors"`, which misclassified any payload merely containing that word.

## Security

**`allowBackup` was `true`** — the DataStore file written by `AuthManager` holds the full Sauce+ session credential (`__Host-sp-sess` + `cf_clearance`), and Auto Backup copied it off-device into the user's Google account. Disabled, with a comment recording why.

## Medium

- **Cancelled login was a dead end.** The login `ActivityResultLauncher` only handled `RESULT_OK`, so backing out or hitting the page-load-error path left the user on an empty browse screen with no route back into login short of restarting the app. Now shows a retry dialog.
- **Stale card content.** `CardPresenter.setData` gated the entire bind on the thumbnail being present, so a recycled card kept the previous video's title, description and tags for any post without one. Every field binds unconditionally; only the image load is conditional, and the placeholder is set explicitly when there is no thumbnail.
- **Pagination accounting.** `gotVideos` treated a creator's later pages as an initial load when its first page came back empty, driving `subCount` negative and re-firing `fetchProgressAsync()` on every subsequent page. Pagination is now keyed off `initialBatchComplete`. Separately, `paginationInFlight` was cleared by the first response to arrive, defeating the counter that tracks the rest; `loadNextPage`'s `AtomicInteger` now owns the flag exclusively. Offset paging can also re-serve items when new posts land between requests, so appends dedupe by guid.
- **`getTagColor` crashed on an empty tag** — indexed `[0]` on the tag name.
- **Related-video clicks passed the wrong object** — the already-open video, under a key `DetailsActivity` does not read. Unreachable today, but a trap once a related row exists.

## Smaller items

- `Delivery`/`Group` collections made nullable to match what Gson actually produces, so the existing null checks are meaningful rather than dead to the compiler.
- Image loaders reuse the session User-Agent instead of a hardcoded string, consistent with the project's Cloudflare UA rule.
- `SocketClient` reuses a single `OkHttpClient` rather than allocating connection and thread pools per connect.
- The livestream probe sends the User-Agent but deliberately **not** the session cookie — it targets a CDN host that authenticates by URL token, and the cookie is the whole account credential.
- `getReponseStatus` typo fixed.
- ProGuard now keeps `@JavascriptInterface` methods, so the WebView login probe survives R8 whenever `minifyEnabled` is turned on.
- Removed unused `ItemViewSelectedListener`, `MapExtension`, `getCreatorByName` and `REQ_CODE_*` constants; refreshed stale comments (`sails.sid`, OkHttp version) and CLAUDE.md's test/SDK notes.

## Verification

`assembleDebug`, `testDebugUnitTest` (15 tests, all passing) and `lintDebug` all pass.

Note that this environment had no Android SDK installed; I installed one to verify. The platform package is `platforms;android-37.0` — plain `android-37` does not exist, which is worth knowing for CI. This is recorded in CLAUDE.md.

No device testing was possible here, so the D-pad and playback behaviour of the CardPresenter and login-retry changes is unverified on real hardware.

author: frankies2727
body:
## What & why

Replaces the #174 keyword-threshold omnibus hack (**reverted here**) with the approach the local model is actually good at: after the cheap keyword net selects a bill, the LLM reads the real bill text and confirms the bill is **genuinely about the feed's topic** before posting.

This fixes the reported failure — NC's entire state budget ("2026 Appropriations Act") landing in the AI/Crypto feed because its 449-tag subject list happened to include `CRYPTOCURRENCY & NFTS` — without the brittle size heuristics a keyword rule needs.

## Changes

- **`topic.py`** — revert #174; add `Topic.relevance_gate_system_prompt()` (a strict "is this bill genuinely and substantively about <topic>?" classifier).
- **`post_to_bluesky.py`** — add `is_on_topic(b)`: one focused LLM call on the extracted bill text (reuses `_get_full_text`'s cache — no double extraction), returning a boolean. **Fails open**: gate disabled, no groundable text, or any extraction/LLM/parse error → `True`, so a hiccup never drops a run's posts. Toggle with `RELEVANCE_GATE=0`.
- **All four daily posters** (bluesky / x / threads / instagram) skip a selected bill when the gate says off-topic. Applied in the **daily loops only** — manual force-posts stay ungated.
- **README** — documents the gate as a pipeline step.

## Why a separate call (tested on the production model, gemma3:4b)

- A **separate focused relevance call is reliable**; **folding** relevance into the copy-writing call is **not** — with both tasks in one prompt the 4B model set `on_topic=true` for the NC budget while admitting *in the summary* that it has no AI content. So relevance is its own call, run before copy.

## Verification (real bills, real model)

| Bill | Feed | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| NC "2026 Appropriations Act" (whole budget) | AI/Crypto | **off-topic → skip** ✓ |
| GA AI-in-insurance | AI/Crypto | on-topic ✓ |
| MO AI provisions | AI/Crypto | on-topic ✓ |
| MN school-bus safety | Transportation | on-topic ✓ |
| MN tax-increment financing | Taxation | on-topic ✓ |
| IA renewable-energy siting | Environment | on-topic ✓ |
| MO doula coverage | Reproductive rights | on-topic ✓ |
| DE banking (matched crypto kw) | AI/Crypto | off-topic (defensible) |

**Zero false-negatives** on the legit body-matched bills. End-to-end through the integrated `is_on_topic()`: NC `False`, GA `True`.

## Cost
One extra local-LLM call per **selected** bill (a handful per run), before the existing copy call; off-topic bills cost only that one call. Ollama is already running in the posting workflows, so **no workflow changes**.

## Note
Per request, **not merging** — opening for review. Ready to merge on your go-ahead.

author: michaeltroelsen
body:
Second clean sweep in a row. All six closed on **non-tautological** matches — a relocated rebuild at a different base that still traces register-write-exact, not merely a byte-identical reconstruction.

| Card | Result |
|---|---|
| `stephen-legg` | 6 files, all 32 subtunes, **0/3,834** write divergences, 812–1270 bytes per file genuinely differing in the relocated control |
| `steve-bak` | 6/6 files byte-exact **and cycle-exact**; all six confirmed to share one driver |
| `jason-briggs` | 5/5 files, full coverage, no partial scope |
| `chris-grigg` | 5/5 files byte-exact with a relocation control on each; scope stated as the *engine* explicitly |
| `marco-scheepers` | 5/5 tagged files byte-exact and relocation-trace-exact, with an explicit note that the tag is **not** one routine |
| `rene-romijn` | 6/6 files byte-exact — see caveat |

## The one soft spot, stated rather than smoothed over

`rene-romijn`'s relocation-invariance control is clean on **5 of 6** files (6,184 writes, 0 divergences). `Orion_Intro` diverges at every base tried (52/1388 writes, voice 3 only), and two of the five clean files pass only at page-aligned bases. That is a defect in the *relocation control*, not in the byte-exact native reconstruction — and it is localised rather than hand-waved: the wrong frequency-table index tracks the control base's **low byte**, with an `adc` lacking a preceding `clc` in the note-index search loop as the candidate mechanism. The card says all of this.

That card also closed its own central identity question from primary evidence in the payloads: every tagged file carries a plain-ASCII credit block naming **R. Romijn as the routine's author**, independently corroborating the previously single-sourced "Musicians on Duty" affiliation.

## Counts

170 → **176 verified** / 61 in-progress / 283 stub, across 520 cards.

`lessons_learned` **79–84** appended. 79 is the most immediately useful, and it records a real dead end as well as a technique:

- **Technique**: run the relocation control at *both* a page-aligned and a non-page-aligned base. One extra 64tass run, and the pass/fail split classifies the defect into three states instead of two.
- **Dead end**: lesson 64's group-complement isolation is structurally **inapplicable** to a relocated build. Reverting a code operand to its "pristine" native value points execution at the *original* base, so every group breaks playback and the experiment carries no signal — which superficially reads as "no group is responsible". The valid analogue is bisecting between two control builds at adjacent bases.

`blackbird` is deliberately **not** in this PR; its solo run is being re-applied to its card separately.

`check-cards.js`: 520 cards, 520 ids, 0 broken prose links, 0 failures.

author: adammarquette
body:
Closes #412.

## What & why

X1's **last unbuilt item** — the epic could not close without it. AI spend was recorded to the `AIUsage` ledger and emitted to Prometheus, but nothing rendered it: Grafana had boards for execution, auto-flatten and synthetic risk, and none for cost.

This adds the provisioned **AI usage & spend** dashboard, reading the LLM meter (gh#477, `ai_llm_*`) and the embedding meter (gh#403, `ai_embed_*`) — both on the `MarqSpec.TradingCopilot.Ai` meter. It answers: what is AI costing in total and against the daily cap, is the ADR-0008 tiering bet actually paying, where is spend going, and are calls failing.

**The stated blocker is gone.** #412 said *"blocked by #16 — #16 is open with zero sub-issues and zero code, no `ILlmProvider` anywhere in `src/`"*. A2 has since shipped the provider (#423), ledger (#431), governor (#448), escalation (#449) and the LLM meter (#477). Epic #26's note is corrected in this PR.

## Panels

Total spend (24h) · governor headroom vs the daily cap · LLM calls · 30-day rollup · spend **by model tier** (the ADR-0008 bet, measured) · **LLM vs embeddings** · calls by outcome · tokens in/out by tier · embedding outcomes · latency p95/p99 **with exemplars**.

## Verified against a live stack — not transcribed

This is the part worth reading. I stood up `prometheus` + `otel-collector`, emitted the **exact** instrument set through the real collector → Prometheus path, and read back `/api/v1/label/__name__/values`. The cost series are actually:

```
ai_llm_cost_usd_USD_total
ai_embed_cost_usd_USD_total
```

The exporter appends the `"USD"` unit **verbatim and case-sensitively**, and because the instrument name already ends in lowercase `usd` the duplicate-suffix check does not match. **The intuitive `ai_llm_cost_usd_total` returns no series** — I ran it as a negative control. A spend panel over that name shows *"No data"* forever, which reads as *"nothing was spent"*: the exact invisible-spend failure this dashboard exists to prevent.

ADR-0002 had already recorded this same unit trap once (`_milliseconds_bucket`) and concluded queries must be *"validated against a live Prometheus rather than transcribed"*. It recurred; the ADR now records it a second time with the rule stated plainly.

Then **every panel query** was run against live multi-point data — all returned values; the negative control returned none. Grafana provisioned the file from a clean `up`, re-read it after edit, and logged no dashboard errors. Probe data was destroyed with `down -v` so it cannot masquerade as real spend.

## Two limits — filed, not papered over

- **Headroom** is drawn against a Grafana constant mirroring `Governor__DailyBudgetUsd`, because Prometheus cannot read application config. Drift risk is real → **#506** emits the cap as a gauge.
- **Per-feature** attribution isn't possible yet: the meter tags model/tier/outcome, not feature. The LLM-vs-embeddings split stands in — lossless today, since every LLM row is `Feature = Triage` (gh#449) → **#507** adds the tag.
- The stuttering metric name → **#505**. Whichever fix lands, this dashboard's queries must move in the same PR or the spend panels go blank; that coupling is stated on the issue.

Neither is enforcement: a meter is export-only, so the governor still caps on the `AIUsage` ledger floor (gh#448).

## Docs in lockstep

- **ADR-0002** — dashboard inventory row + an update recording the naming finding and the "never transcribe a metric name" rule.
- **Engineering §7** — the Grafana half marked delivered, with both limits named.
- **Epic #26** — the stale *"blocked by #16 / zero code"* note corrected.

No application code, schema, compose or `.env` change — provisioning only.

author: justinchuby
body:
## What

Implements `com.microsoft::LinearAttention` (Gated DeltaNet / gated delta-rule linear attention) on the **CUDA EP** — the recurrent attention of the Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next **hybrid** family, and the second-ranked CUDA coverage gap after `CausalConvWithState` (#480). Together they land the hybrid (Mamba / linear-attention) decode path on CUDA.

Refs #67, #384. **Draft — do not merge.**

## Design (see `.squad/decisions/inbox/cohaagen-linear-attention-design.md`)

**Oracle:** the CPU EP kernel `onnx-runtime-ep-cpu/src/kernels/linear_attention.rs` (a faithful port of ORT `contrib_ops/cpu/bert/linear_attention.cc`).

**Key structural fact:** each column `j` of the per-head state matrix `S[d_k, d_v]` evolves *independently* — retrieval `r[j]=Σ_i S[i,j]·k[i]`, the delta/linear update, and readout `o[j]=scale·Σ_i q[i]·S[i,j]` all touch only column `j`. So the op is embarrassingly parallel across `(b, h_kv, j)`; each is one sequential scan over `t`.

**Mapping:** one CUDA thread per `(b, h_kv, j)`; each thread keeps its state column in a **per-thread f32 register array** and runs the whole recurrent scan in **f32**, so the arithmetic matches ORT's `float` CPU kernel regardless of I/O dtype (`f16`/`bf16` widened on read, narrowed on write). No shared memory, no cross-thread reduction, no scratch alloc.

## Coverage

- All four `update_rule` variants: `linear`, `gated`, `delta`, `gated_delta`.
- Standard GQA (`H_q ≥ H_kv`) **and** inverse GQA (`H_q < H_kv`, the 9b config).
- Key-head sharing (`n_k < H_kv`), per-head **and** per-key-dim decay, per-head **and** shared beta.
- Step-to-step state carry via `past_state` / `present_state`.
- Dtypes `Float32` / `Float16` / `BFloat16`, f32 accumulation.
- Claim gate fail-closes on unsupported dtypes and `d_k > 256`.

## Verification (GPU device 0)

- **Parity vs CPU EP oracle** (`tests/linear_attention_gpu.rs`, 4 tests): every config's `output` **and** `present_state` compared to the CPU kernel (tol f32 2e-4 / f16 5e-2 / bf16 2e-1), plus a **chained-vs-full state-carry** proof (two 3-step halves chained through `past_state` == one 6-step run). All green.
- **Coverage-of-coverage**: `LinearAttention` added to `CUDA_COVERED_OPS` + a `dedicated()` conformance entry; `every_covered_op_has_a_conformance_entry` and `dedicated_suites_exist_and_name_their_op` pass. Full `cuda_conformance_gpu` suite: 4/4.
- **Lib**: 274/274.
- **Placement proof** (probe over real Foundry models): LinearAttention nodes placed on CUDA went **0 → 18** (qwen3.5-0.8b), **0 → 18** (2b), **0 → 24** (9b).
- `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; `cargo clippy` clean for `-p onnx-runtime-ep-cuda` (cuda / no-cuda) and `-p onnx-genai-engine --features cuda,native-backend` (no new warnings from these files).

## Deferred (kept out to keep this PR focused)

`com.microsoft` domain `RotaryEmbedding` registration and `Bool`-input `NonZero` — independent of LinearAttention, each with its own semantic checks; tracked as small follow-ups.

author: timtebeek
body:
Adds `https://artifacts.codegenomeproject.org/maven` as an additional source for `org.openrewrite` artifacts and forwards `CGP_ARTIFACTS_MAVEN_USERNAME` / `CGP_ARTIFACTS_MAVEN_TOKEN` to the CI build, the Maven counterpart to openrewrite/rewrite-github-actions@56b1b07 (where the Gradle convention plugin already does this). It sits alongside the existing repositories rather than replacing them, because CGP does not yet publish every snapshot we consume — `org.openrewrite:rewrite-bom:8.89.0-SNAPSHOT` returns 422 "no snapshot matching ... is published", while `rewrite-core`, `rewrite-java`, `rewrite-maven` and `rewrite-polyglot` are all present.

The repository is gated behind a `codegenome` profile activated by `CODEGENOME_USERNAME`, since CGP rejects anonymous requests and an unconditional declaration would 401 for contributors and fork PRs, which receive no secrets. `setup-java` is invoked a second time to write the default `~/.m2/settings.xml` the build step uses, as it emits only one server per call and the existing settings are read solely by the steps passing `--settings`. Publishing is untouched and still goes to Sonatype; switching that to CGP is a separate follow-up.

author: johnchia
body:
# RFC: SigmaStar Infinity6E MI backend

The backend half of a SigmaStar port. Companion to
[raptor#9](https://github.com/gtxaspec/raptor/pull/9)
and [raptor-common#1](https://github.com/gtxaspec/raptor-common/pull/1);
they land together and this is where the decisions are.

Brought up and running on an SSC30KQ + GC4653 board under OpenIPC: video (H.264
and H.265, main + sub), colour with working AWB, orientation, audio via `MI_AI`,
OSD via `MI_RGN`, day/night, exposure readback, JPEG and MJPEG.

27 files, +14975 −48. Nothing outside `src/star/` changes behaviour for Ingenic:
the shared edits are three new vtable entries (`sensor_detect`,
`isp_set_ae_target`, `isp_get_ae_target`), a `has_sensor_detect` capability flag,
and a direction argument on the GPIO ops. Existing backends leave the new entries
NULL and `RSS_HAL_CALL`'s NULL guard turns them into `RSS_ERR_NOTSUP`.

## How it reaches MI

`dlopen`, never `-l`. No `libmi_*` link flag appears anywhere; each `i6_*.h`
module loads the libraries it needs, and the load order is written up in
raptor's Makefile. That order is a real constraint, not a preference:
`libcam_os_wrapper` before `libmi_sys`, and `libispalgo` → `libcus3a` →
`libmi_isp`, because `libmi_isp` calls `CUS3A_*`.

Two consequences. A board missing a vendor library degrades rather than failing
to start. And the logic tests `#include` the real translation units and stub MI
through the function pointers in `star_state_t`, so `tests/` runs on the host
with no hardware — `t_isp.c`, `t_osd.c`, `t_audio.c` and `t_gpio.c`, four suites,
all passing.

## Vendored ABI headers

Nine MIT headers from divinus, `src/star/i6_*.h`. Each states its provenance at
the top, including the corroborating source, and where the vendor documentation
contradicts the layout it says so and why the doc was not followed —
`MI_AUDIO_Attr_t` is documented for SSD20X with a different field order, which is
a different chip generation. Please tell me if you want the licensing handled
differently.

## Deliberately absent

`OP COVERAGE` blocks at the top of `hal_isp.c`, `hal_osd.c`, `hal_audio.c`,
`hal_common.c` and `star_state.h` argue each absence where it applies. They are
decisions, not gaps — read them before implementing anything listed as missing,
because in several cases the obvious implementation is wrong.

The two that cost the most to learn:

- **Ring reference mode** (`enc_get_rmem_info`, `enc_inject_stream_shm`) must
  stay unimplemented until somebody solves buffer lifetime. MI recycles one
  stream buffer as soon as `MI_VENC_ReleaseStream` returns; three consecutive
  frames of 61634, 2582 and 4073 bytes were seen landing at the same address.
- **`MI_VPE_GetPortMode` and `MI_VPE_SetPortCrop` stay unbound.** Their struct
  layouts could not be verified. The first killed a working port; the second read
  back a rectangle it was never passed. Guessing a vendor struct layout broke
  this port twice, so unverified layouts are not called.

## ISP notes

AE grid placement and the `r,g,b,y` lane order are confirmed from cell data
rather than assumed, and the lane identification is answerable — it reports when
another ordering fits the cells better instead of quietly trusting itself.

`ae_comp`'s neutral is learned from the tuning binary on the first read after
each load, not assumed to be the midpoint. It has no auto mode (`IQ_FLAT`), so
raptor's neutral 128 has to be *made* inert rather than assumed to be; without
this, every board ran with EV compensation written to a value the tuning never
chose. On this board the learned baseline is MI 0, so neutral is inert and
raising it brightens, but there is no headroom below.

`ae_target` scales the AE's own target-luma curve. Its 132-byte payload layout is
reconstructed from a single board dump, so it is validated on every read — the
load-bearing check is that the light axis is strictly increasing, which the
target curve provably is not, so the two arrays cannot be swapped undetected. A
reading that fails validation declines rather than writes.

## Note on the history — read the diff, not the commits

This branch is 57 bring-up commits and I have deliberately not rewritten them,
so that you can decide. Three things you should know before spending time on
them:

- It does not bisect. The four test suites arrive at commit 23 of 57, so most
  historical points have no working suite.
- Three commit subjects name `star_probe`, a bring-up tool that is not in the
  final tree — it was removed once it had served its purpose.
- Five carry internal task and phase numbering, and there is a run of ISP
  debugging hatches that are added and later removed. None of it survives into
  the diff.

I have a topical series mapped out — roughly eleven commits, one per subsystem,
splitting mostly along file boundaries with `hal_isp.c` as the awkward part.
Say the word and it is yours; I did not want to force a rewrite on you
unasked.

author: robcohen
body:
Fuzzing is **89 of the 169 machine-minutes** a PR push costs, and 12.7 of its 113 minutes of wall clock: 7 targets × 10 minutes of mutation each. Ten minutes of mutation is a *discovery* budget, and discovery is not the question a PR needs answered.

## The split

**PRs replay the corpus** with `-runs=0` and mutate for 30 seconds. The replay re-executes every input the fuzzer has ever found interesting, so it catches a change that breaks any of them, in seconds rather than minutes. **Nightly keeps the full 30 minutes** per target.

## Why this needed a corpus fix first

The trade is only sound if the corpus is durable, and it was not. It lived in:

- `actions/cache`, keyed `fuzz-corpus-<target>-<sha>` — 7-day idle eviction, 10 GB repo cap, a fresh entry per commit
- an artifact with `retention-days: 7`

So a week of nightly discovery was routinely discarded and never reached a PR. Shortening the PR run without fixing that would have made fuzzing genuinely weaker rather than faster.

Nightly now minimizes with `cargo fuzz cmin` and commits to a **`fuzz-corpus` data branch**, the same convention `benchmarks` and `profiling` already use. Every PR replays a corpus strictly stronger than the day before.

## Crash inputs get a permanent home

`crates/<crate>/fuzz/regressions/<target>/`, in-tree, committed with the fix, seeded on top of the corpus in every run. The corpus branch is minimized, so an input left only there can be dropped by a later `cmin`. A regression file cannot. That is the difference between "we fixed it" and "it cannot come back". The crash-check step now tells you to do this when it fails.

## Also

Four near-identical job blocks collapse into one matrix, **488 lines → 364**. Each carried its own copy of the duration logic, crash check, upload steps and summary. The careful `slow-unit-*` handling from #1342 is preserved verbatim as the single shared check, rather than four copies that can drift.

`cargo-fuzz` is now cached. Building it from source costs ~2 minutes, which was noise beside a 10-minute run but would otherwise *be* the job in a 30-second one. Keyed on an epoch rather than a pinned version, so refreshing is deliberate; I could not reach crates.io from the dev environment to verify a version number and would not invent one.

## Expected effect

| | now | after |
|---|---|---|
| fuzz machine time per PR | 89 min | ~14 min |
| fuzz critical path | 12.7 min | ~2 min |

## Verification

The workflow shell cannot be exercised until it runs in CI, so both new paths were simulated against real git repositories first:

- **corpus restore** — target with a populated corpus, target with none, and no `fuzz-corpus` branch at all
- **publication** — first run creating the orphan branch, and a second run appending to it

`git archive` refuses a path that is not in the tree, so the restore asks `git ls-tree` first; a target with no corpus yet is normal, not an error. The fetch is a `run:` step rather than `actions/checkout` because checking out a missing ref fails the step even under `continue-on-error`, which would mark every PR red until the first nightly creates the branch.

## Note on the first run

Until the first nightly publishes, PR runs start from a cold corpus and the replay is a no-op. That is expected and self-correcting after one night.
