author: kelvinmattos
body:
## Contexto

Você reportou 500 em `/reports` (Relatórios & BI).

## Causa

`ReportController` nunca foi atualizado desde que foi escrito (só tem 1 commit no histórico) e assumia colunas fixas sem checar se existem — o mesmo padrão de bug documentado em CLAUDE.md §4:

- `whereBetween('date_created', ...)` e `SUM(net_profit)` direto no SQL, sem `Schema::hasColumn()`. `net_profit` em particular é uma coluna recente (migration de 2026-07-29) que pode não ter chegado em produção por causa do bug de deploy já corrigido (PR #9).
- JOIN obrigatório com `integrations` via `orders.integration_id` (pedidos importados por CSV/planilha — Magazord, Netshoes — não têm esse vínculo).
- `exportData()` chamava `$order->date_created->format(...)` sem checar null — quebra sempre que o importador não conseguiu parsear a data do pedido.

## Achado adicional (investigando o mesmo bug)

A tabela `orders` tem uma coluna JSON legada e **nunca escrita** chamada `items`, que colide com o relacionamento Eloquent `items()` (hasMany OrderItem). `$order->items` (propriedade) sempre retorna essa coluna morta (`null`) em vez da coleção de itens — confirmado via `tinker`. Isso:
- Quebrava `exportData()` com "Call to a member function pluck() on null".
- Zerava **silenciosamente** o cálculo de comissão/CMV/lucro líquido em `OrderSyncService::performDeepSync()` (`foreach` sobre `null` não lança erro em PHP 8, só ignora).

Corrigido usando `getRelation('items')` nos 3 pontos afetados. `OrderSyncService` é código morto hoje (não roteado, e ainda chama um método que não existe no adapter — `fetchSingleOrder`), mas corrigi mesmo assim por segurança, já que a auditoria "corrigir tudo que encontrar" está em vigor.

## Ajuste na regra de commit (CLAUDE.md §3.2)

Também corrigi um erro na própria regra que documentei antes: só tirar o `Co-Authored-By: Claude` do **texto** da mensagem não bastou — o GitHub adiciona esse rodapé sozinho no squash-merge com base no **autor real** do commit, não no texto. A partir de agora todo commit usa `--author="Kelvin Mattos ..."`.

## Validação

- Suíte completa: **199 testes passando** (+4 novos), incluindo um que reproduz a hipótese mais provável do 500 real: derruba a coluna `net_profit` em teste e confirma que a tela continua funcionando.
- `php -l` limpo.

author: daniel-m-campos
body:
PR 2 of the bench-tooling redesign (after #226; next: VRAM sampler, pod driver template, iso-volume spec).

## What

- **`python -m bonsai.bench run --spec <file>.json`**: declarative specs (cells or generators, variants, threads, per-device repeats policy, gates, timeout cap) expand into the existing worker protocol. `plan` prints the expansion without running; `variants` prints the registry; `worker` is the child protocol.
- **`iso_volume` generator**: constant rows x cols, aspect-ratio sweep with exact-division check and `aspect` recorded per cell. First consumer: the RTX PRO 6000 shape-frontier campaign.
- **`bench/driver.py`**: parent orchestration extracted from scaling; every row emits via `runlog.emit_row` (schema v1: ts, git_sha, script, cmd, host with folded worker libs) plus an optional `run` label. This is the structural fix for the four ad-hoc row schemas in committed campaign files.
- **Gates are policy**: the VRAM/RAM estimators and `GPU_MAX_COLS` stay as defaults, but a spec can set `"gates": {"mem_gate": "off", "gpu_max_cols": null}` — required for iso-volume, where a measured OOM is the datum.
- **Resume by default** in spec mode (ok/unsupported final; error/oom/timeout re-attempt), key extended with depth/iters/seed and backward-readable against committed scaling.jsonl rows.
- **`bonsai.bench.scaling` unchanged surface**: same flags, same `--worker` protocol (verified live), delegating to the new path. `scripts/bench_scaling.py` and `gpu_pareto.py` untouched.

## Verification

- New tests: spec expansion (iso-volume exact division, repeats policy, variant_iters cross-product), driver resume keys against legacy-shaped rows, emit path (schema v1, run label, host.libs fold, skip rows), CLI plan lazy-import guard. Full `make python-test` green.
- Live: mini spec ran end to end (rows carry run/suite/axis/aspect/git_sha), rerun resume-skipped every job, legacy worker heredoc protocol returned a correct RESULT line.

author: waitstepbro
body:
Four config-driven additions to both bar profiles:

- HP Color Gradient (per profile, default off): blends Bar Color at full HP through Mid at a configurable midpoint to Low at empty. There is no colorHigh, so enabling it changes nothing until HP drops and disabling it restores the previous look exactly. Wired in as the last fallback in drawBar, so the loot-taint grey and status tints still take precedence. targetMidpoint allows 0-100 (the two-colour degenerate ramps); playerMidpoint stays 1-99. hpFillColor guards rather than clamps, so those endpoints survive a hand-edited profile.

- Prayer Bar Color: the hardcoded PRAYER_COLOR constant is gone, replaced by a config item defaulting to the same OSRS prayer-orb blue.

- Color Aggressive NPC Bars: fills an aggressive NPC's bar with the aggressive colour. Loses to the status-effect tint deliberately, since aggression persists for the whole tolerance window while a status tint is transient and the name and icon still carry it. Aggressive NPC Name Color is broadened into one shared Aggressive NPC Color driving the name and the bar; its keyName is unchanged so saved profiles carry over.

- HP Text Spacing (per profile, default 0): pushes the HP number and the percentage apart in Both mode, clamped at render time to the bar's width. Both halves are still measured off the undivided label, so they share a baseline and spacing 0 renders identically to before. Both mode also drops the parentheses it used to put around a player's percentage.

author: alexander-turner
body:
## Summary

- `check-drift-guards` had a blind spot with a name: a comment reading `SSOT char sets (mirrored from the per-layer suites)`. It names a real SSOT, which is the *sanctioned* single-source idiom, so the phrasing pass reads it as clean — while the value beside it is a hand-kept copy. Adds a third trigger on the **conjunction** of an authority word and a copy word inside a comment.
- The comment-locating machinery underneath was a text scan (`comment_body`: startswith `#`/`//`, else `find(" # ")`). Both languages that have a grammar here now use it — `tokenize` for Python, tree-sitter-bash for shell. This fixes a **fail-open** and a false-positive class that both predate the new trigger.

## Changes

### New trigger — laundered authority

| | |
|---|---|
| Authority | `SSOT`, `single source of truth`, `canonical` |
| Copy | `mirror(s/ed/ing)`, `cop(y/ies/ied)`, `duplicat*`, `restat*`, `hand-maintained/kept/copied`, `in step with` |
| Fires on | the conjunction only — each half alone is a normal, honest thing to write |
| Suppressed by | a denial governing the copy word (`read from the SSOT, never a copy`), `@pytest.mark.drift_guard(reason)`, or `drift-guard-ok: <reason>` |

A laundering hit is a self-declaration, so — like intent phrasing, and unlike a structural hit — it is **not** cleared by `# not-a-drift-guard:`. Both opt-out comments are skipped when scanning, so an opted-out test never re-flags on the wording of its own opt-out.

The denial window is counted in **words**, not characters: a character window can cut mid-token and turn `cannot` into a string starting `not`, which `\b` then reads as a denial nobody wrote.

### Comments now come from a grammar, not a text scan

"Is this `#` a comment, or data?" is a question about the grammar. The text answer was wrong in three ways:

| language | what the text scan got wrong | now |
|---|---|---|
| Python | `got = "# canonical rows, mirrored from X"` — a value the program *builds* read as a comment | `tokenize` COMMENT tokens |
| Python | **fail open**: `_has_optout` *suppresses*, so a string literal spelling `# not-a-drift-guard:` silently disarmed the structural trigger for a whole test | same |
| shell | a **heredoc body** read as a run of comments | `iter_nodes(parse(script), "comment")` |

The shell case is this repo's own documented probe, and the new trigger failed it on first run:

```
probe             before(text)   after(grammar)
message string           False            False
heredoc body              True            False   <- false positive
real comment              True             True
```

Only the *structural* half moved. Judging the prose inside a comment stays a regex — English has no grammar here to parse. JS/TS still scans text; no JS grammar is a dependency yet, and that gap is now recorded in the rule's audit table rather than left implicit.

### Fixed while here

- `is_shell_source` becomes the SSOT for "is this shell", **extracted** from `tracked_shell_files` rather than copied out of it.
- The standalone `check-drift-guards` hook declared **no** `additional_dependencies` while already importing PyYAML through `_linecheck` — latent until a downstream repo enabled the id directly. Now declares PyYAML plus the grammar bindings.

## Testing

- `uv run pytest -q` → **2488 passed**; the check's own file **141 passed**. Every pre-existing assertion passes **unchanged** — the rule is identical, only the decision procedure moved.
- Non-vacuity, verified rather than assumed: `comment_body` was run on each new Python test's input and read all three string literals as comments. The shell probes are pinned as a parametrized test through `main()`, with a real-comment positive control so the two "no" rows can't pass by the check going inert.
- Hook dependency check run for real: a venv holding **exactly** the three declared packages — real comment exits 1, heredoc exits 0.
- Dogfood over the tracked tree: unchanged at 7, all docstring-phrasing self-hits in the file `check-extras` already excludes. The four string-literal self-hits the new trigger initially produced are gone.
- Downstream on `agent-glovebox`: baseline 0 findings → 3, **all three true classes**; one (`pretooluse-sanitize-property.test.mjs`) had already been found and fixed by hand in glovebox#2989, independent confirmation the trigger finds what a reviewer would. The other two are handled in [agent-glovebox#2998](https://github.com/AlexanderMattTurner/agent-glovebox/pull/2998). Re-run after this rewrite: still rc=0.

## Decisions made

- **One false positive is accepted, not designed out.** `write-python-pins.test.mjs` narrates its *subject* (`a copy drifting off the SSOT`) rather than its own value. No regex separates that from the real thing, so it takes a `drift-guard-ok:` annotation.
- **`_launders_a_copy` is deleted, not kept as a wrapper.** Once shell routed through the grammar it was a vestigial text path; its parametrized cases now drive `text_violations` — behaviour, not a helper. One fixture changed: `kept in step with` is claimed by the older phrase pass first, so it proved nothing about this trigger and is now `in step with`.
- **`_python_comments` stays local** rather than moving to `_linecheck`. Promoting it is the right move at the second caller, with its own tests there.

## Lessons Learned

- **What**: when a lint reads narration (comments) rather than code, locate the comment with the language's own parser — `tokenize` for Python, tree-sitter for shell — and reserve text scanning for judging the prose inside it. A shared `comment_body`-style text helper is the right tool only for a language with no grammar on hand.
- **Where**: `.claude/rules/` — the shell-parsing rule generalizes beyond shell, and downstream repos carry the same helper.
- **Why**: the text form is wrong in both directions, and the dangerous one is silent: a lint whose opt-out token can be spelled inside a string literal **fails open**, disarming itself on exactly the file whose fixtures quote the idiom it polices.

author: quincyo
body:
Field report, the same day as the pace-card fix and on the same card:

  "The next day's work orders are shuffling up every time. I download the WORK
  list when I start my day, I say that I'm going to do X, or my target. I would
  like the WORK list to stay at that unless I manually add more for the same day.
  I don't want to shuffle the tail down to the next day, and I don't want to
  shuffle the next day into the end of today. I only want to manually add days or
  work orders to today's day, not automatically."

The today anchor always froze WHICH orders are today. It never froze HOW MANY,
and two rules re-sized it all day. The Drive screen's 5-minute auto-refresh
re-ran both on a timer, which is what turned a background quirk into "every
time". Neither rule came from the commit the report blames; that one only made
the damage visible.

1. Day 1 was min(dayCapacity(target, installedToday) + anchor.extend, |set ∩
   pending|). The target counts METERS and the set counts ORDERS, and that
   mismatch is the whole defect: a two-meter order, or any walk-up found in the
   field, spent the day's room faster than it spent the day's list, so the tail
   of a committed day was stamped Day 2 by mid-morning. Once the target was MET
   with orders still pending, capacity hit 0, day1Count hit 0, and every
   remaining order was stamped day 2+ — a full afternoon's work declared
   tomorrow's, and since todayPending reads day === 1 strictly, the pace card
   disappeared off the Drive screen with the crew still working.

   Day 1 is day1Count(day1Ids) now: today's committed set, entire. The target
   sizes the day when the day is PLANNED and then lets go. anchor.extend goes
   with the clamp it existed to buy room back from; a legacy anchor is ignored.
   dayCapacity survives for one job — bounding how far a deliberate mid-day
   target raise may GROW the day.

2. needsCommit re-committed the instant anchorDay1Ids emptied and freshAnchorIds
   pulled the next chunk up, on any call site. It returns Boolean(opts.replan)
   there now: a finished day stays finished. replan is passed by exactly two
   callers, the Optimize press and the meters/day box, and on a spent set the
   press re-commits whatever the target says — that press is the manual ask that
   replaces the automatic roll. applyTodayAnchor grew an `exhausted` flag for it,
   or the capacity > 0 guard (which stops a target change freezing an EMPTY set)
   would leave an installer who met their target and finished every order with no
   way to ask for more work at all.

Installing extra now reads as being ahead rather than as a shorter list: paceFor
returns targetOver beside targetShort and the caption prints "· 4 over your 24",
where the footnote used to vanish at the moment it had the best news to give. The
Route done ~ clock moves later for the same reason — the stops are still on the
route. The add-order sheet loses "Add to today, keep the day's size", which
rolled the tail out on a tap; it is offered on a FINISHED day now, since adding
by hand is the only way work joins a cleared list.

The two-device flow is untouched and is the point: autoSync still pulls the list
(preserveDone), adopts the office's day 1, refreshes the day cache and re-anchors
— that last call re-prices the remaining ETAs from where the crew is now. The one
shrink that stays is shrink-by-completion, an order logged on the work phone
dropping off the driving phone's Day 1 on the next tick. What a tick can no
longer do is move work between days.

The estimate.js comment arguing Day 1 "does not move underneath the answer"
because a completed install drops both terms of the min() by one is recorded as
wrong: true at one meter per order and nowhere else. The conclusion it defended
(onPace reads the route) is right and now stands on its own footing.

Both defects were reproduced against the shipped build first, headless against
the real app with the spine blocked at the browser: a met target stamped all ten
pending orders day 2 and hid the pace card, and a finished day re-committed the
anchor to tomorrow's six. On the fixed build today's four stay on day 1 with the
card reading "24 of 28 stops · 4 over your 24", the finished day leaves its
anchor alone, and a deliberate re-plan still brings the next batch in. 549 tests
pass, including a new tests/worklist-day-frozen.test.mjs pinning which call sites
may move the day.

## Summary

Lands the v0.9.0 engine line on `main`. This is a release-line sync, not a feature PR: `main` has had no tagged release since `v0.7.0` (2025-10-03) and is 273 commits behind `dev_v0.9.0`.

Per the milestone decision of 2026-07-30, **this merge is deliberately not tagged `v0.9.0`.** It unstales `main` while development continues under the 0.9.0 milestone (10 open issues). The `v0.9.0` tag is spent when that milestone completes, so no renumbering is needed.

Brings in: VISSIM driver refactor + DSProxy adoption (#158), backend-agnostic VirtualEnvironment core (#174), CarMaker XIL, SUMO TraCI perf work, TL sync, and the release/CI pipeline (#191, #57).

## Conflict resolution — please review this section

The merge had **9 conflicts, all resolved in favour of `dev_v0.9.0`.** The reasoning, since this is the reviewable decision in this PR:

Both branches independently grew a Carla tooling set from a merge-base (`6d0b78b8`) that contained neither — `run_cosim.py`, `import_map.py`, and `Carla/README.md` are `add/add` conflicts, born twice. `dev_v0.9.0` is the more developed fork of every conflicting file:

| file | main | dev_v0.9.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `Carla/run_cosim.py` | 612 lines, 14 commits, last 2026-07-22 | **2334 lines, 29 commits, last 2026-07-30** |
| `Carla/import_map.py` | 661 lines, 8 commits | **1177 lines, 16 commits** |

`.gitignore` is a **union** of both sides rather than a takeover.

## Content that disappears from `main` (all verified intentional)

- **237 files** under `CommonLib/libevent/` — vendored dep removed on `dev_v0.9.0`; #131/#138 scope
- `CommonLib/ryml_all.hpp` — removed by `09cf9f3f` "remove dead ryml_all.hpp amalgamation (#127)"
- `tests/Python/SimpleTrafficLight/*.xml`, `tests/Sumo/SimpleLoop/*.xml` — consolidated by `b8976f56` / `f58f279f` under #174

Each was checked against the merge base: present at base, deliberately deleted on `dev_v0.9.0`. None was added on `main` and dropped here. Genuinely main-only content is preserved (`doc/Carla_Linux_building.md`, `tests/Sumo/Carla/*`).

## Related Issues / Tasks

Relates to #191, #57, #158, #174, #127. Closes nothing directly — release sync.

## Type of Change
- [x] Maintenance / Refactor

## Affected Modules / Components

Effectively the whole tree. Concentrated in `Carla/`, `VirCarlaEnv/`, `CommonLib/`, `scripts/dispatch/`, `TrafficLayer/`.

## Test Cases

**None run. This is the outstanding blocker before merge.**

The conflict resolution above is textual and structural — verified against git history, not against a running system. Because both lines rewrote the Carla co-sim tooling in parallel, a functional check is required: one `run_cosim` end-to-end on the merged tree. I could not run it here (needs a CARLA + SUMO box).

CI on this PR will exercise the build gate in `release.yml`. `bundle-guard.yml` should pass — the merge moves the `ProprietaryFiles` pointer to `bd800bf5477...`, and `Binaries-bd800bf54778` is already published.

## Environment

Not exercised — see above.

- [ ] Code compiles/runs as expected — *pending CI + manual `run_cosim` smoke test*
- [ ] Tests pass locally — *not run*
- [x] Documentation is updated (if applicable) — n/a, no doc changes authored here
- [x] Relevant issues are linked
- [x] Version-specific changes are noted

## Additional Notes

A sibling worktree in this workspace sits on `chore/merge_main_into_v090`, i.e. the **opposite** direction. If that branch is live work by someone else, reconcile before merging this — landing both would be redundant. This PR was built on its own branch off `origin/main` and touched nothing else.

body:
## OMN-15482 follow-up — the cross-repo seam pin was skipped in CI and pinned nothing

`OmniNode-ai/omnimarket#1978` (merged `fb99acf2`) closed the three delegation-wire
fidelity gaps and cited **`test_steel_payload_validates_against_the_wire_model`** as the
mitigation for the one residual it declared honestly: the `uv run ... onex node --input`
subprocess hop between `steel_onslaught` and omnimarket is not exercised end to end, so
the seam is pinned from both sides instead.

**That pin does not run.** It shipped inside `test_live_completion_fidelity_omn15482.py`,
whose module-level

```python
pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(os.environ.get("OMN_ALLOW_LIVE_LADDER") != "1", ...)
```

applies to every test in the file. A per-test `@pytest.mark.unit` does **not** cancel a
module-level `skipif` — so the test's own docstring ("Marked `unit` deliberately: it needs
no live backend and must run in CI") described an intent the code did not implement.

### RED-before, on the merge commit, exactly as CI runs it

```
$ git log --oneline -1
fb99acf2d feat(OMN-15482): thread temperature, system/user role split, and json_mode ...

$ env -u OMN_ALLOW_LIVE_LADDER uv run pytest \
    tests/unit/nodes/node_delegate_skill_orchestrator/test_live_completion_fidelity_omn15482.py::test_steel_payload_validates_against_the_wire_model -rs -q
SKIPPED [1] .../test_live_completion_fidelity_omn15482.py:315: live LLM call against the
  pinned local-coder-mlx backend; set OMN_ALLOW_LIVE_LADDER=1 ... to enable
1 skipped in 0.31s
```

Net effect: since `#1978` merged, a steel-side payload key rename would **not** have been
caught on the consuming side. `extra="forbid"` would still have failed it at runtime
inside the CLI — loudly, not silently — but the pre-merge pin both PR bodies relied on was
inert.

### Fix

The test moves to the sibling **non-gated** module `test_wire_completion_fidelity_omn15482.py`
and now executes. The live module keeps a comment recording why it must not come back.

### GREEN-after

```
$ env -u OMN_ALLOW_LIVE_LADDER uv run pytest .../test_wire_completion_fidelity_omn15482.py -v -k "steel_payload or hides_behind"
test_steel_payload_validates_against_the_wire_model              PASSED
test_no_unit_marked_test_hides_behind_a_module_level_skipif      PASSED
2 passed
```

### A rule is not a mechanism

Moving one test fixes one instance. `test_no_unit_marked_test_hides_behind_a_module_level_skipif`
is the mechanism: it AST-scans this node's test package (statically — no import, no
collection) for any `unit`-marked test sitting under a module-level `skipif` and fails
naming the offender.

**Mutation-proved in both directions on `.200`** — a detector that only ever passes is not
a detector:

```
# offender injected into the live-gated module
FAILED test_no_unit_marked_test_hides_behind_a_module_level_skipif
E   Left contains one more item:
E   'test_live_completion_fidelity_omn15482.py::test_mutation_probe_offender'

# restored -> 25 passed; file sha256 f0f7b63d3c0e35a9, identical to pre-mutation
```

## dod_evidence

Ticket: **OMN-15482**. No `src/` change — the three fidelity fields and their runtime
behaviour are untouched; this is test-placement only.

**Gates — all on `.200` (`stickybeatz-studio`), patch-transfer with per-file sha256
verification (byte-identical to the local worktree before every run):**

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `ruff format --check src/ tests/` | exit 0 — 4542 files already formatted |
| `ruff check src/ tests/` | exit 0 — all checks passed |
| `mypy src/omnimarket/ --strict` | exit 0 — no issues in 2985 source files |
| `pre-commit run --all-files` | exit 0 — 68 hooks passed |
| `pytest tests/ -m "not kafka"` | exit 0 — **15686 passed, 82 skipped, 9 deselected** (679s) |

**Disclosed, not waved off:** `mypy` over the two changed *test* files reports 5 errors
(`transport` not explicitly exported ×4, `"type" has no attribute "dispatch"` ×1). All 5
are **pre-existing** — reproduced identically on unmodified `fb99acf2` by stashing this
patch, same count, same lines. CI's mypy scope is `src/omnimarket/`, which is clean. Not
introduced here and not fixed here.

`pre-commit` initially failed `topic-naming-lint` with
`ERROR: lint_topic_names.py not found at ../omnibase_infra/...` — a worktree-relative path
that does not resolve from `omni_worktrees/`, resolved by exporting
`OMNIBASE_INFRA_PATH=/Users/jonah/Code/omni_home/omnibase_infra` as the hook's own error
message instructs. Environment resolution, not a code defect.

**Residual:** the steel half (`jonahgabriel/steel_onslaught#238`) is still open, so the
subprocess hop remains uncovered end to end by design; this PR restores the pre-merge
guarantee that the seam is pinned on the consuming side, nothing more.

Refs OMN-15482, OMN-14208.

Evidence-Source: OCC#5653

body:
This PR is a mix of fixes, nerfs, and buffs.
- Fixed Detective/Combat Medic longcoats having the wrong armor levels
- Nerfed various winter wear to be roughly equivalent to winter coats, including neck ponchos and armored winter coats.
- Trench coats no longer protect you from heat. (??)
- Gave lots of clothes cold resistance, including neck gaiters, old-fashioned coats, jensen coats, colored gloves, ponchos, santa suits, hoodies, windbreakers, and expensive coats.

## Why / Balance
These are mostly fixes; when we nerfed winter coats and boots, we missed a few items, and we've added more clothes since then that don't exactly follow starcup standards.

I would rather have proper mittens than just cold resistance to all colored gloves, but this feels fine for now. The other items just make sense to provide some protection, and it expands player options when assembling an ensemble for Glacier or Ptarmigan.

**Changelog**
:cl:
- fix: Standardized cold protection levels on various overpowered winterwear, including trench coats and armored coats.
- tweak: Gaiters, colored gloves, and various coats now provide some cold protection!
- fix: Fixed some Security personnel's winterwear not providing the proper armored protection!

author: dannielperez
body:
## Summary

1. **Current behavior:** `pyhikvision` enumerates recorder channels but cannot fetch their JPEGs or map them to RTSP streams.
2. **Root cause:** the facade and ISAPI client expose inventory/configuration only; no typed media surface exists for a consumer such as UniqueOS Access Control.
3. **Minimal fix:** map one-based input IDs to Hikvision streaming IDs, expose native ISAPI JPEG capture, expose credential-safe channel RTSP construction, and add a bounded tuned one-frame RTSP grab.
4. **Risks:** RTSP capture depends on `ffmpeg`; missing binaries and timeouts become typed, redacted errors. Native success bodies must contain a JPEG. No device writes are introduced.
5. **Impacted components:** `HikClient`, `IsapiClient`, and media/delegation tests.
6. **Required tests:** exact `6 → 602` and `16 → 1602` mapping, native JPEG validation, credential URL escaping, ffmpeg arguments, exact subprocess deadline, timeout redaction, and facade parity.
7. **Regression estimate:** low; the change is additive and the full suite passes.

## Validation

- `PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest -q` — **91 passed**
- changed-file `ruff check` — **passed**
- changed-file `ruff format --check` — **passed**
- CI — **passed** on Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12; build passed
- repository-wide ruff baseline still has one unrelated unused import and three unrelated format drifts, recorded in the handoff

## Risk

`RISK:med` — additive read-only media transport; timeout, JPEG validation, and secret-redaction behavior are pinned.

## Autonomous checklist

- [x] Scope is one SDK media contract.
- [x] Tests cover new behavior and failure paths.
- [x] Handoff added.
- [x] No migration.
- [x] No secret read or output.
- [x] No live vendor call.
- [x] No force push.
- [x] No merge.

## What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This change updates SCM to instantiate the configured `DNSToSwitchMapping` directly instead of wrapping every non-cached mapping in `CachedDNSToSwitchMapping`.

This follows up on the topology mapping behavior discussed in [apache/ozone#10598](https://github.com/apache/ozone/pull/10598), where static host-to-rack mappings should not be affected by an additional SCM-side cache wrapper.

The default mapping behavior remains cached because Hadoop `ScriptBasedMapping` already extends `CachedDNSToSwitchMapping`. Using configured mappings directly avoids changing their input through the cache wrapper hostname normalization step, which is important for mappings such as `StaticMapping`.

The patch also adds focused SCM coverage for the default cached mapping and direct configured mapping usage.

## What is the link to the Apache JIRA

https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HDDS-16018

## How was this patch tested?

```
mvn -B --no-transfer-progress -pl :hdds-server-scm -am -Dtest=TestStorageContainerManager,TestSCMBlockProtocolServer test -DskipShade -DskipRecon -DskipDocs
git diff --check
```

author: redhat-chai-bot
body:
## Cherry-pick: etcd memory regression fix for 4.21

Cherry-pick of upstream [etcd-io/etcd#21443](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/21443) — Revert "Reuse events between sync loops"

### Problem

etcd 3.6 introduced a memory regression that scales with cluster size ([OCPBUGS-76329](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPBUGS-76329)). The `rangeEventsWithReuse` optimization held event objects across sync loops, causing unbounded memory growth:

| Cluster Size | etcd 3.5 Max RSS | etcd 3.6 Max RSS | Max Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 24 nodes | 468 MiB | 541 MiB | +15.6% |
| 120 nodes | 893 MiB | 1.24 GiB | +42.2% |
| 250 nodes | 1.13 GiB | 2.96 GiB | +162% |

### Fix

This cherry-picks the upstream revert which:
- Removes the `rangeEventsWithReuse` function
- Removes the shared `evs` variable from `syncWatchersLoop`
- Restores the original `rangeEvents` and `kvsToEvents` signatures with `contains` filtering

### Why cherry-pick instead of full rebase

OCP 4.21 etcd is on 3.6.5. A full rebase to 3.6.9+ is complicated by Go version constraints (see [openshift/etcd#377](https://github.com/openshift/etcd/pull/377) which is held). This targeted cherry-pick addresses the critical memory regression without introducing other changes.

### Build and test verification

- `go build ./...` ✅
- `go test ./server/storage/mvcc/...` ✅ (11.7s)

### References

- Upstream issue: https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/issues/21355
- Upstream fix: https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/21443
- Jira: https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPBUGS-76329
- 4.22 rebase (includes this fix): https://github.com/openshift/etcd/pull/393

author: alicup29
body:
## Summary

Adds a mediabunny `CustomVideoDecoder` that decodes H.264 entirely in WASM (a libav.js/FFmpeg build the **app** vendors), so **Linux desktop (Tauri → WebKitGTK)** users whose system can't decode H.264 natively see MP4 video instead of blank frames. The `avdec_h264` GStreamer plugin is omitted by many distros for patent reasons, which is what causes the blank frames today.

Pairs with the app-side wiring PR: **talmolab/sleap-app#feat/linux-h264-decode-app**.

## Zero-regression by design

mediabunny uses a registered custom decoder *unconditionally* when its static `supports()` returns true — it never falls back to native. So `supports()` gates on a **cached, async `VideoDecoder.isConfigSupported` probe**: the decoder engages **only when native H.264 decode is unavailable** — capability-based, not OS-based (some Linux boxes have the codec; some browsers lack it). macOS, Windows, and Linux-with-codec keep using native → no regression. `factory.ts` likewise routes MP4 → MediaBunny (which has the custom-decoder hook, unlike Mp4Box) only on that same fallback condition.

## What's here

- `src/video/libav-h264-decoder.ts` — the shim (AVCC→decode, PTS, B-frame reorder, I420 output, SAR + colorSpace propagation), a `configureLibavDecoder({ wasmBaseUrl })` URL seam, `ensureNativeH264Probe()`, `registerLibavH264Decoder()`, the pure `shouldUseLibavH264()` gate, and an `overrideNativeH264Decodable()` dev/test force-toggle.
- `src/video/h264-colorspace.ts` — SPS-VUI parse → `VideoColorSpaceInit` with SD=BT.601 / HD=BT.709 limited-range defaults (fixes a WebKitGTK color shift on untagged I420 frames).
- `MediaBunnyVideoBackend` awaits the probe in `initialize()`; exported from **both** entry points.
- **io ships no WASM** — the decoder is kept off npm / out of the bundle and loaded from the app's vendored copy only when needed.

## Testing

- 15 new unit tests (the anti-regression gate + SPS colorspace parser on real bytes); **full suite 2141 pass**, biome + tsc + build clean; browser-bundle stays node-builtin-free.
- Decode path validated **byte-exact vs native WebCodecs** on macOS (synthetic High-profile GOP-12; real 384×384 fixture incl. random seek).
- **Validated end-to-end in the real Tauri app on Linux/WebKitGTK**: forced fallback loads + scrubs an external-MP4 project, predicted instances land frame-accurately, no console errors; unforced run confirms native path + zero regression.

## Follow-ups (separate)

- Threaded (SAB) build variant for extra 1080p seek headroom.
- HEVC.

author: unforcedagi
body:
Two fixes surfaced by running the installer end-to-end on a real DigitalOcean box.

## 1. The Caddyfile needs the marker `set-origin` looks for

Observed live:

```
No Parachute-managed Caddyfile at /etc/caddy/Caddyfile — origin set; restart modules to apply.
```

`parachute hub set-origin` matches the prefix `# Managed by Parachute install` (`hub/src/commands/hub.ts:56`) to decide whether a Caddyfile is its own to rewrite. Our script didn't write it — so set-origin stored the origin but **silently lost the ability to update that vhost later.** HTTPS worked; the two halves just disagreed about who owned the file.

## 2. Re-running re-installed transcription from scratch

The script's header promises safe re-runs. It was safe but not *cheap*: it re-downloaded and re-verified the speech model even when already installed — several minutes and a few hundred MB to arrive back where it started, and the re-verify is the heaviest thing the script does.

### The probe is filesystem-based, and that's the interesting part

I wrote it first as a grep against `transcription status` output — then tested it:

```
$ transcription status | head -1
Configured provider: whisper-cpp        ← old format
predicate: no match → would install
```

The readiness line it grepped for only exists in a vault version **that isn't released yet**. On every real box the skip would have silently never fired — a no-op that looks like a feature, and one no test would have caught.

So it probes the filesystem: model + engine + ffmpeg on disk *is* what "ready" means, and those paths are stable across versions.

**Verified both directions:**
- machine with transcription set up → matches, skips ✓
- empty `PARACHUTE_HOME` → no match, installs ✓

## Not verified

The **Caddyfile marker is written and syntax-checked but never exercised on hardware** — the test droplet was deleted before I could re-run. The change is a one-line prefix matching a documented constant, but I'd rather say that than imply it was tested.

The first full run's results stand: ffmpeg → hub + vault → `init` → transcription verified transcribing → sslip.io hostname → Caddy → **valid Let's Encrypt cert from outside**, with `['parachute-vault', 'parachute-app']` and no scribe.

author: rocketman-21
body:
## Why this PR exists

Murph currently over-vetoes or sanitizes ordinary, opted-in group dares when dramatic wording makes a safe concrete act sound risky. This change calibrates the group prompt and challenge/comedy skills to judge the actual act while preserving the narrow boundary for real hazards.

## User goal / user-visible behavior

A group can propose an ordinary timed stake or playful consequence and have Murph confidently lock it in when the concrete act is safe and consensual. Murph still intervenes when the substance, amount, mechanics, setting, participant context, coercion, impairment, or pressure through distress creates a material hazard.

## User experience

The initiating actor is a member posting a proposed stake in the current Linq group room; the receiving audience is the same room and its opted-in participants. Murph answers in the foreground reply, classifies the concrete act, and either locks in the safe group-authored stake with one clear witnessed payoff or states only the boundary required by an actual hazard. There is no new async continuation, reminder, notification, screen, or external audience; the normal assistant provider turn remains the longest wait, and the terminal destination is the same group thread. If material facts are missing, Murph can ask the narrow clarification needed; if a real hazard exists, it preserves the premise where a safe version remains. Direct-chat behavior is unchanged. The room can continue the challenge without an unrelated new inbound action. Direct journey evidence: the existing real-Codex group candidate evaluation now covers the blank-slate payoff, one-serving safe stake, extreme amount, harmful substance, known contraindication, coercion, impairment, and pressure-through-distress cases; lower-level prompt wiring has 82 passing focused regressions.

## Invariants

- Consent and participant opt-in remain required; dramatic wording never overrides concrete coercion, impairment, contraindication, or pressure through distress.
- Dangerous consumption and other material hazards still receive the narrow safety boundary the actual risk requires.
- Safe stakes remain group-authored and are not silently replaced with a sanitized Murph-authored premise.
- Direct-chat prompt behavior, persisted state, tool authority, delivery behavior, and runtime side effects remain unchanged.

## Non-obvious affected surfaces

- The base group health-reasoning prompt now carries the concrete-act classification rule so every group turn sees the same boundary; `model-behavior.test.ts` proves group inclusion and direct exclusion.
- The `group-challenge` and `groupchat-comedy` skills now preserve safe authored stakes and prioritize one visible primary payoff; `assistant-groupchat-comedy-skill.test.ts` proves those contracts.
- The existing real-Codex group candidate evaluation now loads all three affected skills and covers the product spec’s safe and hazardous judgment matrix; it is test-only and opt-in when live provider credentials are configured.
- The durable group social-dynamics spec is aligned with the prompt, skill behavior, and real-model candidate cases so future changes retain the same risk and payoff hierarchy.

## Architecture and reuse

- Existing systems reused: The existing conversation-scope prompt builder, group challenge skill, groupchat comedy skill, authored group behavior spec, and real-Codex group candidate evaluation remain the single owners.
- New logic: Prompt guidance classifies proposed dares from concrete risk factors and strengthens one primary visible challenge payoff while keeping secondary avatar/name/apology consequences as garnish.
- New abstractions: None; the existing prompt, skill, and candidate-evaluation contracts are sufficient, and no runtime owner or helper is needed.
- Complexity intentionally avoided: No new state, policy engine, schema, service, queue, compatibility layer, dependency, tool, or bespoke test harness was added.

## Hot reply path impact

- Path status: Touched only in the provider-visible instructions assembled for group replies; control flow and call cardinality are unchanged.
- Database calls: None added or moved; before and after remain unchanged.
- Network/provider calls: None added or moved; the existing provider start remains one call at the admitted turn cardinality with unchanged timeout, retry, and fallback behavior.
- Other awaited latency: None added or moved.
- Before/after proof: Deterministic first-request capture shows only a 774-byte / 154-token group developer-guidance increase; individual input and every non-prompt request layer are unchanged.

## Murph initial provider input impact

| Runtime | Base input tokens | Head input tokens | Delta | Percent | Base bytes | Head bytes | Byte delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Individual Murph | 25,319 | 25,319 | +0 | +0.00% | 114,895 | 114,895 | +0 |
| Group Murph | 21,613 | 21,767 | +154 | +0.71% | 98,192 | 98,966 | +774 |

- Assembled instructions: The base instruction item is unchanged at 3,077 bytes / 570 tokens for both runtimes. The combined Murph/Codex developer-guidance item is unchanged for individual turns at 78,357 bytes / 16,640 tokens and changes for group turns from 61,667 bytes / 12,934 tokens to 62,441 bytes / 13,088 tokens (+774 bytes / +154 tokens). The changed first-request layer is `packages/assistant-engine/src/assistant/system-prompt.ts`; the two changed skill bodies remain deferred and do not add first-request bytes.
- Tool/schema/generated guidance: Production code mode was captured. The eager `additional_tools` item, including argument schemas, is unchanged at 29,933 bytes / 7,278 tokens for individual turns and 29,920 bytes / 7,278 tokens for group turns. Codex-generated permissions, skill metadata, and code-mode guidance are included in the developer bundle; only the group Murph instruction layer changes.
- Other provider-visible input: The identical synthetic user fixture, environment wrapper, root-agent/multi-agent guidance, response format, include list, tool choice, and parallel-tool setting are unchanged.
- Measurement method: Base `63eab95239a09a65a07307a4f146d12106c03c02`; current head `6aaa80ba2fed90e0a79ac0dcf61941aef18995c1`. A deterministic local capture intercepted the complete first `/v1/responses` body at provider-equivalent head `14d4e35f5002b7d7a0511b526660cee2b3b909f9`; the only PR-specific remediation delta after that capture is `packages/assistant-engine/test/assistant-codex-real-e2e.test.ts`; subsequent commits only merge the latest base and leave the PR's provider-input paths unchanged, so the measured PR delta is byte-for-byte unchanged. author: ivanviragine
body:
Closes #84 (absorbs #89).

MCP sync targeting Claude was **inert**: crossby wrote servers to a file Claude Code doesn't read, and remote entries were shaped so Claude would reject them anyway. This fixes that plus the surrounding scope/lossy-rewrite issues, each verified against the official docs (`code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp`, `/settings`).

## What changed

**1. Write where Claude actually reads (`sync/mcp.py`)**
- `ClaudeMCPWriter` now writes `.mcp.json` → `mcpServers` (the project-scope file Claude Code loads), not `.claude/settings.json` (which holds only MCP *policy* keys). Discovery still reads `settings.json`, so anything a user or an older crossby left there keeps working.
- The written names are approved narrowly via `enabledMcpjsonServers` — **not** `enableAllProjectMcpServers`, which would bless servers crossby never wrote. Disabling a server revokes its approval. A malformed `settings.json` is left byte-for-byte intact (servers still reach `.mcp.json`).
- A server present in both `.mcp.json` and `settings.json` gets one informational report row rather than being silently resolved — the non-destructive migration nudge.

**2. Correct remote transport (`sync/mcp.py`, `sync/mcp_discovery.py`)**
- Remote entries emit `type`, not `transport`. Claude Code reads a `url` with no `type` as a stdio server, skips it, and reports the error. `streamable-http` is folded to `http` on read so such servers stop being dropped at validation.

**3. Project scope by default (`sync/mcp_discovery.py`, `sync/readers.py`, `cli/sync.py`)**
- Discovery no longer reads `~/.claude.json` unless `--include-user-scope` is passed. A bare `crossby sync` used to rake personal servers into committed project files; that default isn't defensible. `DiscoveredServer` carries a `scope` (`project`/`user`); the wizard prompt, the scan summary, and the "none found" hint label it and mention the flag.

**4. No silent lossy rewrite (`sync/mcp.py`, `sync/mcp_transports.py`)**
- A `${VAR:-default}` header/env whose default Codex's config can't represent now emits a manual-fix report row (mirroring the existing oauth detect-and-report pattern) instead of dropping the default with no trace.

**5. Every site agrees (`sync/validate.py`, `config/detection.py`)**
- `--doctor`/validate now check `.mcp.json`, `.claude/settings.json`, and (only under `--include-user-scope`) `~/.claude.json` — dropping the project-local `.claude.json` it used to validate but crossby never reads. `detection` counts the union of `.mcp.json` + `settings.json` names without double-counting.

## Verification

1773 tests passing (new coverage: `.mcp.json` write + narrow approval, `type`-not-`transport`, user-scope isolation, `${VAR:-default}` note, validate/detection alignment, Claude→Claude round-trip through one file). ruff + mypy strict clean.

Reviewed in three passes (two independent fresh-eyes reviewers on the diff plus a plan/report interaction check). author: abdulsamadr943-code
body:
fix: use consistent SHA-256 key derivation for AES-256-CBC across all services
  
  Problem
  
  Five Soroban-facing services all contained an identical broken decryptSecret():
  
  crypto.createDecipheriv(ALGORITHM, Buffer.from(ENCRYPTION_KEY), iv)
  
  aes-256-cbc requires an exact 32-byte key. Buffer.from(ENCRYPTION_KEY)
  interprets the string as UTF-8, so any env var that isn't exactly 32 ASCII
  bytes — a UUID (36 chars), a base64 string (44 chars), a passphrase — throws
  Invalid key length at request time, silently breaking agent escrow, dispute
  resolution, fee distribution, KYC attestation, and loyalty minting.
  
  The inconsistency was hidden because two other services in the same codebase
  already handled this safely:
  
  - paymentChannel.js — truncates via .slice(0, 32)
  - channelAccountPool.js — hashes via
  crypto.createHash('sha256').update(key).digest()
  
  The exact same ENCRYPTION_KEY env var could work for payment channels but crash
  all five Soroban services.
  
  Solution
  
  Single shared helper in utils/symmetricEncryption.js:
  
  function deriveAesKey(rawKey) {
    const key = rawKey ?? process.env.ENCRYPTION_KEY;
    if (!key || key.length === 0) throw new Error('ENCRYPTION_KEY is not
  set...');
    if (key.length < 16)          throw new Error('ENCRYPTION_KEY is too
  short...');
    return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(key, 'utf8').digest(); // always 32
  bytes
  }
  
  SHA-256 hashing is preferred over truncation because it folds all entropy from
  the original secret into the derived key uniformly — a 44-char base64 key is as
  strong as a 32-char ASCII key, and no entropy is silently discarded.
  
  All five services now call decryptAesCbc(encryptedValue) from the shared
  helper. Their local crypto imports, ALGORITHM constants, ENCRYPTION_KEY
  captures, and inline decryptSecret() bodies are removed.
  
  Changes
  
  ┌──────┬────────┐
  │ File │ Change │
  ├──────────────────────────────┼────────┤
  │ utils/symmetricEncryption.js │
  │                              │ decryptAesCbc() alongside existing         │
  │                              │ AES-256-GCM webhook helpers                │
  ├──────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ services/agentEscrow.js      │
  │                              │ decryptAesCbc()                            │
  ├──────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ services/disputeResolution.js │ Same                                      │
  ├───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ services/feeDistributor.js    │ Same                                      │
  ├───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ services/kycAttestation.js    │ Same                                      │
  ├───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ services/loyaltyToken.js      │ Same                                      │
  ├───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ utils/validateEnv.js          │
  │                               │ warn if < 32 chars                        │
  ├───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ .env.example                  │
  │                               │ requirements, entropy guidance,           │
  │                               │ generation commands                       │
  ├───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ .env.example        │ Expanded documentation: format requirements,       │
  │                     │ entropy guidance, generation commands              │
  ├─────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ src/__tests__/aesKe │
  │ yDerivation.test.js │
  └─────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  
  Tests
  
  All tests use a 44-character base64 key — exactly the kind of value that
  previously caused Invalid key length.
  
  ┌───────┬───────┐
  │ Suite │ Tests │
  ├───────┼───────┤
  │ deriveAesKey — 32-byte output, deterministic, rejects             │ 9     │
  │ short/missing keys                                                │       │

  │ agentEscrow — confirmPayout, cancelEscrow                         │ 2     │

author: agustincarriso
body:
## UI revamp: remove all PNGs, mobile-first redesign

### Summary
Rebuilt every screen-space UI element (HUD, panels, NPC dialog) using solid
colors and fully rounded shapes — no PNG/texture assets anywhere. Desktop
keeps a compact layout; mobile gets a deliberately different, "Roblox-style"
treatment (bigger buttons, bigger fonts, different composition) instead of
just scaling the desktop layout up. Also fixes several mobile layout bugs
found through live testing (elements bleeding past the safe area, clipped
content, oversized panels) and adds a proper "waiting for server" gate.

### No more PNGs
Removed every texture reference and replaced it with color/shape-based
equivalents:
- Pet panel background, stat bar icons/track/fill, and the Feed/Bath/Sleep/Play
  action buttons
- Bottom nav (My Pets / Inventory / Goals) selected/unselected states
- Caretaker NPC dialog: modal background, character portrait, Next/Adopt/Close
  buttons
- All close ("X") buttons across panels

New shared building blocks in `ui/theme.tsx`: `RoundedBadge` (colored
disc/rounded-square with a short glyph — replaces every icon PNG),
`CloseButton`, a texture-free `StatBar` (badge instead of icon art), and a
texture-free `TactileButton`.

### Mobile specific redesign
Mobile detection wraps the SDK's `isMobile()` (`@dcl/sdk/platform`) with a
`getExplorerInformation` fallback for reliability. Desktop and mobile now
diverge in composition, not just scale:
- **ProfileBar** — desktop: centered top bar. Mobile: top-left corner pill.
- **ColonyBar** — desktop: next to the profile bar. Mobile: top-right corner
  pill.
- **PetPanel** — desktop: compact card above the HUD. Mobile: bottom-anchored
  sheet with big circular care buttons (thumb-reachable).
- **BottomNav** — desktop: compact pills. Mobile: large rounded-square tiles.
- **SideButtons** (Spin / Whistle) — desktop: thin side rail. Mobile: floating
  circular action buttons in the bottom corners.
- **PanelShell** (Adopt / Shop / Inventory / Roster / Spin / Goals / Daily /
  Meteor) — desktop: centered card. Mobile: near-fullscreen sheet with a
  bigger title and close button.

### Safe-area and sizing fixes (from live device testing)
- ProfileBar / ColonyBar pushed down and inset further from the screen edges
  (were bleeding into the device safe area).
- BottomNav buttons made smaller while keeping the same label font size.
- `ServerStatus` connection indicator pulled in from the right edge (was
  rendering partially off-screen on mobile).
- PetPanel and PanelShell backgrounds reduced 40% on mobile (the compact
  mobile virtual canvas made the original near-fullscreen sizing overflow).
- Caretaker dialog background reduced 20% and shifted left, with name/body/
  button font sizes left untouched.

### Scroll support
Swapped `overflow: 'hidden'` for `overflow: 'scroll'` on `PanelShell`'s
content wrapper and the Adopt (species grid) / Roster (pet list) / Goals
(achievement list) containers, so content that doesn't fit is reachable
instead of silently clipped. The NPC dialog's body text is now wrapped in a
scrollable container too, for long pages.

### "Waiting for server" gate
Added `everConnected()` in `state.ts` — distinct from the existing
`serverConnected()` health check, this is a one-time flag that never flips
back to false once the server has answered (so a later disconnect doesn't
yank the whole HUD away, only the connection *indicator* reacts to that).
`ui.tsx` now renders a small `ConnectingScreen` instead of the entire HUD
until the first `stateSnapshot` arrives.

### Testing
- `tsc --noEmit` and `sdk-commands build` pass clean.
- Not visually verified in-engine (no way to render 3D UI from this
  environment) — please confirm on both desktop and a real mobile client,
  especially panels with longer lists (Goals, Roster) for the new scroll
  behavior and the 40%-smaller mobile panel height.

Closes #47

## What changed

- raise the Fly API TLS certificate-chain depth from 2 to 10, matching OTP default
- stop including request headers in Fly API exceptions
- add a regression test proving the authorization header is sent but the token is absent from the raised error

## Why

Fly certificate moved to the longer Let’s Encrypt Generation Y chain, causing FLAME hardcoded depth of 2 to fail with `max_path_length_reached`. Because FLAME also interpolated request headers into exceptions, the resulting Sentry event exposed the Fly API token.

Related upstream incident: https://github.com/phoenixframework/flame/issues/88

- `mix format --check-formatted lib/flame/fly_backend.ex test/fly_backend_test.exs`

author: cu2cu2
body:
## What

Triage of all **6 T1 findings** in this repo. T1 is *"CI step cannot fail — suppression on a step that should gate."* Wave 2 of the estate-wide triage.

**2 FIX, 4 DECLARE.** The interesting result: one of the suppressed copies in the deploy-package step **has never copied anything, in any deploy**, and `|| true` is why nobody knew.

---

## FIX — a copy that has never copied anything

```bash
cp .next/standalone/package.json deploy/package.json 2>/dev/null || true
```

Next 16 with `output: "standalone"` **in a monorepo** writes no `.next/standalone/package.json` — the app manifest lands at `.next/standalone/apps/web/package.json`. So this line has always failed, silently, on every deploy.

Proven from the **shipped artifact** rather than inferred. The zip step lists every file it packages (`zip -r … -x '*.map'` excludes only source maps), so a real Deploy Web run is authoritative. From job `89556600916`:

| entry | count in the shipped zip |
|---|---|
| `node_modules/` | 4198 |
| `.next/` | 519 |
| `server.js` | 1 |
| `.next/BUILD_ID` | 1 |
| `.next/server/` | 431 |
| `node_modules/next/` | 1111 |
| **`package.json`** | **0** |
| **`public/`** | **0** |

**Removed rather than repointed.** `broflo-web` runs `server.js` directly and has never had a `package.json` in its package, so pointing the copy at the correct path would *change what a live App Service receives* — a deliberate decision, not a side effect of a CI-triage PR. If one is wanted, the correct monorepo source is noted in a comment at the removal site.

The `public/` zero is different and benign: **`apps/web/public` does not exist**, so that copy is a genuine no-op. It stays, declared, so that adding a `public/` later needs no workflow change.

## FIX — assert the package instead of trusting eight exit codes

The step ran eight `cp` commands, five of which tolerate failure, and then handed the directory straight to `zip` and `azure/webapps-deploy`. Nothing checked that the thing being deployed was complete. Line 123 in particular copies **the compiled application**:

```bash
cp -r .next/standalone/apps/web/.next/* deploy/.next/ 2>/dev/null || true
```

If Next's standalone layout shifts again — as it already did for `package.json` — that copy fails silently and broflo-web ships with no compiled output.

New `Verify deploy package before zipping` step asserts the **end state** of the artifact: `server.js` and `.next/BUILD_ID` non-empty, and `.next/server`, `.next/static`, `node_modules/next` present and non-empty. Every one of those was confirmed present in the real shipped zip **before** the assertion was written, so it cannot red-line a deploy that would otherwise have worked.

## DECLARE (4)

* **`ci.yml:116`, `:119`** — `cp -n` exits non-zero merely for **skipping an existing file**, so its exit status cannot mean "the hoist failed". Both are best-effort merges into a `node_modules` that line 114 already populated unsuppressed, and both are now covered by the package assertion.
* **`ci.yml:123`** — the compiled-pages copy, now covered by the assertion above (this is the one whose declaration is doing real work).
* **`ci.yml:126`** — `public/` does not exist; genuine no-op.
* **`ci.yml:241`** — single-name idempotent removal of the pre-gateway orphan secret, with the gateway env end state asserted immediately after. Checked against live Azure rather than assumed, because the *same command* in `ops-platform` had silently never run:

```
broflo-ai: anthropic-api-key -> absent
           ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -> litellm-api-key
```

Working as intended. (In `ops-platform` the call passes **two** names, and `az containerapp secret remove` raises on the first already-absent name and only PUTs after the whole list succeeds — so the two-name form removed nothing for months. One name is idempotent; two is a trap.)

---

## Verification

The new assertion positive-controlled **in both directions**, exit codes measured without a pipe, against packages built to match the real artifact:

| case | exit |
|---|---|
| A. complete package (mirrors the real zip) | **0** |
| B. `.next/*` copy silently failed — no `BUILD_ID`, empty `.next/server` | **1** |
| C. `node_modules/next` empty | **1** |
| D. `server.js` missing | **1** |
| **E. no `package.json` — the state that ships TODAY** | **0** |

Row E is the one that matters for safety: it proves removing the dead copy does not red-line the live deploy. Rows B–D are the failures that were previously invisible.

**Scanner:** `--detector T1 --tracked-only` → **CLEAN**, 4 declared (was 6 undeclared).
**`bash -n` over all 28 `run:` blocks — 0 failed.** Included because on the `cu2-billing` PR in this wave, appending a `# theater-ok:` comment to a line ending in `|| true)` swallowed the closing paren of a `$( )` — YAML still parsed and reading did not reveal it.

## Correction to a standing note

`cu-agent-standards` is now **PUBLIC**, so the caller-visibility restriction no longer applies to this repo. broflo's Theater gate run `30414823547` was confirmed to have a **real job** (`theater / Theater gate (ratchet)`, success) rather than being a zero-job green — so the inventory note listing broflo among repos that "cannot call the detector" is stale.

author: chrislusf
body:
A volume's replication lives in two places that can disagree, and nothing tested which one wins.

`Store.ConfigureVolume` rewrites the **`.vif`** and never the replica-placement byte in the `.dat` superblock, so that byte keeps whatever the volume was created with for good. `readSuperBlock` reads it and then overrides it from the `.vif`:

```go
v.SuperBlock, err = super_block.ReadSuperBlock(v.DataBackend)

if v.volumeInfo != nil && v.volumeInfo.Replication != "" {
	...
	v.SuperBlock.ReplicaPlacement = replication
}
```

That override is the only reason a replication change takes effect and survives a remount. Invert it and **every replication change silently reverts on the next mount**, while the `.vif` on disk still records what the operator asked for — a durability setting going back to its old value with nothing to indicate it happened.

## Why a test rather than reading the code

The field immediately beside it resolves the **other way**: `version` takes the superblock over the `.vif`. Two fields, one function, opposite precedence, each one line to invert wrongly — and one of the two directions loses data durability silently.

Confirmed the test catches it. Disabling the override gives:

```
replication after reload = "000", want 010 from the .vif;
a reconfigured volume must not revert to the byte in its .dat
```

The second test covers the empty case: a `.vif` declaring no replication has to leave the superblock standing, or a volume whose replication was never configured would be forced to whatever the zero value parses as. It passes either way, which is the point — it constrains the fix rather than the bug.

`go test ./weed/storage/` green.

## Context

Found while tracing what a tiering replication change actually writes to disk. The Rust volume server in the enterprise tree implements the same override with a `// Match Go:` comment, against nothing that would notice if the two stopped matching; that side is being pinned separately.

  * Added coverage for replication settings when volumes are reloaded.
  * Verified that explicitly configured replication values take precedence over existing volume metadata.
  * Confirmed that empty replication settings preserve the previously stored value, helping ensure consistent volume behavior across reloads.
  * Improved validation of volume information loading before replication settings are updated.

author: jackdanger
body:
Behaviour-neutral: L1 stays on `fast::run` and its bytes are verified back to main's exactly (`data.csv` 4,111,742). This lands the finder plus every falsification, so the search isn't re-run.

## Four hand-optimisations, all bit-identical in output, all measured

Cachegrind on 6,000,000 B of `data.csv` at L1 T1 (Zen2); wall where run is frozen solvency, paired interleaved n=15, /dev/null both arms.

| hand-optimisation | D reads | D writes | wall |
|---|---|---|---|
| u32-packed bucket (1 store, not 2) | flat | **−26.7%** | **zero movement** |
| `hash3` read sunk to the miss path | +0.4% | **+6.9%** | not run — counters worse |
| bounds-check elision | flat | flat | zero movement |
| drop `hash3` insert inside matches | — | — | **falsified on size** |

**The pattern is this codebase's oldest trap: LLVM had already done it, and doing it by hand added work.** The prefilter invariant-load hoist drove Dr up for the same reason. Three more instances here.

The load sink is the sharpest, because the reasoning was *right* — `cur_node3` is genuinely consumed only when the 4-byte search misses (~29% of positions). LLVM sinks it anyway; the manual `if/else` split blocked whatever store merging it was doing, costing 1,353,289 writes.

The u32 packing quantifies exactly: **1.92 extra instructions per removed write** (10,601,417 ÷ 5,517,429) — the shape of `load32+shift+or+convert+store32` against a 16-bit copy. **Stores are not the binding cost here; instructions are.**

## The length-3 argument I got wrong

`armexe.elf` 598,647 → 604,416 B, *worse than the 599,781 B baseline* — a clause-3 flip. My argument conflated **"we never START a match at an interior position"** (true) with **"nothing ever MATCHES AGAINST an interior position"** (false — that's the table's whole purpose). The offset guard discards by *offset*, not by target class.

The vendor precedent is against it too: `hc_matchfinder_skip_bytes` inserts `hash3_tab` at **every** skipped position under the **same** `offset <= 4096` guard I cited. Review also caught that it would have silently un-indexed the entire preset dictionary via a second `skip_bytes` call site my argument never contemplated.

## So the search is closed

The gap isn't shavable overhead: the finder executes **201,359,346** instructions against `parse::fast`'s **92,057,657** — 2.19×, from probing twice and hashing a third table. Counter-level edits move 1–2% and the wall not at all. Recorded in the module doc.

**What remains:** igzip's two-positions-per-iteration, which derives the second probe from work already done for the first rather than paying for a second probe.

Reviews by `claude-fable-5-thinking-xhigh` and `gpt-5.3-codex-xhigh` via cursor-agent; every finding above that I didn't measure myself came from them and was then verified.

Monta el versionado que acordamos: `package.json` como única fuente de verdad, botón "Prepare release" por tipo (+ force), tag automático desde `package.json`, y versión visible en el footer con `-dev` en dev.

## Piezas
- **`package.json` → `0.2.0`** (base, = prod actual) + `package-lock` sincronizado.
- **Footer** (`SiteFooter.tsx`): muestra `v<version>`; en el Worker de dev sale `v<version>-dev` (nuevo `vars.APP_ENV` por entorno en `wrangler.jsonc`: `production` / `dev`).
- **`release.yml`** (modificado): en el push a `main`, taggea `v$(package.json)` (si no existe) + publica Release. Se jubila el token `#minor`.
- **`prepare-release.yml`** (nuevo, `workflow_dispatch`): input `bump` (patch/minor/major) o `exact_version` (force). Calcula desde el último tag, bumpea `package.json` en `release/<v>` y abre PR a `main`. No despliega ni taggea.
- **README**: sección de versionado.

## Bootstrap (cómo se activa la primera vez)
Es auto-arrancable: al mergear esta PR a `develop`, el workflow "Prepare release" ya vive en `develop`. Entonces:
1. Lanzas **Prepare release** (minor) → crea `release/0.3.0` (que ya incluye el nuevo `release.yml`) + PR a `main`.
2. Mergeas a `main` → el nuevo `release.yml` taggea `v0.3.0` y despliega. Prod pasa a `v0.3.0`, dev a `v0.3.0-dev` (tras back-merge).

## Verificación
- `tsc` / `eslint` / `vitest` (53) verde. `wrangler.jsonc` parsea. Footer en local muestra `v0.2.0` (sin `-dev`, `APP_ENV` no está en local).
- ⚠️ **Los workflows solo se validan de verdad ejecutándolos en GitHub.** En la primera ejecución de "Prepare release" y el primer release confirmamos que taggea bien. Requisito de repo: que Actions tenga permiso para **crear PRs** (Settings → Actions → "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests").

## Preferencia aplicada
Comentarios de código y configuración (workflows, wrangler, footer) en **inglés**.

author: schickling-assistant
body:
## Summary

- add `st2 tasks --json` as a versioned, fail-closed desired-task/runtime inventory
- persist exact strict exec generations while reading legacy PID records conservatively and without rewriting them
- join exact PTY and exec evidence behind the shared catalog boundary
- document and prove the two-phase adopt-only replacement order

This is a sibling stack directly on PR #106 exact head `57bb7452a4e5a464b752e82e282b3974be4d97fd`; it is intentionally independent of PR #113. The eventual integration of both stacks has small mechanical overlap in `src/main.rs` and `src/lib.rs`.

## Safety contract

The typed envelope is `st2.task-inventory.v1`. Unknown, malformed, timed-out, duplicate, unreadable, PID-reused, or otherwise incomplete evidence is `indeterminate`, sets `complete: false`, and exits nonzero. A missing PTY root is positively absent and is not created. Observation never reconciles, kills, cleans, or rewrites legacy state.

The cutover order is:

1. CAS active provider tasks to `adopt-only`.
2. Record a complete baseline behind the fence.
3. Stop only the old supervisor and start the replacement.
4. Require a second complete inventory with exact baseline generations.
5. CAS provider lifecycle back to `service`.

Ambiguous legacy exec records remain a truthful cutover blocker. Their narrow, explicitly authorized replacement is follow-up work; this PR does not add a general reset or mutate them during observation.

## Verification

- `cargo check --tests`
- 7 task-inventory unit tests
- 7 strict/legacy exec-generation unit tests
- 6 existing exec-backend integration tests
- 12 task-inventory CLI/E2E tests, including packaged `st2 tasks` with a real PTY generation replacement
- existing hermetic real-PTY targeted lifecycle proof
- existing Nomad-style exec replacement proof
- existing Linux transport-isolation proof
- invariant proof-reference gate
- `git diff --check`

Independent read-only architecture/correctness review approved the final factored diff. No live catalog, supervisor, activation, or runtime state was mutated; one live-catalog inventory measurement was read-only.

author: converseolive
body:
🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) and Auth Bypass in chat APIs. `session_id` was only initialized on the root `/` UI route. A user directly calling API endpoints like `/api/chats` could bypass authorization checks because their uninitialized `session_id` evaluated to `None`. Additionally, any user could view, rename, delete, and chat in any other user's chat session because no authorization isolation checks were performed.
🎯 Impact: Attackers could read private chat histories, mutate others' chats, or manipulate chat sessions without authorization.
🔧 Fix:
- Moved `session_id` initialization from the `index()` route to a globally scoped `@app.before_request` hook.
- Stored the user's `session_id` within the created chat session state.
- Enforced strict authorization checks on all API endpoints that mutate or retrieve chat states, ensuring the object's `user_id` matches the current session.
✅ Verification: Ensure the app correctly provisions and validates sessions for all requests. A new test suite `test_idor.py` has been added which validates that chats created by User A cannot be listed, viewed, renamed, deleted, or interacted with by User B. Run `python -m pytest test_idor.py` to verify.

author: higherorderfunctor
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #609. `kiro-cli acp` still failed for any consumer with a non-empty `trustedMcpTools` — reported from a real project:

```console
$ kiro-cli acp
error: the following arguments are not supported with --agent-engine=v3: --trust-tools
```

#609 fixed the argv *position* of the launcher globals. It did not account for the fact that **the two wrappers compose.**

## Root cause

`kiro-cli` resolves `kiro-cli-chat` through **`PATH`**, not from its own store directory. Proof: drop the wrapped bin dir from `PATH` and the launcher fails with `No such file or directory (os error 2)` rather than falling back to its sibling.

So a real profile runs **both** wrappers on one invocation:

```
kiro-cli acp
  → launcher wrapper  prepends --v3
  → launcher rewrites --v3 to `--agent-engine v3`, finds kiro-cli-chat on PATH
  → chat wrapper      appends --trust-tools
  ⇒ error: … not supported with --agent-engine=v3: --trust-tools
```

Each wrapper was individually correct. The pair was not. I had explicitly assumed the opposite in #609 — that the launcher exec'd its sibling inside the store dir, so the chat wrapper couldn't be in the path of `kiro-cli acp`. That assumption was wrong and is now documented as measured fact.

## Fix

`--trust-tools` is withheld from `acp` when the **runtime-resolved** engine is v3, resolved from argv with the chat binary's own clap default (`v2`) as the fallback.

| | v3 in argv | otherwise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `acp` | withheld | `--trust-tools` |
| `chat` | `--trust-tools` | `--trust-tools` |

The fallback is deliberately **not** what the Nix config bakes in. The chat wrapper cannot know whether the launcher wrapper is in the chain, and `kiro-cli-chat acp` invoked directly runs the **v2** engine however `v3 = true` is set — so a v3 fallback silently stripped a grant the session would have accepted. Nothing is lost on the normal path, because the launcher rewrites argv: `kiro-cli --v3 acp` arrives as an explicit `acp --agent-engine v3`, so the withhold fires on the token rather than on a guess.

## What the launcher actually forwards

Measured by putting a `kiro-cli-chat` that prints its argv first on `PATH`. The launcher injects, translates and drops — it does not relay:

| Invocation | `kiro-cli-chat` receives |
| --- | --- |
| `kiro-cli` | `chat` |
| `kiro-cli --` | `chat` |
| `kiro-cli --agent acp` | `chat --agent acp` |
| `kiro-cli --tui` | `chat --tui` |
| `kiro-cli --tui chat` | `chat` |
| `kiro-cli --tui --v3 chat` | `chat --v3` |
| `kiro-cli acp` | `acp` |
| `kiro-cli --v3 acp` | `acp --agent-engine v3` |
| `kiro-cli --v3 acp --agent-engine=v2` | `acp --agent-engine=v2` |
| `kiro-cli --v3 mcp list` | `mcp list` |
| `kiro-cli settings all` | `settings list` |
| `kiro-cli whoami` | *(kept in-process)* |

`--tui` survives **only** on a bare launch; `--v3` is translated **only** for `acp`.

## Verification

- **The check exercises the chain, and now models the rewrite.** A launcher stub dispatches through `PATH` like the real one, injects `chat` on a bare launch, skips a value-taking option's value, strips `--`, and translates `--v3` per the table above. Several chain assertions were previously asserting argv shapes that never occur in production (they carried a `--tui` the launcher eats); they now assert what the chat wrapper really receives.
- **Positive controls, both measured:** reverting the engine fallback fails exactly the direct-invocation assertion, 1 of 52, with `got [acp]`. Reverting the stub's value-flag skip fails exactly 2 of 52.
- **Real binary:** `acp`, `mcp list`, `agent list`, `settings all`, `whoami` all run under the failing config shape (`tui = true` + `trustedMcpTools`), and `acp` still emits the `--auth=acp-callback` line only v3 emits.
- **52/52 argv assertions**, `nix flake check` green, and all **four** commits evaluate independently (`git test run` across `stack()`, 4 passed / 0 failed).

## Doc corrections in the same commits

An adversarial audit refuted several claims the fragment carried. All are corrected and re-measured:

- `--tui`'s inertness is **structural** — the launcher forwards it only on a bare launch and drops it whenever a subcommand is present. The old justification (byte-identical stdout on `acp`) proved nothing, since the forwarded argv is identical either way.
- The `--v3` translation is **`acp`-only**, not "the dispatched subcommand". `chat` gets it verbatim; `mcp`/`agent` have it dropped.
- `-a/--trust-all-tools` conflicts under v3 on `chat` too, so the conflict set is not purely `acp`-specific. Probe it with input supplied — the "Input must be supplied" error fires first and hides the conflict.
- The TUI's `allow_always` auto-answer is gated on `--trust-all-tools`, **not** `--trust-tools`; `trustTools` appears once in `tui.js`, in the flag table, and is never read by the approval handler.
- `mkPermissionRules` is home-manager-only, so the devenv backend does not recover a withheld grant declaratively.
- No probe script under `docs/plans/` reads back the exec line — the check is the only thing pinning its shape.

The fragment header no longer claims every line is a measured parse result; that blanket assurance is what let the above ship unqualified.

## Known, deliberately out of scope

`--trust-tools` is still appended **past** a caller's `--`, which turns a valid `kiro-cli-chat chat -- hello` (rc=0) into `rc=2 unexpected argument`. Pre-existing, needs its own insertion logic and test matrix. Tracked with six other open items in the private notes as O1–O7.
