author: edwingao28
body:
## Motivation

The default two-GPU speech layout pairs the wrong stages. Today the thinker gets one GPU, and the talker and the code2wav vocoder share the other. But the talker is by far the heaviest stage in the pipeline: at concurrency 8 it holds its GPU at about 86% median utilization. The vocoder is light, at 9-13% median on a shared GPU. Putting the heavy stage next to the near-idle thinker starves both, while the light stage sits on a device it barely uses.

This PR flips the default. code2wav moves onto the thinker's GPU, and the talker gets a device to itself. This costs no extra hardware. It is a reassignment of the same two GPUs.

## Modifications

One production line changes. In `_speech_stages` (`sglang_omni/models/qwen3_omni/config.py`), the code2wav stage is now built with `gpu=thinker_gpu` instead of `gpu=talker_gpu`.

The rest follows from that:

- `tests/unit_test/qwen3_omni/test_colocation_config.py` — two new tests pin the new layout (talker alone, code2wav with the thinker) and confirm the single-GPU variant is untouched. Two pre-existing tests asserted the old placement and were updated to the new one.
- `docs/basic_usage/qwen3_omni.md` — a new "Speech Stage Placement" section describing the layout, the measured numbers, and the memory note below. The two manual-override tutorials now pass `--gpu-code2wav 0`.
- `docs/_static/js/qwen3_omni_server_generator.js` — the three-GPU speech preset no longer emits `--code2wav-gpu 2`. That flag pinned the vocoder to the talker's GPU; dropping it lets the new default apply.
- `examples/README.md` and `examples/launchers/qwen3_omni.py` — the example command lines now show `--gpu-code2wav 0`. The launcher's own argument default was already `0`, so the config default and the launcher default now agree.

The single-GPU colocated pipeline is unaffected by construction. It sets `thinker_gpu == talker_gpu == 0`, so the old and the new expression both resolve to GPU 0.

## Related Issues

Related to #1018.

## Accuracy Test

Byte-identity smoke on hyper01 (H200), one quiet GPU pair, main at `d957911f` against this branch. Both arms ran the same command with no placement flags at all — no `--talker-gpu`, no `--code2wav-gpu`, no `--thinker-gpus`, no `--mem-fraction-static` — so the topology and the memory budgets came entirely from the shipped defaults.

Deterministic recipe: `temperature 0`, `top_k 1`, `talker_temperature 0.0`, `talker_top_k 1`, `talker_top_p 1.0`, concurrency 1, four fixed prompts, `max_tokens 200`. Each arm ran a warmup first, so neither identity run was its server's first work.

All four prompts are byte-identical between the two trees, audio and text:

| prompt | audio bytes | audio sha256 prefix (identical on both trees) |
|---|---|---|
| p0 | 2863198 | `4675198b` |
| p1 | 963004 | `63d821f2` |
| p2 | 2751196 | `3c74db00` |
| p3 | 275632 | `d0c656aa` |

Text hashes matched on all four as well, and neither arm produced a request error. A concurrency-8 run of eight requests against the branch completed 8/8 with zero errors, with every request returning both text and real audio.

A live `nvidia-smi` census taken while each server was serving confirms the move. The small code2wav process (about 1.4-1.6 GiB) sits on the talker's GPU on main and on the thinker's GPU on this branch, leaving the talker as the only pipeline process on its device.

## Benchmark & Profiling

All numbers below were measured on hyper01 (H200), sixteen requests per arm at concurrency 8, arms interleaved with one server running at a time.

**Read the shape of the main experiment carefully, because it is not a direct A/B of this flip.** It ran a tensor-parallel-2 thinker across GPUs 4 and 5, held code2wav fixed on GPU 5 in every arm, and varied only the talker's placement — GPU 4 (sharing with thinker rank 0) versus GPU 2 (its own device). So it is the evidence that *the talker must not share a GPU*. The case for where the vocoder should go rests on the separate follow-up pair further down, plus the box smoke above.

### The talker needs its own GPU

| arm | talker | wall-clock s | time to first audio (TTFA) p50 s | TTFA p90 s | end-to-end p50 s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| colo1 | GPU 4, shared with thinker rank 0 | 24.086 | 1.425 | 2.697 | 10.043 |
| disj1 | GPU 2, alone | 20.159 | 1.198 | 1.463 | 8.937 |
| colo2 | GPU 4, shared with thinker rank 0 | 22.808 | 1.712 | 2.663 | 10.052 |
| disj2 | GPU 2, alone | 20.715 | 0.991 | 1.415 | 9.438 |

Per-pair deltas, talker alone against talker shared (negative is better):

| pair | wall-clock | TTFA p50 | TTFA p90 | end-to-end p50 | stall total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | −16.3% | −15.9% | −45.7% | −11.0% | −48.5% |
| 2 | −9.2% | −42.1% | −46.8% | −6.1% | −55.3% |

Every concurrent metric improves in both pairs. One calibration caveat: an earlier batch on the same host and harness put single-pair deltas of 10-30% inside the measured noise band. The TTFA p90 numbers (−46/−47%) and the stall totals (−49/−55%) are clearly outside that band. The TTFA p50 and end-to-end p50 numbers are consistent in direction across both pairs, but each one on its own sits inside it.

### Why: per-GPU occupancy (median / max utilization)

| arm | GPU 2 (talker when alone) | GPU 4 (thinker rank 0, plus talker when shared) | GPU 5 (thinker rank 1 plus code2wav) |
|---|---|---|---|
| colo1 | — | 86% / 100% | 13% / 89% |
| disj1 | 86% / 100% | 0% / 76% | 9% / 91% |
| colo2 | — | 86% / 100% | 12% / 94% |
| disj2 | 86% / 100% | 0% / 68% | 9% / 95% |

The talker holds 86% median in both placements. Shared, it starves thinker rank 0 on the same device. Alone, thinker rank 0 falls to 0% median. Both thinker ranks are near-idle at this concurrency, so the talker is the bottleneck and the shared shape just oversubscribes one device. code2wav, on the GPU it shares with thinker rank 1, sits at 9-13% median.

### The vocoder does not need a GPU of its own

A follow-up single-variable pair moved only code2wav, with the talker already isolated in both arms: GPU 5 (shared with thinker rank 1) against GPU 3 (alone).

| arm | code2wav | wall-clock s | end-to-end p50 s |
|---|---|---|---|
| c2wA | GPU 5, shared with thinker rank 1 | 20.214 | 8.762 |
| c2wB | GPU 3, alone | 20.068 | 8.685 |
| delta | | −0.7% | −0.9% |

Both are flat. This is a single interleaved pair, so it is weaker evidence than the four-arm experiment above, and it should be read as such. It does point the same way as the occupancy table: giving the vocoder its own device buys nothing, and it does not need to be isolated the way the talker does.

### The single-stream trade

At concurrency 1 there is no contention to relieve, and the thinker-to-talker hidden-state handoff now crosses a device boundary. Single-stream end-to-end latency gets 14-17% worse in both pairs. Single-stream TTFA improves by about 30% in the same pairs, from 0.484 s and 0.493 s down to 0.346 s and 0.343 s. First audio arrives sooner, and the full generation takes modestly longer. Streaming text-to-speech workloads care about TTFA first, which is why this is the right default, but the trade is real and should not be buried.

### Memory

When code2wav shares the thinker's GPU, the thinker's auto-sized KV pool absorbs it rather than the two stacking. On the smoke box the thinker's reservation fell from 123098 MiB to 118712 MiB, about 4.3 GiB, while the vocoder itself needs roughly 1.4-1.6 GiB. Total usage on the shared GPU actually dropped by 1882 MiB, and about 19 GiB of 140 GiB stayed free. There was no out-of-memory error and no mem-fraction tuning of any kind.

The caveat: that absorption only applies to the auto-sized budget. An explicitly pinned `--thinker-mem-fraction-static` gets no automatic carve-out for the vocoder, so a tightly pinned fraction should leave headroom for it. The new docs section says the same thing.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example

author: vertix
body:
`_reset` commands the home pose with `asynchronous=False`, so `run`'s loop stops executing for
the duration of the move. Nothing polls `state()` while it blocks, so the `recover_from_errors()`
call that clears every other reflex never runs. When a reflex stops the control thread, the
blocking call raises into `run`, the exception escapes the control system, and the World goes down
with it.

This happened on the lab rig on 2026-07-30 (internal#154). Nine reflexes during the run were each
logged and cleared by the loop; the tenth landed during a `Discard & Home` and killed the process,
ending the session. In the log that tenth reflex is the only one with no `Robot error:` line after
it — direct evidence the loop was not running.

## What this ships

**The fix** (`franka.py`): catch the reflex where it surfaces and clear it the way the loop would,
re-raising anything the arm does not report as an error so a genuine fault is not swallowed. The
arm holds where the reflex stopped it rather than homing again into whatever tripped it — a retry
there would drive it back into the obstacle.

**The tests** (`tests/test_franka.py`, new): a fake arm fires a reflex on the next commanded move;
the driver runs through a `pimm.World` on a virtual clock, so it is deterministic and needs no
hardware. Against the unfixed driver three of them fail with the rig's exact two frames:

```
positronic/drivers/roboarm/franka.py:300: in run     -> self._reset(robot, robot_state)
positronic/drivers/roboarm/franka.py:225: in _reset  -> robot.set_target_joints(target, asynchronous=False)
RuntimeError: control loop stopped before the joint target was reached
```

They cover the commanded reset (the incident path), the startup reset (the driver's other `_reset`
call site), and that the driver keeps serving commands afterwards. A fourth pins that a failure the
arm does *not* report still propagates.

The driver imports `positronic_franka`, which ships only in the Linux-only `hardware` extra, so
these tests would not run in CI at all. The test module stands the vendor package in when it is
genuinely missing and leaves a real install alone, so a hardware box still tests against the real
thing.

## Still open, deliberately

`_reset` continues to block. This removes the process death but not the blocking window — during
the homing move the loop still is not polling. Closing that means `asynchronous=True` plus a
polling loop, which needs a completion criterion, a timeout and a retry policy; those are design
calls, and this PR does not guess them. Tracked on internal#154.

author: wujingyue
body:
## What changed

- collect MFSDP v2 parameter registrations without deduplicating names, while representing each physical `Parameter` once
- retain every owning-module-relative FQN and use the complete tuple when swapping sharded and unsharded parameter replacements
- register one gradient hook per physical trainable parameter and track backward readiness with a resettable counter
- add a tied-embedding regression test covering two forward/backward cycles, balanced annotations, DBuffer size, and optimizer-visible parameter count

## Why

PyTorch's default parameter enumeration deduplicates tied parameters by object identity. MFSDP v2 instead collected registrations by FQN, so the same physical parameter could receive multiple buffer entries and replacement objects. That broke weight identity and prevented the ready-parameter set from reaching the duplicated trainable-parameter count during backward.

## Impact

MFSDP v2 now preserves tied parameter aliases while allocating, sharding, reducing, and exposing only one physical optimizer parameter.

## Validation

- Black check on all changed Python files

author: alverezyari
body:
Carries tychofleet PR #37, the last piece of putting the pooled master on the site.

The fleet page rendered the M13 master, its source and its preview image, and showed 0h 00m for its per-source seconds, with no error in the log. The reader resolved a master's combine_input edges by joining sub_object_key to the sub table. Those edges hold per-session result keys, so the join matched nothing and returned an empty set rather than failing.

combine_input.sub_object_key is polymorphic: a session-level result's inputs are raw subs, a master's inputs are per-session results. ADR 0005 declared the column as a foreign key into sub, assuming every combine input is a frame; the gateway's writer took the correct reading for masters and dropped the constraint. This fixes the reader to match, and pins it with a test using result-key edges so it cannot regress to what the column name implies.

Expected on the live data: three sources, 5340 + 3680 + 4620 seconds, about 3h 47m.

body:
Motivation:

The ProxyTunnel test fixture could terminate TLS on its listener but had no way to require a client certificate, so tests couldn't assert true proxy mTLS. Client auth is a property of the SSLServerSocket (setNeedClientAuth), not the SSLContext, though the fixture's javadoc claimed otherwise.

Modifications:

- Add needClientAuth(), flipping setNeedClientAuth(true) on the TLS server socket.
- Capture the client cert chain and expose it via lastPeerCertificates().
- Fix the misleading sslContext(...) javadoc.
- Add HttpsProxyTest.testProxyMtlsClientPresentsCertificate.

Result:

Tests can assert proxy mTLS without wrapping the SSLContext. Test fixtures only.

## Resumo

Este PR fecha o **Strike 1** do card Kanban `t_690ebeeb` (Node Think Backend Unification): tipar o contrato Node Think no backend Rust do `kryxd` e corrigir o namespace Nix no tradutor, sem alterar frontend, particionador Disko ou o fluxo de instalação.

## Commits

1. `e3ce276 chore(dev): add rust-toolchain.toml for deterministic builds`
2. `a8b76af feat(kryxd): implement typed NodeThinkPlan in InstallPlanV2`

## Mudanças

### `crates/kryx/src/domain/config.rs`

- Adiciona `NodeThinkPlan { enable, host_id }` com `serde(rename_all = "camelCase")` e `deny_unknown_fields`.
- `InstallPlanV2` ganha `pub node_think: Option<NodeThinkPlan>` ao lado do legado `is_think_server`.
- `host_id` é `String` obrigatória quando `enable = true` — espelha a obrigatoriedade do módulo Nix `node.thinkServer.hostId` para ZFS pool import.

### `crates/kryx/src/services/translator.rs`

- Troca a emissão de `kryonix.thinkServer.enable = true` por `node.thinkServer.enable = true` + `node.thinkServer.hostId = "<valor>"`, lidos de `plan.node_think`.
- O tradutor não consulta mais `plan.is_think_server` (campo legado, aposentado pelo tradutor mas preservado na struct para retrocompatibilidade com call sites externos — será removido no Strike 2).
- Atualiza `test_think_server_translation` para preencher `node_think: Some(NodeThinkPlan { enable: true, host_id: "8425e349" })` e asserir a saída nova + a regressão `!contains("kryonix.thinkServer")`.
- Adiciona `test_think_server_disabled_emits_nothing` (cobre `enable: false`).
- Adiciona `test_node_think_absent_emits_nothing` (cobre `node_think: None`).

### Tooling

- Adiciona `rust-toolchain.toml` com `channel = "stable"` na raiz do repo, para garantir builds determinísticos em CI e em qualquer agente que clone o repo.

## Validação

- `cargo check -p kryx` ✅
- `cargo test -p kryx --lib domain::config::` ✅ (10/10)
- `cargo test -p kryx --lib services::translator::` ✅ (3/3 — preexistente + 2 novos)

- **Strike 2**: remover `is_think_server` da struct e de todos os call sites; atualizar o capability registry e o frontend UI; alinhar schema JSON.
- **Strike 3**: alinhar Disko com os mounts fixos exigidos pelo Node Think (`/srv/data/{home,images,snapshots,storage}` em `zroot`); adicionar regra `node_think.enable ⇒ filesystem == ZFS`.
- **Strike 4**: integrar `target_tree.rs` e `translator.rs` num único pipeline de geração de configuração (hoje ainda há dois artefatos: `disko-config.nix` e `/tmp/generated-install-config.nix`).

author: hexagonal
body:
Closes #177. **Stacked on `sweep-172-shipped-comments` (#178)** — that branch is the base; review this diff alone.

Ten combinators in `stdlib/Seq.hex` bound their pull step to a local and passed the name — `let step = () => ...` then `Seq({ pull = step })` — because a comment in the file said an inline `match` could not be a record-field value. They now read `Seq({ pull = () => ... })`, the shape the four producers above them already used.

## The comment was wrong when it was written

This is the part worth recording, and it corrects this PR's own issue. Checked against `9e135be`, the commit that introduced both `Seq.hex` and the comment, using that era's `pull:` field spelling:

| spelling | `9e135be` | `main` |
|---|---|---|
| `Seq({ pull = () =>` · `match` on the next line · `})` on its own line | clean | clean |
| `Seq({ pull = () => match next(source)` · arms below · `})` trailing | **fails** | **fails** |

Layout is clean for both at both commits; the failure is in the parser. So the working spelling was available the whole time, and ten combinators were shaped around a claim nobody had checked. The failing row is [defect-log finding 5](spec/notes/compiler-conformance-defects.md) — **genuine, still open, unchanged**, and narrower than the comment made it.

This is therefore *not* a revert of a fixed defect, and the tests no longer say it is.

## Verification, done rather than assumed

**Emission strictly improves.** Ten `const step` indirections gone; the IIFE `take` needed to sequence a binding inside a ternary branch gone; 12906 → 12644 bytes; `.d.ts` byte-identical.

**Behaviour is untouched.** The lambda was never invoked at construction in either form, so Loops §6.4's laziness and re-derivation guarantees are unaffected. The `var` cursors in `filter`/`drop`/`dropWhile`/`flatMapWith` were already inside the lambda in both forms.

**Three guards, each mutation-tested** (`seq-stdlib.test.ts`): no `let step`; no `pull =` followed by anything but a literal lambda, which no rename escapes; and a count of 14 constructions, which alone catches an indirection reintroduced across a line break. The count also pins formatting — declared in the comment rather than left as a surprise.

**Two layout tests pin the working shapes directly**, so the prelude is no longer the only thing depending on them.

## Corpus updated where it asserted the opposite

- **Finding 5** gains a correction fixing its scope. It stays open. It also now records that `seq-core-representation.md` §4.1's canonical examples are written in the *failing* spelling and do not compile as printed — left unedited, since that note is a closed rationale archive.
- **`seq-deintrinsification-plan.md`**'s open-items entry: the local-`let` form no longer stands; the ruling is still owed but blocks nothing.
- **Comments §12**'s sweep note settles the #177 IOU, with the general lesson: a shipped comment asserting an impossibility is a claim about the compiler, and nothing was checking it.
- **The grammar's hanging-split note** loses an "every" that this file now disproves. Highlighting is unaffected — `grammar.test.ts` sweeps every `stdlib/` and `runtime/` `.hex` file for invalid and unscoped tokens and passes.

## Judgment calls

Kept `match` on the line *below* the `=>` rather than the design note's §4.1 spelling — §4.1's does not parse, and even if it did, the four loop-bearing combinators open with `var current = source` and have nothing to put on the `=>` line, so adopting it would split one file across two shapes. Did not adopt §4.2's `filterFrom` helper: `filter` is self-recursive, not mutually recursive with a helper, so the note's stated reason for it does not apply.

Compiler 704/704, grammar 143/143, playground 117/117, `check` clean.

Deja listo: 1. **Esqueleto Next.js 14** (App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, shadcn/ui) con autenticación por Magic Link, callback, middleware y tema claro/oscuro. 2. **Esquema Supabase v5 completo** con todas las decisiones tomadas hasta ahora (v2/v3/v4/v5): tipos, funciones contables, vistas de reportes, políticas RLS estrictas. 3. **README con instrucciones** paso a paso. ## Cambios respecto al plan inicial (v1 → v5) - **Sin `retiro_externo`** — los gastos absorben el retiro de efectivo con la categoría correspondiente. - **Sin `adelanto`** en aportes; solo `prestamo`, `pago_deuda`, `reembolso`, `cooperacion`. - **Nesim = administrador** (`perfiles.es_admin`). Único que agrega usuarios, aprueba movimientos en Bolsa General y en bolsas asignadas. - **Bolsas asignadas por Nesim** (`bolsas.assigned_by_admin`): el usuario asignado solo hace solicitudes de ingreso/gasto que Nesim aprueba. - **Sub-bolsas** como compartimentos del padre (`bolsas.parent_id`); saldo padre incluye sub-bolsas. - **Categorías por usuario, sin catálogo por defecto**. Al eliminar, los movimientos históricos quedan como *Sin categoría*. - **Movimientos con estado extendido** (`pendiente_aprobacion | activo | rechazado | anulado`), aprobado_por, motivo_rechazo, dos fechas (`fecha_solicitud`, `fecha_ejecucion`). - **Préstamos con plazo** (`plazo_dias`, `fecha_vencimiento`). Pago de deuda y reembolso se **amarran a un préstamo específico** (`prestamo_id`) que se cierra al saldarse. - **Plantillas de reportes** privadas por usuario. - **Sin tabla de presupuestos**. - **Umbral de saldo bajo Bolsa General** en `config_global`, solo lo edita el admin. ## Funciones clave (todas SECURITY DEFINER con validaciones) - `crear_bolsa_propia`, `asignar_bolsa_a_usuario`, `crear_bolsa_general`. - `registrar_movimiento` — deja `pendiente_aprobacion` cuando la bolsa es General o asignada y el autor no es admin. - `aprobar_movimiento` / `rechazar_movimiento` — el segundo reversa el par si es un aporte ya cobrado al remitente. - `crear_aporte` — genera par sender/receiver; el `aporte_recibido` queda pendiente hasta que el receptor apruebe. - `cancelar_aporte_pendiente` — remitente cancela mientras siga pendiente. - `crear_transferencia_interna`, `anular_movimiento`, `archivar_bolsa`. - `actualizar_umbral_saldo_bajo` (solo admin). - `saldo_bolsa` (directo) y `saldo_total_bolsa` (con sub-bolsas). ## Vistas listas para reportes - `v_saldos_bolsa` (saldo directo y total, avance de meta). - `v_resumen_mensual_bolsa`. - `v_contribuciones_bolsa_general` (quién aportó cuánto). - `v_prestamos_activos` (con saldo pendiente y estado de vencimiento). - `v_deudas_entre_usuarios` (deudas netas). ## Cómo aplicar 1. `cp .env.example .env.local` y llenar variables Supabase. 2. En Supabase Dashboard → SQL Editor → pegar `supabase/apply_all.sql` → Run. 3. Que los 3 usuarios entren con Magic Link una vez. 4. Editar `supabase/scripts/bootstrap.sql` con los correos reales y ejecutar (marca a Nesim como admin + crea la Bolsa General). 5. `npm install && npm run dev` para arrancar la app local. ## Notas - Todas las tablas tienen RLS estricta. Un usuario no ve movimientos de bolsas donde no es miembro. - Los saldos nunca se guardan; se recalculan desde los movimientos activos. - El PR #2 (dashboard) se actualizará para reflejar la RPC `crear_bolsa_propia` y los nuevos campos.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide runtime controls to adjust and reload fake player behavior without restarting the server.
- Rotate and refresh fake player names periodically and on demand while keeping the TAB and server ping counts accurate.
- Allow muting/activating automatic fake-player chat and ensure name validation prevents invalid or currently-online names.

### Description
- Added new command handlers `ZeroCommand`, `PopulatedReloadCommand`, `GirarCommand`, and `ChatMuteCommand` and a helper `registerSimpleCommand` to wire them in `PopulatedPlayerPlugin` and declared them in `plugin.yml` as `zero`, `reload`, `girar` and `mutarchat` (with aliases).
- Introduced a periodic tab-rotation task (`startTabRotationTask`) scheduled every 5 minutes and cleaned up the task on disable and on config reload, and exposed `fakePlayerManager()` accessor used by `reload` command.
- Implemented `ServerPingPacketListener` to include fake players in the status ping shown to the client, and registered it on plugin enable.
- Enhanced `FakePlayerManager` with `targetAmount`, robust name handling via `validAvailableNames()`, rotation utilities (`rotateOnePlayer`, `rotateAllPlayers`, `refreshCurrentTarget`), safer `setTargetAmount` bounds, and removal of players that are no longer allowed.
- Updated `PeriodCommand` to accept an `AutomaticMessageTask` and restart automatic messaging when periods change, and improved `AutomaticMessageTask` message formatting, `isRunning()` introspection, and scheduling behavior.

### Testing
- Built the project with `mvn package` and the build completed successfully with no unit tests present.
- Performed automated packaging smoke check by running the Maven build lifecycle, which succeeded.

author: gsxdsm
body:
Two small things, neither of which changes behaviour.

## 1. A conversion I attempted, measured, and reverted

`hasProgressed` in the wedge-episode path names four column ids outright. I converted them to a resolved lane set. It **broke an existing gate test** — `task-wedge-notification.test.ts` → *"sends one actionable push and mailbox message per active terminal episode"*: 1 message delivered, 2 expected.

The note already in that file was right, and stronger than it read. The hazard is **not** specific to the resolve/claim ordering — it is **any `await` added before the resolve**. Column resolution needs one. `task:updated` listeners fire synchronously, so a re-wedge arriving close behind a recovery reaches `claim` while the first episode is still open, and the operator's second alert is dropped.

Product change reverted; only the comment lands, now carrying the measurement and naming the failing test as the acceptance check for whoever owns the wedge-episode contract. **Left counted, not exempted** — the census should keep pointing here.

Worth stating: the pre-existing note was a warning written speculatively. Attempting the conversion is what turned it into evidence, and the evidence says the blocker is real but sits somewhere else (per-task serialisation) than the note implied.

## 2. `main`'s gate is red, and not from this branch

`pnpm test:gate` fails on a clean `origin/main` tree at `check-sql-column-literals`:

```
packages/core/src/team-analytics.ts: 3 site(s) now, baseline still allows 6 — re-record it
```

A reduction landed without re-recording the baseline in the same commit, which that check explicitly asks for. Reproduced on `origin/main` with my changes stashed, so it is not mine — but it blocks **every** open PR until recorded. Ratchets **31 → 28** sites across 14 files, downward only.

## The vacuous assertion this round (sixth)

The first version of the reverted test passed **with the fix reverted**. `hasProgressed` is a three-clause OR, and the middle clause — *status is a string and is not `failed`* — is true for a recovered task on any board, so `status: "in-progress"` in the fixture satisfied it regardless of column. Same shape as the other five: something the code does anyway. Found by running the revert, not by reading it.

## Verification

`pnpm test:gate` 161 + 487 + 13 + 71 (green only with the baseline commit); `tsc` engine clean; notification suite 77 passed; `pnpm lint` and census `--strict` clean.

author: razumru
body:
Implements `.geniro/planning/chat-ux-improvements/spec.md` — 19 reported items resolving to 16 defects, sequenced as evidence-ordered waves.

## What changed

**Transcript** — tables scroll instead of clipping and GFM alignment passes through (the mechanism is the *opposite* of the spec's first reading: react-markdown translates hast `align` into `style.textAlign` before the component sees it). Fenced blocks route through `CodeBlock` with a copy control. One "answered" row per verdict — the card carries two settled blocks, not one. Auto-scroll follows the tail only from the bottom, while opening a chat still jumps to the newest message.

**Live signals** — `message.usage` rides the ephemeral delta plane so context moves mid-turn; thinking accumulates across the whole turn with elapsed time; `ContextMeter` is extracted and shared by header and panel; run status is written on cancel and *announced* from one helper both the chat path and the graph executor use.

**Composer and rows** — the queue drain keeps the head rendered, is keyed per run, and honours a removal that lands during the RUN_BUSY backoff. Inline rename replaces the modal. `DELETE /v1/chats/:runId` clears rows, attachments, PTY mirrors and call tokens. Reasoning effort became an adapter capability; cursor reports none and renders no chip rather than a disabled one.

**Questions** — AskUserQuestion renders as tabs, one per question, each returnable and re-answerable, with header titles, multiSelect, free text on every tab, and a per-tab budget that *says why* Submit is disabled instead of greying out. Changed across both declared twin parsers in the same commit.

**Structure** — every per-CLI fact moved behind `AgentAdapter`; one `AgentAdapterRegistry` replaces five private kind→adapter dispatches.

## Review

Three rounds of parallel review (five dimensions plus an adversarial tester) produced **52 findings**. Every round found real bugs in the previous round's fixes:

| Round | Findings | Live bugs |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 32 | 6 |
| 2 | 14 | 4 — all inside round 1's fixes |
| 3 | 6 | 2 — both inside round 2's fixes |

Three of round 1's bugs were introduced by this work's own units: a chat with history opened at the *top*, delete left orphan rows surviving an "irreversible" delete, and the thinking row never cleared past the 64 KB tail cap. The adversarial tester independently found two more that no reviewer caught.

Worth flagging for reviewers: `hardDeleteIncludingSoftDeleted` — an irreversible data path in a **vendored** package — had shipped with no tests, and now disables the `softDelete` filter *by name* rather than disabling every filter, which matters wherever a scoping filter exists.

## Verification

`pnpm full-check` green — **750 daemon / 653 UI / 27 mikroorm**, zero lint warnings. Both new UI surfaces (the tabbed question card and the inline rename row) were also verified visually in a browser, since the suites pin behaviour and ARIA rather than appearance.

author: pyshx
body:
Addresses two reliability findings raised against #2185, plus two more of the same shape found while verifying them.

## Why a retry is the problem

`pgxx.Client.WithinTransaction` re-runs the **entire callback**:

```go
for attempt := 0; ; attempt++ {
    err = c.runOnce(ctx, fn)
    if err == nil || !errors.Is(err, usecasex.ErrTransaction) || attempt >= c.retries { return err }
}
```

`pgxx.WrapError` maps Postgres `40001`/`40P01` to `errors.Join(usecasex.ErrTransaction, err)`, the Postgres repos route errors through it, and `postgres/container.go:18` turns it on:

```go
client := pgxx.NewClient(pool, pgxx.WithTxRetry(2))
```

So every external effect inside a closure can happen twice.

## What was wrong

**Cloud job submission inside the closure** — 5 sites: `deployment.go:381`, `project.go:277`, `project.go:400`, `trigger.go:239`, `trigger.go:354`. Because `job.New().NewID()` was *also* inside, a retry minted a **new job ID** and submitted a **second** cloud job. The first kept running and billing with no DB row and no monitoring.

**Irreversible GCS deletes inside the closure** — `Deployment.Update` removed the old workflow object before the row that stopped referencing it was durable. Any later failure (upload, `FindHead`, `Save`, the commit, or a retry) rolled the row back to a `WorkflowURL` whose object was already deleted → deployment permanently unrunnable. `Deployment.Delete` had the identical shape; it was not in the original report but is the same defect, so it is fixed here rather than leaving two of three instances in place.

## One correction to the report

The report stated *"Previously (pre-PR) SubmitJob ran outside any transaction; this PR moved it inside."* That is not what happened — at `d10ad0a^` it was already wrapped:

```
363  tx, err := i.transaction.Begin(ctx)
415  gcpJobID, err := i.batch.SubmitJob(...)
425  tx.Commit()
```

What #2185 actually introduced is **retry**. That splits the two failure modes:

| Failure mode | Status |
|---|---|
| Duplicate concurrent cloud jobs via retry | **New in #2185** |
| Orphaned cloud job when the commit fails | **Pre-existing** |

Commit failures wrap as `rerror.ErrInternal`, not `ErrTransaction`, so they never retry — they just roll back after the job is live. Worth noting the realistic trigger is `40P01` **deadlock** rather than `40001`, since `pool.Begin` uses the server default isolation (READ COMMITTED).

## The change

Build the job and upload its objects first, keep the transaction to **DB work only**, and submit after it commits. If submission then fails, the row is marked `FAILED` (`failJob`) so the user sees a terminal state instead of a job stuck `PENDING` behind a cloud job that never started. `StartMonitoring` also moved out of the time-driven trigger's closure — it spawns a goroutine, which a retry would launch per attempt.

Both GCS deletes now collect what to remove and do it after the commit, best-effort: a failure there leaks an object instead of breaking the deployment.

## Also fixed: latent nil dereference

`deployment.go:237` called `currentHead.Version()` **before** the `currentHead != nil` check three lines below, so the first deployment of a project could panic. The guard's existence shows nil was considered reachable.

## Deliberately unchanged

The two `UploadWorkflow` calls still inside transactions. Upload is additive — a retry leaks an unreferenced object rather than corrupting state or double-billing — so hoisting them is a tidiness fix, not a correctness one, and would widen this diff further. Happy to follow up separately.

The pre-existing window where the row commits and the process then dies before submitting still leaves a `PENDING` row. Closing that needs a sweeper, which needs a new `repo.Job` query implemented across all four backends plus leader election, and it overlaps a separate pre-existing gap: `StartMonitoring` is in-process (`activeWatchers` map + goroutine), so in-flight jobs already lose monitoring on any restart. That deserves its own design rather than being bolted on here.

## Verification

- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt` clean
- `go test ./internal/usecase/...` green, including the existing permission tests from #2186
- A scripted scan confirms no `SubmitJob`/`SubmitProbeJob`/`RemoveWorkflow`/`StartMonitoring`/`UploadMetadata` remains inside any `WithinTransaction` closure

The regression test drives the closure twice, exactly as a retried serialization failure does, and asserts a single submission. Against the previous code it fails:

```
Error: Not equal:
  expected: 1
  actual  : 2      // two probe jobs submitted, two workflow uploads
```

author: jperla
body:
Closes the end-to-end loop on both non-GCP clouds. **Identical smoke, both green.**

| | Azure Sydney | AWS Dublin |
|---|---|---|
| `verify_deployment.sh --expect-monitor` | **6/6** | **6/6** |
| Synthetic freshness | 66s | **0s** |
| Database | own Postgres | **Aurora DSQL (multi-region pair)** |
| Scheduler | Container Apps cron job | EventBridge → API destination |

## The AWS blocker was auth lifetime, not infrastructure

**Aurora DSQL tokens expire in minutes.** A static-password `ConnectionPool` works at deploy time and then dies within the hour, and the failure surfaces as assorted `OperationalError`s that look nothing like auth — a genuinely nasty way to find out.

`TR_POSTGRES_IAM_AUTH=aws-dsql` installs a pool subclass that mints a fresh token before **every physical connection**, from the ambient instance role. The DSN carries no password and there is no key in config. Empty setting leaves the static path byte-identical, and `boto3` stays lazily imported so `tests/test_cloud_sdk_boundary.py` still holds.

## A trap that would have produced convincing wrong data

`TR_API_BASE_URL` defaults to GCP prod. Without pointing each deployment at **itself**, both clouds' synthetics would have probed GCP and recorded *the wrong cloud's health* on their own status pages — green dashboards proving nothing. Both are now self-targeted.

## `--expect-monitor`

`verify_deployment.sh` gains a check requiring a synthetic sample under 30 minutes old. That is the difference between "the status page serves" and "the synthetics are actually running", and it is what upgrades both clouds from 5/6 to 6/6.

## Honest about the attestation probe

The attestation synthetic runs on both clouds and reports **`trust_degraded`** — correctly, because no TEE exists there yet. It goes green when an enclave answers, not before. Nitro work for Dublin is in progress separately.

## Verification

Codex wrote the pool + smoke extension to spec and was straight that its sandbox blocked localhost TCP, so the live-backend runs are mine: **52 conformance passed** (memory + postgres + spanner-pg), ruff and mypy clean across 194 files.

## Still gating inference

`reserve`/`settle`/`refund` remain stubs, so both deployments are control planes, not routers.

author: mikeab7
body:
## The defect

`MapFinder.jsx` created its Leaflet map with `const cfg = COUNTIES_MAP.harris; // default landing view (no pre-picked county)`. Harris County was therefore the opening view for **every account on earth** — a brand-new user in Denver, Phoenix or Atlanta opened over Houston, Texas, which reads as broken software.

`B1102` had noted this on the record and deliberately left it alone ("where the app opens is a product decision, not a bug fix"). This is that decision.

## The rule — derived, never a preference

No setting, no toggle. Three cases:

1. **No located sites → the whole continental US.** The honest empty state.
2. **Exactly one site → that site's AREA at metro scale**, never its parcel.
3. **More than one → the DENSEST CLUSTER**, so a single distant outlier cannot drag the camera.

Case 3 is the one that matters today: 26 sites around Houston (Harris, Fort Bend, Waller, Chambers) and exactly ONE in Weld County, Colorado must land on **Houston**, with the Colorado site simply not pulling the view — and if Colorado ever becomes the denser market, the landing view follows on its own.

## What's in the diff

- **`src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/landingView.js`** — pure (no Leaflet, no DOM, no React). Single-linkage clustering at a 50-mile threshold; most sites wins; ties to the most recently updated, then first-seen order so the answer is deterministic. **Single-linkage is load-bearing, not incidental:** Waller to Chambers is ~75 miles apart — further than the threshold — and only chains into one market through the Harris sites between them, exactly as a person reads it.
- **Zoom.** Bounds are fitted with generous padding, the fit is FLOORED to Leaflet's integer steps (so it errs wide, never tight), and the result is clamped to a metro/county ceiling. Degenerate bounds — one site, or every site within a mile — fit to infinity by construction and fall straight onto that clamp, which is exactly what it's for.
- **It's where the map OPENS, not a leash.** `landedRef` / `userMovedRef` latch on real input (a press, a wheel, a drag) rather than on Leaflet's `movestart`/`zoomstart`, which our own programmatic `setView` also fires — so a late-arriving cloud site list can never yank a camera the user is already driving.
- **`counties.countyForView(lat, lng)`** (new, pure). The Layers-panel jurisdiction follower read `candidateCountiesForPoint(...)[0]`, whose out-of-bbox answer is **harris-first by contract** (click routing depends on that order, and `test/counties.test.js` asserts it) — reading it as a jurisdiction would have claimed Harris County over Denver. The new resolver takes a bbox hit (nearest county center among overlapping padded boxes, so downtown Denver reads Denver), otherwise the nearest configured county **within the point's own state**; statewide parcel pseudo-keys are never returned. Click routing is untouched, and a test asserts it stayed untouched.

## Verification

- `test/landingView.test.js` — **28 pure cases** with the owner's real distribution as the fixture: zero sites yields the US *and the US actually fits the opening viewport*; one site clamps to metro scale; 26 clustered + 1 far outlier yields the cluster and **not** a bounding box of both (asserted three ways, including that the Weld point is outside the computed visible rect); equal clusters tie-break to the most recent and flip when the other is touched; a missing timestamp reads oldest; sites within one mile still clamp out; two coincident sites don't divide by zero; the clamp holds at phone / laptop / 4K sizes; clustering is order-independent; plus a **source guard** that fails if a fixed county is ever assigned as a view again or the follower goes back to `candidate[0]`.
- `test/counties.test.js` — +7 for `countyForView`.
- `ui-audit/verify-landing-view.mjs` — **16/16 in headless Chromium** across three seeded accounts, reading the map's real position from the app's own cursor readout (needs no tile host) and asserting off-screen-ness against the real site pins in the DOM. Account C — the owner's 26 + 1 — opens on **Houston (29.714, -95.306) at zoom 9, all 26 Houston pins on screen, the single Colorado pin off-screen**; and after a hard pan the view does not yank back.
- Full suite green · lint 0 errors · build green · `MAP.md` + `BACKLOG_OPEN.md` regenerated · doc-pointer and panel-copy audits green.

## Perf budget — a recorded raise, not a silent one

`bundle.siteRouteJsBytes` 2242.2 → 2289.4 KB, logged via `npm run perf:ratchet -- --allow-raise` with its reason on the record. **This diff is +3.5 KB** of that; it cannot be lazy-loaded because it decides the map's first frame. The other **+43.7 KB is accumulated drift that rode inside the 44.8 KB headroom band unrecorded** — `main` at a748911 already measured 2285.9 KB against a 2287.1 KB derived ceiling, i.e. 1.2 KB of band left, so any feature at all would have breached it. Payback stays tracked by B1064.

## Still pending live (V592, `Blocker: auth`)

The sandbox proxy CORS-blocks Supabase sign-in, so every account here is seeded into local storage and its site list is present at first paint. What's owed is the **signed-in** timing: the map is created before a cloud site list arrives, and the landing effect is what re-lands once it does.

author: malinmalliyawadu
body:
Fixes the two guidelines iOS 1.0 (7) was rejected on (submission `fa77907a-01b8-4932-b1ac-abef1f77813a`, 30 Jul 2026).

## 4.8 — Sign in with Apple

Offered beside Google on both the sign-in and register screens, using Apple's own `AppleAuthenticationButton` rather than a redrawn one — App Review checks the mark's proportions and localisation, and the native component gets both right by construction (it also localises itself into te reo).

- `apple-sign-in.ts` mirrors the existing Google service: lazy native import, cancel treated as a decision rather than an error, hidden outright where the sheet can't work.
- `apple-id-token.ts` re-verifies the token against Apple's published keys — signature, issuer, audience, expiry — before trusting a single claim. Unit-tested.
- `apple-accounts.ts` links on `sub` and refuses to adopt an email that already belongs to a password account, the same rule the Google path uses.

## 5.1.1(v) — Account deletion

Self-service erasure in the app (Profile → Delete account) and on the web (`/staff/account`). Both call the same code, so what "erased" means can't drift between them.

**The blocker worth reviewing:** deletion could not succeed for the people who actually run the kitchen. `Shift`, `TrainingSession`, `Announcement` and `Event` all required a `createdById`, so the old code refused with "archive them instead" — precisely what the guideline forbids. Those columns are now nullable with `onDelete: SetNull`, so a shift that happened still happened and simply stops naming anybody. This follows the reasoning already used for `Announcement.eventId`.

The only remaining blocker is being the last active admin — not a data-retention excuse, but that erasing them leaves an organisation nobody can administer, with no way back in.

## Two things this turned up

**A deleted or archived user kept browsing.** Web sessions are JWTs and the layout gates never re-read the database, so access outlived the account by up to 30 days. This was pre-existing and also affected archiving, but shipping self-service deletion on top of it wasn't defensible. The gates now re-check and send a dead session through a route handler — only a handler can clear a cookie, and redirecting straight to `/login` loops because the token still reads as signed in. The mobile API never had this problem: `authenticateApiRequest` already re-reads the user per request.

**Apple returns the email only on the first authorisation.** That couples the two fixes: deletion must also revoke the Apple token (itself a 5.1.1(v) requirement), because without it someone who deletes their account can never sign up with Apple again — their next attempt arrives with a `sub` we don't know and no address to build an account from.

## Testing

- Lint, typecheck and tests green: 873 web, 22 mobile.
- Deletion verified end-to-end against a real database: deleting the seeded coordinator removed the account and left all 14 shifts, 3 training sessions and 1 pānui intact with the author dropped; the last-admin blocker and the dead-session lockout both behave.
- **Not visually verified on iOS** — Xcode is installed but not selected on this machine (`sudo xcode-select -s ...` needs a password I can't supply), so the mobile screens are covered by typecheck, lint and tests only. Apple sign-in needs `build:ios:dev` regardless; it can't run in Expo Go.

## Before this can ship

1. Create a "Sign in with Apple" key in the Apple Developer portal and set `APPLE_TEAM_ID` / `APPLE_KEY_ID` / `APPLE_PRIVATE_KEY` in production. Sign-in works without them; **revocation does not**, and that is part of the guideline.
2. If Resend mail should reach "Hide My Email" users, register the sending domain with Apple's Private Email Relay or those pānui bounce silently.
3. `pnpm mobile build:ios` — the entitlement change moves the runtime fingerprint, so **no EAS Update can deliver this**.
4. Reply in App Store Connect with a screen recording of the deletion flow on a physical device.

## Alternative worth knowing

You could instead reply to App Review arguing the first-party email/password login satisfies 4.8; reviewers sometimes accept that, and it costs no Apple key management. Sign in with Apple is the definitive fix and likely wanted anyway, so that's what's built here.

author: operinko
body:
Follow-up to #1639. The unit still fails, now for a different sandboxing reason:

```
Identity file /root/.ssh/technitium-cert-sync not accessible: No such file or directory.
Host key verification failed.
```

against files that plainly exist:

```
-rw------- 1 root root 1101 Jul 31 01:56 known_hosts
-rw------- 1 root root  399 Jul 31 01:51 technitium-cert-sync
```

**`ProtectHome=yes` mounts `/root` as an empty directory.** ssh could see neither the key nor `known_hosts` — hence both errors at once, which is what makes it look baffling rather than like a permissions problem.

```diff
-ProtectHome=yes
+ProtectHome=read-only
```

Read-only is all the service needs: it reads both files and writes neither.

## Also: `StateDirectory` instead of a `ReadWritePaths` entry

```diff
-ReadWritePaths=/etc/dns /var/lib/technitium-cert
+ReadWritePaths=/etc/dns
+StateDirectory=technitium-cert
```

`ReadWritePaths` requires its paths to **already exist** or the unit fails setting up its mount namespace. `/var/lib/technitium-cert` only exists on `ns1` because the script was run by hand there — on `ns2` the previous version would have failed for this second, unrelated reason. `StateDirectory` creates and owns it.

## The pattern behind both bugs

This is the second sandboxing failure in this unit, after `ProtectSystem=full` made `/etc` read-only. Same root cause: **the script works from a shell and fails as a service**, because the sandbox decides which paths are visible at all — and the resulting errors describe missing files rather than a restricted namespace.

README now says to run the first test via `systemctl start` rather than invoking the script directly, since a direct run proves nothing about whether the timer will work. That would have caught both of these immediately.

## Summary
- Follow-up to #28: `sshhost --ssh`, and `sshyou`'s `-L`/`-R`/`--ssh`, take their value as a single quoted argument so the flag and its value travel together through option parsing. That quoting prevents the shell from tilde-expanding paths like `~/.gnupg/S.gpg-agent`, so `ssh` received a literal `~` and failed to bind (`unix_listener: cannot bind to path ~/.gnupg/S.gpg-agent: No such file or directory`).
- Expand `~` to `$HOME` ourselves in these option values so paths like `sshhost --ssh "-L ~/.gnupg/S.gpg-agent:/Users/laseryuan/.gnupg/S.gpg-agent"` work as originally typed.
- Updated `--help` text in both scripts to document the expansion.

author: kbennett2000
body:
Adds `0x0877` set-modulation and its `0x0878` reply — **F7**. FM and AM. Reasoning lives in radio-server [ADR 0149](https://github.com/kbennett2000/radio-server/pull/206), per AGENTS.md.

## `0x0877`, not `0x0875`

radio-server's ADR 0111:52 records the classic Dock's full-control extras as *"0x0872 modulation, **0x0873/4 backlight, 0x0875/6 AM emulation**"*. nicsure's source is not vendored here so that census cannot be re-verified — per guardrail 1 it is treated as **claimed**, not free-until-proven.

Reading it turned up something worse: **`0x0873/4` is on the same list**, and it was allocated after ruling out `0x0872` alone. That one is shipped, on hardware, in a cut release. It cannot be walked back. This one was cheap to place correctly, so it was. `PROTOCOL.md` now tells the next implementer to check the census before allocating.

## A new opcode, not a 14th byte on `0x0873`

A field appended there changes bytes on a frame radio-server already sends and breaks **both** directions **silently** — an old host's 13-byte frame is refused `ERR_SHORT` and reads as a tuning failure; a new host's 14-byte frame decodes fine on old firmware, which then tunes on a modulation nobody set. A new opcode is additive: an old host never sends it, a new host gets silence from firmware that lacks it. **An empty `0x0877` is the F7 probe**, safe because the length check is the first branch.

## The modulation is sticky, and `0x0873` applies it

Not a convenience. **This link drops frames** (ADR 0131 — single-threaded firmware, anything arriving while it is busy is discarded, not queued), so "tune, then set modulation" as two frames can leave the radio on the right channel in the wrong demodulator with nothing on the wire saying so.

- **Seeded FM from a constant**, never read back off the radio — that is the "adopt whatever state you find" fault (ADR 0132), and would tune a repeater channel in whatever the front panel was last left on. A host that never sends `0x0877` sees F6 behaviour exactly.
- **A refusal never moves it.** Committing during decode would let a refused request silently become what every later tune applies — the same bug in mirror image, and invisible because the refusal itself was reported correctly.
- **`0x0873`'s wire bytes are untouched.** One literal at `uart.c:850` became a table lookup whose default is that literal.

## `0x0878` reports what the radio is on — and whether it can still transmit

Read back out of the radio's VFO after applying, not echoed, plus the radio's own raw enum value. **On any non-zero status both are `0xFF`, not `0`** — `0x0874` blanks frequencies to zero because 0 Hz is obviously not a channel, but **`0` is FM**, so copying that would answer a refusal with a plausible claim about where the radio is. The one place a literal copy of the existing code produces a shipped bug.

And a **flags** byte, because a successful set-AM stops the transmitter: without `ENABLE_TX_WHEN_AM` (this tree is not built with it) `RADIO_PrepareTX` refuses any non-FM modulation, and that is the path the radio's **PTT pin** drives — where radio-server's `baofeng` backend keys from via the AIOC's DTR line. Dock REG_30 keying bypasses it, so the same state means "cannot transmit" on one backend and "transmits normally" on another. **The flag reports the condition; it does not remove it. AM stays receive-only.**

## The wire names its own values

`ModulationMode_t`'s numeric end **moves with `ENABLE_BYP_RAW_DEMODULATORS`**, so a wire bound derived from it means different things in two builds of the same protocol. `uart.c` maps both ways: in, a `_Static_assert`'d designated-initialiser table; out, a `switch` with a `default`, because an array indexed by that enum reads off its own end on exactly the build where the extra members exist. `DOCK_POWER_MAP`'s lesson applied before it bites.

USB's **number** is reserved; its **value** is refused. Nobody has put this radio on USB at a bench, it cannot transmit in it anyway, and accepting it later is purely additive.

## Fail-first — run against the bug, twice

| Build | Result |
|---|---|
| Stub: always reports success, echoes the request, commits the sticky value unconditionally | **98 checks, 15 failures** |
| Correct command, but `0x0873` keeps its `MODULATION_FM` hardcode | **98 checks, 2 failures** — exactly the two stickiness cases |
| This branch | **98 checks, 0 failures** (66 before) |

The second run is the one that matters: it fails only what it should, so green on the real build means something.

- The byte-exact **`0x0874` golden stays green** — that is the gate on `0x0873`'s wire being untouched.
- New goldens came from a **separately written framer** validated by reproducing `PROTOCOL.md`'s published `0x0951` and `0x0874` vectors byte-for-byte first. A vector produced by the implementation it checks is a transcript, not an oracle.
- Two tests are commented to say they **stay green against the stub** (31 "reaches the binding once", 33 "F6 compatibility") so nobody later cites them as proof the refusals work.

## Lockout: confirmed no

`gSerialConfigCountDown_500ms` is armed at exactly four sites — `CMD_0514`, `CMD_051B`, `CMD_051D`, `CMD_052F` — none reachable from the dock dispatch, and it appears nowhere else in `App/` but its declaration, definition, the scheduler decrement and `SerialConfigInProgress()`. The only post-switch statement in `UART_HandleCommand` is `gUART_LockK5Viewer`, which suppresses telemetry.

## Size

**FLASH 105,576 B of 118 KB (87.37%)**, +240 B over F6's 105,336. Headroom 15,256 B. RAM unchanged at 13,088 B (79.88%).

## Also fixed

`dock.h`'s module docstring still claimed the module has **no modulation commands** and had never mentioned `0x0873`. The `⚠ CONFIRM AT BENCH` counts in `BENCH.md` ("four") and `AGENTS.md` ("five", while naming four) disagreed with each other before this cycle added to them — both now describe the items instead of counting them.

## Not claimed

**Not flashed. No hardware result.** AM audio over the AIOC and the PTT refusal are new `⚠ CONFIRM AT BENCH` items in `BENCH.md`, left as placeholders (guardrail 1). The F7 pre-release's `PROVENANCE.md` says so rather than carrying F6's measured-on-hardware paragraph forward.

## Resumen
El final del script tenía `create policy if not exists (...)`, que no es sintaxis válida en Postgres (a diferencia de `create table if not exists`, que sí existe). Supabase corre el SQL pegado en el editor como una única transacción implícita, así que ese error de sintaxis hacía fallar y deshacer **todo el script** — incluida la carga de los 52 locales reales, que nunca llegaba a guardarse.

También se saca el bloque de `inspections`/`audios` que había quedado al final: ese modelo viejo se reemplaza por completo en `migrate_v3_equipment_state.sql`, no correspondía tenerlo acá.

## Test plan
- No aplica build/test automatizado (es un script SQL). Verificado manualmente que no queden `create policy if not exists` en ningún archivo de `supabase/`.

author: alpha9463
body:
Every label in the `.pdf` and `.png` output was drawn at three quarters of the
size the sheet sets it in. The `.svg` was and is correct; only the export path
was wrong, and it has been since cairosvg was replaced.

## The mechanism

Confirmed in svglib 2.0.2, and it is the double conversion it was reported as.

- `AttributeConverter.convertLengthToPt` (svglib.py:606) returns
  `convertLength(...) * PX_TO_PT`, and `applyStyleOnShape`'s `mappingF` maps
  `font-size` through it (svglib.py:2304), so a `<text font-size="100">` sets the
  ReportLab `String`'s `fontSize` to **75**.
- `SvgRenderer.renderSvg`, for the outermost `<svg>`, computes
  `x_scale = (width * PX_TO_PT) / view_box.width` and applies
  `group.scale(x_scale, -y_scale)` (svglib.py:1604, 1642). For a sheet whose
  width and viewBox agree in user units — which is every sheet pandid writes,
  including the ones sized in mm — that is exactly **0.75**.

So the string is drawn inside a transform that has already made the px-to-pt
conversion its own size carries: `100 → 75 → 56.25 pt`, against geometry's
`100 → 75 pt`. The PDF content stream says it out loud: `.75 0 0 -0.75 0 150 cm`
followed by `/F2 75 Tf`.

Reproducing the reported measurement (400×200 SVG, a 100-tall rect with a 2-wide
stroke, and a `font-size="100"` Helvetica `H`, rasterised through `to_png` and
measured on the ink):

| | drawn | expected | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| geometry, before and after | 102.00 | 102.0 | **1.000** |
| cap height, before | 54.00 | 71.8 | **0.752** |
| cap height, after | 72.00 | 71.8 | **1.003** |

## The fix

No rewriting of the SVG can state this away — svglib *does* implement
`font-size`, it just applies the conversion twice — so unlike `<use>`,
`marker-end` and `dominant-baseline` this one does not belong in `flatten()`.
The correction goes on the ReportLab drawing instead: after `svg2rlg` has built
it, before `renderPDF` writes the page, and on nothing but `String.fontSize`. No
geometry can follow it. What `text-anchor` shifts a centred or right-set string
by is worked out from that same `fontSize` when ReportLab draws it
(`renderPDF.py:165-172`), so a centred label is re-centred on the new size.

The factor is **measured, not written down**, for the reason `_ascent_descent()`
asks `pdfmetrics` instead of carrying a constant: `_TYPE_PROBE` declares a square
and a capital at one size, and whatever `svg2rlg` makes of it states what the
backend draws a glyph at against what it draws a line of the same length at. On
an svglib that has stopped converting twice the probe reads 1.0 and nothing is
applied, so this ages into a no-op rather than into lettering 4/3 too big with
nothing to say so. If the probe comes back as anything but one rule and one
string, the export raises rather than guesses, the way an unsupported construct
already does.

## Held by measurement

`test_lettering_is_drawn_at_the_size_the_file_asks_for` is the invariant that
was missing: a capital's rendered cap height against the 0.718 em Helvetica
declares, with a rule of the same declared length in the same document as the
control, rasterised so the capital is ~170 device px whatever size it is set in.
It is parametrized over **every distinct `font-size` the goldens carry** — read
off them rather than listed, so a new one is covered the day it is drawn; today
6.5, 7.5, 8, 9, 10, 10.5, 11, 12, 12.5, 18 — in both weights.

Without the fix it fails at all ten sizes (0.537–0.538 against 0.718) and the
geometry control passes either way, which is the whole claim in one test.

## Composing with the vertical centring (#159)

#159's shift is a fraction of the size the *file* states, and the size drawn is
now that one, so the two now agree. Its residual — the gap between the x-height
middle `middle` names and the middle of an all-capitals ink box, about 0.10 em —
is now at its full value rather than 0.10 em of three quarters:

| | measured offset from the halo's middle |
|---|---|
| before, `03_distillation_train` | −0.16 px (accidentally near zero) |
| after | −1.03 to −1.24 px, matching the arithmetic |

**Its tolerance could not be tightened; it had to be re-stated.** At true size
`T-100` lands at exactly −1.50 px and the old assertion was `abs(off) < 1.5`, so
it fails on the boundary. The test now asserts the offset it *expects* —
`(_MIDDLE - _CAP_HEIGHT / 2) * size`, which is where the SVG's own alignment rule
puts the ink and where a browser draws it too — to **0.5 px**, on a raster of two
device pixels per user unit. That is a tightening, not a loosening: it holds the
type size and the alignment at once, and it fails if the type-size correction is
removed (`'S1' sits −0.25 px … where its 10 type puts it −1.03`).

## Does anything collide at true size?

**No.** Audited on `11_ethanol_pid` and every golden, and the reason it is safe
is structural: `pandid.render.furniture.text_width` and the layout engine have
always measured text at its *declared* size, and the `.svg` has always drawn it
there, so the room was reserved all along. The export was drawing smaller than
the room already set aside for it.

- **Label against label** — ink boxes from `pdfmetrics`, halo/ink duplicate pairs
  excluded: **0 overlapping pairs** at true size on `11_ethanol_pid` (222 labels)
  and on all ten goldens. Same count as at three quarters.
- **Label against its own white halo** — worst overrun **0.02 units** across all
  sheets, which is the halo rect's own `%.1f` rounding. Nothing escapes the
  knock-out it was struck.
- **Balloon tags**, the tightest fixed box on a sheet — the closest ink corner to
  a balloon edge anywhere has **4.45 units** of clearance (`LIC` in a panel
  balloon); on `11_ethanol_pid` it is 6.04 (`PAH`). The SIS diamond, which is
  drawn for a two-figure number, carries a single figure on that sheet.
- **Title block, legend, notes** — `fs.validate()` reports no cell overrun on any
  of the eleven examples.

Visually: title-block rows, balloon tags, valve tags and note rows all fill their
cells properly instead of floating small inside them, and nothing is clipped.

`test_every_label_on_the_sheet_reaches_the_page` (the `Tj`-run count, per golden)
and `test_the_exported_pdf_draws_the_sheet_rather_than_a_picture_of_it` (vector
PDF, real `/BaseFont /Helvetica`) both still pass.

## Scope

- `pandid/render/svg.py` untouched; **no golden moves** — the SVG writer is not
  involved.
- **`docs/gallery/` is deliberately not regenerated here.** The gallery PNGs are
  re-rasterised in one pass, at a higher resolution, once the export path is
  settled; doing it in this PR would mix a 3 MB binary diff into a 200-line fix.
- No change to `pyproject.toml`, the Python floor, CI config, `scripts/`,
  `examples/` or `pandid/units.py`.

## Gates

All four, locally, on this branch rebased onto `origin/main` (`70ff905`):

```
python -m pytest -q            3633 passed, 16 skipped
python -m ruff check .         All checks passed!
python -m ruff format --check tests   45 files already formatted
python -m mypy pandid          Success: no issues found in 33 source files
```

## One thing found and not folded in

`svglib.convertText` measures its fragment advances with `stringWidth(text, ff,
fs_pt)` where `fs_pt` is the same doubly-converted size, and uses them to place a
`<text>` that has no `x` of its own, or a multi-`<tspan>` one. Under the bug that
was self-consistently wrong; with `fontSize` corrected on the drawing it would be
self-consistently *right* only for the single-fragment `<text x= y=>` pandid
actually writes, which is all of them. Worth knowing if the renderer ever grows a
`<tspan>` — it would want handling alongside, not instead of, this.

body:
Items **2–4** of the doc-vs-code audit (item 1, `CLAUDE.md`, is PR #346). Every claim below was
verified against the tree at this commit **before** editing; corrections are marked in place rather
than rewriting the documents, so the original intent stays readable and reviewable.

### `LEGAL_INVARIANTS.md` — the file an auditor would be handed
| Claim | Reality |
|---|---|
| Channel lock enforcement **✅ Реалізовано і покрито тестами** | **VERIFIED FALSE** — zero occurrences of `integration_owner` / `channel_lock` / `opened_via` / `SHIFT_CHANNEL_SWITCH_FORBIDDEN` in migrations or src. Frozen invariant #3 holds **by construction** (profiles come from `node_state` and don't change at runtime; the only guard is `MissingProfileBinding`), not by a mechanical check |
| 24h / 36h / 168h limits **⚠ not yet enforced** | They **are** enforced — `services::time_budget` constants + a pre-mint check in `write_path/inline.rs`, toggles default on |
| INV-11/12 via `offline_ranges`, `next_fiscal_no`, `uq_fiscal_documents_offline_no` | **None exist** (Python-era). The *guarantee* holds — the mechanism is the FN-scoped `offline_codes` pool + `ux_offline_codes_consumed_by_doc` + a consumed-row immutability trigger |
| Five recovery classes (AutoOfflineFallback, …) | **Zero occurrences** in `rust/prro/src`; shipped behaviour is **fail-closed** (WrapperBug → ErrorRetryable + CRITICAL audit + STOP_MODE), not auto-offline |
| Close-code reserve **"exactly 1"**, code `OFFLINE_CODE_RESERVED_FOR_CLOSE`, "W10 pending" | Reserve is **dynamic** — `(BEGIN missing) + (offline Z needed)`, admit iff `free >= 1 + reserve`; the real code is `OFFLINE_CODE_RESERVE_HELD`; **W10 landed** |
| Cash formula without the issued-set qualifier | Production counts only `state IN ('ACK','OFFLINE_LOCAL_ACK')` (bd x5o) and the opening carry now orders by `closed_at DESC, rowid DESC` (bd seb); service-in/out + EPZ are wired, not TODO-gated |
| "ledger of issued receipts **only**" | Restated as the real pin: **no doc rests in a NON-TERMINAL state at a quiescent boundary**, with the persisted non-issued terminals listed (A.3) |

The two most expensive here are the **false assurance** about a frozen invariant (someone trusts a
guard that does not exist) and the **inverted** time-limit status (someone re-implements a closed gap
or demands a pilot risk sign-off for a risk that is gone).

### M3b shift spec — pins that would make someone "fix" correct code back to broken
- **"Total: 14 edges"** vs the shipped whitelist, whose **locked-count test asserts 18**. The four
  CS-3 additions are now listed: 15 `Opened→RMR`, 16 `Opening→Closed`, 17
  `OpenedLocalPendingDrain→Closed`, 18 `ClosingLocalPendingDrain→OpenedLocalPendingDrain`.
- `OpenedLocalPendingDrain → Closed` was listed under **FORBIDDEN** — it is **edge 17**, driven only
  by the operator-completion seam for an offline `SHIFT_OPEN` DPS never accepted (a rollback, not a
  close-with-a-Z, so the absent `z_report_document_id` link is correct there).
- **"OFFLINE_LOCAL_ACK docs are stored UNSIGNED until drain" / "signed bytes MUST be NULL"** is
  inverted by **B9**: offline docs are signed at `stage_sign` with the code stamped in-band as
  `<MAC ID>` in the same pin-tx; offline-ack is a slim CAS and drain never re-signs.

### `CONSOLIDATION_SPRINT_ROADMAP.md`
The copy on `main` still said **"CS-0 (in progress) … Nothing coded yet"** with CS-1/2/3 red, while
CS-0…CS-3 are all merged. Status board corrected with the evidence (plan + specs #1/#2 in `docs/`,
`rust/prro-domain/`, migration 032, the S7-1 cutover `224ad46e`, the fuzzer track `949d7cc1`),
CS-3 marked closed with its recovery follow-ups (2nk / hpc / x5o / mcc), and the next gate named:
**CS-4, spec #6**.

Docs-only; no code touched. A **full CS-3-vs-documentation reconciliation** is tracked as
`PRRO_GATE-9xl` — CS-3 outgrew its spec family and no single document describes the shipped shape.

## Summary
- The Flink e2e suite only ever started a jobmanager+taskmanager with no job running, so it never exercised task/operator-scope metrics (`numRecordsIn`, watermarks, etc.) — only JVM-level metrics.
- Submits Flink's bundled `StateMachineExample.jar` (self-contained, no external deps, runs continuously) as part of `dd_environment` setup, gated by a `WaitFor` poll of the taskmanager's `/metrics` endpoint instead of a blind `sleep`.
- Extends `test_e2e_discovery` (not `test_e2e_jobmanager_metrics` — task/operator metrics are only exposed via the TaskManager's own endpoint) with presence assertions for representative task and operator metrics, now exercising real tag extraction (`job_name`, `task_name`, `operator_name`, `subtask_index`) against genuine Flink-emitted data instead of only the hand-written `tests/fixtures/metrics.txt` fixture used by unit tests.

Stacked on `fix/flink-openmetrics-counter-types` (DataDog/integrations-core#24740) since that's what makes `flink.task.numRecordsIn`/`flink.operator.numRecordsIn` submit correctly. This PR is opened against that branch in my fork so the diff stays test-only; it'll get retargeted at `master` once #24740 merges.

Note: this does **not** assert `metric_type=MONOTONIC_COUNT` in e2e — the real Agent's `monotonic_count` sender computes its delta internally and the e2e replay JSON reports the result as `gauge` regardless, which is why no e2e test in this repo asserts that type. author: charlesgreen
body:
Closes #51. **Do not merge before running the copy — see the order below.**

## The name
`skills-cdn-prod`. Repo `skills`, thing `cdn` (it matches the Worker's own name), env `prod`. The issue asked to settle the missing env suffix in the same change: that suffix is the part that actually stops environments colliding, so a future `skills-cdn-dev` now has somewhere to go.

Renamed in `workers/cdn/wrangler.jsonc`, `provision.yml`, `r2-sync.yml`, `r2-upload.yml`, **and the two script defaults** — `r2-bootstrap.mjs` and `r2-migrate.mjs` both fell back to `simplycubed-skills` when `R2_BUCKET` was unset, so leaving them would have let a run silently target the old bucket.

## What I got wrong first, because it changes the plan
My initial approach was to repopulate the new bucket from git, since `r2-migrate.mjs` re-verifies against the manifest before every PUT. **That does not work here.** Only `manifest.json` is committed; the unit bytes exist solely in R2. A local dry run failed on a missing `snapshots/<slug>/unit`, which is also why `r2-sync` is safe on every merge (its `--sync` mode skips anything already on the CDN and so never needs to pack).

So this is a genuine object copy, exactly as the issue described. What git *does* provide is the **key list**: objects are content-addressed off `contentHash`, so the 110 active manifests name all 220 objects without ever listing the bucket. The offline dry run derives **220** — the same count the issue reports, which is a useful independent check that nothing is missed.

## `scripts/r2-copy.mjs`
- **Fail-closed:** each blob is re-hashed against the git manifest after the read and before the write, so a corrupt or truncated source object cannot propagate.
- **Idempotent:** an object already in the destination is skipped, so a re-run after a partial failure resumes.
- **Never deletes.** Dropping the old bucket stays a deliberate human step.
- **`--dry-run` is offline** and needs no credentials, matching `r2-migrate`'s convention. (My first version probed the destination before checking the flag, which made the dry run hang without credentials. Fixed.)

## A latent flaw this surfaced, left alone on purpose
`provision.yml` creates the bucket and then immediately deploys the Worker. On a rename that binds the live CDN to an **empty** bucket, so every snapshot 404s until an upload runs. I tried adding a populate step there and reverted it once I found the bytes are not reproducible from git. The ordering below avoids the window instead; worth its own issue.

## Order of operations
1. **Dry run:** dispatch *Copy R2 objects between buckets* from this branch, `source=simplycubed-skills`, `dest=skills-cdn-prod`, dry-run **on**. Expect 220 derived, 0 failed.
2. **Copy for real:** same dispatch, dry-run **off**. Creates the bucket and copies. The old bucket keeps serving throughout, so there is no downtime.
3. **Cut the binding over:** dispatch `provision.yml` **from this branch**. It deploys the Worker against the now-populated `skills-cdn-prod` and smokes the CDN.
4. **Verify:** run `r2-verify.yml` (or `pnpm r2:verify`) and confirm the CDN round-trips.
5. **Merge this PR.** `r2-sync` fires on merge and will target a bucket that exists and is populated. Merging *before* step 2 makes that run fail against a missing bucket.
6. **Delete `simplycubed-skills`** once verified. Destructive and deliberately not automated.

Steps 1 to 4 need Cloudflare credentials, which is why they run as dispatched Actions rather than from a terminal.

## Gate
`pnpm gate`: 12 passed, 0 failed (2 scanner steps skipped locally). `pnpm workflow:lint` passes on all seven workflows. The copy script itself is unexercised against live R2 — its dry run is the furthest it can be verified without credentials.
